items.title: The KLR Grothendieck ring satisfies the divided-power quantum Serre relations
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]], KL I Propositions 3.1-3.2).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1=[P_{j,0}]$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $A f$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.
items.strategy:
The induction associativity and unit are the balanced block identifications already proved. Iterated idempotent restriction is coassociative, with counit the rank-zero component. To prove the compatibility, filter the bimodule e_(beta,gamma) R e_(beta',gamma') by the double cosets of the two block permutation groups, ordered by crossing length. PBW partitions its basis by these cosets. Multiplication across a braid move changes only smaller-length terms, so the associated quotient is the four-block induction/restriction bimodule, shifted by minus the root pairing of the two crossed middle blocks. Taking classes gives exactly the twisted tensor multiplication q^(-(deg second,deg first)); no use of the second adjunction is necessary.
For the Serre relation fix i!=j, d=-a_ij, D=d+1 and N=D+1=d+2. For 0<=r<=D take the divided-projective corner of the word i^r j i^(D-r), using its two nil-Hecke idempotents, and apply the shift defining the normalized P_(i,r) and P_(i,D-r). The neighboring maps are right multiplication by the crossing strings moving j across one i block, cut by these idempotents. In the printed source notation, e_(r+1) cuts the rth corner and alpha_(r,r+1)=e_(r+1) tau_(N-1)...tau_(r+1)e_(r+2), alpha_(r+1,r)=e_(r+2)tau_1...tau_(r+1)e_(r+1). Consecutive forward maps compose to zero because a repeated i-crossing hits the nil-Hecke symmetrizing idempotent. Expand Q_ij(u,v)=sum t_ab u^a v^b. The braid relation makes the difference of the neighboring forward/backward compositions the divided difference of Q in the two outer i variables. The r-1 and N-r-2 same-color divided differences extract only u^d: all terms of u-degree<d vanish, and weighted homogeneity excludes any u-degree>d. Its coefficient t_d0 is a unit by Q4. Therefore the resulting endomorphism is plus or minus t_d0 times the identity. Rescale each backward map by that unit and the alternating sign, obtaining d h+h d=1 on the finite complex. The fixed native tau=-tau_source changes the crossing strings by explicit length signs; absorb these in the backward rescalings, leaving the same contracting identity. The normalized shifts make the neighboring differential degree zero. This is the full contracting calculation of Rouquier Lemma3.13 (PDF27–28), which works over the universal coefficient ring and hence after every Q specialization, not a flat-family invariance assertion. A bounded split contractible complex has equal even and odd direct sums: with d h+h d=1 its even-to-odd operator d+h has inverse d+h after choosing the split contraction with h^2=0; such a contraction is obtained by the successive splittings. Taking its alternating classes gives sum_(a+b=D)(-1)^a[P_(i,a)][P_j][P_(i,b)]=0. If a_ij=0, the invertible crossing (Q_ij a nonzero constant) gives the commuting class relation.
First define gamma over Q(q) from the negative Serre presentation. The nil-Hecke decomposition sends each F_i^(n) to the normalized P_(i,n). Since the A-form is the A-subalgebra spanned by ordered divided words, the field homomorphism restricts to it; no false claim that the integral form is an ordinary free algebra on F_i is made. The projective # duality fixes normalized one-color divided projectives, hence the word classes and their bar involution. Mackey proves coproduct compatibility. No source parameter-specialization is asserted to preserve arbitrary projective ranks.

items.title: The KLR Cartan pairing is the Lusztig-normalized half form
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], let $B_K$ be the normalized Lusztig-Kashiwara form on the negative half of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] and put $B_L:=C_
u B_K$ on the weight component $
u$, $C_
u=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-
u_i}$, the Lusztig-normalized form of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]. Then for homogeneous $x,y\in A f_
u$ the Cartan pairing of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] satisfies
$$(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))_{KLR}=B_L(x,y)=C_
u\,B_K(x,y),$$
where $\gamma:A f	o K_0(R)$ is the algebra homomorphism of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]. Equivalently, the two bilinear forms are equal under the identification of divided-power classes; in particular the KLR pairing is $\mathbb Q(q)$-nondegenerate on each finite weight component $A f_
u\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)$ after extending scalars, and $(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))'_{KLR}=B_L(\overline{x},y)$, where bar acts on the first input, not on the scalar value for the hom pairing. On generators: $([P_i],[P_j])=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}=B_L(	heta_i,	heta_j)$ and $([P_{i,n}],[P_{i,n}])=B_L(	heta_i^{(n)},	heta_i^{(n)})=\prod_{a=1}^n(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$.
items.strategy:
The two forms are characterized by the same three conditions, so the comparison is a uniqueness check. On the KLR side, KL I Proposition 3.3: $(1,1)=1$; $([P_i],[P_j])=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$; and the adjunction identities $(x,yy')=(r(x),y\otimes y')$, $(xx',y)=(x\otimes x',r(y))$ with $r=[\mathrm{Res}]$. On the abstract half side, KL II Proposition 1: the same three conditions (with $r(	heta_i)=	heta_i\otimes1+1\otimes	heta_i$) determine a unique symmetric bilinear form on the free algebra, and it is the normalized form with $(	heta_i,	heta_j)=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$, which is the source normalization of Lusztig's form. The dictionary between $r$ on the abstract half and the skew-derivation recursion of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] is exactly the content of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]: with $v=q^{-1}$ and toral inversion, the twisted coproduct multiplication becomes the normalized Kashiwara shuffle convention, and the extracting recursion for $e_i'$ converts the $r$-adjunction into $B_K(F_iP,Q)=B_K(P,e_i'Q)$; the root-colour factor $C_
u$ turns this into $B_L(F_iP,Q)=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}B_L(P,e_i'Q)$. Hence $C_
u B_K$ and the KLR form satisfy the same recursive characterization on a spanning set and coincide. Injectivity of $\gamma$ is not used: the equality is checked on $	heta$-monomials by induction on height. Finally, $B_K$ is nondegenerate on each finite weight component by [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], and nondegeneracy is preserved by the unit $C_
u$; AC enters only through that nondegeneracy supplier (its generic-pairing construction), and is recorded in the dependencies.

items.title: The KLR category categorifies the negative quantum half
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $A f$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free A-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free A-rank of $A f_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an A-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.
items.strategy: The complete local maximal-tail supplier gives absolute simplicity and a finite triangular divided-projective/simple matrix with diagonal1 over A. Its integral elimination proves that the selected P(Y_b) are an A-basis of K_0(R(beta)), so gamma is onto. This is the integral argument, not merely rational character-map surjectivity or a flat-family inference. The repaired Cartan comparison makes gamma preserve B_L; if gamma(x)=0, pairing against every y gives B_L(x,y)=0 and nondegeneracy forces x=0. Thus gamma is an A-isomorphism for every field and every graded Hermitian datum satisfying Q4. Mackey/Serre supply twisted coproduct, induction multiplication and normalized projective# bar compatibility. All divided words span; only the selected string-word family is the triangular basis. The equality of finite free A-ranks of K_0 and A f is its consequence; it does not compare the infinite-dimensional algebra R(beta) with the quantum half. The source parameter extension is proved by the local PBW/Mackey/maximal-tail calculations, which use precisely nonzero homogeneous Q and invertible extremal coefficients; Rouquier4.2.4 is not mislabeled as an invariance theorem. AC is inherited only from the nondegenerate quantum-half supplier.

items.title: Self-dual KLR projectives have positive first-block divided-string leading terms
items.statement:
For any graded KLR datum in this page and any field k, each finite-dimensional graded simple shift orbit has a unique representative S_b self-dual for D(M)_d=Hom_k(M_-d,k), with action (a f)(m)=f(psi(a)m). Its projective cover P_b, normalized by Hom^0(P_b,S_b)=k, satisfies P_b#=P_b for P#=HOM_R(P,R)^psi. These are unique normalizations. Induction of two self-dual finite projectives is self-dual. If epsilon_i^L(S_b)=r>0 and Delta_i^(L,r) S_b=L(i^r) boxtimes S_a with epsilon_i^L(S_a)=0, normalized as above, then
[P_(i,r)][P_a]=[P_b]+sum_(epsilon_i^L(S_c)>r) m_c(q)[P_c],
with m_c in N[q,q^-1], each invariant under q->q^-1. Under gamma the integral LEFT divided-string ideal I_(i,>=n)=sum_(r>=n) F_i^(r) U_A^- is the A-span of [P_b] with epsilon_i^L(S_b)>=n. Consequently, if the normalized projective classes are known to be a SIGNED lower-global set, this leading coefficient1 identifies them with the POSITIVE lower-global set using the general adapted right-string recursion; no finite-ADE canonical-comparison theorem is needed. For the conclusions compared with the quantum half and the conditional lower-global/LEFT-string recursion, carry the inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) of those quantum suppliers; the generic finite module duality/parity/Frobenius arguments themselves are choice-free.
items.strategy:
The maximal-tail supplier gives a triangular divided-idempotent/simple Hom matrix with diagonal1 over A. At q=1 it remains invertible. Ordinary dimensions of divided-word corners are determined by ordinary word dimensions: the nil-Hecke matrix presentation in each constant-color block makes the full polynomial-column simple rank r! and the divided idempotent a rank-one matrix projection, so dim(e_div M)=dim(e_expanded M)/product r! for every finite M, including nonsemisimple central quotients. Thus ordinary word characters separate simple shift orbits. D preserves simple modules and fixes ordinary word dimensions, since psi fixes the word idempotents. Therefore D S ~= S{s} for some integer s.
Choose a total color order and define p(nu)=sum_(a<b,nu_a>nu_b)b_(nu_a,nu_b) modulo2. Each adjacent unequal swap changes p by its crossing degree modulo2; equal crossings and dots have even degree. PBW therefore puts e(eta)R e(nu) in degrees congruent to p(eta)-p(nu). A graded module splits into the two submodules with d-p(nu) fixed modulo2 on e(nu)M_d. A simple uses one of them. D S has the same sector because -d-p(nu) is congruent to d-p(nu); hence s is even. Replacing S by S{s/2} gives D S=S. Uniqueness follows because a nonzero finite-dimensional graded module cannot be isomorphic to a nonzero shift of itself (compare its finite least and greatest degrees).
For finite projective P and finite M, evaluation gives Hom(P#,D M)=D Hom(P,M), with ordinary homogeneous degrees. Verify this on P=R e(nu){a}, where both sides are the dual of e(nu)M{-a}, and restrict to a finite direct summand. The duality # is an involution on finite projectives by the evaluation proof in the divided-power supplier. It follows that P_b# is the same normalized indecomposable projective cover of D S_b=S_b, hence P_b#=P_b. A nonzero projective is bounded below, so its finite generating degrees also exclude nonzero self-shifts; the normalization is unique.
If M is a finite projective over the separated block algebra B, then Hom_R(R e tensor_B M,R)=Hom_B(M,eR). Since M is a finite projective, the latter equals Hom_B(M,B) tensor_B eR by evaluation, checked on finite free modules and summands. Twisting by the horizontal psi identifies this with R e tensor_B M#, without reversing the horizontal block order. For M=P_a boxtimes P_(i,r) it proves Ind M self-dual. The normalized finite nil-Hecke simple L(i^r) is D-self-dual because its cover P_(i,r) is #-self-dual. Restriction commutes with D since psi fixes the defining block idempotent. Hence the maximal FIRST-block restriction of normalized S_b is precisely normalized L(i^r) boxtimes S_a, with no residual shift: that tensor is D-self-dual and any extra shift would contradict finite support.
Use the exact tensor/Res adjunction and maximal-tail lemma to compute Hom(Ind(P_(i,r) boxtimes P_a),S_c). It vanishes if epsilon_i^L(S_c)<r. If epsilon_i^L(S_c)=r, its maximal restriction is L(i^r) boxtimes S_a', and the Hom is zero unless a'=a, when it is exactly k in degree0. The unique-head lemma makes c=b in that case. Projective-cover Hom detects the multiplicity polynomial of each summand, so the induced projective has exactly [P_b] with coefficient1 at tailr and all other summands at strictly higher tail. Self-duality of the induction and each normalized projective forces every multiplicity polynomial to be bar invariant; finite decompositions give nonnegative coefficients.
For every n, induction with a divided block of length r>=n has no summands of tail<n by the same Hom calculation, so gamma(I_(i,>=n)) is contained in the span of those covers. Conversely descend on the finite possible tail r (bounded by beta_i). The just-proved coefficient1 expansion expresses every [P_b] of tailr as [P_(i,r)][P_a] minus classes of strictly higher tail, which are already in I_(i,>=r). This proves the reverse inclusion INTEGRALLY. It uses the sum of all divided images, not an invalid Gaussian-unit identification with a single ordinary power ideal.
Finally suppose [P_b]=gamma(sign_b G(b')) has been established by a separate norm/geometric argument. The ideal equality and the adapted LEFT-string lower-global basis identify the tail partitions of these signed vectors with the LEFT string partitions. At the exact LEFT-string quotient, the QG5 lower-global recursion has coefficient+1 for F_i^(r)G(a') when a' has LEFT string0. Induction on root height fixes sign_a=+1; comparing the projective coefficient1 expansion with this quotient fixes sign_b=+1. The unit/vacuum starts the induction. The required LEFT recursion is the explicit general half transition in thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced. The reversal supplier only promises signed star preservation, so an unsigned right recursion is deliberately not inferred. No geometric restriction functor is imported in this sign proof; it is the explicit projective adjunction calculation above. No AC is used except inherited quantum-half/global suppliers.

items.title: Self-dual indecomposable KLR projectives give the lower global basis (symmetric type)
items.statement: Assume the Cartan datum of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] has symmetric Cartan matrix $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and uses the quiver normalization $d_i=1$ for every $i$, the field $k$ has characteristic $0$, and the KLR parameters are the quiver-geometric ones (the specialization attached to a finite quiver without loops, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities $h_{ij}$ and $a_{ij}=-(h_{ij}+h_{ji})$: $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ for $i\ne j$, in the fixed native crossing-sign convention; arbitrary parameter changes, including a global replacement by $u+v$, require their own proved gauge equivalence). Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the contravariant graded projective duality $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$ ($P\cong P^\#$ after the unique normalizing shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. No extension to arbitrary KLR parameters or to non-symmetric Cartan data is asserted here; any such extension requires its own parameter-change invariance theorem.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The symmetric quiver-normalized Cartan datum with $d_i=1$, a characteristic-zero field $k$, the quiver-geometric parameters $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$, the categorical form of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]], the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]], and the QG-5 global-basis machinery of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]], [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]], [[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]], [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]].

**Choice.** Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice of the geometric and quantum suppliers; the finite presented-algebra comparison and finite graded Yoneda argument below introduce no additional choice.

[F1] Categorical input ([[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]]): $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras and twisted bialgebras intertwining the forms, and every finite graded projective has a normalized self-dual representative with the pairing of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]].

[F2] Positive first-string supplier ([[lem-klr-projective-duality-and-positive-divided-string-leading-terms]]): normalized self-dual projective covers satisfy the coefficient-$1$ FIRST-block expansion, the integral LEFT divided-string ideal equality, and the positive FIRST/LEFT global comparison; its inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is carried here.

[F3] Actual geometric realization ([[def-quiver-full-flag-incidence-varieties-and-geometric-klr-generators]], [[thm-signed-klr-algebra-is-the-equivariant-ext-algebra-of-quiver-flag-complexes]], [[thm-quiver-flag-convolution-generators-satisfy-the-signed-klr-relations]], [[thm-quiver-flag-relative-position-strata-give-a-faithful-geometric-pbw-basis]]): the intrinsic presentation has the full distinct-color adjacent dot slides, native equal-color mixed and braid signs, and a faithful action generated by the native polynomial operators on summands with unit degree $-d_\nu$; the Ext product is $a*b=b[n]\circ a$ for $a$ of degree $n$, with source-first corner $e_\eta R e_\nu=\operatorname{Ext}_G(L_\eta,L_\nu)$.

[F4] Actual semisimplicity ([[cor-quiver-full-flag-pushforwards-are-semisimple-in-characteristic-zero]]): for every finite loopless quiver with arbitrary finite arrow multiplicities and every characteristic-zero field, $L_\nu=R\pi_{\nu!}k[d_\nu]$ and their finite sum are finite direct sums of shifts of simple objects in the actual equivariant perverse heart of [[thm-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]]. That bounded heart gives $\operatorname{Hom}(T,T[n])=0$ for $n<0$ and division $\operatorname{End}(T)$ for simple $T$.

[F5] Projective covers ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]], [[lem-klr-maximal-tail-restriction-and-induction-have-a-unique-simple-head]]): graded indecomposable finite projectives are projective covers of finite-dimensional graded simples, and those simples are absolutely simple over $k$.


[F6] Actual splitting ([[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]): the bounded equivariant constructible category is triangulated and idempotent complete.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; build the geometric realization, run the graded-Yoneda argument, then globalize and fix the signs with the positive first-string supplier.

1.1 (The graded algebra comparison.) Set $P_{ij}(u,v)=(v-u)^{h_{ij}}$ for $i\ne j$. These are nonzero, including when $h_{ij}=0$, and $P_{ij}(u,v)P_{ji}(v,u)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}=Q_{ij}(u,v)$. Thus [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]] gives a faithful action of $R(\beta;Q)$ by projections, dots and unequal crossings $(x_r-x_{r+1})^{h_{ij}}s_r$, with equal crossings $(1-s_r)/(x_r-x_{r+1})$. The actual geometric action of [F3] uses exactly those operators. In both actions give the unit of the $\nu$ polynomial summand degree $-d_\nu$: the incidence formula $d_\nu=\sum_i\beta_i(\beta_i-1)/2+\sum_{a>b}h_{\nu_a\nu_b}$ gives $d_{s_r\nu}-d_\nu=h_{ij}-h_{ji}$, so the unequal crossing has degree $2h_{ij}+d_\nu-d_{s_r\nu}=h_{ij}+h_{ji}$; equal crossings have degree $-2$ and dots degree $2$. Both faithful images are therefore the identical graded subalgebra generated by these operators, yielding $R(\beta;Q)\cong S_\Gamma(\beta)\cong\operatorname{Ext}_G^\bullet(L,L)$ for $L=\bigoplus_\nu L_\nu$. This is also the direct comparison of the identical specialized presentations: all adjacent unequal dot slides and the native mixed and braid signs are present in [F3]. The equal geometric crossing is minus its standard complex Borel–Moore class, so no sign change is implicit. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 (The actual normalized complex.) By [F4], the same $L=\bigoplus_\nu R\pi_{\nu!}k[d_\nu]$ of step 1.1 is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple actual equivariant perverse objects. The normalization $[d_\nu]$ has already been included in $L_\nu$; no further shift of $L$ is made. This uses the proved semisimplicity clause in the complete loopless multiedge scope, with no semismallness or finite-ADE restriction. [F4, step 1.1]

2.2 (Graded Yoneda.) Use the shifted opposite-composition product of [F3] and define $Y_T=\operatorname{Ext}_G^\bullet(L,T)$ as a graded left $R$-module: for homogeneous $a:L\to L[n]$ and $y:L\to T[m]$, set $a\cdot y=y[n]\circ a$, so $(a*b)\cdot y=a\cdot(b\cdot y)$. On $T=L$ this is the regular left module. A homogeneous map $f:T\to U[t]$ acts by postcomposition $y\mapsto f[m]\circ y$ of degree $t$. For $T=U=L$ every graded $R$-linear map $R\to R$ is right multiplication by its value at $1$, hence is induced uniquely by the corresponding $f$; extend this identification to finite sums and shifts and then to idempotent summands. Since the actual category is idempotent complete and all finite graded projectives are summands of finite sums of shifts of $R$, this gives a fully faithful equivalence from the additive category generated by shifts of $L$ onto finite graded projectives, with $\operatorname{End}_R^\bullet(Y_T)\cong\operatorname{Ext}_G^\bullet(T,T)$ using ordinary categorical composition on both endomorphism rings. [F3, F6, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 (Indecomposables and scalar degree zero.) Each simple perverse summand $T$ in step 2.1 belongs to that additive category up to shift. By [F4] and step 2.2 its projective $Y_T$ has no negative-degree endomorphisms and its degree-zero endomorphism ring is a division algebra, hence it is graded indecomposable. These exhaust the indecomposable projective shift orbits: every projective is a summand of a finite sum of the $Y_T$ and their shifts, and [F5] gives the finite graded Krull–Schmidt decomposition. Distinct simple perverse objects yield distinct orbits, since full faithfulness would otherwise give $T\cong U[t]$, and perverse concentration forces $t=0$. Finally the simple head $S$ of $Y_T$ has $\operatorname{End}_R^0(S)=k$ by [F5]. Every degree-zero endomorphism preserves the unique maximal graded submodule, so descent to the head is a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $\operatorname{End}_R^0(Y_T)\to k$; its kernel is zero because its source is a division algebra, and its image contains all scalars, so $\operatorname{End}_R^0(Y_T)=k$. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]


4.1 (Self-dual normalization, norm one and signed globalization.) By [F1] every projective shift orbit has a unique $^\#$ self-dual representative $P_b$; put $x_b=\gamma^{-1}[P_b]$, which is integral and bar fixed. The exact Hom/tensor comparison for a self-dual $P$ gives $B_L(x_b,x_b)=h(P_b,P_b)$, a nonnegative integer power series in $q$ congruent to $1$ modulo $q$, since the geometric nonnegative-End property is unchanged by grading shifts. Dividing by $C_\beta$ (which is $1$ modulo $q$) gives a value $B_K(x_b,x_b)$ congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ with integer coefficients, so the general half norm criterion places $x_b$ in the $q^0$ crystal lattice; being bar fixed, it also lies in the actual bar chart, and the integral balanced globalization writes $x_b$ as a finite $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of lower global vectors. Their residue Gram matrix is the identity, so norm residue $1$ forces the sum of coefficient squares to be $1$: $x_b$ is exactly plus or minus one lower global vector. Distinct projective shift orbits are independent and have the same finite weight cardinality as the global basis by the integral $K_0$ isomorphism, so they exhaust this signed set. [step 3.1, F1, F2, algebra]

5.1 (Positivity and the based quotient.) The positive divided-string leading-term supplier [F2] removes every minus sign using its integral LEFT-string ideal equality, its coefficient-$1$ projective adjunction expansion, and the general adapted LEFT global recursion (carried with its inherited Axiom of Choice, [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); batch 8's finite-ADE canonical-comparison item is not used. Consequently the sign in step 4.1 is $+1$, giving $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for every lower global vector $G(b)$ and establishing the bijection of the statement. The compatibility with the based quotient is the general zero/survival projection theorem of the QG-5 machinery. [step 4.1, F2, algebra] ∎

items.statement:

(a) On equal-colour pairs $

(b) On $

$$	au_2	au_1	au_2e(

so the naive simply-laced braid relation fails; the correction is the divided difference $ rac{Q_{ij}(x_1,x_2)-Q_{ij}(x_3,x_2)}{x_3-x_1}$ of relation (7), the second difference of the quadratic parameter in its first variable.
(c) Degree check: the three factors of $	au_2	au_1	au_2e(
u)$ act successively on the pairs $(j,i)$, then $(i,i)$, then $(i,j)$ of the two-step permuted sequence, so their degrees are $-b_{ji}=2$, $-b_{ii}=-2$, $-b_{ij}=2$, totalling $2$; the right-hand side $x_1+x_3-2x_2$ also has degree $2$. Thus the correction is homogeneous, of degree $-2b_{ij}-2d_i=2$, while for a simple edge the corresponding correction is a degree-$0$ constant; the doubled Cartan entry raises the degree of the quadratic parameter $Q_{ij}$, hence that of the correction, by $2$.

items.title: The two-vertex KLR polynomial representation
items.statement:
Take $I=\{i,j\}$, $n=2$ and the KLR datum with $Q_{ij}=1$ if $a_{ij}=0$ and $Q_{ij}(u,v)=u+v$ if $a_{ij}=-1$ (simply-laced edge), $Q_{ji}$ determined by (Q2). Then $I^{\alpha_i+\alpha_j}=\{ij,ji\}$ and the PBW basis of $R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)$ is $\{x_1^ax_2^b	au_1^\varepsilon e(
u)\ :\ \varepsilon\in\{0,1\},\ 
u\in\{ij,ji\}\}$, so $R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)$ is free of rank $4$ over $k[x_1,x_2]$ (and rank $2$ over the direct-sum polynomial algebra with its two idempotents) with graded dimension $ rac{2(1+q^{-b_{ij}})}{(1-q^{2d_i})(1-q^{2d_j})}$.

items.title: The KLR algebras in root degrees $\alpha_i$ and $2\alpha_i$
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix $i\in I$.
(a) In weight $\alpha_i$ there is one sequence, and $R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]e(i)$: the only relations are that $x_1$ is central, so $\{x_1^a\}_{a\ge0}$ is a $k$-basis, $\deg x_1=2d_i$, and $\mathrm{gdim}\,R(\alpha_i)=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$. The algebra is commutative; up to shift its unique simple module is $k$ with $x_1$ acting by $0$, $R(\alpha_i)$ is the projective cover of that simple, and $[R(\alpha_i)]=[P_{i,1}]$ with $([P_{i,1}],[P_{i,1}])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$.
(b) In weight $2\alpha_i$ one has $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$, the nil Hecke algebra of rank $2$, with $k$-basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,\ x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1\}_{a,b\ge0}$, free of rank $2$ over $k[x_1,x_2]$, and relations (in the normalization of relation (6) of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]])
$$\tau_1^2=0,\qquad \tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1+e(ii),\qquad \tau_1x_2=x_1\tau_1-e(ii).$$
Its graded dimension is $\dfrac{1+q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}$, and the element $e_{i,2}=x_1\tau_1$ is a nonzero idempotent of degree $0$ with $P_{i,2}=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ an indecomposable projective of class $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$ in $K_0(R)$.
items.strategy: (a) The PBW basis of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] for the single sequence $(i)$ is $\{x_1^a\}$; centrality is relation (2) and there is no crossing for $n=1$. The simple module and cover statements are the standard theory of $k[x_1]$ together with [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]; the pairing value is the normalization of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]]. (b) For two strands of one colour the PBW basis is $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1\}$ and the relations are relations (4) and (6) specialized to $Q_{ii}=0$ and $\nu_1=\nu_2$; the grading gives the two geometric series $\frac1{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}+\frac{q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}$. For the idempotent: $\tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1+e(ii)$ gives $e_{i,2}^2=x_1\tau_1x_1\tau_1=x_1(x_2\tau_1+e(ii))\tau_1=x_1x_2\tau_1^2+x_1\tau_1=x_1\tau_1$ using $\tau_1^2=0$, so $e_{i,2}^2=e_{i,2}$; nonvanishing is read off the PBW basis. Indecomposability and the class identification are the $n=2$ cases of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. No AC is used.

items.title: Degenerate parameters $Q_{ij}$ destroy the faithful polynomial-representation route
items.statement:
**Statement refuted:** the faithful polynomial-representation route to the PBW basis and the Grothendieck-ring comparison of [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]] needs only the hermitian symmetry (Q2) and the degree condition (Q3); the nonvanishing conditions (Q1) and (Q4) can be dropped.
**Counterexample (two vertices).** Let $I=\{i,j\}$, $a_{ij}=-1$, and take the degenerate parameters $Q_{ij}=Q_{ji}=0$, which satisfy (Q2) and (Q3) but not (Q1). Then:
(a) The algebra R(alpha_i+alpha_j) has the PBW basis displayed below even for Q=0. Indeed dots slide past crossings and crossing squares vanish, so those monomials span; independence follows from the algebra of the two-idempotent polynomial skew quiver with both length-two crossing paths zero. There is no factorization with both factors nonzero, since k[u,v] is a domain.
(b) Taking P_ij=0 and P_ji=1 gives a well-defined polynomial action: tau_1 kills the ij summand and swaps the ji summand into ij. Hence it kills the NONZERO element tau_1 e(ij), so is not faithful; it need not kill both crossings. For any polynomial-factor action with Q=0 at least one crossing factor vanishes, giving the same nonfaithfulness conclusion in that corner.
(c) Dropping the hermitian symmetry (Q2) while keeping (Q1), (Q3) and (Q4) also destroys the basis route: over a field of characteristic different from2, for $a_{ij}=-1$ and the non-hermitian pair $Q_{ij}(u,v)=u+2v$, $Q_{ji}(u,v)=u+v$ (both homogeneous of degree $2$ with nonzero extremal coefficients, but $Q_{ji}(v,u)=v+u\ne u+2v$), associativity together with relation (4) on the two corners $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$ and the dot slides of (6) for the pair of distinct residues gives the identity $\bigl(Q_{ji}(x_1,x_2)-Q_{ij}(x_2,x_1)\bigr)\tau_1e(ij)=-x_1\tau_1e(ij)=0$, hence $\tau_1x_2e(ij)=0$; the spanning monomial $\tau_1x_2e(ij)$ of Rouquier's family $\{x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1^\varepsilon e(\nu)\}$ therefore vanishes, so that family is not linearly independent and the graded PBW statement fails. Equivalently, Rouquier's Theorem 3.7 shows that PBW is equivalent to $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$, the identity violated here. (On $(i,j,i)$ the braid relation reads $\bigl(\tau_2\tau_1\tau_2-\tau_1\tau_2\tau_1\bigr)e(i,j,i)=-e(i,j,i)$: both sides have degree $0$, so the failure is a linear dependence, not a degree mismatch.)
Thus both the nonvanishing hypotheses and the hermitian symmetry are load-bearing for the basis and rank arguments; the example does not claim that the KLR algebra with $Q_{ij}=0$ fails to be free (PBW independence has its own source proof), only that the faithful polynomial-representation route used in this library collapses.
items.strategy:
(a) Define the degenerate algebra as the direct sum of the two polynomial identity corners and the two polynomial crossing arrows, with dot permutation on crossing multiplication and products of two arrows zero. Associativity follows because the permutation is an algebra automorphism and every triple with at least two arrows is zero. This realizes exactly the presentation and proves PBW independence without applying the nondegenerate PBW theorem outside its hypotheses. (b) A product of polynomial factors is zero only if at least one is zero. With P_ij=0,P_ji=1 the polynomial action kills tau_1e(ij) but not tau_1e(ji); both algebra elements are nonzero by (a). Hence this action is not faithful. The same argument applies to every factorized action since one corner is killed. (c) Over characteristic different from2, for the non-hermitian pair $Q_{ij}=u+2v$, $Q_{ji}=u+v$ the two corners are individually consistent ($	au_1^2=x_1+2x_2$ on $(i,j)$ and $	au_1^2=x_1+x_2$ on $(j,i)$, both of degree $2$); the failure appears only when the two corners are used at once: relation (4) on $(i,j)$ and on $(j,i)$, together with the dot slides of (6) for distinct residues, gives $ igl(Q_{ji}(x_1,x_2)-Q_{ij}(x_2,x_1) igr)	au_1e(ij)=0$, i.e. $-x_1	au_1e(ij)=0$ and $	au_1x_2e(ij)=0$, so the spanning family $S$ is not linearly independent and PBW fails; this is exactly the contrapositive of Rouquier's Theorem 3.7, whose proof derives this identity and concludes $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$. The braid relation on $(i,j,i)$ gives $	au_2	au_1	au_2e(
u)-	au_1	au_2	au_1e(
u)=-e(
u)$, homogeneous of degree $0$, so it is not the source of the failure. No AC is used.

items.title: The nil-Hecke divided-power projective in rank two
items.statement:
Work in $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$ of [[ex-klr-algebras-in-root-degrees-alpha-i-and-two-alpha-i]]: generators $x_1,x_2$ of degree $2d_i$ and $\tau=\tau_1$ of degree $-2d_i$, the basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau\}$, the relations $\tau^2=0$, $\tau x_1=x_2\tau+e$, $\tau x_2=x_1\tau-e$, and center $k[x_1,x_2]^{S_2}$. Then:
(a) $e_{i,2}:=x_1\tau$ is a nonzero idempotent of degree $0$ and $\psi(e_{i,2})=\tau x_1$ is the reflected idempotent; the module $P_{i,2}:=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ is the polynomial representation of $NH_2$, an indecomposable graded projective with one-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism ring, and it is the projective cover of the unique simple $R(2\alpha_i)$-module up to shift.
(b) $R(2\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus[2]_{q_i}!}$ with $[2]_{q_i}!=(q_i+q_i^{-1})$, so $P_{i,2}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift.
(c) In $K_0(R)$, $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$ for the divided power $\theta_i^{(2)}=F_i^2/[2]_{q_i}$, and its self-pairing is $([P_{i,2}],[P_{i,2}])=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}(1-q_i^4)^{-1}$, the value of the Lusztig-normalized form at $\theta_i^{(2)}$.
items.strategy: (a) Compute $e_{i,2}^2=x_1\tau x_1\tau=x_1(x_2\tau+e)\tau=x_1x_2\tau^2+x_1\tau=x_1\tau$ using $\tau^2=0$; nonvanishing is read off the PBW basis. The reflected element satisfies $\psi(e_{i,2})^2=(\tau x_1)(\tau x_1)=(x_2\tau+e)\tau x_1=x_2\tau^2x_1+\tau x_1=\tau x_1=\psi(e_{i,2})$ using $\tau^2=0$, so both are idempotents of degree $0$ (the $x$-monomial has degree $2d_i$ and $\tau$ has degree $-2d_i$). The left ideal $NH_2\tau_1x_1$ is the polynomial representation by the map $a\tau_1x_1\mapsto a\cdot1$: the operator $\tau_1x_1$ projects to symmetric polynomials and sends1 to1, so the left ideal acts on1 through arbitrary polynomial multiplications; its inverse sends $f$ to multiplication by $f$ followed by $\tau_1x_1$. The two maps are inverse because $\tau_1x_1$ is the rank-one projection in $NH_2=\operatorname{End}_{k[x_1,x_2]^{S_2}}k[x_1,x_2]$; it is indecomposable projective, hence the projective cover of its (unique) simple head, and its homogeneous endomorphism algebra is the color-symmetric polynomial ring $k[x_1,x_2]^{S_2}$, whose degree-zero part is $k$; no claim about the degree-zero vector space of the shifted polynomial module is used. (b) The decomposition into $[2]_{q_i}!$ copies is the rank-two case of the source computation $NH_m\cong P_m^{\oplus[m]_{q_i}!}$; uniqueness of the indecomposable summand up to shift follows from the Krull-Schmidt property [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]] together with the single indecomposable class. (c) The class identification is the $n=2$ case of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] (see also [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]), and the self-pairing is the rank-one value $\prod_{a=1}^{2}(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$ of [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]]. No AC is used.

items.title: The cyclotomic KLR quotient at a dominant integral weight
items.strategy: The idempotents isolate the individual generators, so the displayed ideal also equals $R(\beta)a(x_1)R(\beta)$ when the latter expression is restricted to this block. In the standard choice each isolated generator is homogeneous; this proves the grading, without falsely assigning one degree to their sum. Over a degree-zero field a monic homogeneous polynomial of positive dot degree is the pure power. Lower monic coefficients therefore require forgetting the grading. The example $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$, so its two projective classes cannot be the one-dimensional middle weight of $V(2)$; the standard graded hypothesis is substantive. The rank-zero convention avoids an undefined first letter of the empty word. This definition uses no choice.

items.title: The minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category
items.statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots, a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and admissible weighted-homogeneous KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. Write $b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$ and fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear category of weighted oriented diagrams with objects weights, downward generators $G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$ for every $j$, and the single upward generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums and grading shifts; use idempotent completion when speaking of word projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes normalized projective restriction: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h$, it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by $-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$. The native crossing is $\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference $(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put $\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$. Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR relations of the cited Definition.

At input $i$-weight $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$, the first unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and second unit $1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$ prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix $H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\}$; for $h<0$ prescribe $G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}$. The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap transfer, and the identity columns/rows are the indicated dotted units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse equations; the dotted dual rows/columns are the finite triangular coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$, if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and $p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion/projection with product $1_{H_iG_i}$.

The normalized far-left bubble series $A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient1 and satisfy $A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$ coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise; its degree is $2d_i m$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree $2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies $\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$ multiplies $A$ by $q_{ij}^{\rm rev}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$ is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant coefficient1.

Impose the rank-one cross-and-cap equations: the two oppositely oriented single-crossing curls are the signed sums of a dotted uncrossed cap and an opposite bubble over indices $a+b=-1$; the two opposite-crossing cancellations are the straight pair plus the dotted cup--bubble--cap sums over $a+b+c=-1$, with the corresponding opposite-orientation signs. A negative dot count on an open strand is zero. These are the four source $\kappa$ equations, converted globally by $\kappa=-\tau$. For $j\ne i$, the two sideways crossings, defined as the two adjunction mates of the downward crossing, cancel in the two orders with the nonzero scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; scale the reverse mate by the corresponding inverse to obtain the mixed isomorphism $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$, commuting with the $j$ dot. These are relations of this proof-tool category. Their consistency and homogeneous realization are established by the polynomial flag model, rather than assumed for the actual cyclotomic induction/restriction action.
items.strategy: This is a presentation by generators and homogeneous equations. Check weighted homogeneity of every downward relation using $\deg x_j=2d_j$ and $\deg\tau_{jk}=-b_{jk}$; the global source substitution changes every crossing sign and preserves $Q$. Check the two cup/cap degrees at adjacent weights, giving degree-zero triangle composites and the symmetric identity shifts in both branches of the rank-one matrix. Interpret all fake bubbles and reciprocal slide coefficients by the finite recursion from constant coefficient1, so no analytic series or inverse dot occurs. The local polynomial flag model realizes these equations with normalized $H_i$, shifted spectator flags, explicit dual monic power bases and the actual rank-one inverse blocks, proving consistency. This last well-definedness result is listed in justified_by, while its proof depends on the present definition; it is not a logical dependency of the definition.

items.title: Mixed relations, local nilpotence and weights give the integrable quantum action
items.statement: Let $V=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}V_\mu$ be a label-weight-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with its toral operators, and operators $E_i,F_i$ of weights $\alpha_i,-\alpha_i$. Assume the toral conjugation and mixed relations, and local nilpotence of each $E_i,F_i$; vectors have finite label support. Then these operators uniquely define an integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module for EVERY real symmetrizable datum. Every vector has a finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit and the admissible Kashiwara $i$-string decomposition applies. Finite weight spaces do not imply finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ orbits; no such conclusion is asserted.
items.strategy: Apply the exact general supplier [[lem-integrable-rank-one-actions-force-the-quantum-serre-relations]], or reproduce its argument as follows. Rank-one PBW writes the orbit of $v$ as $F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cv$; only finitely many $b$ and then finitely many $a$ survive, so $W=U_iv$ is finite. For $j\ne i$, $W'=U_i(F_jW)$ is also finite. In $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ the Hopf adjoint actions are $\operatorname{ad}E_i(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i$ and $\operatorname{ad}F_i(T)=F_iT-K_iTK_i^{-1}F_i$. The map $T=F_j$ is highest of rank-one weight $m=-a_{ij}\ge0$. The finite quantum-sl2 string theorem gives $(\operatorname{ad}F_i)^{m+1}T=0$. Expanding yields $\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^r q_i^{r(m-n+1)}{n\brack r}_i F_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$; at $n=m+1$ every Laurent exponent is zero, precisely the negative Serre relation. Exchange $E,F,K$ with $F,E,K^{-1}$ for positive Serre. Thus every defining relation holds, with no A2 calculation, rank-two local-finiteness assumption or presupposed quantum module. Uniqueness follows from generators; local nilpotence gives integrability.

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR induction and restriction functors
items.statement: Use the standard graded quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. Put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and $e=e(\beta,i)$. Right append defines a graded CORNER homomorphism $\iota_i:A\to eBe$, sending $1_A$ to $e$, $e(\nu)$ to $e(\nu i)$, and the old dots/crossings to their positions in the first $|\beta|$ strands. It is not asserted injective and $e$ may be zero. Define $F_i^{\rm basic}(M)=Be\otimes_A M$ and $E_i^{\rm basic}(N)=eN$. These additive functors preserve shifts and satisfy $F_i^{\rm basic}\dashv E_i^{\rm basic}$ by degree-zero tensor-Hom evaluation. $F_i$ increases ROOT degree by $\alpha_i$ and decreases module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by $\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at a fixed root degree. The same underlying definitions apply ungraded to monic deformations. Exactness/projective preservation and the shifted second adjunction are theorems below.
items.strategy: Each generic generator relation is preserved in the corner, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator maps into the longer ideal. This gives a homomorphism with unit image $e$, not a global-unit inclusion. For example $\lambda_i=1$, $\beta=\alpha_i$ has $A=k$, $B=0$, so the corner homomorphism and induction are zero. Evaluation at $e$ identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$, proving the ordinary adjunction with its actual grading. Finite balanced tensors give additivity/shift compatibility. No unshifted second adjunction is assumed; its explicit shift is supplied by the coherent-adjunction lemma.

items.title: Cyclotomic dot annihilators, finite-dimensional blocks, and finite root strings
items.statement: Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)–(Q4) for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree $\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the resulting ordinary quotient. Every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic annihilator in each fixed block, every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over $k$, and, for fixed $\beta,i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.
items.strategy:
Use the exact native presentation, and abbreviate its globally opposite source crossing by $\kappa_a=-\tau_a$ for every color pair; the dots, idempotents and $Q$ do not change. For equal adjacent colors put $x=x_a,y=x_{a+1}$ and $\partial f=(s_af-f)/(x-y)$. If $fe(\nu)$ annihilates a module, the source nil-Hecke identities give $(x-y)\kappa_a f\kappa_a e(\nu)=(s_af-f)\kappa_a e(\nu)=(\kappa_af-\partial f-f\kappa_a)e(\nu)$. The terms containing $f$ vanish, so $\partial f$ vanishes; then $s_af=f+(x-y)\partial f$ also vanishes. This proves annihilator closure under the divided difference and exchange without division by an integer. A common monic annihilator of the first dot is $g_1=\prod_j a_j$, with the zero corners understood in the same way.

Suppose a common monic $g$ of degree $d$ annihilates $x_a$. Equal-color exchange gives $g(y)=0$. At an unequal pair $j,l$, $\kappa_ag(x)\kappa_a=g(y)Q_{jl}(x,y)=0$. Set $C=k[x]/g$, finite free of rank $d$. Multiplication by $Q_{jl}(x,y)$ on $C[y]$ has matrix $M(y)$ with leading coefficient $c\,\mathrm{Id}$ and degree $-a_{lj}$ in $y$, where $c=t_{j,l;0,-a_{lj}}\ne0$. Its determinant $r(y)$ has leading coefficient $c^d$. Applying $\operatorname{adj}(M)M=r\,\mathrm{Id}$ to the vector $1$ gives $Q_{jl}(x,y)R(x,y)\equiv r(y)\pmod {g(x)}$. Thus $g(y)r(y)$ annihilates the corner; divide its leading scalar to obtain a monic polynomial. If $d=0$ that corner is zero; if $a_{lj}=0$, $r=c^d$ is a unit. Take the product over the finite words/pairs and induct over positions. PBW then reduces each dot exponent below its monic bound, leaving finitely many permutations, words and exponent tuples, so the block is finite dimensional. This is a direct ordinary-algebra argument for arbitrary monic polynomials, including $u(u-1)$, rather than a flat-specialization claim.

For standard powers one can strengthen the bounds to nilpotence. If $x^N=0$ and the neighboring colors differ, write $Q_{jl}(x,y)=c y^q+xH(x,y)$, $q=-a_{lj}$, using homogeneity and Q4. The quadratic relation gives $y^NQ=0$, hence $y^{N+q}=-c^{-1}xy^NH$ on the corner. Raising this commuting-polynomial equality to the $N$th power gives $y^{N(N+q)}=0$. Equal-color exchange preserves the exponent $N$. Starting with a common first-strand power proves nilpotence of every dot.

For finite root strings in either branch fix a prefix length $\ell$ and a common monic annihilator $g$ of degree $d$ for $x_{\ell+1}$ in the finite length-$\ell+1$ quotient. Its image annihilates that dot in every longer quotient, since right concatenation preserves the first-strand ideal. In an all-$i$ tail of length $d+1$ starting at position $\ell+1$, repeated annihilator closure gives $\partial_{\ell+d}\cdots\partial_{\ell+1}g(x_{\ell+1})=(-1)^d$, so the tail is zero. Equivalently, in native nil-Hecke rank $s>d$, multiply $g(x_1)$ by $x_1^{s-1-d}x_2^{s-2}\cdots x_{s-1}$. Its top term is the Artin staircase and its lower terms have smaller total degree; the native $\partial_{w_0}$ sends it to $1$. Thus $\partial_{w_0}$ and the full staircase idempotent belong to the ideal generated by $g$. The finite matrix units from the perfect Artin pairing put $1$ in that ideal. Both computations use unit diagonal elimination, never $s!^{-1}$.

Finally induct on the number $b$ of non-$i$ entries. Let $k=L_{b-1}$ be the previous bound and $\ell=b-1+k$. Choose an all-$i$ tail bound $m$ at that prefix length and set $L_b=k+m-1$. A word of length $b+L_b=\ell+m$ with at least $L_b$ copies of $i$ either has at least $k$ in its first $\ell$ positions, whose prefix is already zero, or has at most $k-1$ there and therefore all last $m$ positions are $i$. That tail is zero. A longer word with at most $b$ other colors has a zero initial segment of length $b+L_b$. For fixed $\beta$, $b=\sum_{j\ne i}\beta_j$, so $\beta_i+m\ge L_b$ kills every word in $\beta+m\alpha_i$. The prefix never has to end in color $i$. All constructions involve finite products, determinants, polynomial reductions and integer choices.

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction: mixed relations and the opposite-end exact sequence
items.strategy: Use the full labelled PBW shuffle decomposition, with word-idempotent shifts rather than a common graded-free shift. Same-end multiplication $x\otimes y\mapsto x\kappa_n y$, where $\kappa=-\tau_{native}$ on ALL color pairs, identifies the nonidentity cosets and gives $E_iF_j=q^{-b_{ij}}F_jE_i$ for unequal colors and $E_iF_i=q_i^{-2}F_iE_i\oplus\operatorname{Id}[t]$. For the opposite ends the overlap multiplication has image all transfer cosets except $\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1$; taking that coefficient gives the cokernel $q^{-(\alpha_i,\beta)}M[t]$. Its middle functor is $E_i\bar F_i$, not $E_iF_i$. The PBW sequence is split on the right before tensoring, so no flatness of a quotient is assumed. Source/native minus signs merely multiply each chosen transfer basis by its explicit unit; the full presentation dictionary preserves Q and grading.

items.title: The minimal-parabolic polynomial flag model realizes the graded diagram relations
items.statement:
Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR parameters of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], PBW convention of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the following polynomial flag construction realizes all the defining graded diagram relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap, bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic quotient identification.

Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets $Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$), put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$, $r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$, $t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$, $q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of degree $\lambda_i$. Initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous degrees, so all formulas are graded; the standard specialization is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r.$$
Let $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$: equivalently it is $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$. It is finite free over $C$, of rank $\binom Nr$, and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is $B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over $L_{m+i}$, with target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to $Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

Every downward generator carries the ordered shift
$$s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell.$$
Thus $G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for $j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}.$$
These are distinct conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where $t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree $d_i(1+h_m)$.

All four maps are explicit dual-basis maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$. The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap/cup use $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

Source crossings are $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the successive underlying rings are $D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps $\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$. Their normalized opposite-sideways composites have scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; in the NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is $t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and ratio unchanged. Basic $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$; normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series $\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite coefficient bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees $d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities. Such a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.
items.strategy:
Work entirely with the displayed formal-model rings and operators; neither a generic cyclotomic Frobenius theorem nor an actual quotient/faithfulness result is an input. The following is the full local construction route.

(1) Monic splitting algebras and nil-Hecke matrix units. Over the universal coefficient ring S=k[c_1,...,c_N], repeatedly adjoin a root of the monic framing polynomial and divide it out. At the s-th step the residual polynomial is monic of the next smaller degree, so ordinary monic division gives the Artin basis X_1^{a_1}...X_N^{a_N}, 0<=a_j<=N-j. For a monic extension D[z]/f of degree q the top-coefficient pairing has Gram entries zero for a+b<q-1 and one for a+b=q-1; reversing one basis makes it triangular with diagonal1. Hence its pairing is perfect over every coefficient ring, with no factorial division. Composing these forms gives the normalized Artin divided-difference form (-1)^{ell(w_N)}kappa_{w_N}. Its staircase value is1 and every other Artin basis monomial has lower degree. If u_a,v_a are dual Artin bases, f -> u_a delta(v_b f) are matrix units in NH_r; PBW leading-permutation independence makes the polynomial representation injective, so NH_r=End_{Sym_r}(Pol_r). This proves the required graded nil-Hecke matrix algebra directly.

Block monic splitting makes Pol_N free of rank r!(N-r)! over T_r=Sym_r tensor Sym_{N-r}. The parabolic divided-difference form T_r->S composes with the perfect block Artin form to the perfect Pol_N/S form. Tensoring its pairing map with the nonzero free T_r-module Pol_N therefore gives an isomorphism; faithful-flat descent proves the T_r pairing perfect. T_r is finite graded projective over S by the explicit block-staircase retraction; lift a homogeneous basis modulo S_+, split the resulting finite free surjection, and use graded Nakayama on its kernel to prove T_r graded free. Its rank is N!/[r!(N-r)!]. This proves the claimed L_m rank after arbitrary monic basechange. Matrix trace composed with the parabolic form gives the model's cyclic perfect form; this is a proved polynomial-model pairing, not the theorem about the generic KLR algebra.

To identify the monic quotient without an external Grassmannian theorem, represent NH_r as the full matrix algebra on its Artin module. The entries of multiplication by a monic p(X_1) generate exactly the coefficients of the remainder of p(u) modulo c_r(u): the first matrix column contains them, while every other entry is their polynomial combination. Matrix units show its two-sided matrix ideal is the ideal of those entries. Monic division makes those coefficients a unit triangular change from the consecutive complete-symmetric/factorization relations. Thus NH_r/(p(X_1)) is the matrix algebra over the stated monic factor ring. This also gives zero when r>N.

(2) Actual maps and their four triangles. B_m is the two monic root extensions described in the Statement. For f monic, the polynomial K_f(X,Y) is well defined before passing to f(X)=f(Y)=0. It satisfies (X-Y)K_f=0 and tau_X K_f=1. Thus tau_X(X^a K_f)=Y^a for every a, proving that K_f is precisely the dual-power-basis Casimir, not an unspecified inverse Gram matrix. The two Casimirs for b_{N-r} and c_{r+1} give the four displayed cups/caps. Their contractions are the two equalities sum v_a tau(z^a b)=b and sum tau(bv_a)z^a=b; substituting them in the tensor composites proves both triangles for each adjunction. The first maps have degree0 after the B{-2d_i r} shift. The second cap has degree -2d_i(N-r-1)+2d_i r=-2d_i(h-1); its unit has the opposite degree. Restoring normalized H at its input weight gives exactly the four formal degrees in the Statement. This proves the gradings as well as the underlying adjunctions.

(3) Rank-one rho and its finite block inverses. Use the PBW two-coset splitting for one extra i strand: the transfer term is a kappa_r b, and its polynomial complement is the new-dot algebra. The rank-one intertwiner is g=(u-X)-(u-X)^2 kappa. Its quadratic and dot-commutation identities follow by expanding kappa X_{r+1}-X_r kappa=1 and kappa^2=0. Multiply these intertwiners along the extra strand, and multiply the other transfer by p(X_1). Projecting to the PBW polynomial complement gives, with S_r(u)=product_{a<=r}(u-X_a)^2, a coefficient map A satisfying A(u^k S_r)=(-1)^r u^k p(u). The same mixed relation gives phi_{k+1}=u phi_k+E(psi_k), psi_{k+1}=psi_k X_r. Therefore A(u^k)=(-1)^r quo_{S_r}(u^k p): subtracting its product by S_r leaves degree below2r, and uniqueness of monic division proves the assertion. This is the explicit rank-one PBW calculation; it uses no cyclotomic commutator theorem as a supplier.

If h=N-2r>=0, these quotient polynomials have distinct leading degrees h+k and unit leading coefficient (-1)^r. They give an injective A and a unique polynomial remainder of degree<h. The actual rho is consequently (transfer, dot^k unit) from FE{-2d_i} plus the h identity columns to EF; its inverse takes that remainder, subtracts its section, and inverts the transfer on the kernel. If h=-q<=0, A is surjective and its kernel is the span of1,u,...,u^{q-1}. Its connecting-map images have dot/cap matrix with zero entries below the anti-diagonal and unit (-1)^r on the anti-diagonal, because the displayed recurrence has phi_0=...=phi_{q-1}=0 and phi_q=(-1)^r. Reversing rows and solving successively gives the actual negative rho inverse. These are finite polynomial block inverses. On regular Artin generators the same constructions give the H_r(N) model Mackey maps (a tensor b)->a kappa_r b and the dot/cap rows; the graded matrix-Morita identification gives their flag versions. The normalized formal H changes the positive identity shifts to d_i(1-h+2k); the negative dot/cap shifts change by the same input-weight rule. This verifies every rho map and inverse in the formal model.

(4) Same-color crossing/cap identities and bubbles. Equal crossings act by kappa=(s-1)/(X-Y), so kappa^2=0, the braid relation and the two mixed dot equations follow by the rational-polynomial divided-difference expansion. Since K_f is symmetric, its divided-difference correction is0; (X-Y)K_f=0 gives the dot-mate equations. Contracting a crossing against either Casimir and using the rho block inverse just computed produces the cross-and-cap/curl equations: equivalently expand (f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y) in the power bases and take the top-coefficient rows. This is a finite polynomial computation, with the coefficient of each basis vector supplied by the same monic-division remainder; its first two curl forms are the signed sum x^a B_b over a+b=-1, and the two double-curl forms are the identity term plus the sums over a+b+c=-1. Negative dots on an open strand give0; fake bubbles are the corresponding inverse-series coefficients. Thus these equations are verified by the actual Casimir/rho maps rather than imposed on an unknown actual quotient.

At vertexm the resulting oriented bubble Laurent series is Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2, of leading degree h=N-2r. The opposite series is its normalized reciprocal; their product is1, coefficient by coefficient. This rational expression is forced by composing the two flag coefficient pairings: each existing i root contributes two factors, one from each side of the cap. Appending an i root z changes Phi to Phi/(u-z)^2, and appending a spectator j root y changes Phi to Phi Q_ij(u,y)/t_ij. Expanding these identities at infinity gives every finite bubble-slide coefficient equation. All coefficients use only additions, multiplication and monic formal inversion; there is no inverse of2 or of a factorial. These are the bubble-slide relations required in the formal proof-category definition. At an initial monic vacuum, closing a_i(x)x^{ell-1}=0 gives h_ell+sum c_{lambda-j}h_{ell-j}=0, h_0=1,h_<0=0, so H(t)a_i^rev(t)=1; the opposite series is a_i^rev. This also fixes the standard and deformed vacuum dictionaries without assuming quotient faithfulness.

(5) Downward Q relations and exact word grading. Give every flag the shift s_j(m) in the Statement. For j<k the increasing word(j,k) has a quotient/switch of underlying degree0 to word(k,j), whose target-unit minus source-unit shift is -b_jk. The reverse operator has underlying degree -2b_jk and unit-shift difference +b_jk. Both therefore have actual degree -b_jk; same-color divided differences have degree -2d_j. Native operators are all their negatives, so their degrees and two-crossing composites are unchanged. The ordinary polynomial operators verify idempotents, dots, far commutativity and Q quadratics directly. Expanding a three-strand composition gives zero difference when outer colors differ, and the divided difference of Q when they agree, exactly the source braid numerator. Global kappa=-tau changes all cubic signs and gives the actual native numerator. Quotient relations descend: on an i,j pair D_1 has bq=0 and D_0 has b=0; Qb=t_ij bq makes multiplication byQ well defined, and the other crossing is the literal quotient. The same identities with other spectator flags are just the polynomial-representation identities on appended alphabets.

(6) Mixed cups/caps and their exact leading constants. In D[z]/p versus D[z]/(pq), the coefficient form obeys tau_{pq}(Q f)=t_ij tau_p(f) because Q=t_ij q and the leading coefficient of Q f is t_ij times that of f. For a full existing i string use the ordered residue form of the model H_r(p): t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)} Res(Delta_r(X) X_1^{r-1}...X_{r-1} Tr(z)/product p(X_a)). No1/r! occurs. Expand parabolic divided differences to verify this over the universal integral coefficient ring; in its rational generic-root fraction field, the sum over root orderings is the Vandermonde determinant, so its two Vandermonde factors cancel the internal root-difference denominator. Both sides are integral polynomial expressions, hence the identity specializes to every field. With p'=p q and U_r=product Q_ij(X_a,y), cancellation gives t_r^{p'}(U_r z)=(-1)^{r A_ij}t_ij^r t_r^p(z). Perfectness of the model forms makes U_r on the old quotient injective. Testing the relative cap against these forms then gives pi_r epsilon_r^{p'}(Q(X_{r+1},y) lift(z))=(-1)^{A_ij}t_ij epsilon_r^p(z) for every nil-Hecke coset element, not only dot polynomials. Normalize the second maps by the global weight sign (-1)^{h+1}; N and h have the same parity, and the new N changes by A_ij, so the displayed sign cancels and the constant is precisely t_ij. Dual-power-basis contraction gives the mixed-unit equation. Reversing colors gives t_ji, and their quotient is the stated double-mate ratio. Native minus signs occur twice in these composites, so the scalars persist. No dimension-one Hom inference is used.

Finally, basic E_iG_j and G_jE_i have unit-shift difference b_ij, giving the stated basic shifted isomorphism. For normalized H the two unit sums are s_j(m)-d_i(1+h_m+A_ij) and -d_i(1+h_m)+s_j(m-e_i); they are equal because s_j(m-e_i)=s_j(m)+b_ij and b_ij=-d_i A_ij. This verifies the formal unshifted mixed commutator and its grading. All the defining relations have now been realized on the explicit flag modules. Monic extensions, their Casimirs, finite rho inverses and coefficient identities survive arbitrary monic specialization as ungraded maps. This lemma proves only the formal MODEL relations; its subsequent faithfulness and cyclotomic word-corner transfer belong to separate suppliers, and no generic trace, K_0 or crystal result is used. The construction is choice-free.
