items.title: One-step simple restriction and induction, and the first-dot index
items.statement: Let k be any field and R(Q) the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum and any homogeneous Q satisfying the standing symmetry and nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up to internal shift. For a simple S of root weight beta and r=epsilon_i(S)>0, its ordinary one-step last-i restriction has a single simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same shift orbit, with epsilon_i=r-1; its maximum-epsilon composition part has coefficient a grading shift of [r]_i. The last-dot nilpotence index on that restriction is exactly r. The first-end statements hold with epsilon_i^L and the first dot. For every n>=1, Ind(S boxtimes L(i^n)) has a unique simple graded head f_i^n S, occurring once in its whole composition series, with epsilon_i=r+n (also when r=0); all other constituents have smaller epsilon_i. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial inverses. A simple S survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with exponents lambda_i exactly when epsilon_i^L(S)<=lambda_i for all i. Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle multiplicity.
items.strategy:
## Nil-Hecke branching computation

Let L_r be the nil-Hecke simple, modeled by the coinvariant algebra C_r=k[t_1,...,t_r]/(e_1,...,e_r) with polynomial multiplication and divided differences. Put z=t_r, and write E_a for elementary symmetric polynomials in t_1,...,t_(r-1). The equations e_a=E_a+z E_(a-1)=0 give E_a=(-z)^a for 1<=a<=r-1, and the final equation gives z^r=0. Consequently

    C_r = k[t_1,...,t_(r-1)] tensor_(k[E_1,...,E_(r-1)]) k[z]/(z^r),

where E_a acts on the second factor by (-z)^a. This is an equality of presented algebras, not a dimension heuristic. The polynomial representation of NH_(r-1) is a free module of rank (r-1)! over its symmetric center and identifies NH_(r-1) with the full matrix algebra over that center. After this specialization its image on C_r is Mat_((r-1)!)(k[z]/(z^r)), and C_r is its standard column module. Thus its graded socle and head are each one shifted L_(r-1), its simple composition coefficient is a shifted [r]_i, and multiplication by z has nilpotence index exactly r. The simple socle is the column over z^(r-1)k, the head the column modulo z. For r=1 this is the statement C_1=k and z=0. The same calculation with the first variable distinguished gives first-end branching. Matrix units and a monic Artin polynomial basis make the computation valid in all characteristics.

The induction NH_r tensor NH_n -> NH_(r+n) of L_r tensor L_n is L_(r+n), up to shift. Every positive full symmetric polynomial acts by zero, since its coproduct is a sum of products of block symmetric polynomials with at least one positive factor. Hence the induced module is a module over the full nil-Hecke central matrix quotient. PBW freeness computes its dimension as binomial(r+n,r)r!n!=(r+n)!, exactly the standard column dimension; it is therefore one simple column, not a factorial number of simples.

## Restriction has a simple socle

Let S have epsilon_i(S)=r>0. The maximum possible epsilon_i of a composition factor of e_i S is r-1 by the exact defining corners. Let U be any simple subobject of e_i S, and put t=epsilon_i(U). The final dot z commutes with R(beta-alpha_i) and acts nilpotently on e_i S: this holds on the whole S by positive dot degree and finite grading support. It preserves the socle and its ungraded isotypic components. On the isotypic component containing U, a suitable nonzero power image has a nonzero kernel copy of the same underlying simple type, killed by z. Absolute simplicity and the finite graded semisimple decomposition let one choose that copy homogeneously, with the appropriate shift. The induction–restriction adjunction therefore gives a nonzero map Ind(U,L_1)->S, hence a surjection. The graded shuffle formula bounds every induced tail by t+1, so r<=t+1. The preceding upper bound gives t=r-1.

Now apply the maximal (r-1)-tail corner p to e_i S, retaining R(beta-r alpha_i) tensor NH_(r-1). Original10 gives Delta_i^r S=N tensor L_r, with epsilon_i(N)=0. Hence

    p(e_i S)=N tensor Res_(NH_(r-1))L_r.

The right side has a single simple socle by the nil-Hecke computation and the absolute simplicity of N. Every simple subobject U of e_i S has t=r-1, so original10 makes pU a nonzero simple object. Exactness of p makes p(soc e_i S) semisimple and injects it into the one-simple socle of p(e_i S). Thus soc e_i S is itself a single simple object, once, with epsilon r-1. This also proves detection: any nonzero submodule of e_i S contains a simple graded submodule U, whose pU is nonzero.

## Simple head and global dot index

Finite graded psi-duality D is exact, takes simples to simples, fixes the corner idempotents and commutes with restriction; it needs no self-dual representative. Apply the socle proof to DS, whose epsilon equals r, and dualize. It follows that e_i S has a single simple head, once. The maximum-tail restriction of the head and socle have the same first factor N up to the corresponding duals and grading shifts: the nil-Hecke head/socle differ only by shift. Original10's unique-head recursion therefore identifies their shift orbits.

On p(e_i S), z^r=0 while z^(r-1)!=0 by the explicit nil-Hecke model. The image of z^r on all of e_i S is a graded submodule. Its p-corner is zero; the just-proved detection property forces that image to be zero. Nonvanishing of z^(r-1) in the p-corner implies its nonvanishing globally. Therefore the last-dot nilpotence index on e_i S is exactly r. Repeating the proof for the first-end maximal restriction gives first-dot nilpotence index exactly epsilon_i^L(S). Notice that this argument uses detection of all submodules; knowing the index only on the maximal corner would not suffice on its own.

## Nonreduced induction and partial inverses

Put M_n=Ind(S,L_n), n>=1. Its maximum tail is at most r+n by shuffle. At tail r+n the Mackey filtration can only retain all n added i-strands and precisely r original terminal i-strands: taking fewer added strands would require more than r from S, while taking fewer original strands would not fill the requested tail. Thus the maximum corner is

    Delta_i^(r+n)M_n = N tensor Ind_(NH_r tensor NH_n)^(NH_(r+n))(L_r tensor L_n)
                      = N tensor L_(r+n),

up to the fixed grading shift. This is one actual surviving filtration term and is simple.

Every simple quotient T of M_n has that maximum tail. Indeed adjunction gives a nonzero injection S tensor L_n -> Delta_i^n T. Restrict its first factor to S's maximal r-tail; the resulting nonzero corner implies epsilon_i(T)>=r+n. The shuffle bound gives equality. The finite semisimple head of M_n therefore has only constituents detected by its simple maximum corner; exactness implies that head is one simple constituent, once. Its maximum corner is the displayed simple module. The kernel of M_n->hd M_n has zero maximum corner, so every other composition factor has smaller epsilon and the head occurs once in the entire composition series.

For n=1 write f_i S=hd M_1 and e-tilde_i T=soc e_i T. Adjunction realizes S in e_i(f_i S), so the simple-socle result gives e-tilde_i f_i S=S, with shifts restored. Conversely if S=soc e_i T, adjunction gives T as a simple quotient of Ind(S,L_1), hence T=f_i S. These are actual partial inverses. The raising operator decreases epsilon by1; lowering increases it by1. Iterating partial inverses shows hd Ind(S,L_n)=f_i^n S: strip the maximum-tail head n times using the unique original10 recursion, or apply the same adjunction and uniqueness at each one-strand stage. All statements hold at the first end by the identical first-end Mackey and dot arguments.

## Exact cyclotomic criterion

Let J^Lambda be generated by x_1^lambda_i on every word beginning with i. It annihilates a simple S exactly when each first-i corner has first-dot index at most lambda_i. The preceding theorem proves that index is epsilon_i^L(S). Thus

    J^Lambda S=0 iff epsilon_i^L(S)<=lambda_i for every i.

If a generator is nonzero, simplicity makes J^Lambda S=S and the quotient projection vanishes. If every generator vanishes, projection is S. This proves the criterion over all fields and Q without citing the omitted proof of LV Proposition2.4. Since first strands are preserved by right restriction, raising preserves the cyclotomic subcategory. For right induction, its generic unique head either survives, in which case quotient induction has that same unique head, or dies, in which case the quotient induction is zero: any nonzero finite module has a simple quotient, and any such quotient of the original induction must be its unique head.

The maximal-epsilon composition factors of e_i S are precisely the same simple shift orbit as its head/socle: their maximal corner is a constituent of N tensor Res L_r, whose single simple type identifies them by the maximal-tail recursion. The nil-Hecke branching calculation gives their graded coefficient as a shift of [r]_i. This concerns the full composition part; the socle and head each have one copy. The proof uses no choice and no self-dual representative.

items.title: PBW and bubble normal form in the minimal-parabolic diagram category
items.statement: Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial flag models of [[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]], with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.
items.strategy:
Use $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for all colors. The formal category's relations are the exact model-verified local equations: downward KLR, both rank-one triangles, cyclic dots, rho/cross-and-cap equations and bubble inversion, mixed cap/cup equations, and the finite-coefficient bubble slides. For an $i$ root $x$, its normalized bubble series changes by $(1-xt)^{\pm2}$; for a spectator $j$ root $y$ it changes by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)^{\pm1}$, where $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$ has constant coefficient $1$. These are verified directly because the model series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, adjoining an $i$ root multiplies $c_r$ by $u-x$, and adjoining a spectator multiplies $p$ by $Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$. Every fixed inverse coefficient is a finite polynomial recursion. These slides are specified formal relations checked on the model; deriving a slide from the faithfulness being proved is not used.

To span, move dots to fixed component positions with cyclicity and KLR dot moves. An equal-color correction has one fewer crossing. Sort each $i$ cup/cap toward a boundary or the far-left closed-component position using the specified mate equations. A main term passes one of its finitely many crossing obstacles; a correction term removes an unsorted open-component extremum or such an obstacle. Rank-one cross-and-cap sums are finite: open dot counts are nonnegative and negative-degree bubbles vanish, bounding the indices at a fixed total degree. Adjacent opposed cup/cap pairs cancel by the triangles. Induct on the lexicographic pair of unsorted extrema and remaining crossing obstacles, and on crossing length for correction terms. Closed components have color $i$; cancel extra extrema, slide them left by the finite coefficient equations, and express the reverse family by bubble inversion. Coxeter deletion and KLR braid/quadratic straightening then reduce each open matching to the selected reduced diagram, with all braid defects shorter. This yields the stated finite span. At all-downward boundaries every open arc joins bottom to top, hence is a colored permutation; the reduced matching and its dots are exactly a PBW monomial. For general boundaries the two triangles give invertible Hom correspondences bending the upward $i$ endpoints to the other boundary, and the same straightening has unit leading matching coefficients.

For independence hold the physical source weight $\mu$ fixed and write $\mu_i=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Choose fixed nonnegative spectator background counts $m_j$ and let $A_{\rm spect}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$. For an increasing background $i$ count $r$, set $N=\mu_i+2r$ and $\lambda_i=N-A_{\rm spect}$. These equations keep the physical weight $N-2r=\mu_i$ fixed. Only $i$ dominance is needed, since the model has no spectator upward generator; one may take all $m_j=0$. Use the universal graded monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with independent $\deg z_a=2d_i a$. Put $p=a_i\prod Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$. The correct normalized series is $\mathcal B(t)=p^{\rm rev}/(c_r^{\rm rev})^2=a_i^{\rm rev}U(t)$, $U_0=1$. Its coefficient $\mathcal B_a=z_a+\sum_{1\le\ell<a}z_\ell U_{a-\ell}+U_a$ is unit triangular in the framing variables. The reciprocal family's coefficient is $-z_a$ plus lower framing indices. Thus the first $D$ bubble coefficients are independent whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$, even in characteristic two and at negative physical weight. No claim of a unit old-root coefficient is made: $\mathcal B_1=p_1+2e_1$ can lose its root term in characteristic two.

A nonzero finite PBW/bubble combination remains nonzero after that triangular substitution over the independent polynomial coefficient domain. The generic KLR polynomial representation has a distinct nonzero leading permutation for each selected crossing word; choose a polynomial test vector with nonzero output, clearing a finite denominator if needed. Let $D$ bound the bubble indices and let $B$ bound the actual internal degrees of that vector and its output; both are finite and are determined in the untruncated polynomial ring. Let $L$ bound the number of added $i$ flags in the tested words. Every monic flag relation and factor-ring coefficient relation after those flags has degree at least $2d_i(N-r-L+1)=2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)$; spectator appends can only increase $N$. All coefficient and root variables are nonnegatively graded and all dot degrees are positive. Choose $r\ge0$, $\lambda_i\ge D$, and $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)>B$, also making any finitely required background root count large enough. Such an integer exists while $\mu$ is fixed. The ideal generated by the homogeneous model relations cannot meet degrees at most $B$, so the nonzero PBW output survives in that flag model. This is exact degree separation, not a deformation-flatness inference. The model's ordered word shifts, $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$ with $i$ last, make every crossing homogeneous of degree $-b_{jk}$; the polynomial witness is checked before its overall word shift. The formal upward generator is $H_i=E_i^{\rm basic}\{-d_i(1+h_{\rm input})\}$, not unnormalized restriction, so its spectator commutators are truly degree zero. Hence the faithful underlying witness is also a witness in the specified graded model.

The downward spanning map is therefore injective. The finite unit-triangular bending change then gives independence for the full matching family. Specializing the far-left bubble variables acts only on that tensor factor in the downward normal form; no ordinary KLR relation appears from coefficient evaluation alone. Universal grading is used only to witness formal faithfulness; subsequent inhomogeneous monic field specialization is governed by the separately proved algebraic cap-off kernel.

items.title: Cyclotomic induction is projective on the right
items.strategy:
Write $S=R( eta+i)$, $A=R^\Lambda( eta)$, $e_R=e( eta,i)$ and $e_L=e(i, eta)$. PBW gives finite right $A[t]$-projectives $K_0=Se_R/Sa(x_1)R( eta)e_R$ and $K_1=Se_L/Sa(x_2)R_1( eta)e_L$. With source $\kappa=-	au_{native}$, define $P(u)=u a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ and $Q(v)=v g_n\cdots g_1$, where unequal $g=\kappa$ and equal $g=(y-x)-(y-x)^2\kappa$. Moving each dot/crossing gives block bilinearity; expanding the cyclotomic ideal by the left cosets shows $\operatorname{im}P=\ker(K_0	o R^\Lambda( eta+i)e_R)$. The local quadratic/braid calculation gives $QP=a_i(t)\prod_{
u_a
e i}Q_{i
u_a}(t,x_a)$, with a uniform unit leading coefficient; consequently $P$ is injective. This is an actual monic comparison, not a filtered-colon citation.
The target is killed by a central monic dot polynomial. For a projective $A[t]$-resolution $0	o P_1\xrightarrow{j}P_0	o M	o0$ and central monic $fM=0$, factor $f=jh$; injectivity gives $hj=f$. Each $P_r/fP_r$ is projective over $A$ by monic division, so the sequence for multiplication by $f$ splits over $A$. A splitting $pf=1$ yields $phj=1$, making $M$ projective. In the graded standard case keep the degree-zero part of the splitting. Apply this to $K_1,K_0$ and the target. The generator-fixing anti-involution gives the left counterpart; restriction of target projectives and induction now preserve projectives. Tensor exactness of the comparison follows because the target is right $A$-projective, and its functor sequence has target category $R( eta+i)$-modules. The same P/Q and monic splitting argument is valid ungraded for arbitrary monic deformation coefficients; degrees concern only the homogeneous branch.

items.title: The cyclotomic cap-off quotient has no extra downward relations
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be dominant, $\lambda_j=\langle h_j,\Lambda\rangle$, and let $\mathcal P_i$ be [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], with its homogeneous polynomial realization and PBW/bubble normal form. Fix monic $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}+\sum_{r<\lambda_j}c_{j,r}u^r$. For the standard graded cyclotomic quotient take $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$ as in [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. More generally first take universal graded coefficients of degree $2d_j(\lambda_j-r)$; arbitrary monic specializations over the field are interpreted as ungraded.

In the representable category $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)$, let $J$ be the ideal generated by $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and $a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$ for every $j$, closed under arbitrary vertical pre/postcomposition and horizontal whiskering by the allowed 1-morphisms. For downward words $\mu,\nu$ of the same weight $\beta$, include their ordinary KLR corner by the PBW/bubble normal form. Then
$$J\cap e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\mu)=e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu),\qquad I_a(\beta)=\sum_j R(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta).$$
The vacuum bubble specialization is forced by these generators: $A_\Lambda(t)=1+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}t+\cdots+c_{i,0}t^{\lambda_i}$ and $\mathsf H_\Lambda=A_\Lambda^{-1}$. Consequently the map from the ordinary monic cyclotomic corner to the downward-word Hom corner of $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ is an isomorphism, with composition corresponding to multiplication. This holds over every degree-zero field for the entire admissible homogeneous $Q$ family, without finite-type or characteristic-zero restrictions. Inhomogeneous monic specializations assert the ungraded corner equality, not a graded quantum-action conclusion.
items.strategy:
Use [[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]] for the formal graded maps, both triangles, rho inverse blocks, mixed dot compatibility, cross-and-cap identities and normalized bubble slides, and [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]] for the complete matching normal form and the downward PBW tensor independent vacuum bubbles. The formal $H_i$ is normalized projective restriction with input shift $-d_i(1+h)$ in the model; it is distinct from raw basic restriction. These are mathematical suppliers, not a citation-only import. Apply the following finite argument before transporting any formal relation to the actual cyclotomic action.

## Vacuum coefficients: the specialization is forced, not an extra assumption

Use the trace packet's normalized cups/caps; let h_l be the bubble closed with lambda_i-1+l dots and extend negative-dot symbols by formal inversion. The formal rank-one identities give h_l=0 for l<0 and h_0=1. Close a_i(x)x^{l-1}=0 for l>=1. The exponent l-1 is nonnegative, so this is a lawful defining-ideal consequence, including when some resulting indices are negative. It gives

$$h_l+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}h_{l-1}+\cdots+c_{i,0}h_{l-\lambda_i}=0.$$

Thus H(t)=sum_{l>=0} h_l t^l is the inverse of a_i^{rev}(t)=1+c_{i,lambda_i-1}t+...+c_{i,0}t^{lambda_i}. Bubble inversion determines the opposite family A(t)=H(t)^{-1}=a_i^{rev}(t). Consequently Phi_i(u)=u^{lambda_i}A(u^{-1})=a_i(u). Each coefficient conclusion uses only a finite recurrence. The local polynomial-model supplier proves these rank-one identities; no faithful cyclotomic action or generic Frobenius theorem is used.

Distinguish the index from the literal dot count. An actual vacancy loop with r>=0 dots has A index lambda_i+1+r; it vanishes because A is a polynomial of degree at most lambda_i. The A coefficients with index 1,...,lambda_i are fake bubbles of negative dot count; in the monic branch they are prescribed coefficients, not zero. The opposite H family is generally an infinite reciprocal series. For a_i=u(u-1), A=1-t and H=(1-t)^{-1}. Setting all positive bubbles in both orientations to zero would wrongly change this deformation. In the standard branch both positive coefficient families vanish. If lambda_i=0, a_i=1 kills F_i v and A=H=1; the degree-zero fake coefficient remains 1.

Write S for this vacuum bubble coefficient specialization. By the recurrence S is already contained in J. By [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]], specializing these central vacuum coefficients alone gives the all-downward corner R(beta), with no relations in its ordinary polynomial/crossing part. This uses the tensor-product normal form, not a flatness assertion. We can calculate in P_i/S and then include the E_i and first-strand generators.

## Bringing every bubble coefficient to the vacuum

After bending, a coefficient may initially be a bubble at source Lambda+alpha_i, immediately to the left of an added first i strand with dot z. It may not be replaced directly by the Lambda vacuum value. The required rank-one bubble-slide equation in coefficient normalization is

$$A_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^2A_\Lambda(t),\qquad H_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^{-2}H_\Lambda(t).$$

The weight indices differ by 2; these are normalized power series with constant coefficient 1. For each fixed coefficient this is a finite polynomial equation in z and the vacuum coefficients. Negative exponents on (1-zt) denote formal coefficient recursion, not inversion of z or an analytic infinite sum.

Here is an algebraic verification, independent of quotient faithfulness. In the unquotiented rank-one polynomial flag model, with total monic polynomial p and existing-root factor c_r, the normalized bubble series is p^{rev}/(c_r^{rev})^2; this is the coefficient/cap identity for the two monic flag pairings (equivalently complement factor divided by root factor). Adding the distinguished root z replaces c_r^{rev} by c_r^{rev}(1-zt). The target series is therefore the source series divided by (1-zt)^2. Multiplying proves the displayed equation; inversion gives the H equation. These finite coefficient equalities are explicit relations in the definition of the formal proof category and are verified by the local polynomial-model supplier. They are not derived from the normal-form faithfulness theorem that subsequently uses them for spanning. This uses only monic polynomial multiplication and coefficient inversion before quotienting, and does not claim that faithfulness survives a quotient.

Thus a finite diagram has, after finitely many coefficient slides, only polynomial dots on the added strand and bubble coefficients at Lambda. In P_i/S these coefficients are scalars. No source-weight bubble specialization or collision of two distinguished roots is assumed.

## The actual local straight and curl calculations

Use the actual rank-one cross-and-cap equations and their finite polynomial verification in the local model supplier; the same equations appear in Webster Figure2. The following dot-index calculation types the contraction directly and requires no two-root-collision identification.

The straight closure of the added leftmost i strand with r dots is the actual vacancy loop, with A index lambda_i+1+r. It is zero in P_i/S. This remains true for any polynomial dots with coefficients on the neighboring original strand, by linearity and dot cyclicity.

For the leftward single-crossing curl, Figure 2 expands it as a signed sum of a dotted uncrossed cap and a far-left bubble, with dot indices a+b=-1 and a>=0. Put b=-lambda_i-1+m. The bubble coefficient is A_m, and a=lambda_i-m. Terms with m<0 have negative bubble degree and vanish; terms with m>lambda_i have negative dots on the open strand and vanish. Therefore the undotted local curl is

$$\epsilon\sum_{m=0}^{\lambda_i}A_m x^{\lambda_i-m}=\epsilon a_i(x),\qquad \epsilon\in\{1,-1\}.$$

The sign is the fixed orientation/source-crossing unit. Since the statement is ideal membership, its value is immaterial; no unsigned equality of canonical maps is claimed. In characteristic 2 it is still a unit. When lambda_i=0 the sum is epsilon times the identity, matching a_i=1.

Let C(P) be this crossed closure with polynomial dots P(u,x), u on the added first strand and x on the first physical strand. The source nil-Hecke relation is kappa_1 u = x kappa_1 -1; natively tau_1 u = x tau_1 +1. Moving a u dot through the unique crossing gives

$$C(uP)=xC(P)+\epsilon' B(P),$$

where B(P) is a straight closure and epsilon' is the corresponding sign. All B(P)=0 by the preceding paragraph. Dots on the physical strand pull out by cyclicity. Induction on the two nonnegative dot exponents and linearity give

$$C(P)=\epsilon a_i(x)P(x,x).$$

This is the typed local calculation for arbitrary polynomial dots. It also equals epsilon times the coefficient of u^{-1} in a_i(u)P(u,x)/(u-x); the residue notation is a convenient finite coefficient identity, not an additional model identification. Spectator Q factors only change P or the exterior word morphisms; no factorization or specialization of Q is made.

## Bending every E_i-vacuum factor and the complete PBW split

An arbitrary generator summand factoring through A E_i v has maps f:F_mu v -> A E_i v and g:A E_i v -> F_nu v. The two specified adjunctions bend its vacuum E_i boundary. They yield f^flat:F_mu F_i(Lambda+alpha_i) -> A and g^sharp:A -> F_nu F_i(Lambda+alpha_i), with the prescribed shifts. The composite a=g^sharp f^flat has all-downward boundaries with one extra **first** i strand. Closing that added strand with the same cups/caps recovers gf by the adjunction triangles. This is a typed bend of the factor maps, not a claim that the internal word A is downward.

Apply [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]] to a, straightening all its internal cups/caps into the matching/dot/far-left-bubble normal form. With all-downward boundaries, each open component connects bottom to top; their matching is a permutation. The result is a finite sum of downward PBW terms with bubble coefficients. Slide the coefficients across the first added strand as above and specialize S.

Let W=S_{n+1} and W_P be the subgroup permuting positions 2,...,n+1. There are exactly two W_P double cosets: W_P and W_P s_1 W_P. In the first, w fixes position 1. In the second, choose the minimal parabolic coset representatives that move the departing first strand to position 2 and the arriving strand from position 2; then complete with a permutation of the last n positions. This gives w=u s_1 v, u,v in W_P, with lengths adding. The resulting reduced word contains s_1 exactly once. Equivalently the two cosets record whether the distinguished first input is matched to the distinguished first output; the second coset's remaining matching is an arbitrary permutation after those distinguished endpoints are removed. The standard insertion/removal reduced-word construction proves length additivity. These are **double** cosets; merely choosing right cosets is insufficient.

Choose precisely these reduced words in PBW. Every term is either a word using crossings kappa_2,...,kappa_n only, or L kappa_1 M with both exterior crossing words using only those crossings and arbitrary polynomial dots. Reduced-word replacement errors have fewer crossings and polynomial coefficients, so PBW straightening terminates in this same finite family. Bubble and dot coefficients never require inverting a dot or Q.

In the first case the last n strands pull past the first cup/cap, leaving a straight vacancy loop; its value is zero. In the second, the first endpoint has color i at both boundaries. L and M fix position 1, so the color at position 2 immediately at the sole kappa_1 must also be i: otherwise the first output color would differ from i. This proves that the sole boundary crossing is equal-color. No unlike-color cap-off case has been omitted. Exterior L,M act on only the physical n strands and pull through the left closure by horizontal functoriality; polynomial dots on the two crossing strands are exactly the P already calculated. The local result is epsilon a_i(x_1)P(x_1,x_1) on the first physical i strand. Hence the total term lies in

$$R(\beta)a_i(x_1)e(i,\beta-\alpha_i)R(\beta).$$

Consequently **every** E_i-vacuum ideal summand, with arbitrary internal word A and arbitrary factor maps, has its downward value in the ordinary first-strand i ideal. This is the finite completeness statement missing from a merely faithful generic model. For n=0 there is only the straight case, so it imposes no vacuum scalar relation.

## Why arbitrary whiskers of the other monic generators add no relations

It is necessary to handle A a_j(x) id(F_j v) when A itself contains E_i; cap-off of unmarked E_i-vacuum factors alone does not establish this. The following finite normalization supplies that check.

First, in P_i/S modulo the E_i-vacuum ideal, the rank-one rho at dominant vacuum decomposes E_i F_i v as lambda_i shifted identity summands; the F_i E_i summand is zero. The dotted cup columns v_r, r=0,...,lambda_i-1, are a basis of these summands after the finite triangular adjustment determined by the inverse bubble coefficients. In that basis dot multiplication x is the companion matrix of a_i:

$$xv_r=v_{r+1}\ (r<\lambda_i-1),\qquad xv_{\lambda_i-1}=-\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}c_{i,r}v_r.$$

One can verify the last column without assuming a one-dimensional Hom: pair it with each of the explicit dual cap rows of rho^{-1}. A raw cap row with s additional dots pairs with a cup column x^r by h_{r+s-lambda_i+1}; hence pairing a_i(x) with that row gives the recurrence at l=s+1. The dual rows are finite triangular combinations of these raw rows, so their entries are precisely linear combinations of h_l+c_{i,lambda_i-1}h_{l-1}+...+c_{i,0}h_{l-lambda_i}, all zero by the vacuum recurrence. All the projections vanish; rho's already imposed inverse matrix says the column itself vanishes. The earlier columns follow by one added dot. Thus a_i(x)=0 on E_i F_i v. For lambda_i=0 the object is zero, so the statement is vacuous. This is finite matrix algebra over the coefficient ring, not a rank or flatness argument.

Now normalize A a_j(x) at the intermediate **word-object** level and at its endomorphism simultaneously. Select the chronologically earliest E_i in A and move it toward the initial F_j v through the shorter negative prefix. Different-color commutation is the formal mixed isomorphism, natural in its input. For a same-color pair at input weight mu, put h=<h_i,mu> and retain the actual shifts in the following maps. If h>=0, write the appropriate canonical rho isomorphism (or its specified inverse, according to the orientation of rho) as r_h:E_i F_i -> F_i E_i direct-sum D_h, where D_h is the finite sum of h shifted identity functors. Conjugating an input-induced endomorphism by r_h gives the F_i E_i branch and the identity branches. This is a functor decomposition, natural in that endomorphism.

If h<0, the actual rho isomorphism instead has direction

$$r_h:F_iE_i\longrightarrow E_iF_i\oplus D_{-h}.$$

It does **not** decompose E_i F_i as F_i E_i plus identities. Let j_E,p_E be the inclusion and projection of its E_i F_i summand and define the natural retract maps

$$\iota_h=r_h^{-1}j_E:E_iF_i\longrightarrow F_iE_i,\qquad \pi_h=p_Er_h:F_iE_i\longrightarrow E_iF_i,\qquad \pi_h\iota_h=1.$$

For every input endomorphism b, naturality of r_h and its inverse gives iota_h (E_i F_i)(b) = (F_i E_i)(b) iota_h and pi_h (F_i E_i)(b) = (E_i F_i)(b) pi_h. Consequently

$$(E_iF_i)(b)=\pi_h(F_iE_i)(b)\iota_h.$$

Whisker these inclusion/projection maps by the remaining outer word. An arbitrary vertically sandwiched marked term g (E_i F_i)(b) f is therefore exactly (g pi_h) (F_i E_i)(b) (iota_h f). This moves the retained E_i one place toward the vacuum without asserting a false negative-weight direct-sum decomposition. The extra cups/caps in iota_h and pi_h belong to the adapted factor maps, not to the intermediate word whose normalization is being measured.

In both signs the input endomorphism b is the initial a_j on F_j v, with the shorter downward prefix attached. Naturality ensures the marker stays on that initial first strand. Positive-weight identity branches remove the chosen E_i and retain the ordinary first-strand marker. The branch retaining E_i (including the negative-weight retract branch) moves it one position nearer the initial F_j. At that strand, if j!=i, mixed dot compatibility sends the marker to F_j a_j(x) E_i v, hence zero modulo the E_i-vacuum ideal. If j=i, the vacuum weight is lambda_i>=0: the F_i E_i summand vanishes, and the identity-summand companion calculation above kills a_i. This last use of the companion matrix occurs only at the dominant vacuum, never at a negative intermediate weight.

Continue with the E_i generators in the resulting intermediate word objects. The lexicographic measure is (number of E_i letters in that word object, number of initial downward letters between its chronologically earliest E_i and the vacuum). An identity branch lowers the first coordinate; a retained-E_i branch lowers the second. For the negative-weight case this is the word F_i E_i in the displayed retract factorization, not the syntactic number of cups/caps or upward segments inside iota_h, pi_h, f or g. Outer whiskering and vertical composition leave this interpretation unchanged. Each step has a finite number of branches, and each branch terminates because the measure is a pair of nonnegative integers. Once the intermediate word is downward, its arbitrary adapted factor maps have all-downward boundaries and are reduced by [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]]'s formal normal form; their internal cups/caps do not restart the object-word induction. Therefore every horizontal whisker of an initial monic generator reduces to ordinary downward first-strand ideal insertions plus E_i-vacuum ideal summands. The latter were completely handled above. The equalities and retract maps are natural transformations and actual vertical factorizations, not equalities in K_0.

## Exact intersection

For f in the included downward R corner belonging to J, express f as a finite sum of vertically factored horizontal whiskers of the defining generators. Add S, which was already forced by J. The E_i summands have downward values in I_a by the typed bend, PBW two-double-coset split, and local curl calculation. The marked a_j summands have downward values in I_a by the finite marked normalization. Any S coefficient summands are zero after the tensor-product coefficient specialization. Thus the value of f in the specialized downward corner lies in I_a. Because the same specialization leaves every ordinary downward polynomial/crossing f unchanged, f belongs to I_a as an element of R. This is the required reverse inclusion. The forward inclusion follows directly from the initial a_j generators and downward whiskering/vertical composition. No quotient faithfulness, cyclotomic basis rank, generic symmetric/Frobenius theorem, or unproved intersection premise has entered this argument.

items.title: The two-colour jump formula and strict elementary embeddings
items.statement: Let k be any field and R(Q) the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum and any homogeneous Q satisfying the standing symmetry and nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up to internal shift. Set c_i(S)=epsilon_i^L(S) and J_i(S)=max{n>=0:c_i(f_i^n S)=c_i(S)}. This maximum is finite and J_i(S)=epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-<h_i,beta>. For i!=j one has c_i(f_j S)=c_i(S); for j=i it stays constant or increases by1, and increase is equivalent to f_i S=f_i^L S and to simplicity of Ind(S,L(i)). Once it increases, it increases at every later right-i step. Put wt(S)=-beta and phi_i=epsilon_i+<h_i,wt>. The maps Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^c_i(S) S tensor b_i(-c_i(S)) are strict injective elementary-crystal maps, and every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at some i. The simple graph is lowering-generated with every generic f_i nonzero. In any first-strand cyclotomic quotient containing S the actual surviving lowering length is lambda_i+epsilon_i(S)-<h_i,beta>. All containing-weight arguments take place in the auxiliary primitive-coroot finite-support datum, leaving R,A,D,Q unchanged, so no positive-dominant-label assumption on the original P is added. Linear divided restriction/G_0 operators satisfy the quantum Serre relation; the simple-socle crystal operators are not asserted to satisfy a linear Serre identity.
items.strategy:
Use the simple-socle/head symbols e_i,f_i only for crystal operators. Use mathsf E_i^(r) below for exact divided restriction functors and their A-linear G_0 operators. Consume the existing native10 positive second-adjunction contract Coind_(beta,gamma)(M,N)=Ind_(gamma,beta)(N,M){+(beta|gamma)}; all head/socle comparisons in this proof are shift-orbit statements.

For every finite containing-weight argument, first restrict to the finite color support of the modules and the selected i/j strings and use lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules. Its auxiliary primitive coroots admit labels with independently prescribed nonnegative lambda_l. The KLR algebras and their module, shuffle, restriction and induction calculations are unchanged because A,D,Q are unchanged; the first-strand quotient depends only on these lambda_l integers. Lambda/Omega used below are such auxiliary labels. No existence of a strictly positive dominant weight in the original P is assumed. Transport actual label weights back through the injective finite-support labeling when a label statement is needed. All choices of bounds and coordinates are finite.

## Two elementary tools

For an exact induction functor Ind(A,-), a composition-series argument produces a surjection Ind(A,U)->T from some simple composition factor U of H whenever Ind(A,H)->T is surjective and T simple. Indeed choose the first term in a composition series whose induced image is nonzero; that image is T and the previous term maps to zero. When only one simple factor has the required tail support, it must be this U. This argument obtains an actual map from the simple subquotient; it does not assert that every original map factors through an arbitrarily chosen head.

If epsilon_i(A)=0 and Ind(A,U)->T is nonzero with U,T simple, then epsilon_i(T)=epsilon_i(U). Shuffle gives the upper bound; adjunction injects A tensor U into restriction of T, whose terminal epsilon_i(U) corner is nonzero, giving the lower bound. Consequently every simple factor with the wrong epsilon is excluded in the preceding composition-series argument.

## The jump lemma

Adjunction for Ind(M,L(j))->f_j M and shuffle give

    c_i(M)<=c_i(f_j M)<=c_i(M)+delta_ij.

For i!=j this is equality, and first-end symmetry gives epsilon_i(f_j^L M)=epsilon_i(M). Suppose c_i(f_i M)=c_i(M)+1. Reversed induction Ind(L(i),M) has the same ungraded character as Ind(M,L(i)); character injectivity gives the same ungraded composition factors. Its unique maximal-first-tail factor is f_i^L M, once, so f_i M=f_i^L M. Conversely this equality immediately forces the increase of c_i.

C1, finite psi-duality and the coincidence of one-step head/socle shift orbits give D e_i M=e_i DM and D f_i M=f_i DM on shift orbits. Therefore coInd(M,L_n) has simple socle f_i^n M; the existing positive-shift Coind formula gives soc Ind(M,L_n)=(f_i^L)^n M and soc Ind(L_n,M)=f_i^n M on shift orbits (the actual socle shifts are the coinduction socle shifts minus (root(M),n alpha_i)). If f_i M=f_i^L M, the same simple is both head and socle of Ind(M,L_1), and occurs once in its whole composition series by C1. Such a finite-length module is simple: if its length were greater than1, its simple socle lies in its radical and gives a second occurrence of the head. Ind(M,L_1) is thus simple and equals Ind(L_1,M). Iterated induction and nil-Hecke induction identify Ind(M,L_n)=Ind(L_n,M), up to shift; their unique heads and socles agree and occur once, so they too are simple. In particular c_i(f_i^n M)=c_i(M)+n for all n. Thus once c_i increases, it increases at every later step.

Set J_i(M)=max{n:c_i(f_i^n M)=c_i(M)}. Its finiteness is proved by the separate root-height induction below, using eventual two-color growth and the annihilation lemma, without presuming integrability in an unbounded i-direction. Once finite, the zero-jump lemma proves J_i(f_i M)=max(0,J_i(M)-1); the symmetric jump formula below gives its first-end analogue.

For any Lambda containing M, write p_i^Lambda(M) for its actual surviving f_i length. Once finiteness is established, the first-color criterion and cross-color invariance give exactly

    p_i^Lambda(M)=J_i(M)+lambda_i-c_i(M).                 (1)

Hence differences of p_i for two surviving simples are independent of the containing dominant weight. There is no assumption here that p_i already equals epsilon_i+weight.

## Complete two-color classification

Here is the algebra calculation needed to use the direct §6.3.1 route for general Q, rather than the unproved p5 extension sentence. Fix i!=j, a=-a_ij and t the nonzero coefficient of u^a in Q_ij. The one-j simple has its dot acting by0. Homogeneity gives Q_ij(u,0)=t u^a. For a triple i,j,i whose j-dot acts by0, the divided braid polynomial is, up to the fixed presentation sign,

    t sum_(r=0)^(a-1) x_left^r x_right^(a-1-r).

Mixed Q monomials with positive j-exponent vanish. The coefficient t remains invertible over every field. In the nil-Hecke simple of m strands each dot has nilpotence index exactly m: the coinvariant algebra model k[x_1,...,x_m]/(positive symmetric polynomials) has x_s^m=0 and x_s^(m-1)!=0; the latter follows from the monic Artin basis after permuting s to the chosen last coordinate. Its polynomial representation contains a vector on which this power is nonzero.

For m+n<=a, the length-decreasing quadratic terms at either i/j boundary vanish, since x_i^a=0 on a block of size m or n. The divided braid term vanishes since every r has r>=m or a-1-r>=n. Thus the positive-shuffle span in Ind(L(i^m),L(j),L(i^n)) is invariant under dots, idempotents and crossings: dot slides keep j in the same position; far moves preserve positive length; only the boundary square and i,j,i divided braid can remove the last unequal crossing, and their correction terms just vanished. The quotient supported on i^m j i^n is precisely the simple tensor of the two nil-Hecke simples and L(j), hence is simple, with character [m]!_i[n]!_i i^m j i^n. Any simple of ci+j has a nonzero such corner; a simple submodule in that corner induces onto it, so these exhaust the simples for c<=a. The tensor quotient is generated by its defining corner, giving the indicated quotient map. This constructs the small two-color simples without Serre minimality or Gabber–Kac imports.

For m+n=a+1 with m,n>0, the same divided braid polynomial has a single possibly nonzero term on a tensor of top-dot vectors: r=m-1, a-1-r=n-1. Its coefficient is the unit t. Both neighboring unequal crossings belong to the kernel of a hypothetical quotient supported only at i^m j i^n, so the braid difference would belong to that kernel; its correction instead equals t times a nonzero defining-corner vector generating the tensor simple. This forces the whole induced module into the kernel and contradicts its being proper. For m=0 or n=0 the boundary square replaces the braid: t x_i^a acts nontrivially on the block of a+1 strands. Consequently at the critical degree the induction head cannot remain on a single word. The C1 nonreduced head/once theorem and the linear projective-Serre proof below establish the remaining critical and larger-degree structure.

For c<=a the following direct generic-Q calculation constructs the simple L(i^(c-n) j i^n), 0<=n<=c, with character [c-n]!_i[n]!_i i^(c-n)j i^n and epsilon_i=n, c_i=c-n. These exhaust simples: every simple has a nonzero word corner of this form, that corner has a simple submodule for the tensor product of its three block algebras, and induction from that tensor maps onto the simple. The constructed simple quotient has the only defining-word tensor multiplicity and the unique-head recursion selects it. For uniqueness with a specified n>0 strip one last i and induct on c using C1. For n=0 use first-end stripping; the last and first zero conditions cannot both hold at a positive i-count. Thus there is exactly one simple per n.

Write L(n)=L(i^(a-n) j i^n), 0<=n<=a. To prove Ind(L(n),L_1) simple, C1 gives its head T and epsilon_i(T)=n+1. Shuffle permits only two positions of j in its character: i^(a-n)j i^(n+1) and i^(a-n+1)j i^n. The first position is nonzero by the maximal-tail formula. Here the simple-socle symbols e_i do NOT satisfy quantum Serre relations. Define the EXACT divided restriction functor mathsf E_i^(r)(X)=HOM_(NH_r)(P_(i,r),Delta_i^r X), retaining the remaining R action; it is exact because the divided projective is projective. Its class gives an A-linear operator on G_0, and repeated one-strand restriction has [r]_i! times that class with the native shifts. Native10 projective Serre and induction–restriction adjunction imply sum_(s=0)^(a+1)(-1)^s mathsf E_i^(a+1-s) mathsf E_j^(1) mathsf E_i^(s)=0 on G_0: pair with any projective P of the remaining root weight; the result is the Hom pairing of Ind(P, sum_s(-1)^s P_(i,a+1-s)P_(j,1)P_(i,s)) with X, which vanishes by the native relation; the unscaled perfect cover–simple pairing forces the operator relation. Its sign agrees with native (-1)^(a+1-s) after multiplication by one common sign. Apply THIS LINEAR relation to [T]. Equivalently at the critical full root weight, apply the Hom functional h(-,T) to the projective Serre class. Only the actual word corners i^(a+1-s) j i^s for s=n and s=n+1 can be nonzero, by the preceding two-position shuffle support. The s=n+1 corner is nonzero by epsilon_i(T)=n+1 and the maximal-tail theorem. Applying the divided block idempotents does not erase a nonzero such corner: each nil-Hecke divided idempotent is full, so its tensor product is full in the block algebra and detects every nonzero module. Thus the s=n+1 contribution is a nonzero positive Laurent polynomial (a scalar class in G_0(k)); the alternating relation forces the s=n contribution also nonzero. That actual word support forces c_i(T)=a-n+1=c_i(L(n))+1. No nonlinear crystal Serre identity is used. The jump lemma therefore makes Ind(L(n),L_1) simple. It follows for every m that Ind(L(n),L_m)=Ind(L_m,L(n)) is simple. This proof uses a locally proved Serre relation, not a minimality/Gabber–Kac theorem or a parameter-independence claim.

For c>=a, every simple of ci+j is exactly

    Ind(L(n-(c-a)),L_(c-a)),  c-a<=n<=c, epsilon_i=n.     (2)

Induct on c. A simple with epsilon_i=0 would have only the word i^c j, since there is only one j and any other position of j leaves a terminal i. For c>=a+1 multiply the native projective Serre relation on the LEFT by P_(i,c-a-1) and pair with this simple. Every s>0 term has a terminal i^s block and its actual word corner is zero. The s=0 term has the nonzero defining i^c j corner; the tensor product of the divided nil-Hecke idempotents on its consecutive i-blocks is full and therefore detects it. This gives one nonzero positive Laurent polynomial equal to zero, a contradiction. Equivalently these are exact divided restriction/G_0 operators; no simple-socle crystal operator is substituted into a Serre sum. So strip one i by C1, use the inductive formula and the just-proved commuting/simple induction of L(n), and restore it. This proves existence, uniqueness, and all larger-degree characters. In particular the classifications and composition-series selection show that the head of Ind(L(i^b j i^d),L_m) is L(i^b j i^(d+m)) while b+d+m<a; at and beyond the boundary it is Ind(L(a-b),L_(m-a+b+d)).

A useful consequence: if T is a simple quotient of Ind(L(n_1),...,L(n_r),L_m), then

    epsilon_i(T)=m+sum n_t,  c_i(T)=m+sum(a-n_t).         (3)

For the first equality, shuffle bounds the tail above by that value. Split each L(n_t) as the head of Ind(L(i^(a-n_t)j),L_(n_t)), commute its appended i-block past the subsequent L(n_s) using their just-proved simple commuting induction, and obtain a surjection with all m+sum n_t i-strands at the end. Adjunction gives the matching lower bound. Repeat at the first end for the second equality. If Ind(B,L(n))->T is nonzero then epsilon_i(T)=epsilon_i(B)+n by the same stripping/commuting argument.

If B is a nontrivial simple of ci+dj with epsilon_i(B)=0, strip a last j, then strip the newly exposed maximal i-tail b. This gives Ind(B',L_b,L(j))->B with epsilon_i(B')=0. The classification (2) and simple-subquotient selection force b<=a and select L(i^b j). Repeating decreases height, giving

    Ind(L(i^b_1 j),...,L(i^b_r j))->B,  0<=b_t<=a.       (4)

All factors are actual constructed two-color simples.

## Eventual first-tail calculation for two-color modules

Let M be simple of ci+dj, m=epsilon_i(M), and let N=e_i^m M. Choose (4) for N. Induction then gives a surjection

    Ind(L(i^b_1 j),...,L(i^b_r j),L_(m+h))->f_i^h M.

Move the appended i-strands through the factors from right to left. The classification says that a factor L(i^b j) absorbs a-b i-strands to become L(a-b); beyond that point additional i-strands commute past it. Simple-subquotient selection uses epsilon_i of the target to exclude every lower-tail factor. Thus, for m+h>=sum(a-b_t), there is a surjection

    Ind(L(a-b_1),...,L(a-b_r),L_g)->f_i^h M,
    g=m+h-sum(a-b_t).

Equation (3) yields

    c_i(f_i^h M)=h+m-ar+2 sum b_t.                       (5)

This is eventual linear growth of slope1, proving J_i(M)<infinity for two-color M. The absorption algorithm in the insufficient-i case stops at the unique factor s satisfying sum_(t>s)(a-b_t)<=m+h<sum_(t>=s)(a-b_t), with that factor L(i^b_s j i^g') and all factors to its right saturated; the same classification proves that case as well.

Let T=f_j M, i!=j, gamma=epsilon_i(T). The map Ind(N,L_m,L(j))->T and simple-subquotient selection choose the unique simple U_gamma of mi+j with that tail. The classification gives gamma=m-(a-n), 0<=n<=a, and f_i^a U_gamma=Ind(L(n),L_m). For sufficiently large h, absorb the appended i-strands through U_gamma, then through all factors (4). Equation (3) now gives

    c_i(f_i^h T)=h+m-n-ar+2 sum b_t=c_i(f_i^h M)-n.      (6)

All selections are justified by the exact induction, the tail bound when the preceding factor has epsilon_i=0, and the strict lower-tail property of C1. Choose omega_i equal to (5) at some sufficiently large h and other omega_l large enough for M and T; cross-color invariance ensures those other first-tail bounds are unchanged along their f_i strings. Equations (5)–(6), the slope1 continuation, and the cyclotomic criterion give p_i^Omega(M)=h and p_i^Omega(T)=h+n. Equation (1) shows their difference is independent of the containing weight. Thus in any common containing quotient,

    epsilon_i(T)=m-(a-n),  p_i(T)=p_i(M)+n.              (7)

For j=i, C1 and the definition of p_i instead give epsilon_i(f_i M)=m+1 and p_i(f_i M)=p_i(M)-1.

## Annihilation and survival lemmas

Let A survive Lambda and let k=p_i^Lambda(A), assumed finite. If t>k, C1 says Ind(A,L_t) has only one simple quotient f_i^t A, which dies under projection. Therefore its projected module is zero: otherwise that finite-dimensional projection would have a surviving simple quotient, contradicting uniqueness. Appending any further factor U keeps the projection zero. To see this directly, choose tensor generators for A,L_t and U; the first two induced factors lie in their cyclotomic ideal multiple, and that same ideal embeds as a first-strand ideal in the full induction, so their tensors still lie in the full ideal multiple. If B is simple with c_i(B)>k, write B as the head of Ind(L_(c_i(B)),C) using the first-tail lemma. Exact induction and right exact projection now give

    pr_Lambda Ind(A,B)=0.                               (8)

Suppose instead epsilon_i(A)=epsilon_j(A)=0, B is simple of ci+dj, and c_i(B)<=k. Put b=c_i(B), C=(e_i^L)^b B. Ind(A,L_b,C)->Q is surjective for every simple quotient Q of Ind(A,B). In its first two factors the unique head f_i^b A survives. Any other factor U of Ind(A,L_b) has epsilon_i(U)<b. The original defining A|i^b|C corner of Q is nonzero by adjunction. No Ind(U,C) has this defining corner. Every word of A ends in a color outside {i,j}; in any shuffle producing U from Ind(A,L_b), all original A i/j letters occur before A's final outside-color letter, since their order is preserved. In the target defining A|i^b|C word, the prefix through that final outside-color letter contains exactly the original A i/j counts. Thus no j from C can occur in that prefix: it would increase the j count, and no original A j can move past that final letter to compensate. Nor can an added i from C or from the L_b block occur there, by the identical i-count argument. The following i^b block cannot get an i from C, because C has first-i tail0, so every nonempty word of C starts in j; its preceding j can enter neither the prefix just counted nor the pure i^b block. Hence all b consecutive i after the final outside-color letter must come from U, giving a terminal i-tail of length at least b in U, contrary to epsilon_i(U)<b. If C is the vacuum the same conclusion is immediate. This is the actual count/ordering exclusion, rather than an inference from the smaller-epsilon inequality alone. Thus the simple-subquotient selection lemma produces Ind(f_i^b A,C)->Q. Shuffle bounds c_i(Q)<=c_i(f_i^b A)+c_i(C)<=lambda_i. The same argument for j proves survival in the j-coordinate provided c_j(B)<=p_j^Lambda(A). All other coordinates are bounded by c_l(A), since B has only colors i,j. In particular choosing lambda_j sufficiently large ensures that extra inequality: c_j(f_j^d A)<=c_j(A)+d by shuffle, so lambda_j>=c_j(A)+d ensures p_j^Lambda(A)>=d>=c_j(B), without using a normal-length formula.

This survival lemma uses the actual defining-corner exclusion, not merely the inequality epsilon_i(U)<b in isolation; the latter would not control an arbitrary additional factor. It is precisely why A is required to be reduced at both i and j.

## Finiteness of jump for every simple: a separate height induction

This avoids a tacit integrability assumption in the source. The vacuum has f_i^n 1=L_n and c_i(L_n)=n, so J_i(1)=0. Assume finiteness for all strictly smaller heights than M. If r=epsilon_i(M)>0, put N=e_i^r M; then M=f_i^r N. Once first-tail growth has begun it continues at every step, by the jump lemma. Thus J_i(M)=max(0,J_i(N)-r), which is finite by induction.

If epsilon_i(M)=0 and M is nonvacuum, choose a terminal color j with epsilon_j(M)>0; necessarily j!=i. Alternately strip maximal j- and i-tails until both vanish. Height strictly decreases at the first stripping, so the resulting A has smaller height than M. Exact induction reconstructs M as a simple quotient of Ind(A,B), where B is a simple two-color module with epsilon_i(B)=0 and epsilon_i(A)=epsilon_j(A)=0. To choose B, apply the simple-subquotient selection lemma to the induced product of all stripped blocks; the terminal-tail bounds pick an actual simple factor. C1's strict-leading factor selection gives surjections Ind(A,f_i^h B)->f_i^h M for every h. Choose a dominant Lambda containing both A and M. By inductive J_i(A)<infinity, equation (1) gives finite k=p_i^Lambda(A). Equation (5) proves c_i(f_i^h B)>k for all sufficiently large h. Equation (8) forces pr_Lambda f_i^h M=0. If J_i(M) were infinite, cross-color invariance and constant c_i would instead make every f_i^h M survive that same Lambda by the cyclotomic criterion. This contradiction proves finiteness. Now (1) is established for every simple without assuming normality or per-color categorical integrability.

## Transfer of (7) to arbitrary root support

Let M,T=f_j M survive Lambda and i!=j. Strip m=epsilon_i(M) to N, then alternately strip i/j tails from N until obtaining A reduced at both colors. Reconstruct N as a simple quotient of Ind(A,B_0), with B_0 a two-color simple reduced at i. Its j-tail equals that of N by the upper/lower tail bounds. Strict-leading selection converts

    Ind(A,B_0,L_m)->M

into Ind(A,B)->M with B=f_i^m B_0 and epsilon_i(B)=m. Similarly the j-leading selection gives Ind(A,f_j B)->T and epsilon_i(f_j B)=epsilon_i(T). For every h the same argument gives Ind(A,f_i^h B)->f_i^h M and Ind(A,f_i^h f_j B)->f_i^h T.

Choose Omega containing all four A,M,B,f_j B, with omega_j sufficiently large to make the survival lemma's j-condition automatic for every candidate two-color factor above. Its j count is fixed while i-count varies, and cross-color invariance fixes its c_j. Other omega_l can be fixed because two-color factors have no other colors. Put h=p_i^Omega(M), h'=p_i^Omega(T), and k=p_i^Omega(A). These numbers are finite by the preceding height induction. Applying the contrapositive of (8) at the surviving endpoints gives c_i(f_i^h B)<=k and c_i(f_i^h' f_j B)<=k. Applying the contrapositive of the survival lemma at the next, nonsurviving endpoints gives c_i(f_i^(h+1) B)>k and c_i(f_i^(h'+1) f_j B)>k. Since each increase is at most1, both surviving endpoint coordinates equal k. Since an increase has begun, their jumps are zero.

Equation (1) applied to those endpoint modules yields p_i^Omega(f_i^h B)=omega_i-k=p_i^Omega(f_i^h' f_j B). Subtracting gives

    p_i^Omega(f_j B)-p_i^Omega(B)=h'-h
      =p_i^Omega(T)-p_i^Omega(M).

The two-color formula (7) gives its value n, where epsilon_i(T)=m-(a-n), 0<=n<=a. Equation (1) and cross-color invariance make p_i(T)-p_i(M) independent of containing quotient, proving (7) for arbitrary support.

## The jump formula

For every surviving M of root weight beta, prove

    p_i^Lambda(M)=lambda_i+epsilon_i(M)-<h_i,beta>       (9)

by induction on height. At the vacuum, p_i=lambda_i because f_i^n 1=L_n has first-tail n; epsilon=0. At positive height choose a last color j and N=e_j M, so M=f_j N and N survives the same quotient. If j=i, epsilon increases1 and actual lowering length decreases1, while <h_i,beta> increases2; (9) follows. If j!=i, equation (7) gives p_i(M)-p_i(N)=n and epsilon_i(M)-epsilon_i(N)=-(a-n), while <h_i,beta>-<h_i,beta-alpha_j>=-a. Again (9) follows. The proof never uses a connected-normality recognition theorem.

Choose any dominant weight containing a generic simple M. Combine (1) and (9):

    J_i(M)=epsilon_i(M)+c_i(M)-<h_i,beta>.              (10)

The right side is invariant under first/last reversal, so all first-end versions of jump and decrease formulas follow. This completes the actual full-support jump calculation, subject only to the explicitly listed local PBW/Mackey/Serre/coinduction suppliers and C1.

## Strict elementary embeddings: all branch cases

For generic wt(M)=-beta put c=c_i(M), bar M=(e_i^L)^c M, and Psi_i(M)=bar M tensor b_i(-c). Reversal symmetry and (10) show that applying f_i^L decreases jump by1 until it becomes zero. Since c_i(bar M)=0, initially J_i(bar M)=epsilon_i(bar M)+<h_i,wt(bar M)>. While jump is positive, first-end lowering preserves epsilon_i; after jump reaches zero, zero-jump equality makes each first-end lowering equal right lowering and epsilon_i increases1. Therefore

    epsilon_i(M)=max(epsilon_i(bar M),c-<h_i,wt(bar M)>).

For e_i, if epsilon_i(bar M)>=c-<h_i,wt(bar M)>, the jump of (e_i^L)M is positive when c>0. Raising cannot decrease c: otherwise zero-jump applied to e_i M would force e_i M=e_i^L M, contradicting that positive jump. Thus it preserves c, and cross-end stripping identifies the stripped result with e_i bar M. If epsilon_i(bar M)<c-<h_i,wt(bar M)>, then J_i(e_i^L M)=0, so zero-jump gives f_i(e_i^L M)=M and e_i M=e_i^L M; its first-tail is c-1 and stripping gives bar M. At c=0 only the first branch can occur. At epsilon_i(M)=0 the max formula forces epsilon_i(bar M)=0 and phi_i(bar M)>=c, so tensor raising is zero in its first branch. These are exactly the tensor e_i branch inequalities, including equality in the first branch.

For j!=i, first-tail invariance and Mackey stripping give (e_i^L)^c f_j M=f_j bar M, hence the lowering rule directly; applying this to e_j M gives the raising rule whenever it is nonzero. For zero raising, the equality of epsilon_j(M) and epsilon_j(bar M), obtained by repeated first-end lowering invariance, makes both sides zero. Weight is preserved, the max formula preserves epsilon_i, cross-color invariance preserves all other epsilon, and phi=epsilon+weight is consequently preserved. The map is injective because M=(f_i^L)^c bar M. Thus Psi_i is strict. A nonvacuum M has a word beginning with some i, so some c_i(M)>0; every elementary coordinate is nonpositive. Generic lowering generation follows from repeated right-socle stripping, and all f_i are nonzero by C1.

The module crystal now satisfies all finite-extraction comparison hypotheses: lowering generation, everywhere nonzero generic lowering, strict elementary embeddings, nonpositive elementary coordinates, and positive extraction at every nonvacuum vertex. The subsequent canonical extraction lemma supplies the independent canonical comparison crystal; no connected rank-one normality assertion is used here.

For the remaining i-lowering check, f_i is nonzero in the generic module crystal and in the elementary tensor target: either it acts on the everywhere-lowerable first factor or on the elementary string. Applying the already verified raising identity to f_i M gives e_i Psi_i(f_i M)=Psi_i(M). Tensor partial inverses then force Psi_i(f_i M)=f_i Psi_i(M). This proves strict lowering including its opposite equality convention, rather than merely saying its check is similar.

items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator for cyclotomic KLR functors
items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let $E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\,\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$
(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\,\mathrm{Id}.$$
Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift conventions).

items.title: Coherent graded biadjunction and the crossing mates
items.statement:
For the standard homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient over any field and every homogeneous Q1–Q4 datum, use basic right-append induction $F_i$ from $ eta$ to $ eta+\alpha_i$ and basic restriction $E_i$ in the reverse direction. Put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda- etaangle$ and $t_i( eta)=2d_i(1-h)=(\alpha_i|\alpha_i)-2(\Lambda- eta|\alpha_i)$. There are explicit homogeneous bimodule units and counits with both triangle identities giving $E_i\{t_i( eta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded module categories. They preserve the standard dot-cyclic and same-color crossing-mate identities and the coherent different-color double-mate identity: for $p_
u=	au_r e(
u)$ with bottom adjacent colors $(i,j)$, $i
e j$, its double right mate is $(t_{ji}/t_{ij})p_
u$, where $t_{ij}$ is the coefficient of $u^{-a_{ij}}$ in $Q_{ij}(u,v)$ and the strand of color $i$ runs SW to NE. Equivalently the associated right closure satisfies $\operatorname{cl}(p_
u a)=(t_{ji}/t_{ij})\operatorname{cl}(a p_
u)$ for $a\in e(
u)R^\Lambda( eta)e(s_r
u)$; dots, idempotents and equal-color crossings have ratio $1$. The corresponding arbitrary monic field quotients have the same underlying ungraded biadjunction and ordered crossing-mate identities after forgetting internal shifts. items.strategy:
Work throughout with $\kappa=-\tau_{\rm native}$ for every color pair. This is a graded algebra isomorphism preserving $Q$ and all first-strand monic ideals: quadratic relations have two signs, the braid defect three, and $\kappa_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\tau_w$. Hence model crossings are native $-\pi$ and $-Q$; changing only equal-color crossings is not allowed. Use the formal category and its explicit graded flag model from the declared suppliers. With $i$ last in a total color order, raw downward flags have shifts $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. A degree-$D$ raw map between word shifts $S,T$ has degree $D+T-S$. Thus a source increasing crossing $\pi$ of degree zero and its reverse multiplier $Q$ of degree $-2b_{jk}$ both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$. Basic $E_iG_j$ has the prescribed $-b_{ij}$ shifted commutation. Formal $H_i=E_i^{\rm basic}\{-d_i(1+h_{\rm input})\}$ cancels that shift: $h$ increases by $-a_{ij}$ under $G_j$ and $s_j(m-e_i)=s_j(m)+b_{ij}$. It is formal $H_i$, rather than basic $E_i$, that commutes unshiftedly with the spectator flag.

At a vertex with $r$ i roots and total monic degree $N$, put $L=C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]/(\text{factor coefficients above }N-r)$, $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$, $p=a_i\prod Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $b=p/c_r$. The i-flag algebra is $B=L[z]/b(z)$, free over the old ring on powers $0\le j<N-r$ and free over the target root-append ring on powers $0\le j\le r$. The two coefficient traces $\tau_{\rm old}$ and $\tau_{\rm new}$ extract the respective top powers in their monic remainders. Their Gram matrices in power/complementary bases are triangular with diagonal one, so they have explicit dual bases without factorial denominators. Basic $F_i=B\{-2d_i r\}\otimes-$ and basic reverse $E_i=B\otimes-$ use $\tau_{\rm new}$ and its dual bases for the first adjunction and $\tau_{\rm old}$ for the second. If $(u_a,v_a)$ are either pair of dual bases, the unit is $1\mapsto\sum_av_a\otimes u_a$ and the counit is its coefficient trace. The identities $\sum_av_a\tau(u_ax)=x$ and $\sum_a\tau(xv_a)u_a=x$ give both triangles directly. The trace-degree difference is $-2d_i(N-2r-1)=t_i(\beta)$. Source second maps are normalized by $(-1)^{N+1}=(-1)^{h+1}$, with the unit given the inverse scalar; degree-zero bubbles are one. Transporting $\kappa=-\tau$ preserves these maps and triangles, and dots/crossings inherit their actual pairing-adjoint identities.

For coherent mixed maps, let $Q_{ij}(u,y)=t_{ij}q(u,y)$ with $q$ monic and replace $p$ by $pq$. The successive i/j flags have rings modulo $b$ and $bq$; their source crossings are quotient $\pi$ and multiplication by $Q$. Monic coefficient extraction gives $\epsilon_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\epsilon_p(f)$ on the one-variable power basis. On all nil-Hecke matrix entries use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}(\Delta_r b_r\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_s p(X_s))$, with $\Delta_r=\prod_{s<t}(X_s-X_t)$ and $b_r=X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}$. It equals the integral parabolic divided-difference form: summing ordered distinct roots gives $\Delta^2$, repeated roots vanish, and the resulting integral polynomial identity specializes to every characteristic. There is no $1/r!$. For $U_r=\prod_sQ_{ij}(X_s,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{pq}(U_rz)=(-1)^{r(-a_{ij})}t_{ij}^r t_r^p(z)$. Perfect coefficient pairings then give the full relative identity $\pi_r\widehat\epsilon^{pq}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}z)=t_{ij}\widehat\epsilon^p(z)$ after the global second-map normalization; it holds for every matrix/coset element. Its ordinary mate is the mixed-unit identity. Native single crossings add one minus sign, while the two-sideways composites have two and retain $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$. Their ordered quotient is $t_{ji}/t_{ij}$ for the i strand running SW–NE. This proves the formal crossing-mate relation without assuming a one-dimensional Hom space.

Transfer that formal relation to the actual first-strand quotient using the declared cap-off kernel supplier and PBW/bubble normal form, not rank-one detection of arbitrary map equality. Let $J$ be generated by $H_iv_\Lambda$ and $a_j(x)G_jv_\Lambda$. The marked i generator closed with dot powers forces $H(t)a_i^{\rm rev}(t)=1$; its canonical unit columns $x^k\eta$, $k<\lambda_i$, have companion polynomial exactly $a_i$. Genuine vacancy loops have index $\lambda_i+1+s$ and vanish, whereas the lower fake coefficients in the monic branch are retained. Every factor through a vacuum $H_i$ bends to an added first i strand. The cap-off supplier proves the full two-double-coset PBW reduction: no first crossing closes to that zero loop; one first crossing must be equal-color and its actual cross-and-cap sum is a unit sign times $a_i(x)$, with decorated value $a_i(x)P(x,x)$. Physical exterior factors commute with closure. Arbitrary upward whiskers of a marked $a_j$ reduce by input naturality of the mixed maps/rho; for negative h use the actual retract $\iota=\rho^{-1}j_{EF}$, $\pi=p_{EF}\rho$, $\pi\iota=1$. The branch reaching the marker is zero by the companion matrix when j=i or by mixed dot commutation and $H_iv=0$ otherwise. The finite word-object induction treats every marked whisker and every factor map. Thus $J$ meets the downward corner in exactly the ordinary first-strand ideal.

The algebraic right-append kernel agrees explicitly. Set $K_0=Se(\beta,i)/Sa(x_1)R(\beta)e(\beta,i)$ and $K_1=Se(i,\beta)/Sa(x_2)R_1(\beta)e(i,\beta)$. PBW makes them finite right $R^a(\beta)[t]$-projectives. Right multiplication $P=a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ is bilinear; its counterpart $Q=g_n\cdots g_1$ uses the source intertwiners and satisfies $QP=\sum_\nu a_i(t)\prod_{\nu_a\ne i}Q_{i\nu_a}(t,x_a)e(\nu)$, with a unit leading scalar. Hence P is injective. The full-transfer PBW coset gives $\operatorname{im}P=\ker(K_0\to R^a(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i))$; shorter cosets lie in the prefix ideal. This is also valid ungraded for arbitrary monic $a_j$. It identifies the formal quotient's word corners with the actual cyclotomic corners in dependency order. All quotient objects are summands of finite sums of negative words: move formal H through the last downward letter by mixed commutation or the sign-correct EF retract and induct on word length, starting from $H_iv=0$. Thus the idempotent-completed formal quotient is the category of actual word projectives. Right appending is the actual induction, and its first adjoint is actual basic restriction by tensor-Hom uniqueness; the rho/dot formulas fix the second maps coherently under this same identification.

Finally evaluate each formal unit/counit on the regular algebra, which is the finite sum of word idempotent projectives. Naturality with its homogeneous right multiplications (and shifts) makes each evaluated map a homogeneous bimodule map. Their two triangle identities on the regular objects are equalities of those bimodule maps. Tensoring them with any graded module therefore gives units/counits with the same triangles on all graded modules, not only word projectives. The crossing-mate equality similarly is an equality of bimodule maps and extends by tensoring. Forget the internal degrees after arbitrary inhomogeneous monic coefficient specialization; all monic, dual-basis, residue, companion, cap-off and kernel identities remain algebraic identities. No graded highest-weight action is inferred for that deformation. At every stage the finite-dimensional/root-string supplier and projectivity/commutator suppliers are algebraic prerequisites; a symmetric/Frobenius or Grothendieck/crystal theorem is never used.

items.title: Normalized cyclotomic functors give an integrable quantum action
items.statement: For the standard graded quotient over arbitrary $k$ and graded admissible $Q$, let $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$. On projective $K_0$ take $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i=q_i^{1-h}E_i^{\rm basic}$ on input $\beta+i$ to output $\beta$. On module $G_0$ take the KK action $E_i=E_i^{\rm basic}$ and $F_i=q_i^{1-h}F_i^{\rm basic}$ on input $\beta$; also the canonical action with the SAME shifts as projectives. The torus acts on root component $\beta$ by $K_a=q^{\langle a,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$. Each action satisfies all mixed relations, and $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent. After scalar extension to $\mathbb Q(q)$ these are integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules. This does not assert a decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules and does not cover ungraded monic deformations.
items.strategy:
Projectivity supplies exact functors and preservation of finite projectives, so the displayed shifts give $A$-linear operators. In the basic commutator at target $\beta$, multiply $EF$ by $q_i^{1-h}$; the $q_i^{-2}FE$ term becomes precisely the normalized $FE$ at its changed target, and identity terms become $\sum_{k=0}^{h-1}q_i^{1-h+2k}=[h]_i$. The negative case gives the signed counterpart. In the KK representation action the same factors are instead carried by $F$; in the canonical representation action they are carried by $E$, so the same computation holds. Unequal-color basic crossing shift $q^{-b_{ij}}$ cancels the change of the normalizing $h_i$ under removing/adding $j$.
Restriction lowers height. The dot/root-string lemma gives $R^\Lambda(\beta+ni)=0$ for large $n$, so induction is locally nilpotent componentwise. Every Grothendieck element has finite root support and the displayed torus labels are correct. The general mixed/local-nilpotence lemma proves BOTH full symmetrizable Serre families by finite rank-one Hom adjoint modules, giving the unique rational quantum action without an A2 or rank-two local-finiteness assumption. All these steps precede vacuum generation and the integral highest-module identification, so no cyclic dependency is used.

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR algebras are finite-dimensional graded symmetric algebras
items.statement: For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and admissible graded real symmetrizable KLR datum, every block $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional, all dots are nilpotent, and $R^\Lambda(\beta+n\alpha_i)=0$ for large $n$. Put $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$. A nonzero block has a perfect symmetric homogeneous functional $\operatorname{tr}_\beta:B\to k$ of degree $t_\beta=-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)$; on a zero block perfectness is vacuous and the functional is zero. Thus $DB\cong B\{t_\beta\}$ as graded bimodules. For finite projective $P$, with $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$, one has $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{t_\beta\}$, so vector duality preserves projectives. This does not assert $P^\#=P$ for every shifted projective, nor self-duality of every indecomposable finite module. For arbitrary monic deformation polynomials the separate conclusion is finite-dimensional and symmetric UNGRADED, with finite root strings and monic dot annihilators; nilpotence and homogeneous trace degree are not asserted. In rank one the standard trace is the top coefficient on $k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ and has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$.

u)$ to obtain the regular module $B$. The second adjunction gives the NATURAL isomorphism $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,B)=D\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,M)\{-t_ eta\}$. The image of $1_B$ is a degree-$t_ eta$ functional; naturality identifies the induced pairing with composition. The isomorphism therefore proves perfectness, rather than assuming a nonzero diagram closure detects every ideal.
Dot and equal-color mate coherence makes this raw form cyclic on those generators. For an unequal crossing the proved oriented mixed identity is $	au(pa)=(t_{ji}/t_{ij})	au(ap)$ with NE/SW color $i$. Choose a reference word and nonzero diagonal weights $c_

u}(t_{ji}/t_{ij})=c_
u$. Their inversion-pair product is path independent by Coxeter moves. Rescaling by $c=\sum c_
u e(
u)$ makes the trace cyclic for every generator and hence every product. Multiplication by $c$ is invertible, preserving perfectness and degree. The symmetric pairing identifies $B\{t_ eta\}$ with $DB$. Finite-projective evaluation then gives $D_\psi P=P^\#\{t_ eta\}$.
