items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials are alternating sums of ordinary ones
items.statement: Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]. (1) (Antispherical alternating sum.) For all $x,y\in{^JW}$, $$n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}\,v^{\ell(z)}\,p_{zy,\,x},$$ the sum over all $z\in W_J$ (the product $zy$ taken in $S_n$, and $p_{\cdot,x}$ the ordinary coefficient of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], so the inner coefficients vanish unless $zy\le x$). (2) (Spherical reduction.) If $W_J$ is finite with longest element $w_0^J$ then for all $x,y\in{^JW}$ $$m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^J y,\ w_0^J x}.$$ In particular both families are computable from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, with no separate recursion.
items.strategy:
For antispherical reduction, Φ(underlineH_x) has coefficients
Σ_u(-v)^ℓu p_{uy,x}; every lower supported term has uy<x, since x,y are minimal
and in distinct cosets. Hence all lower coefficients lie in vZ[v] directly,
and uniqueness identifies this with D_x. For spherical reduction let
C_J=Σ_u∈WJ v^{ℓwJ−ℓu}H_u. Pairing u with us or su gives left/right H_s eigenvalue
v^-1. Bar preserves these equations and top coefficient1, so C_J is bar-fixed,
and ordinary KL uniqueness identifies it with underlineH_wJ. The map
1⊗h→C_Jh identifies M with the eigen-subspace C_JH. Ordinary underlineH_wJx
has these left eigenvalues by the ordinary KL descent multiplication formula.
Comparing top coefficients on C_JH_y gives exactly p_{wJ y,wJ x}; bar and
triangularity identify it with C_x. The ordinary coefficient degree bound then
gives parity ℓx−ℓy and exponent at most that length difference in both families;
for the antispherical formula ℓuy=ℓu+ℓy. Thus the shifted coefficients are
polynomials in q=v^-2. This well-definedness is proved by the reduction, not an
unstated parity clause of the existence theorem.

 The required coset order comparison is proved by subwords: if y<=x are minimal, prefix a fixed reduced wJ to a subword expression to get wJ y<=wJ x. Conversely a subword of wJ x with product wJ y splits into a J-word followed by a subword z of x. Parabolic projection sends that product and z to the same minimum y; length-additive factorization gives y<=z, and deletion reduces z within the x-subword, so z<=x. Thus y<=x iff wJ y<=wJ x, proving the triangular support of the spherical candidate. Right multiplication by global w0 reverses Bruhat covers because it sends length ell(a) to ell(w0)-ell(a) and keeps the same left reflection; hence it reverses the full order. This proves the order-reversing iota and k dictionaries used below, with no unproved label-mirror assertion.

items.title: Singular category O multiplicities are parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig values
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work in the type-$A$
root datum $W=S_n$ of the page's Hecke module and ordinary multiplicity
theorem. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]
with $J=J(\mu)$, so $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the singular integral block of
[[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]] with labels
normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $W^J$, and let $w_0$ be
the longest element of $W$. Then for all $y,w\in W^J$,
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=P_{yw_0,\,ww_0}(1),$$
the value at $q=1$ of the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial attached to the
pair $(yw_0,ww_0)$ in the classical normalization of
[[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].
Equivalently, put $k(w)=w_0^Jw^{-1}w_0\in{}^JW$. Then
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=m_{k(y),k(w)}(1).$$
This is the spherical family. The antispherical family instead governs the
genuine regular parabolic locally finite category with dominant labels;
changing to an opposite positive system does not identify the two families.
In particular all singular multiplicities are computable from the ordinary
Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, and no individual polynomial
coefficients beyond the value at one occur.
items.strategy:
Apply exact T to a composition series of the regular Delta(y dot lambda_anti). A regular simple contributes the singular L(w dot mu) only when its label lies in wW_J; among that coset the proved survival theorem keeps exactly the unique minimal right representative w. Thus this singular multiplicity equals the regular [Delta(y dot lambda_anti):L(w dot lambda_anti)]. Relative to the dominant base, the two regular labels are y w0 and w w0. Published ordinary BGG gives the projective-standard version. Therefore exact T and the regular KL theorem give [Δ(y·μ):L(w·μ)]=P_{yw0,ww0}(1) for
minimal right representatives y,w. To express this in the fixed LEFT spherical
module use k(w)=wJ w^-1 w0∈^J W. Its validity follows by reversing left descents
with w0 after changing minimum to maximum by wJ. Then
m_{k(y),k(w)}=p_{y^-1w0,w^-1w0}=p_{w0y,w0w}=p_{yw0,ww0}.
The first equality is spherical reduction, the second simultaneous inversion,
and the third longest-conjugation invariance: the Hecke automorphism
H_s→H_{w0 s w0} preserves bar and triangularity, so ordinary KL uniqueness proves
this symmetry. Thus singular blocks are spherical, not an antispherical mirror. Conjugation by w0 preserves the Hecke presentation, bar and Bruhat order; prove its KL-coefficient symmetry locally by uniqueness, then use inverse symmetry to justify the spherical dictionary k(w)=w_Jw^-1w0. Reconcile actual regular dominant-base suppliers before closure.

items.title: Parabolic category O multiplicities are parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig values
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a dominant regular
integral weight $\lambda$ of the complex type-$A$ Lie algebra and the standard
parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$, with reductive Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and longest
Levi Weyl element $w_J$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]). The
$\mathfrak p_J$-dominant weights in this regular block are exactly
$y\cdot\lambda$ for $y\in{}^JW$. Write
$\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=M_{\mathfrak p}(y\cdot\lambda)$,
$L(x\cdot\lambda)$ and $P^J(x\cdot\lambda)$ for its generalized standards,
simples and projective covers
([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]). Then for
$x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$[\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=(P^J(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}P_{uy,x}(1)=n_{y,x}(1).$$

These are the antispherical sign coefficients, with support $y\le x$ and
diagonal $1$. The precise character/Grothendieck identity supplying the
formula is
$$\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}\operatorname{ch}\Delta(uy\cdot\lambda).$$

For the same highest weights in the antidominant base
$\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, the actual longest-left label is
$z=yw_0$, since $y\cdot\lambda=z\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$.
Its shortest-left encoding is $a=\mathrm{lf}(y):=w_Jyw_0\in{}^JW$, so the
weight in that encoding is $(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$, not
$a\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. With $b=\mathrm{lf}(x)$, the reindexed matrix is
$$\widetilde N_{a,b}:=n_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}(1)=n_{w_Jaw_0,\,w_Jbw_0}(1).$$
It is the same multiplicity matrix with both indices permuted and has reversed
support in the transported order. It is not in general $n_{a,b}(1)$.
Every label retains its explicit dot-baseweight.
The highest-weight category theorem applies also to singular integral
parabolic blocks, but this ordinary regular KL matrix formula assumes the
ambient central character is regular. No singular/parabolic category
equivalence, grading or Koszul duality is asserted.
items.strategy: Retain the full finite-Levi Weyl/PBW signed character proof and ordinary antispherical multiplicities. Correct dominant label criterion by pairing lambda+rho with y^-1 alpha_j: it is no LEFT J descent. Actual antidominant longest-left label is z=yw0; shortest-left encoding a=w_Jz carries weight (w_Ja) dot lambda_anti. Reindex matrix by Ntilde_ab=n_{w_Jaw0,w_Jbw0}(1), not n_ab. All regular/general highest-weight and no-Koszul boundaries preserved.

items.title: The parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig character formula
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the dominant regular
integral conventions of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]]. Put
$N=(n_{y,x}(1))_{y,x\in{}^JW}$, with rows indexed by generalized standards and
columns by simples in a Bruhat-compatible order
([[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]). Then $N$ is upper
unitriangular and, for each $x$,
$$\operatorname{ch}L(x\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{y\ge x}(N^{-1})_{x,y}\,\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda).$$
Its inverse entries are integers computed by the finite signed chain sum of
products of $n_{a,b}(1)$; they are weighted incidence inverses, not generally
ordinary Bruhat Mobius values. In the antidominant base $\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, set
$a=\mathrm{lf}(y)=w_Jyw_0$ and encode the same weight as
$(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. The reindexed matrix is
$\widetilde N_{a,b}=N_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}$
and its inverse is reindexed by the same permutation; thus the same formula
has reversed support in the transported order. This does not replace the
entries by $n_{a,b}(1)$.
This is the ungraded
character formula for the regular parabolic block, and constructs no Koszul or
Ext grading.
items.strategy: Invert the unchanged ordinary antispherical multiplicity matrix N in its dominant shortest-left labels. Under shortest-left encoding a=lf(y) of longest-left anti-base label yw0, use weight (w_Ja) dot lambda_anti and conjugate N and N^-1 by the same permutation matrix. Do not substitute n_ab for reindexed entries. Retain signed-chain inverse and no-Koszul conclusions.

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials for S_3 modulo S_2
items.statement: Take $W=S_3$ with simple reflections $s_1,s_2$, let $J=\{s_1\}$, so $W_J=\{1,s_1\}$ and the minimal left coset representatives are ${^JW}=\{e,\ s_2,\ s_2s_1\}$. In the notation of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] the two parabolic families are computed from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_3$ (all ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of comparable pairs in $S_3$ equal $1$): the **antispherical (sign)** coefficients are $$n_{e,e}=1,\quad n_{e,s_2}=v,\quad n_{e,s_2s_1}=0,\quad n_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$ all other coefficients being zero; the **spherical** coefficients are $$m_{e,e}=1,\quad m_{e,s_2}=v,\quad m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2},\quad m_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$ all other coefficients being zero. At $v=1$ the antispherical matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and the spherical matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ in the order $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$. The two families therefore already differ for this smallest nontrivial parabolic: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=0$ while $m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$.
items.strategy: Finite computation inside $H_v(3)$. The ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_3$ are known from [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] and the fact that all ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials of $S_3$ equal $1$: $p_{y,x}=v^{\ell(x)-\ell(y)}$ for $y\le x$ and zero otherwise, so the only nonzero values needed are $p_{e,e}=1$, $p_{e,s_1}=p_{e,s_2}=v$, $p_{e,s_1s_2}=p_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$, $p_{e,w_0}=v^{3}$, $p_{s_1,s_1s_2}=p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v$, $p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$, $p_{s_2,s_1s_2}=p_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v$, $p_{s_2,w_0}=v^{2}$, $p_{s_1s_2,w_0}=p_{s_2s_1,w_0}=v$, and the diagonal ones $1$. The antispherical coefficients are the alternating sums $n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{zy,x}$ of [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]. For $y=e$: $n_{e,e}=p_{e,e}=1$, $n_{e,s_2}=p_{e,s_2}=v$, and $n_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v\cdot v=0$. For $y=s_2$: $n_{s_2,s_2}=p_{s_2,s_2}-v\,p_{s_1s_2,s_2}=1$ (the second term vanishes since $\ell(s_1s_2)>\ell(s_2)$), and $n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=p_{s_2,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1s_2,s_2s_1}=v-0=v$, the second term vanishing because $s_1s_2$ and $s_2s_1$ are distinct of equal length. For $y=s_2s_1$: $n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=p_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{w_0,s_2s_1}=1-0=1$, the second term vanishing by the support condition. The spherical coefficients are $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ with $w_0^J=s_1$ ([[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]): $m_{e,e}=p_{s_1,s_1}=1$, $m_{e,s_2}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2}=v$, $m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$, $m_{s_2,s_2}=p_{s_1s_2,s_1s_2}=1$, $m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1s_2,w_0}=v$, $m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=p_{w_0,w_0}=1$. All arithmetic is in $\mathbb Z[v]$ with the Bruhat comparabilities of $S_3$ ([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]]); the coset set is ${^JW}=\{e,s_2,s_2s_1\}$ ([[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]). An independent construction of the two canonical bases in the normalized Hecke algebra of $S_3$, from the bar involution and the induced-module standard bases, reproduces both tables.

items.title: Spherical and antispherical normalizations give different polynomials
items.statement: For $W=S_3$ and $J=\{s_1\}$ the spherical and antispherical parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] are not the same, and not merely by a unit: for the pair $y=e$, $x=s_2s_1\in{^JW}$ one has $$n_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v^{2}=0\neq m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2},$$ evaluated at $v=1$: the antispherical value vanishes while the spherical value is $1$. The value $n_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=0$ is not a unit multiple of $m_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=1$, and the two coefficients differ as polynomials, so the discrepancy is not an artifact of specializing at $v=1$. Consequently the two normalizations cannot be substituted for one another in a multiplicity statement: a singular-block or parabolic multiplicity theorem must fix the side of the parabolic and the corresponding module (trivial versus sign). In particular the singular-block multiplicity theorem of this page is stated in the spherical normalization whereas genuine regular parabolic locally-finite category O uses the antispherical family with the explicit dominant-base labels, so using the antispherical value $n_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=0$ in place of the spherical $m_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=1$ produces a false multiplicity.
items.strategy: Two-term computation in the Hecke algebra of $S_3$, using the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients $p_{r,s}=v^{\ell(s)-\ell(r)}$ for comparable pairs and zero otherwise. Antispherical: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=\sum_{z\in\{1,s_1\}}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{z,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}$ by [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]; here $p_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$ and $s_1\le s_2s_1$ with length gap one, so $p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v$ and $n_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v^{2}=0$. Spherical: $m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$ by the reduction $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ with $w_0^J=s_1$. The coset set and Bruhat relations are those of [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]] and [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]; the values were checked by an independent construction of the two canonical bases in the normalized Hecke algebra of $S_3$ via the triangular construction of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. The conclusion is a counterexample to any normalization-blind statement of the parabolic multiplicity theorem, not to the theorems themselves.

items.title: Translation to a singular wall in type A_2
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and use the coordinate
$l=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$, so the dot action is $s\cdot l=-l-2$
and the facets are $(-\infty,-1)$, $\{-1\}$, $(-1,\infty)$
([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]], Example 3.11 of
the source). Take $\lambda=-2$, $\mu=-1$. Then the singular block
$\mathcal O_{-1}$ has the single simple $L(-1)=M(-1)=P(-1)$, and the
translation functor $T=T_{-2}^{-1}$ satisfies $TM(-2)=M(-1)$, $TM(0)=M(-1)$,
$$TL(-2)=L(-1)\quad(\text{the label }1\in W^J),\qquad TL(0)=0\quad(\text{the label }s\notin W^J),$$
and $TP(-2)=2\,P(-1)$, because the projective cover $P(-2)$ of $L(-2)$ has
the Verma flag $\Delta(-2),\Delta(0)$ and both factors are sent to
$\Delta(-1)$.

For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$ take $J=\{s_1\}$ and the dot-antidominant
$\mu$ with $\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$; then $W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$ and by
[[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] the
composition and Verma-flag matrices of the singular block are
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$$
in the row/column order $(1,\,s_2,\,s_1s_2)$: explicitly $M(\mu)$ is
irreducible, $M(s_2\cdot\mu)$ has composition factors $L(\mu),L(s_2\cdot\mu)$
once each, and $M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has all three simples once; dually
$(P(\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for all three $y$,
$(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_2\cdot\mu))=(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu))=1$,
with its $\Delta(\mu)$ multiplicity zero, and
$P(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has the single top-label standard.
The surviving
simple labels are exactly the minimal coset representatives, so translation
onto the wall kills $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\notin W^J$ (for instance
$L(s_1\cdot\lambda)$ and $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ case).
items.strategy: Retain exact sl2 wall translation and sl3 LOWER composition matrix. Since yw0<=ww0 iff y>=w, read projective flags from columns of that lower matrix: P(mu) has all3 standards, middle projective has last2, highest projective has only itself. Preserve all simple factor/wall survivor computations.

items.title: A small parabolic category O character formula
items.statement:
For $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, $\lambda=0$, $J=\{s_1\}$, the genuine regular parabolic
category has minimal-left labels $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$, with highest weights
$0,-\alpha_2,-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2$. Its generalized-standard/simple matrix is
$$N=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad N^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&1\\0&1&-1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Thus
$$\operatorname{ch}L(0)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(0)-\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_2)+\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2),$$
$\operatorname{ch}L(-\alpha_2)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_2)-\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)$,
and $\operatorname{ch}L(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)$.

For comparison retain the singular antidominant block with
$\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$ and right-minimal labels $(e,s_2,s_1s_2)$: its
composition matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$ has
inverse
$\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-1&1&0\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}$, giving
$\operatorname{ch}L(\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(\mu)$,
$\operatorname{ch}L(s_2\cdot\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(s_2\cdot\mu)-\operatorname{ch}M(\mu)$,
and
$\operatorname{ch}L(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)-\operatorname{ch}M(s_2\cdot\mu)$.
The latter coefficients are Mobius values in this all-one singular chain only.
The two blocks exemplify distinct spherical and antispherical formulas; the
singular example is not the generalized-Verma character formula of the
parabolic category.
items.strategy: The preceding finite Hecke example gives the antispherical N. The generalized standard highest weights follow from the dot action of s2 and s2s1 on0 and are J-dominant. Apply the repaired regular-parabolic multiplicity theorem and invert its upper matrix explicitly; both matrix products with the displayed inverse are identities. The actual finite Levi identity reads ch Delta^J(y dot0)=ch Delta(y dot0)-ch Delta(s1 y dot0) since W_J={e,s1}. Expanding ordinary S3 KL values therefore supplies N independently. Apply the repaired row-x parabolic character formula. Separately preserve the true singular composition matrix of the wall example and its explicit lower inverse; the corrected spherical k dictionary gives that matrix, and ordinary inversion supplies those singular character identities. Its all-one chain specialization is Mobius; it is not a claim that all inverse-KL matrices are ordinary Mobius. No singular/parabolic equivalence or grading is used. The singular lower matrix has entry one exactly for y>=w, not y<=w; preserve both displayed matrices and character identities.

items.title: Standard- and costandard-filtered objects and tilting objects
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite split highest-weight central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, the labels and structural objects above, and its finite-dimensional basic block algebra $A$, whose finite-dimensional left modules model $\mathcal C$.

[F1] Highest-weight structure ([[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]): finite labels and length, finite-dimensional Hom, standard support $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\mu]\ne0\Rightarrow\mu\preceq\lambda$, diagonal multiplicity one, projective covers, standard-kernel sequences with strictly higher flags, BGG reciprocity, and $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0$ inside the parabolic category.

[F2] The flag terminology agrees with the ordinary category-$\mathcal O$ terminology ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], [[cor-injectives-have-costandard-filtrations]], [[thm-every-category-o-object-has-finite-length]]). The argument here uses the actual generalized-standard structure in [F1].

[F3] Restricted BGG duality ([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]) restricts to an exact contravariant involution of this summand, fixes simples and sends $\Delta_\lambda$ to $\nabla_\lambda$ and $P_\lambda$ to $I_\lambda$.

[F4] In the split basic algebra model, primitive idempotents $e_\lambda$ give $P_\lambda=Ae_\lambda$ and $\dim e_\lambda N=[N:L_\lambda]$. A projective generator is the finite sum of the projective covers; its endomorphism algebra is finite dimensional by [F1]. All modules and multiplicity spaces used below are finite dimensional over $\mathbb C$.

[F5] The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is available when choosing bases, lifts, projective resolutions and injective cogenerators; no stronger field or nonsplit division-algebra assertion is made.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Flags, duality and the injective sequence.** Finite sums have flags by concatenation. Given $0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ with $X,Z$ standard-filtered, pull a flag of $Z$ back to $Y$ and precede it with the flag of $X$; this gives a standard flag of $Y$. Duality proves both claims for costandard flags and exchanges the two flag categories. Dualizing $0\to K_\lambda\to P_\lambda\to\Delta_\lambda\to0$ gives precisely $0\to\nabla_\lambda\to I_\lambda\to DK_\lambda\to0$, whose cokernel is costandard-filtered by labels strictly above $\lambda$. In particular this construction does not identify a general costandard with an injective envelope. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 **All positive standard-costandard Ext groups.** The degree-one vanishing is [F1]. Suppose vanishing holds in degree $j-1$ for every pair of structural labels, where $j\ge2$. A finite standard flag of $K_\lambda$ and its long exact sequences give $\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}(K_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0$. The projective sequence then gives $\operatorname{Ext}^{j}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}(K_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0$. Induction proves all positive degrees. Filtering the first variable now shows $\operatorname{Ext}^{j}(N,\nabla_\mu)=0$ for any standard-filtered $N$; filtering the second variable gives the dual statement for costandard-filtered objects, and also vanishing between any standard-filtered and costandard-filtered pair. [F1, step 1.1, induction]

2.2 **The maximal trace.** Choose a maximal label $\eta$ and put $e=e_\eta$. Since the standard-kernel sequence has no higher labels, $Ae=P_\eta=\Delta_\eta$. Every other standard is killed by $e$, while $\dim e\Delta_\eta=1$. An endomorphism of $\Delta_\eta$ is determined by its action on the generating top space, so $eAe=\operatorname{End}_A(Ae)^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathbb C$. For a standard-filtered $X$, the evaluation map $Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eX\to X$ is injective and its quotient is standard-filtered with no $\eta$ section. To prove this, induct on a chosen flag. If its last section is $\Delta_\eta$, the section splits off because $\Delta_\eta$ is projective. If its last section is another $\Delta_\lambda$, it is killed by $e$, so $eX=eX'$ for the preceding flag subobject $X'$ and the trace lies in $X'$; the induction quotient extends by $\Delta_\lambda$. This proves the claim in both cases, including identification with the canonical trace generated by $eX$. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.1, induction]

3.1 **Multiplicity formulas.** For $0\to N'\to N\to\Delta_\lambda\to0$ with $N'$ standard-filtered, applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,\nabla_\mu)$ and step 2.1 gives a short exact sequence of Hom spaces. Its dimension adds one precisely for $\lambda=\mu$. Inducting along a flag proves $(N:\Delta_\mu)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\mu)$ and independence of the flag. Duality gives $(M:\nabla_\mu)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\mu,M)$ for costandard-filtered $M$. [F1, F3, step 2.1, induction]

3.2 **The genuine heredity ideal.** Apply step 2.2 to each projective column $Ae_\lambda$ and sum the columns. The resulting injective evaluation map is multiplication $Ae\otimes_{eAe}eA\to A$, with image $J=AeA$. Thus $J\cong Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eA$, rather than $J=Ae$. It is projective on both sides: on the left it is a finite sum of $Ae$, and on the right a finite sum of $eA$. Moreover $e\operatorname{rad}(A)e=0$ since $eAe=\mathbb C$, so $J$ is a heredity ideal. Put $A'=A/J$. The finite $A'$-modules are exactly the $A$-modules killed by $e$, hence the Serre subcategory on $\Lambda\setminus\{\eta\}$. Its projective covers for $\lambda\ne\eta$ are $A'e_\lambda=Ae_\lambda/J e_\lambda$. By step 2.2 these have standard flags with all $\eta$ sections removed. The sequence onto $\Delta_\lambda$ has kernel $K_\lambda/J e_\lambda$: the trace $J e_\lambda$ lies in $K_\lambda$ because $e\Delta_\lambda=0$, and applying step 2.2 to $K_\lambda$ gives the required standard flag with the remaining strictly higher labels. Its simple top is still $L_\lambda$, so it is indeed the projective cover. Consequently $A'$ has the smaller highest-weight structure with unchanged standards $\Delta_\lambda$. Duality preserves this Serre subcategory and gives its injective envelopes and unchanged costandards $\nabla_\lambda$. Every injective $A'$-module is therefore costandard-filtered by these smaller labels. This establishes the quotient data needed for induction, without assuming the converse flag criterion. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.3 **Normalized tilting uniqueness.** Suppose $X,X'$ are indecomposable tiltings with normalized inclusions $i:\Delta_\lambda\to X$ and $i':\Delta_\lambda\to X'$. Their cokernels are standard-filtered, so step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{Ext}^1(X/\Delta_\lambda,X')=0$. The Hom exact sequence extends $i'$ to $f:X\to X'$ with $fi=i'$; symmetrically obtain $g:X'\to X$ with $gi'=i$. Then $gf$ and $fg$ restrict to the identity on the common nonzero standard, and no positive power of either is zero. In a finite-dimensional endomorphism algebra of an indecomposable finite-length object, Fitting's decomposition makes every noninvertible endomorphism nilpotent. Hence both composites are invertible and $f$ is an isomorphism. The support of $\Delta_\lambda$ and of the lower-labelled quotient shows that $\lambda$ is the unique maximal support label. No existence or tilting classification was used in the flag-criterion argument. [F1, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Ext1 implies every positive Ext degree.** Suppose $N$ satisfies $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0$ for every label. Finite flags show $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(N,C)=0$ for every costandard-filtered $C$. More generally, if the groups vanish in degree $j-1$ against all costandards, they vanish in that degree against every costandard-filtered object. Apply this to $C_\lambda$ in the actual sequence $0\to\nabla_\lambda\to I_\lambda\to C_\lambda\to0$ from step 1.1. Since $I_\lambda$ is injective, for $j\ge2$ dimension shifting gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,\nabla_\lambda)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}_A(N,C_\lambda)=0$. Induction establishes all positive Ext vanishing, and filtering establishes $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,I')=0$ for every $j>0$ and every injective $A'$-module $I'$ from step 3.2, viewed as an $A$-module. [step 1.1, step 3.2, induction]

5.1 **Tor vanishing detected by injectives.** Choose a projective resolution $P_\bullet\to N$ by finite-dimensional projective $A$-modules. Each $A'\otimes_A P_i$ is projective over $A'$. For an injective $A'$-module $I'$, tensor-Hom adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet,I')$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P_\bullet,I')$. The latter has zero cohomology in every positive degree by step 4.1. Because $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(-,I')$ is exact, the degree-$j$ cohomology of the former is $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(H_j(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet),I')$. Injectives detect nonzero finite-dimensional $A'$-modules: embed the semisimple socle of a finite module in a finite sum of the injective envelopes of the simples and extend the map by injectivity. Its kernel is zero because any nonzero finite-length submodule intersects that socle. Thus the full module embeds in such an injective cogenerator. It follows that $H_j(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet)=\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(A',N)=0$ for every $j>0$. This uses actual homology detection, not an assumed exactness of tensoring. [F4, F5, step 3.2, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **The trace exact sequence and quotient induction.** Tensor $0\to J\to A\to A'\to0$ with $N$. By step 5.1 its Tor boundary vanishes, and step 3.2 identifies the result as $0\to Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eN\to N\to E\to0$, where $E=A'\otimes_A N$. The kernel is a finite sum of $\Delta_\eta$. Moreover $A'\otimes_A P_\bullet$ is a projective resolution of $E$ by step 5.1, and adjunction now gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_{A'}(E,\nabla_\lambda)=\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0$ for $j>0$, $\lambda\ne\eta$. Induct on the number of labels, using the smaller highest-weight category constructed in step 3.2: $E$ is standard-filtered by the smaller labels. The base with no labels is the zero category; with one label the trace sequence itself is $N\cong\Delta_\eta\otimes eN$. Extension closure now makes $N$ standard-filtered. Together with steps 2.1 and 4.1 this proves both displayed standard-flag criteria, using either degree-one or all-positive-Ext vanishing. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, induction]

7.1 **The dual criterion and direct summands.** Exact contravariant duality gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(\Delta_\lambda,M)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(DM,\nabla_\lambda)$ by reversing Yoneda extensions (and likewise in all degrees). The criterion for $DM$ in step 6.1 therefore gives the two costandard-flag criteria for $M$. If a flagged object is a finite direct sum, Ext groups of each summand are direct summands of its vanishing groups. The appropriate criterion shows every summand has the same kind of flag. Thus both flag categories, and their intersection of tilting objects, have all the stated closure properties. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 **Lower ideals.** Let $X$ be a normalized tilting object at $\lambda$, and let $\Gamma$ be a lower ideal containing $\lambda$. Every composition label of $X$ lies below $\lambda$, so $X$ belongs to its Serre subcategory. Its standard flag uses labels in $\Gamma$; every costandard occurring in its costandard flag also has its own labelled simple as a composition factor of $X$, hence has label in $\Gamma$. These are the same standards and costandards in the truncated highest-weight category: iteratively removing maximal labels outside $\Gamma$ uses step 3.2. Thus $X$ remains the same normalized tilting there, and uniqueness follows from step 3.3. The closure, duality, multiplicity and full homological-criterion assertions have been established locally, including the genuine injective and heredity-ideal interfaces. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 3.3] ∎

items.title: The Fock-space convention dictionary for finite type-A quantum modules
items.statement:
Throughout this pair the **source parameter** of the Fock-space literature is
written $s$ and the **library parameter** of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] is written $t$; the
dictionary below sets $t=s^{-1}$.

Let $I$ be a nonempty consecutive set of simple-root indices and put $I^+=I\cup(I+1)$, the coordinate alphabet. On a finite coordinate interval $J=[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ the roots have indices $[k,r-1]$, the coordinate weight lattice is $\bigoplus_{a=k}^r\mathbb Z\delta_a$, $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$ and $h_a=e_a-e_{a+1}$. The full central coordinate is retained. The source algebra $U_s$ has toral generators $D_a^{\pm1}$ for $a\in J$ and root generators $E_a,F_a$ for $k\le a<r$, acting on natural vectors $v_b$, $b\in J$, by

$$D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b,\qquad E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}\,v_a,\qquad F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}\,v_{a+1},$$

$$\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1},\qquad \Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a .$$

The library parameter $t$ is identified with $s^{-1}$; the **semilinear Hopf
dictionary** is the coefficient map $t\mapsto s^{-1}$ together with the
generator assignment

$$E_a\longmapsto E_a,\qquad F_a\longmapsto F_a,\qquad K_h\longmapsto D_{-h},$$

where the $E_a,F_a$ on the source side are the *divided* generators of the
source normalization and on the library side those of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] (the assignments agree on the
undivided generators $E_a=E_a^{(1)}$, $F_a=F_a^{(1)}$, and divided powers are
carried to divided powers because the quantum integers are invariant under
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
Root-label weights are preserved, while toral numerical eigenvalues use the
reciprocal parameter: on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the library generator
$K_h$ acts by $t^{\mu(h)}=s^{-\mu(h)}$, which is the action of $D_{-h}$ because
$(-h)(\mu)=-\mu(h)$.

The **bar involution** sends $s\mapsto s^{-1}$, fixes $E_a$ and $F_a$ and
inverts each $D_a$; the corresponding library operation is the involution with
$t\mapsto t^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$ and
$K_h\mapsto K_h^{-1}$ of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]
and [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].

The **natural highest weight** attached to an interval $[k,r]$ is
$\delta_k=\varepsilon_k$ (equivalently the highest weight reached by the
leading coordinate vector $v_k$), its **dual highest weight** is
$-\delta_r$, and the **fundamental wedge weight** is
$\delta_k+\delta_{k+1}+\cdots+\delta_m$ for $k\le m\le r$. Every fundamental
factor carries its own highest-vector-normalized bar, integral lattice and
divided-string crystal charts ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]);
its internal antisymmetrizer embedding is primitive and integral but is *not*
asserted to be based in the library's raw lower $q_0$ chart. Infinite intervals
are defined by the compatible system of their finite subintervals, and
[[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]] with
[[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] supplies
the library integrable modules used on each finite interval.

The source Fock families $L,T,P$ and the library form-dual upper family
([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]) will
be compared below through their actual forms; they are never identified by
their names.

## Definition

Throughout this pair the **source parameter** of the Fock-space literature is
written $s$ and the **library parameter** of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] is written $t$; the
dictionary below sets $t=s^{-1}$.

Let $I$ be a nonempty consecutive set of simple-root indices and put $I^+=I\cup(I+1)$, the coordinate alphabet. On a finite coordinate interval $J=[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ the roots have indices $[k,r-1]$, the coordinate weight lattice is $\bigoplus_{a=k}^r\mathbb Z\delta_a$, $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$ and $h_a=e_a-e_{a+1}$. The full central coordinate is retained. The source algebra $U_s$ has toral generators $D_a^{\pm1}$ for $a\in J$ and root generators $E_a,F_a$ for $k\le a<r$, acting on natural vectors $v_b$, $b\in J$, by

$$D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b,\qquad E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}\,v_a,\qquad F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}\,v_{a+1},$$

$$\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1},\qquad \Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a .$$

The library parameter $t$ is identified with $s^{-1}$; the **semilinear Hopf
dictionary** is the coefficient map $t\mapsto s^{-1}$ together with the
generator assignment

$$E_a\longmapsto E_a,\qquad F_a\longmapsto F_a,\qquad K_h\longmapsto D_{-h},$$

where the $E_a,F_a$ on the source side are the *divided* generators of the
source normalization and on the library side those of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] (the assignments agree on the
undivided generators $E_a=E_a^{(1)}$, $F_a=F_a^{(1)}$, and divided powers are
carried to divided powers because the quantum integers are invariant under
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
Root-label weights are preserved, while toral numerical eigenvalues use the
reciprocal parameter: on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the library generator
$K_h$ acts by $t^{\mu(h)}=s^{-\mu(h)}$, which is the action of $D_{-h}$ because
$(-h)(\mu)=-\mu(h)$.

The **bar involution** sends $s\mapsto s^{-1}$, fixes $E_a$ and $F_a$ and
inverts each $D_a$; the corresponding library operation is the involution with
$t\mapsto t^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$ and
$K_h\mapsto K_h^{-1}$ of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]
and [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].

The **natural highest weight** attached to an interval $[k,r]$ is
$\delta_k=\varepsilon_k$ (equivalently the highest weight reached by the
leading coordinate vector $v_k$), its **dual highest weight** is
$-\delta_r$, and the **fundamental wedge weight** is
$\delta_k+\delta_{k+1}+\cdots+\delta_m$ for $k\le m\le r$. Every fundamental
factor carries its own highest-vector-normalized bar, integral lattice and
divided-string crystal charts ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]);
its internal antisymmetrizer embedding is primitive and integral but is *not*
asserted to be based in the library's raw lower $q_0$ chart. Infinite intervals
are defined by the compatible system of their finite subintervals, and
[[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]] with
[[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] supplies
the library integrable modules used on each finite interval.

The source Fock families $L,T,P$ and the library form-dual upper family
([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]) will
be compared below through their actual forms; they are never identified by
their names.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The type-$A$ root datum with full coordinate weight lattice, a finite interval $[k,r]\subseteq I^+$, the source generators $D_a,E_a,F_a$ with the displayed action and comultiplication, and the library algebra with its generators $E_a,F_a,K_h$ and parameter $t$.

[F1] Library presentation and toral action ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]): $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$, $K_0=1$, $K_hE_aK_h^{-1}=q^{\langle\alpha_a,h\rangle}E_a$, $K_hF_aK_h^{-1}=q^{-\langle\alpha_a,h\rangle}F_a$, and on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the element $K_h$ acts by $q^{\mu(h)}$; the $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra is generated by the $E_a,F_a,K_h$.

[F2] Quantum integers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]): $[m]_q=(q^m-q^{-m})/(q-q^{-1})$ is invariant under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$; the divided power is $x^{(m)}=x^m/[m]_{q_a}!$.

[F3] Library form and bar ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]], [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]): the bar involution is the semilinear endomorphism with $t\mapsto t^{-1}$ fixing the divided generators and inverting $K_h$; integrable highest-weight modules, their normalized highest vectors, bars and lattices are available on finite intervals.

[F4] Existence and uniqueness of integrable highest-weight modules ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]) on the finite-interval subdatum.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** Check the dictionary on generators and relations and conclude it is a well-defined semilinear Hopf identification on each finite interval.

1.1 **Toral relations.** Under $t\mapsto s^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto D_{-h}$, the library relation $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ becomes $D_{-(h+h')}=D_{-h}D_{-h'}$, and $K_0=1$ becomes $D_0=1$; these are the source toral relations. Toral elements commute in both presentations, so $\varphi$ is well defined on the toral subalgebra $\mathbb Q(t)[P^\vee]\to\mathbb Q(s)[\mathbb Z J]$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 **Mixed relations.** The library relation $K_hE_aK_h^{-1}=t^{\langle\alpha_a,h\rangle}E_a$ becomes, after $t\mapsto s^{-1}$, $D_{-h}E_aD_{-h}^{-1}=s^{-\langle\alpha_a,h\rangle}E_a$, and interchanging $h$ and $-h$ this is the source relation $D_{h'}E_aD_{h'}^{-1}=s^{\langle\alpha_a,h'\rangle}E_a$; the $F_a$-relation is the sign-reversed mirror. This matches the displayed action $D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b$ because $\langle\alpha_b,e_a\rangle=\delta_{ab}-\delta_{a,b+1}$; pairing with $h_a=e_a-e_{a+1}$ gives the type-$A$ Cartan matrix. [F1, algebra]

1.3 **The $E$-$F$ commutator.** The library relation $E_aF_b-F_bE_a=\delta_{ab}(K_a-K_a^{-1})/(t_a-t_a^{-1})$ maps to $\delta_{ab}(D_{-a}-D_a)/(s^{-1}_a-s_a)$ where $D_{\pm a}:=D_{\pm d_a h_a}$; both numerator and denominator change sign under the substitution, so the fraction is unchanged and equals the source relation $\delta_{ab}(D_a-D_a^{-1})/(s_a-s_a^{-1})$ after relabelling. No divided generator is modified, as asserted. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.4 **Serre relations.** The Gaussian binomials and the divided powers $E_a^{(m)}=E_a^m/[m]_{q_a}!$ are unchanged as elements under $q_a\mapsto q_a^{-1}$ by [F2]; hence each positive and negative quantum Serre element of the library presentation maps to the corresponding source Serre element, since only the divided powers and the binomial coefficients occur. [F2, algebra]

1.5 **Comultiplication.** Since $K_a$ maps to $D_{-h_a}=D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}$, its inverse maps to $D_{h_a}=D_aD_{a+1}^{-1}$. Thus the library formulas map to $\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1}$ and $\Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a$, exactly the source coproduct. The counit and antipode agree on these generators and hence on the generated algebra. [F1, algebra]

1.6 **Bar involution.** On the source side bar fixes $E_a,F_a$ and inverts $D_a$, hence it sends $D_{-h}\mapsto D_h=D_{-h}^{-1}$; on the library side bar fixes the divided generators and inverts $K_h$. Under the dictionary the two involutions intertwine, and both conjugate the parameter. Consequently bar commutes with the dictionary on the generating set and hence on the generated algebra. [F3, algebra]

1.7 **Weights and labels.** A weight vector of weight $\mu=\sum_a m_a\varepsilon_a$ is an eigenvector of $K_h$ with eigenvalue $t^{\mu(h)}=s^{-\mu(h)}$, which equals the eigenvalue of $D_{-h}$; hence root-label weights are preserved while the toral eigenvalues use the reciprocal parameter, as asserted. In particular $\delta_k=\varepsilon_k$ and $-\delta_r$ are genuine coordinate characters, and the fundamental wedge carries $\delta_k+\cdots+\delta_m$; the central coordinate $\delta_k+\cdots+\delta_r$ is retained. [F1, algebra]

2.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1-1.6 show that the generator assignment preserves every family of defining relations and the Hopf operations on each finite interval, so it extends uniquely to a semilinear Hopf-algebra map $\varphi:U_t\to U_s$ with $t\mapsto s^{-1}$, and symmetrically for the inverse; it is an isomorphism on the subalgebra generated by the finitely many $D_a^{\pm1},E_a,F_a$ with coordinate indices $k\le a\le r$ and root indices $k\le a<r$. Infinite intervals are covered by the compatible finite subintervals, and the library integrable modules and lattices of [F3], [F4] are transported by $\varphi$ on each of them. The comparison of the Fock families through their actual forms, not their names, is carried out in the following items. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 1.5, step 1.6, step 1.7] ∎

items.title: The higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module
items.statement:
Work with the type-$A$ coordinate lattice and the dictionary of
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]];
weights are written in the coordinates $\delta_a=\varepsilon_a$.

Fix a set $I$ of consecutive residues (for the finite box model
$I=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-2\}$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-1\}$; $I$ may be
unbounded below or above), a positive **level** $l$, and
$$\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+,\qquad m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_l,$$
where $m_j\in I^+$ and, if $I$ has lower endpoint $k$, $\Lambda_m=\sum_{k\le a\le m}\delta_a$. When $I$ is unbounded below, $\Lambda_m$ is the ground semi-infinite fundamental weight with the finite-coordinate-difference interpretation below. For $I$ bounded below put
$n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_j n_j$; for $I$ unbounded
below use semi-infinite columns with a common finite tail below, as explained
after the weight definition.

The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is
$$F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_2})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l}),$$
the tensor product of the fundamental modules of the dictionary item. When $I$
is bounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the fundamental integrable highest
weight module of highest weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ in the library algebra. When
$I$ is unbounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge
$\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with $V$ the natural module for the locally finite
type-$A$ algebra on $I$; its basis is the set of normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$ with $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ and the tail
$i_k=m_j+1-k$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ — the columns
$1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$, with rows indexed by $I^+$ — with entries in
$I^+$; it is **column-strict** if in each column the entries strictly increase
from bottom to top and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and
**standard** if in addition the entries weakly increase from left to right in
each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, respectively $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$,
for the sets of column-strict, respectively standard $\Lambda$-tableaux, and
$A_\Lambda$ for the **ground-state tableau** with row $i$ filled entirely
with $i$.

For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ the **column monomial** is
$$M_A:=\left(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots\right)\otimes\cdots\otimes\left(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots\right),$$
with each wedge normally ordered (the entries strictly decrease from top to
bottom inside a column), and
$$\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)},\qquad \mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A),\qquad \mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$$
for $\alpha\in Q^+$. When a column is semi-infinite, the displayed sum means
its ground fundamental weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ plus the finite sum of the
coordinate differences $\delta_{A(i,j)}-\delta_i$ over the finitely many
positions where $A$ differs from the ground state, evaluated on each
finite-support coroot or torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is
asserted.

The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is defined by $A\le B$ iff
$\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and
$\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$
in the dominance order of [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]] for every
$j<l$; then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$
in columns $i<j$. The column reading of a tableau (list the columns from left
to right, each column read top to bottom) gives the passage to partitions and
to the Young-diagram conventions of
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]; the removable- and
addable-node notation of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]
is used for the box moves of a tableau.

The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is called the **vacuum vector**. Weight
bookkeeping, the uniqueness of the monomial of weight $\Lambda$ and the
bijectivity of the column reading are verified below; the column-monomial theorem records the full integral tensor-basis statement. The well-definedness verification here constructs each fundamental factor explicitly without treating a citation to integrability as a wedge-basis theorem.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The coordinate lattice and dictionary of [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]], a level $l$ and a dominant weight $\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}$ with $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$; the sets $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda,\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ with the ground tableau $A_\Lambda$, the monomials $M_A$, the weights $\mathrm{wt}_j$ and $\mathrm{wt}$, and the Bruhat order of the Definition.

[F1] Dictionary and coordinate weights ([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]): the weight lattice is $\bigoplus_{a\in I^+}\mathbb Z\delta_a$ with the full central coordinate, the natural highest weight of the fundamental factor is $\delta_k$, the dual highest weight is $-\delta_r$, and the fundamental wedge carries $\delta_k+\cdots+\delta_m$.

[F2] Partitions and dominance ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]], [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[lem-conjugation-reverses-dominance]]): dominance $\unrhd$ on partitions of a fixed integer is the termwise dominance of prefix sums, and conjugation reverses it.

[F3] Tableau conventions ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]], [[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]], [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]): standard and semistandard tableaux, shapes and removable/addable nodes in the Young-diagram normalization.

[F4] The dictionary supplies the natural representation and its Hopf action, and the existence and uniqueness of its integrable highest-weight quotients. The elementary ordered-wedge construction is proved in step 1.1, not imported from the definition of integrability.

## Verification

1.1 **Elementary fundamental modules.** On a finite coordinate interval $[k,r]$ let $W_n$ have vectors $w_S$ indexed by $n$-element subsets $S$. Put $D_aw_S=s^{\mathbf1_{a\in S}}w_S$, and let $E_a$ replace $a+1\in S$ by $a\notin S$, while $F_a$ makes the opposite replacement, both with coefficient one and zero otherwise. The toral relations follow from the changed coordinate; $[E_a,F_a]$ is $1$, $-1$ or zero on the three possible $a,a+1$ occupation patterns, exactly the toral fraction. Different-root mixed commutators vanish by the same replacement test. Distant replacements commute; for adjacent roots $E_a^2=F_a^2=0$ and $E_aE_bE_a=F_aF_bF_a=0$, since the last replacement encounters the already occupied endpoint. These are the adjacent Serre relations. Distinct subset weights are separated by the toral operators, and successive raising replacements take any subset to $\{k,\ldots,k+n-1\}$; lowering generates every subset from it. Thus this module is integrable and irreducible, of highest weight $\Lambda_{k+n-1}$, and is the fundamental module in the dictionary. The ordered wedge symbol denotes this model; the primitive antisymmetrizer realizes it integrally, without any assertion that the raw tensor lower chart makes that embedding based. [F1, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 **Root rows and physical rows.** In column $j$ the root row runs from $k$ to $m_j$, whereas its physical height is $n_j=m_j+1-k$. The monomial therefore starts at $A(m_j,j)$ and descends through $A(m_j-1,j),\ldots,A(k,j)$. Its entries are strictly decreasing in that order and define a nonzero $w_S$ from step 1.1. Physical row $h$ means root row $k+h-1$; its row length is $\#\{j:n_j\ge h\}$. Hence the ordinary partition diagram is the conjugate of $(n_1,\ldots,n_l)$, not of the possibly negative multicharge. Column reading is a bijection to tuples of strictly decreasing entry blocks of these fixed lengths; the standard row inequalities are the corresponding semistandard inequalities. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **Weights and the vacuum.** The toral formula in step 1.1 gives precisely $\mathrm{wt}_j(A)$ and their sum on the tensor monomial. The ground column is $\{k,\ldots,m_j\}$, with weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$. Every other column weight differs from its ground by a nonzero element of the positive root cone: repeatedly raise its subset to the initial segment, decreasing its weight difference by a simple root at every step. The tensor top weight can therefore occur only when every factor is its ground vector. Its weight space is one-dimensional, spanned by $v_\Lambda$. This argument uses the explicit finite factor construction, not a yet unproved global-basis inclusion. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

3.2 **The prefix order.** Use root dominance: a weight difference is nonnegative when it is a nonnegative integral combination of $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$; on fixed-total-coordinate weights this agrees with the usual coordinate prefix criterion. Reflexivity and transitivity are immediate; equality of every factor-prefix weight forces equality of each column subset, hence of the column-strict tableaux, proving antisymmetry. If $A$ has $a$ in an earlier column $i$ and $b>a$ in a later column $j$, and $B$ swaps them, the prefix difference $\mathrm{wt}_{\le u}(A)-\mathrm{wt}_{\le u}(B)$ is $\delta_a-\delta_b=\sum_{v=a}^{b-1}\alpha_v$ for $i\le u<j$ and zero otherwise. Thus $A<B$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Infinite intervals.** Every fixed tableau differs from its ground only finitely many times. Choose an actual finite lower cut below all those changes, never an undefined $\inf I$ when $I$ is unbounded below, and a finite upper cut above all displayed entries and charges. Appending a common ground tail gives the same action of every root generator in the common subinterval: its adjacent occupation pattern is unchanged. The finite weight differences and all prefix comparisons are unchanged. The compatible union constructs the semi-infinite factors and tensor module; each fixed finite-support calculation is one of the finite computations above. Highest-weight uniqueness and the ground argument remain valid on those finite cuts. [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2]

5.1 **Conclusion.** The module, tableau labels, column monomials, root-coordinate weights and prefix order are well defined, and the vacuum is the unique normalized highest-weight tensor monomial. Ordinary physical partitions use the shifted column heights. All admitted consecutive intervals and multicharges are retained; no raw-chart basedness or additional choice is asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: Parabolic semi-regular duality and the reverse-column label map
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, with its upper Borel and Cartan, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the standard parabolic of the tableau column sizes $n_1,\ldots,n_l$. Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\bar{\mathfrak l}\oplus\bar{\mathfrak u}$ be the standard parabolic with these block sizes reversed. Set $\alpha_i(\zeta)=0$ on the simple Levi roots and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ on the remaining simple roots, and grade by $\operatorname{ad}\zeta$. Thus
$$\mathfrak g_0=\bar{\mathfrak l},\qquad \mathfrak g_{>0}=\bar{\mathfrak u},\qquad \mathfrak g_{<0}=\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-}.$$
Degrees greater than one are retained. Put $U=U(\mathfrak g)$, $B=U(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, $N=U(\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-})$, and $\gamma=2\rho_{\mathfrak g}-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak l}}$, a character of $\bar{\mathfrak l}$ extended by zero to $\bar{\mathfrak u}$. For a graded vector space $V$, write $V^{\#}=\bigoplus_d(V_{-d})^*$ and
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(V,W)=\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}^d(V,W).$$
Here $\operatorname{Hom}^d$ consists of maps homogeneous of degree $d$; the direct sum allows only finitely many degrees. These conventions are essential.

(1) The algebraic space $S=N^{\#}\otimes B$ has commuting left and right $U$-actions and identifications
$$S\cong N^{\#}\otimes_N U\cong U\otimes_N N^{\#}.$$
Its left action is obtained from the restricted coinduction model
$$S\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B).$$
No completion of $S$ is taken. With $P$ and $Q$ the projections of $\mathfrak g$ to $\mathfrak g_{\ge0}$ and $\mathfrak g_{<0}$, respectively, the polarization trace governing normal ordering is
$$\omega(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{\ge0}}(P\operatorname{ad}XQ\operatorname{ad}YP-P\operatorname{ad}YQ\operatorname{ad}XP)=\gamma_0([X,Y]),$$
where $\gamma_0$ is zero outside degree zero. In particular, for $X\in\mathfrak g_1$ and $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ this is $\gamma([X,Y])=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, not the full adjoint-composition trace.

(2) On graded $U$-modules free over $N$ of finite graded rank, $T=S\otimes_U-$ is an exact equivalence onto the graded $U$-modules cofree over $N$ of finite graded rank. Its inverse is $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_U(S,-)$; finite graded rank means a finite sum of grading shifts of $N$, respectively $N^{\#}$. In this restricted sense
$$\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})\cong N^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This equality is not an assertion about unrestricted endomorphisms: for $N=\mathbb C[x]$ with $\deg x=-1$, the unrestricted ring is $\mathbb C[\![x]\!]$.

(3) With the principal contragredient action $(Xf)(v)=-f(Xv)$ on the restricted dual, $\Phi(M)=(S\otimes_U M)^{\#}$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of the finite generalized-standard flag category for $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its own opposite. On a finite-dimensional simple $\bar{\mathfrak l}$-module $E$,
$$\Phi(\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(E))\cong\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*).$$
The parabolic in this formula is unchanged.

(4) Let $c(X)=-w_0X^{\mathsf T}w_0$, which carries the upper Borel to itself and reverses the Levi blocks, and set $\Psi=c^*\Phi$. For a lower-bounded tableau shape set $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and use the concatenated ordinary highest-weight reading $a_i$, with each column read from top to bottom in strictly decreasing order, and $\lambda_{A,i}=a_i+i-1$. The source reading is the reversed sequence of columns, without reversing positions within a column. Then
$$\Psi:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A).$$
This is an exact contravariant equivalence. It preserves the tableau label and the corresponding central-character summands, including the scalar central coordinate, and the reverse-column label order is opposite to the target order. More explicitly its weight map is
$$\lambda\longmapsto w_0w_{\bar J}\lambda+2w_0\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}.$$

(5) For restricted BGG transpose duality $D$, the composite $F=D\Psi$ is an exact covariant equivalence $\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla)$ with $F(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\nabla(A)$.

For category-$\mathcal O$ modules these constructions use finite weight spaces and the finite direct sum of $\zeta$-eigenvalue cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Internal homogeneous Hom becomes the $\zeta$-locally finite part of Hom, and the dual is the weight-restricted dual. No equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects or unrestricted completed Hom spaces is asserted.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The type-$A$ Lie algebra, reversed-block parabolic, grading element, algebras $U,B,N$, restricted dual and internal Hom conventions, and tableau readings of the Statement.

[F1] PBW and root structure ([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]], [[thm-root-sl-two-triple]], [[prop-brackets-of-root-spaces]]): ordered monomials give both decompositions $U=B\otimes N=N\otimes B$ as vector spaces; the simple positive and negative root vectors and the Cartan generate $\mathfrak g$.

[F2] Parabolic structure ([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]], [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]): $\bar{\mathfrak l}$ is reductive, standards are $U\otimes_B E$ with $E$ finite-dimensional simple and radical acting trivially, and finite flags have finite-dimensional weight spaces and locally finite Levi action.

[F3] Restricted BGG duality ([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]) is exact, preserves weights and central-character summands, and sends standards to costandards.

[F4] Tableau conventions ([[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]): the normally ordered top-to-bottom decreasing column reading and fixed-total-weight prefix-dominance order. Use that same column reading for the ordinary highest-weight tuple here and put $\lambda_{A,i}=a_i+i-1$.

[F5] The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is available for the choice of bases and splittings; trace forms are symmetric and invariant ([[prop-trace-forms-are-symmetric-and-invariant]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **All graded pieces and the crossing trace.** A positive root has degree equal to the number of omitted simple roots in its support. Hence the full positive radical is $\bigoplus_{d>0}\mathfrak g_d$, not generally $\mathfrak g_1$. The simple outside root vectors lie in $\mathfrak g_1$ and their negatives in $\mathfrak g_{-1}$; together with $\mathfrak g_0$ they generate the Lie algebra. For $H\in\mathfrak g_0$, $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{>0}}\operatorname{ad}H=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+\setminus\Phi_{\bar J}^+}\alpha(H)=\gamma(H)$ on the Cartan. Both sides vanish on the derived Levi, so this identity holds on all of $\mathfrak g_0$. In particular $\gamma$ is a Levi character. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 **Restricted coinduction and the two actions.** Every component $N_{-r}$ is finite dimensional and $N_0=\mathbb C$. Give $N^{\#}$ its regular transpose bimodule actions $(nf)(a)=f(an)$ and $(fn)(a)=f(na)$. PBW gives $N^{\#}\otimes_N U=N^{\#}\otimes B$, carrying its right $U$-action. On the other hand restrict a $B$-linear map $U\to\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B$ to $N$ using $U=B\otimes N$. A homogeneous map of degree $d$ sends $N_{-r}$ into $B_{d-r}$, hence is zero for $r>d$. Consequently it has finite support in $r$, and the remaining domains are finite dimensional. This proves $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B)=N^{\#}\otimes B$ even though $B_0$ is infinite dimensional. The left action is $(XG)(u)=G(uX)$. Its Lie relations follow from associativity in $U$; restriction to $N$ gives an algebraic action on $S$. The left $N$-action and right $B$-action already commute with the entire opposite action. [F1, F2, F5, construct]

2.1 For homogeneous $X,Y$ of opposite degrees, take the $P$-block trace of $[\operatorname{ad}X,\operatorname{ad}Y]$. Its terms entirely within $P\mathfrak g$ form a commutator and have trace zero, leaving exactly $\omega(X,Y)$. The bracket has degree zero; its adjoint trace on $\mathfrak g_0$ is zero since that algebra is reductive, so step 1.1 gives $\omega(X,Y)=\gamma([X,Y])$. For degrees whose sum is nonzero the crossing operators have nonzero degree and trace zero, and $\gamma_0([X,Y])=0$; degree-zero pairs have no crossing terms and $\gamma$ annihilates their bracket. This proves the displayed identity for all $X,Y$. For degrees $1,-1$, only $\mathfrak g_0$ crosses the boundary, giving the stated $\mathfrak g_0$ trace. For the root $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ example it is $2$, whereas the full trace on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ is $4$. [F1, F2, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 **Normal ordering.** Choose a basis $H_i$ of $\mathfrak g_0$. For $X\in\mathfrak g_1$, PBW uniquely defines maps $C_i^X,R_X:N\to N$ by $aX=Xa+\sum_iH_iC_i^X(a)+R_X(a)$. All these maps have degree $1$; higher negative degrees of $a$ are retained. On $f\otimes1$ the left formulas are $H(f\otimes1)=-(f\operatorname{ad}H)\otimes1+f\otimes(H+\gamma(H))$ and $X(f\otimes1)=f\otimes X+\sum_i(fC_i^X)\otimes(H_i+\gamma(H_i))+(fR_X)\otimes1$. For $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ right multiplication gives $(f\otimes1)Y=(fL_Y)\otimes1$, where $L_Y$ is left multiplication on $N$. Comparing the two PBW expansions of $(Ya)X=Y(aX)$, with $[Y,X]=\sum_ic_iH_i$, gives $C_i^XL_Y=L_YC_i^X+c_i\operatorname{id}$ and $R_XL_Y=L_YR_X+\sum_iL_{[Y,H_i]}C_i^X$. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 **Restricted endomorphisms and the inverse functor.** Transposing a homogeneous left $N$-endomorphism of $N^{\#}$ gives a homogeneous right $N$-endomorphism of $N$, because its homogeneous pieces are finite dimensional. Such an endomorphism is multiplication by its value at $1$. Transposition reverses composition, and summing finitely many degrees gives $\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})=N^{\mathrm{op}}$. For unrestricted maps this argument produces a product of degrees: in the polynomial example $x$ acts locally nilpotently on the dual basis, so every power series in $x$ acts, and these are all the endomorphisms. Its $\zeta$-locally finite subspace under commutator is exactly the polynomial subalgebra; unrestricted completion is therefore explicitly excluded. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Substitute these two identities into $X((f\otimes1)Y)-(X(f\otimes1))Y$. All terms with a nonconstant operator on $N$ cancel; the remaining scalar is the difference $\gamma([X,Y])-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, multiplied by $f\otimes1$, and is zero by step 2.1. For $H,Y$ the cancellation is $[\operatorname{ad}H,L_Y]=L_{[H,Y]}$. The same relations on $f\otimes b$ follow by induction on a word in the generators $\mathfrak g_0,\mathfrak g_1$ of $B$: commute right multiplication by the next generator past $Y$, whose bracket lies in $\mathfrak g_0$ or $\mathfrak g_{-1}$. Since $U$ is generated by $\mathfrak g_0,\mathfrak g_{\pm1}$, both actions commute everywhere. Thus higher radical degrees require no extra assumption; their relations are already relations in the coinduction and tensor models, and their crossing traces were checked in step 2.1. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 **Left PBW, without a dimension shortcut.** The map $U\otimes_N N^{\#}\to S$ is left multiplication on the inclusion $f\mapsto f\otimes1$. Its PBW domain is $B\otimes N^{\#}$. For a homogeneous $f$ filter first by its nonnegative dual degree and then by the ordinary PBW length of the $B$-word. In the formula for $X$, every correction decreases the dual degree; in the formula for $H$, corrections preserve that degree but decrease the $B$-length. Thus the map on the associated successive quotients is precisely the vector-space interchange $b\otimes f\mapsto f\otimes b$. Inducting over the dual degree and, at fixed degree, over PBW length proves surjectivity. A finite linear relation has a largest pair of filtration indices; its leading symbols are independent under the interchange, proving injectivity. Each expression involves finitely many words, so the argument needs neither finite dimension of $B_0$ nor a completed series. [F1, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 From the right PBW model $T(M)=N^{\#}\otimes_N M$, so free finite rank becomes cofree finite rank. From the left PBW model $H(K)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_N(N^{\#},K)$, which is free finite rank by step 2.3. Tensor-Hom adjunction supplies the unit and counit. On each shifted rank-one summand they are the identity under the endomorphism identification and the evaluation map, respectively, so both are isomorphisms. A short exact sequence of graded free finite-rank objects splits over $N$ since its quotient is graded free. A sequence of graded cofree objects splits over $N$ since its subobject is graded injective: $N^{\#}$ is the graded coinduction of the field, and its Hom functor is the exact dual of the corresponding homogeneous component. Hence $T,H$ preserve the exact sequences at issue. [step 1.2, step 4.1, step 2.3, algebra]

6.1 **Duality and standards.** Restricted duality with the principal antipode gives an exact anti-equivalence from finite cofree to finite free objects; the transpose of that antipode identifies the two regular transpose actions on $N^{\#}$. Finite homogeneous components give biduality, so composing with $T$ gives $\Phi$ with inverse $H\circ(-)^{\#}$; no involutivity of $T$ is assumed. For $M=U\otimes_B E$, tensor cancellation gives $T(M)=S\otimes_B E=N^{\#}\otimes E$. On the augmentation vector $\varepsilon\otimes E$, the Levi action in step 2.2 is the original $E$-action plus $\gamma$, since $\varepsilon\operatorname{ad}H=0$. Dualizing makes the generator space $\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*$. The positive radical annihilates this generator space by degree, and the negative regular action makes the dual free on it. The induced PBW map is therefore an isomorphism $\Phi(M)=U\otimes_B(\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*)$. This is a standard for the same parabolic. [F1, F2, step 2.2, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 A finite standard flag is graded free over $N$ of finite rank, since its standard sections are such and every extension splits over $N$. Applying $\Phi$ gives a reversed finite standard flag by step 6.1. Conversely $H\circ(-)^{\#}$ sends a standard back to a standard: the transformation $E\mapsto\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*$ is involutive, and the unit and counit give its inverse. Induction on flag length thus restricts the equivalence precisely to the standard-flag categories. In category $\mathcal O$, $\zeta$ is semisimple; a finite generating set gives finitely many eigenvalue cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Choose a grading origin on each coset. Each standard has finite-dimensional graded components, because its finite Levi space has scalar $\zeta$-action and the graded pieces of $N$ are finite dimensional; the same holds for finite flags. Weight restriction and degree restriction therefore agree here. All $U$-morphisms preserve the actual $\zeta$-eigenvalues. Changing origins just shifts gradings, so the construction descends to the ungraded flag category using the $\zeta$-locally finite internal Hom. On outputs the eigenvalue cosets are shifted by $\gamma(\zeta)$ and negated by the principal dual; this is part of the construction, not an extra integrality assumption on highest weights. [F1, F2, step 5.1, step 6.1, induction]

7.2 **Reverse-column shifts.** The automorphism $c$ preserves the upper Borel and carries $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ to $\mathfrak p$. If the source Levi highest weight is $\lambda$, that of $E^*$ is $-w_{\bar J}\lambda$, so step 6.1 gives $\nu=-w_{\bar J}\lambda-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}$ before applying $c^*$. Pullback by $c$ sends a highest weight to $-w_0\nu$, giving the displayed weight map. A target block of length $r$ starting after $b$ coordinates has reversed source offset $b'=n-b-r$. The map $w_0w_{\bar J}$ preserves its position $k=1,\ldots,r$ inside the column. The value of $2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}$ on the source block is $n-2b'-r=b-b'$, hence the value of $2w_0\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}$ on the target block is $b-b'$. The source coordinate $a_i+b'+k-1$ is consequently transported to $a_i+b'+k-1+b-b'=a_i+i-1$. Thus $\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))=\Delta(A)$ including the scalar trace-centre coordinate. [F2, F4, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 With $\rho_i=(n+1-2i)/2$, the shifted coordinate is $\lambda_{A,i}+\rho_i=a_i+(n-1)/2$. Reversing columns preserves its multiset, so corresponding source and target standards belong to matching central-character summands; extensions of standards in one summand remain in it, and hence so do the images under $\Psi$. At fixed total weight, each reversed-column prefix is the complementary suffix of the original reading; subtracting from the total changes the direction of each prefix-dominance inequality. This reverses the tableau order. Neither connectedness of a central summand nor an equivalence on arbitrary objects is used. [F2, F4, step 7.1, step 7.2, algebra]

9.1 **Covariant equivalence.** Restricted BGG duality is exact and contravariant, sends target standards to costandards and preserves the target central summands. Composing it with the contravariant equivalence $\Psi$ gives the covariant exact equivalence $F=D\Psi$ and $F(\bar\Delta(A))=\nabla(A)$. The label order reversal comes from step 8.1, whereas applying $D$ changes the variance and the kind of flag. This proves all the stated algebraic and filtered-category assertions with their restricted-Hom boundary. [F3, step 7.1, step 7.2, step 8.1] ∎
