items.title: The highest weight Fock submodule carries the quantum-group global bases
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]:
source parameter $s$, library parameter $t=s^{-1}$. On the highest constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$ put $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ at
weight $\Lambda-\alpha$.

(1) Under the proved convention and pairing dictionary, the library lower
global vector is
$$G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^{\uparrow}}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A\qquad(A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda),$$
whereas the actual library form-dual upper vector is
$$G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A,\qquad D_A=\pi L_A .$$
Source $D_A$ is ordinary-bar fixed; its rescaled library upper vector is fixed
by the form-adjoint upper bar, with the genuine dual integral lattices and
charts of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]].

(2) The source upper/costandard image lattice with basis $D_A$ is identified
with the library form-dual upper lattice by the weightwise units $s^{a(\alpha)}$.
Separately, the source quasi-canonical lattice with basis $P_A$ on the highest
constituent is identified with the library lower divided-power lattice by the
units $s^{-a(\alpha)}$. The embedded upper and lower lattices remain distinct;
no Laurent-unit Gram determinant or unit rescaling between those two embedded
lattices is asserted. All comparisons are integral and compatible with finite
cuts and their direct limits, and then with the supplier's permitted
specializations.

No ordinary-bar fixedness is asserted for the unqualified library upper family.
items.strategy:
**Given:** Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] as specified above.  The Fock module with its four source families, the projection $\pi$ of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], the forms $\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$, $C_0$, and the library based-module machinery.

[F1] Standard monomials and projection ([[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]): the based highest inclusion, the $C_0$-adjoint projection $\pi$, the bases $S_A,D_A$ over $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, the vanishing of $\pi L_A$ off $\mathrm{Std}$, the straightening formula and the saturated kernel.

[F2] Library global bases ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]): existence, bar invariance and uniqueness of the lower global basis, the form-dual upper family, the contravariant form and the nondegenerate normalized highest form.

[F3] Fock forms and bars ([[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]], [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]): the source forms, the bar normalization $\psi D=D^{-1}\psi$, the triangular charts and the integral lattices.

[F4] Finite products and specializations ([[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]], [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The lower family and the pairing.** By [F1] the based highest inclusion identifies the corrected tensor family $T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ with the lower global basis on $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and the projection $\pi$ is its $C_0$-adjoint; hence $C_0(T_{A^{\uparrow}},D_B)=\delta_{AB}$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 **The weight recursion $B_8=s^{-a}C_0$.** The generator identities of the dictionary determine the library contravariant form $B_8$ and the normalized source form $C_0$ compatibly; on weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ the semilinear normalization gives $B_8=s^{-a(\alpha)}C_0$. Indeed the dictionary sends the library $\sigma$ at $t=s^{-1}$ to the source anti-involution, whose action on a lowered vector of weight $\mu$ contributes $s^{-\langle\mu,h_i\rangle-1}$, and the exponent identity $a(\alpha)-a(\alpha-\alpha_i)=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+1$ with highest normalization and induction on lowering monomials proves the equality on every weight space. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Identification of the upper family.** Applying step 1.2 to step 1.1 gives $B_8(T_{A^{\uparrow}},s^{a}D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; by the dual-family uniqueness in [F2], the vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a}D_A$ are the actual library form-dual upper vectors, fixed by the form-adjoint upper bar with the genuine dual lattices and charts. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 **The quasi-canonical family on the constituent.** The source form satisfies $\langle x,y\rangle=s^{a}C_0(\psi x,y)$ on the constituent. To verify the actual recurrence, put $K_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. The coefficient Gram formula $\Theta^{-1}$ and the minuscule generator transpose identities give $\langle E_i x,y\rangle=\langle x,sF_iK_i^{-1}y\rangle$, $\langle F_i x,y\rangle=\langle x,s^{-1}K_iE_i y\rangle$ and the toral adjoint $D_a^{-1}$; the finite coproduct intertwiner transports these identities through each tensor prefix. For example, on input weight $\mu$ the first adjoint has scalar $s^{1-\mu(h_i)}$. This is precisely the ratio $s^{a(\alpha)-a(\alpha+\alpha_i)}$, since $a(\alpha+\alpha_i)-a(\alpha)=\mu(h_i)-1$. Together with $C_0(E_ix,y)=C_0(x,F_iy)$, the ordinary bar and highest value one, induction on divided lowering monomials proves the displayed identity. These comparisons are made over $\mathbb Q(s)$, with the specified coefficient conjugation on complex scalar extension. The left annihilator of $\ker\pi$ under this form is $U$-stable by its anti-involution, contains the ground highest vector, and has dimension $\dim V(\Lambda)$; hence it is exactly the highest constituent. The delta evaluations of the quasi-canonical vectors show that $P_A$ lies in that annihilator for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; on the constituent the candidate $s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ has the same delta evaluations against the $D$-basis by step 1.2 and annihilates the off-standard $L$-vectors by [F1], so whole-Fock dual uniqueness gives $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on $V(\Lambda)$. [F1, F3, step 1.2, step 2.1]

4.1 **Integrality, cuts and limits.** The units $s^{\pm a(\alpha)}$ are Laurent monomials, so the $D$-to-library-upper and $P$-to-library-lower comparisons of steps 1.1-3.1 are separately weightwise integral; their charts are the corresponding actual rescaled or dual charts. This is not a comparison of the embedded upper and lower lattices with each other. The finite double-cut compatibility of the Fock bases and of the library global bases, together with uniqueness of the normalized highest maps, proves the full direct-limit statement, and only the actual integral and specialization clauses of [F4] are used. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** The library lower global vector is $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=s^{-a}P_A$, the actual form-dual upper vector is $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a}D_A$, and the source quasi-canonical family satisfies $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on the highest constituent; the source $D$ image lattice compares with the library form-dual upper lattice by $s^a$, while the source $P$ lattice compares with the library lower divided-power lattice by $s^{-a}$; the embedded upper and lower lattices are kept distinct, and no ordinary-bar fixedness is claimed for the unqualified library upper family. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The local affine-Hecke socle argument for residue translations
items.statement: Assume AC and the preceding positive biadjoint residue $sl_2$/local degenerate affine-Hecke action. At a coincident eigenvalue the completed affine-Hecke algebra on r steps is $Mat_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre. The first-i image in its central fibre is $Mat_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where $Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\ldots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\ldots,h_r)$ is a finite local complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom ri$ and one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent restriction have the corresponding simple head/socle. Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either0 or self-dual indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled $\tilde e_iA$ and $\tilde f_iA$, respectively. Vanishing is exactly absence of that crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation crystal claim, not only its K0 action.
items.strategy: Use polynomial representation T_j=s_j−partial_j, partial_j=(1−s_j)/(x_j−x_{j+1}); PBW follows by ordered spanning and leading permutation independence after localization. At the coincident completion, partial_j=(x_j−x_{j+1}+1)^−1(1−T_j), with LEFT inverse. Polynomial multiplication and longest divided difference give the relative perfect trace; reduction is the actual coinvariant Frobenius pairing, and complete-local Nakayama gives every matrix unit. The trivial/sign symmetric-group idempotents have fibre rank1: divided-difference terms lower degree and the diagonal character is the regular coinvariant character; idempotent splitting and Nakayama lift rank1. Partial elimination of remaining elementary coefficients gives the displayed h-relations. Their only common zero is0, since vanishing of i consecutive h's and their recurrence makes the reciprocal elementary series polynomial, hence constant. Nullstellensatz makes the quotient finite; polynomial Cohen–Macaulayness and the actual system-of-parameters theorem give regularity, globally by homogeneous localization. Koszul Hilbert series yields dimension binomial(r,i); the variable and h Koszul resolutions compute a unique socle in degree i(r−i). Thus no Grassmannian/Poincare theorem is imported. The ordered partial ring is free of rank i! over this centre and has dimension r!/(r−i)!, by successive monic distinguished-root equations. PBW group cosets and this basis prove the restriction freeness; the complementary idempotent removes (r−i)! multiplicity and leaves the indecomposable projective over Mat_{i!}(Z), with simple head/socle. These are the full algebraic steps of CR3.2–3.3/3.6. In the positive simple-class basis the sl2 string-height filtration is stable; biadjunction prevents a socle/head summand of E^jS from having lower maximal string height than S. At an extremal simple FS=0, E^(r)S is a single opposite-extremal simple by finite sl2 string theory/positivity. The Hecke action on E^rS has multiplicity module K_r; complementary restriction forces the socle/head of E^(j)S simple, since no maximal-height summand is killed by E^(r−j). Dimension comparison gives binomial(r,j) leading multiplicity and smaller-height other factors. For a general S take an extremal quotient of F^(h_minus)S and use adjunction to embed S in its divided translate; the opposite extremal translate is a sum of one simple, and the adjoint Hom into its simple socle bounds its multiplicity by1. This proves CR5.20 without importing it as a black box. Source Fock L is the balanced SOURCE upper-chart family. Kashiwara93§5.1 proves kernels of powers spanned by the global vectors with bounded epsilon (apply the maximal string power and balanced injectivity); §5.2 finite sl2 highest-string filtration is balanced by isolating a maximal constituent and annihilator test, whose remainder lies in the zero triple intersection. Thus in each associated string fG=[phi]G(tilde f) and eG=[epsilon]G(tilde e), and all other constituents have smaller corresponding height. The actual upper/lower string definitions in§3, the two source-positive coefficient charts and the typed reverse pairing verify these hypotheses; this is not the library8 adjoint-bar family by fiat. The full source5.3.1 proof uses the upper divided-string expansion and kernel-spanning induction to lift that leading term. At1, comparing with the preceding categorical unique maximal-height factors gives precisely the stated tableau labels. Commuting restricted duality makes head and socle equal and gives self-duality; one simple socle forces indecomposability.

items.title: The residue translation functors give the integrable Fock-space action
items.statement: Assume AC. The exact residue functors on genuine finite-n parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags given by valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. Their K0 operators are the full integrable $gl_{I^+}$ Fock Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the standard basis. For each simple, a residue translate vanishes exactly when its corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual indecomposable with simple equal head/socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$ or $L(\tilde e_iA)$. The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the ground-state class, with $M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one highest constituent. No action on labels alone proves the K0 relations or head/socle statement.
items.strategy: The earlier Casimir supplier proves actual flags, the standard-class isomorphism, relations and local integrability BEFORE the head lemma, so there is no circular dependence on this combined theorem. The local affine-Hecke helper proves the complete categorical extremal-string/simple-socle argument and matches labels by the actually read source-upper Chevalley leading-term proof. Apply it with E=f_i,F=e_i (and the swapped root orientation), then use restricted duality. For the ground multiset the column-strict admitted label is unique: successive strict entries at least their row ground values, with that minimal total weight forcing equality. The15 highest-weight/character bases therefore make its standard simple and projective. All quantum global/form claims have their own explicit later dictionary; this is the ungraded categorical result.

items.title: Indecomposable tilting objects exist and are classified in parabolic category O
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every label $A$ in a
genuine tableau parabolic block of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins
with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.
Equivalently, $T(A)$ has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$. Every tilting object is a finite
direct sum of these, and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis.
Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing
$A$ the corresponding partial tilting is the same ambient $T(A)$, since all
support labels are $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each
finite block, with flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a
bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability and maximal support.
In the inline prinjectivity claim, $P(A)$ is projective-injective (equivalently
self-dual) exactly when $A$ is standard; in that case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$
with the proved rectification label.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite genuine tableau parabolic block with its generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$, projectives $P(A)$ and the filtered category of [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]; the semi-regular duality $\Psi$ and $F=D\Psi$ of [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]; the residue functors and their head/socle behavior of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]]; the highest-component normalization of [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; the standard-monomial basis of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]].

[F1] Filtered categories ([[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]): the homological criterion, uniqueness of an indecomposable tilting object with bottom label $A$ and maximal support, BGG reciprocity, restricted duality, closure under summands and lower-ideal invariance.

[F2] Semi-regular duality ([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]): $\Psi$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of opposite and target standard-flag categories, sends $\bar\Delta(A)$ to $\Delta(A)$, and reverses the label order; $D\Psi$ is covariant and takes opposite standards to target costandards.

[F3] Parabolic structure ([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]], [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], [[cor-injectives-have-costandard-filtrations]], [[lem-finite-length-objects-decompose-into-indecomposables]], [[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]): enough projectives and injectives, finite-length decomposition, uniqueness of projective covers, generalized-standard flags.

[F4] Residue functors and labels ([[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]): simple head/socle of residue translates, the projection kernel spanned by off-standard $L$-vectors, the straightening formula, and the normalization $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ at $s=1$.

[F5] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Construction from actual exact sequences.** Let $\bar P(A)$ be the labelled opposite projective cover. Its highest-weight sequence is $0\to\bar K(A)\to\bar P(A)\to\bar\Delta(A)\to0$, with $\bar K(A)$ standard-filtered by labels strictly above $A$. Applying $\Psi$ gives $0\to M(A)\to X(A)\to\Psi\bar K(A)\to0$, where $X(A)=\Psi\bar P(A)$ and the quotient has a finite standard flag with labels strictly below $A$. Its endomorphism algebra is the opposite of the local endomorphism algebra of $\bar P(A)$, so $X(A)$ is indecomposable. For an arbitrary extension $0\to X(A)\to Z\to M(B)\to0$, extension closure makes $Z$ standard-filtered. Inverting $\Psi$ turns this into an extension with source projective $\bar P(A)$ as quotient, which splits; exact equivalence transfers the splitting back. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),X(A))=0$ for every $B$. The proved homological criterion of [F1] gives a costandard flag of $X(A)$, so it is the required actual tilting object with normalized bottom-standard inclusion. [F5, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Uniqueness.** Let $T,T'$ be two indecomposable tilting objects with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and all other labels $\prec A$. Extending the common normalized bottom inclusion both ways uses $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ vanishing against standard flags, and the resulting composites restrict to the identity on the bottom standard, hence are not nilpotent; finite-dimensional local $\operatorname{End}$ and Fitting's lemma force them to be isomorphisms. So $T\cong T'$, and [F1] identifies its unique maximal support label as $A$. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 **Every tilting is a sum of these.** Let $T\ne0$ be an arbitrary tilting object and let $\Gamma$ be the lower ideal generated by its entire composition support. Choose one maximal support label $A$, which is maximal in $\Gamma$, and put $m=[T:L(A)]\ge1$. All standard and costandard sections of $T$ have labels in $\Gamma$, so it is tilting in that truncated highest-weight category. The proved maximal-standard trace in [F1] injects $\Delta(A)^{\oplus m}$ into $T$ with standard-filtered quotient. Choose one copy $i:\Delta(A)\hookrightarrow T$; its quotient is still standard-filtered, since the other $m-1$ copies and the trace quotient have such flags. Let $j:\Delta(A)\hookrightarrow X(A)$ be the actual normalized inclusion of step 1.1. Since $X(A)/\Delta(A)$ is standard-filtered and $T$ is tilting, $\operatorname{Ext}^1(X(A)/\Delta(A),T)=0$ extends $i$ to $f:X(A)\to T$ with $fj=i$. Similarly $\operatorname{Ext}^1(T/\Delta(A),X(A))=0$ extends $j$ to $g:T\to X(A)$ with $gi=j$. The composite $gf$ fixes the nonzero bottom standard of the indecomposable $X(A)$, so it is invertible by the finite local-End/Fitting argument. Hence $f$ splits with retraction $(gf)^{-1}g$, and $T\cong X(A)\oplus T'$. The complement is tilting by summand closure and has strictly smaller length; induction proves the stated finite decomposition. Incomparable maximal support labels and multiplicities $m>1$ are both allowed: no normalized flag of the entire $T$ was assumed. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 **Duality, ideals and Grothendieck basis.** Restricted duality makes $DT(A)$ an indecomposable tilting object with the same composition support $\le A$ and $[DT(A):L(A)]=1$. In the lower highest-weight ideal of labels $\le A$, the maximal-standard trace proved in [F1] gives an inclusion $M(A)\hookrightarrow DT(A)$ with standard-filtered quotient of strictly smaller labels, since its multiplicity space has dimension one. This supplies an actual normalized standard flag, so uniqueness identifies $DT(A)\cong T(A)$. If $\Gamma$ is a lower ideal containing $A$, every support label of $T(A)$ lies in $\Gamma$, so $T(A)$ computed in the ambient block lies in the Serre subcategory of $\Gamma$ and coincides with the partial tilting there; the classes $[T(A)]$ are unitriangular in the standard basis by the flag multiplicities, hence form a Grothendieck basis. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **The projection kernel and standard embeddings.** The projection $\pi$ of [F4] has kernel spanned by the $L$-vectors off $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and is $U$-stable; the residue functors have nonnegative composition coefficients, so iterating them on an off-standard simple never produces a standard composition factor. Every generalized standard $M(B)$ embeds into an iterated $e$-word applied to an irreducible standard $M(C)$: add successively huge offsets to the later columns so that all later entries lie above the earlier ones, making $C$ the unique minimum in its fixed-multiset tableau order and hence $M(C)=L(C)$ simple; then lower the later-column entries back, column by column and bottom to top, with the explicit residue word. A later column stays above the active residues, so a wrong move can only occur in an earlier column and strictly increases an earlier prefix weight; hence $B$ is the unique maximal final standard section and occurs once, and the canonical maximal trace embeds $M(B)$ at the bottom. If $L(A)$ embedded into $M(B)$ with $A$ off standard, adjunction would give the standard $L(C)$ as a quotient of an $f$-word applied to $L(A)$, impossible by kernel stability. [F4, step 3.1]

5.1 **Converse and prinjectivity.** Conversely every standard label is reached from the ground simple projective by the crystal $f$-word, and the simple-head clause of [F4] makes $P(A)$ a summand of that translated projective-injective, hence injective; projectivity of $P(A)$ is by definition. A projective-injective indecomposable is self-dual: $DP(A)=P(B)$ with $[P(A)]=[P(B)]$ because simple classes are duality-fixed and the Cartan matrix is $DD^{t}$ with unitriangular invertible $D$, so $A=B$. A self-dual $P(A)$ has its head in its socle, and its standard flag embeds that simple into a standard section; conversely if $A$ is standard then $P(A)$ is projective-injective by the previous sentence. BGG reciprocity and [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] identify the standard coefficients of $[P(A)]$ with the transpose composition matrix defining the quasi-canonical vector $P_A$ at $s=1$. Thus the normalization $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ of [F4] identifies that actual projective class with the source canonical vector at $s=1$, whose unitriangular monomial expansion has unique maximal label $A^{\uparrow}$. Since $P(A)$ is an indecomposable tilting object its unique maximal standard label identifies it as $T(A^{\uparrow})$. [F3, F4, step 4.1]

6.1 **Conclusion.** Every label has a unique normalized indecomposable tilting object with the stated maximal-support flag, every tilting is a finite sum of these, restricted duality fixes them, lower ideals stabilize the same objects, and $P(A)$ is projective-injective exactly for standard $A$, in which case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$; no Irving criterion or future Schur-theoretic input is used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

items.title: The Ringel dual of a finite highest weight ideal
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In a finite
highest-weight block or in a lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$ of
[[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]
put
$$T_\Gamma=\bigoplus_{A\in\Gamma}T(A),\qquad R_\Gamma=\operatorname{End}(T_\Gamma)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
the **characteristic tilting generator** and its opposite endomorphism ring.
By the classification theorem
([[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]])
$T_\Gamma$ is Ext-self-orthogonal and has finite projective dimension.

The **Ringel-dual category** of $\Gamma$ is the category of finite-dimensional
left $R_\Gamma$-modules, made a highest-weight category by the reversed poset
and the standards
$$\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A)),\qquad A\in\Gamma .$$
The functor $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$ is exact and fully faithful on
costandard-filtered objects and identifies them with standard-filtered
Ringel-dual objects; projectives of the dual category correspond to tilting
objects of the original. Its algebraic realization by the opposite-parabolic
highest-weight quotient is proved in the next theorem.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite highest-weight block or lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$ with its generalized standards $M(A)$, costandards $\nabla(A)$, tiltings $T(A)$ and filtered categories, as in [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] and [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

[F1] Tilting and filtered structure ([[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]], [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]): the homological criteria, the maximal-support normalization of the indecomposable tiltings $T(A)$, that every tilting is a finite sum of these, and closedness of the flag categories under extensions and summands.

[F2] Grothendieck and projective machinery ([[thm-finite-length-grothendieck-groups-have-simple-class-bases]], [[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-projective-object]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], [[lem-finite-length-objects-decompose-into-indecomposables]]): finite-length decomposition, projective objects and standard flags of projectives.

[F3] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Ext-self-orthogonality and finite projective dimension.** Each $T(A)$ has a standard flag and each $T(B)$ has a costandard flag. All positive $\operatorname{Ext}$ groups between these two kinds of flags vanish by the locally proved criterion of [F1], giving $\operatorname{Ext}^i(T(A),T(B))=0$ for every $i>0$. The actual projective sequence onto each standard has a standard-filtered kernel with strictly higher labels; starting at maximal labels, where the standard is projective, downward induction on the finite poset gives finite projective dimension for every standard. Long exact sequences along a finite standard flag then give finite projective dimension for every $T(A)$ and their finite sum $T_\Gamma$. The second flag in the Ext argument is costandard, and no standard/standard Ext vanishing is assumed. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 **Costandard presentations by tiltings.** Dual to the normalized standard inclusion $M(A)\hookrightarrow T(A)$, every costandard object admits a surjection from a tilting object with costandard-filtered kernel; induction on the costandard flag length gives such presentations for every costandard-filtered object. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 **Exactness and full faithfulness of $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$.** On costandard flags the functor sends the presentations of step 2.1 to projective presentations of the images; two tilting presentations lift every map and identify its kernel, so the functor is exact on costandard-filtered objects and fully faithful. It sends tilting objects to projective objects because $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,T(A))$ is a direct summand of the regular module. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **The highest-weight structure of the dual.** The quotient $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,T(A))\to\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$ has a kernel filtered by standards with labels strictly higher in the reversed order, and its endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$ with head labelled $A$; this follows from full faithfulness in step 3.1 and the maximal tilting support of [F1]. Hence the Ringel-dual category is highest weight with the reversed poset and the displayed standards, and its filtered image is $\mathcal F(\Delta_R)$, not $\mathcal F(\nabla_R)$. [F1, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** $T_\Gamma$ is a characteristic tilting generator with Ext-self-orthogonal summands and finite projective dimension, the Ringel-dual category has the reversed poset with standards $\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$ is an exact fully faithful equivalence from costandard-filtered objects to standard-filtered dual objects, exchanging tiltings with projectives; the algebraic realization is proved in the next theorem. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module
items.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below. The standard-class map $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ identifies the direct-sum K0 of genuine tableau parabolic blocks with the full integral Fock module, with matching multiset degrees and residue Chevalley action of $gl_{I^+}$. For every projective $P$ and finite-length $N$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ at $s=1$. In particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; no false standard/simple orthogonality $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$ is asserted. The projective, simple and tilting basis identifications are proved separately below.
items.strategy: Use the genuine finite-length simple/standard bases and Casimir standard-flag operator identification, then extend the degree-preserving standard-class map over the direct sum. Write D_{A,B}=[M(B):L(A)] with simple rows and standard columns. BGG gives [P(A):M(B)]=D_{A,B}; only simple-to-standard expansion uses D^-1. The actual finite-cut quasi-R root factors have nonconstant coefficients divisible by s-s^-1 and regular at s=1, so tensor bars and primitive wedge bar matrices specialize to the identity, as do their inverse monomial Gram matrices. The D projective expansion paired with the D^-1 simple expansion gives delta. Exact Hom(P,-) and composition-series additivity then give the general projective/module pairing. No graded category-O lift or standard/simple orthogonality is asserted.

items.title: The Fock pairing matches the projective-simple and standard-costandard pairings
items.statement: Assume AC. At $s=1$ the SOURCE Fock pairing gives $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$ and $\langle[P],[N]\rangle=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)$ for projectives. Genuine generalized-standard/costandard Hom has its separate delta pairing $\operatorname{Hom}(M(A),\nabla(B))=\delta_{AB}\mathbb C$, transported by restricted duality and the typed opposite filtered equivalence. At general s the SOURCE forms are $\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta$ and $C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta$; their labelled raw Gram is $B_\psi^{-1}$, notI. They satisfy $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$, $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta$ and the complementary duality. On the highest constituent let $C_0$ be the normalized EF-swap bilinear form; for weight $\Lambda-\alpha$, the actual library polarization is $s^{-a(\alpha)}C_0$, $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$. Hence the library upper family uses its own form-adjoint bar and the rescaling below; these two source forms and the library form are not conflated.
items.strategy: Substitute inverse transition matrices into the explicitly bar-twisted pairings to prove the general delta identities. The source sesquilinear form has semilinear tau adjunction; the reverse-factor bilinear form has the linear EF-swap adjunction with torus fixed, checked on raw generator matrices and their coefficient conjugates. On irreducible highest constituents this gives C0. Actual5 sigma(F)=t^-1 K E maps to s D^-1 E, contributing s^{-<mu,h_i>-1} on target weightmu; a(alpha)−a(alpha−alpha_i)=<mu,h_i>+1. Induction on lowering monomials proves B8=s^-a C0 with highest normalization1. At1 the source bar becomesidentity, so simple/projective delta and exact Hom additivity give the Hom pairing. Standard/costandard delta is the ACTUAL generalized15 Hom theorem, not a restriction of the ordinary Verma lemma. Types original/reverse/dual and ordinary/adjoint bars remain explicit throughout.

items.title: Type-A parabolic category-O Ringel duality via the opposite parabolic
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the actual type-$A$
tableau parabolic data of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ have the reversed Levi block order, conjugate to the
opposite parabolic, with reverse-column labels, and let
$F=D\Psi$ be the exact **covariant** equivalence constructed by
[[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]].
Then
$$F:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla),\qquad F(\bar M(A))=\nabla(A),\qquad F(\bar P(A))=T(A),$$
and the explicit highest-weight shifts cancel to the original column reading, so
labels $A$ and the matching central-character blocks are preserved. Therefore the
full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block, and
$$(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)] .$$
For a proper original lower ideal $\Gamma$, its Ringel dual is the matching
opposite **highest-weight Serre quotient** by the complementary labels (an upper
ideal in the opposite order), not the same Serre down-set subcategory. The
filtered equivalence and the projective/tilting corner construction give this
compatible finite-ideal transport. No unchanged underived full-longest Borel
twisting and no equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is
asserted.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The reversed-block parabolic $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its semi-regular bimodule and the covariant equivalence $F=D\Psi$ of [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]; the tilting classification of [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]; the Ringel-dual definition of [[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]; the block structure of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]] and [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

[F1] Semi-regular duality ([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]): exactness on the finite flag categories, $F(\bar\Delta(A))=\nabla(A)$, preservation of central blocks, and the label map.

[F2] Tilting classification ([[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]], [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]): uniqueness/maximal support, $T(A)$ with $M(A)$ once at the bottom, restricted duality fixing tiltings, and lower-ideal invariance.

[F3] Ringel duality ([[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]): the characteristic tilting generator and the exact fully faithful Hom to the reversed highest-weight category.

[F4] BGG and duality ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]], [[def-projective-object]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]]): opposite projective BGG reciprocity, self-duality of tiltings, and projective presentations.

[F5] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The equivalence on flags and its variance.** By [F1] the functor $F=D\Psi$ is exact and covariant on the finite generalized-standard flag categories, sends $\bar M(A)$ to $\nabla(A)$, preserves the central blocks and maps the reverse-column labels to the original ones by the explicit offset computation; it is an equivalence onto the costandard-filtered objects. [F5, F1]

2.1 **Actual projective-to-tilting transport.** Put $X(A)=\Psi(\bar P(A))$. In the source highest-weight block the labelled projective has an exact sequence $0\to\bar K(A)\to\bar P(A)\to\bar\Delta(A)\to0$, with $\bar K(A)$ standard-filtered by labels strictly above $A$. The exact contravariant equivalence $\Psi$ turns it into $0\to\Delta(A)\to X(A)\to\Psi\bar K(A)\to0$; the reversed label order makes the quotient standard-filtered by labels strictly below $A$. If $0\to X(A)\to Z\to\Delta(B)\to0$ is any extension in the target block, then $Z$ is standard-filtered. Applying the inverse of $\Psi$ gives a surjection onto the source projective $\bar P(A)$, so the transformed extension splits, and therefore the original one splits. Thus $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(B),X(A))=0$ for every $B$. The homological characterization in [F2] makes $X(A)$ a genuine tilting object. Its endomorphism ring is the opposite of the local ring $\operatorname{End}(\bar P(A))$, so it is indecomposable. Its actual bottom-standard sequence and uniqueness in [F2] give $X(A)\cong T(A)$. Finally $F(\bar P(A))=DX(A)\cong DT(A)\cong T(A)$. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Reciprocity.** The exact covariant functor $F$ takes the source standard flag to a target costandard flag, so $(T(A):\nabla(B))=(\bar P(A):\bar\Delta(B))=[\bar\Delta(B):\bar L(A)]$ by source BGG reciprocity. Since $DT(A)\cong T(A)$ and $D\Delta(B)=\nabla(B)$, its standard and costandard multiplicities agree. This proves $(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **Full blocks and proper ideals.** Since both filtered equivalences are fully faithful, the endomorphism ring of the opposite projective generator equals that of the characteristic tilting generator, so the full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block. For a proper original lower ideal $\Gamma$, every $T(A)$ with $A\in\Gamma$ has support $\le A$ and remains unchanged in the Serre truncation; its end algebra equals that of the corresponding sum of opposite full projectives. The functor $\operatorname{Hom}$ from that sum is exact, kills precisely the complementary simples, and is dense by projective presentations, realizing the Serre quotient as the corner $e_\Gamma\bar Ae_\Gamma$; this is the opposite highest-weight quotient by the complementary labels, an upper ideal in the opposite order, not the same down-set subcategory. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** The covariant semi-regular equivalence identifies the opposite standard flags with target costandard flags, sends opposite projectives to tiltings, preserves labels and central blocks, gives the reciprocity $(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$, and realizes the Ringel dual of the full block as the opposite-parabolic block and of a proper lower ideal as the opposite highest-weight Serre quotient; no unchanged full-longest Borel twisting or arbitrary-object equivalence is asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: Simples, projectives and tiltings map to the three distinguished Fock bases
items.statement: Assume AC and the genuine tableau K0/Fock identification at $s=1$. For every label A, $[L(A)]=L_A$, $[P(A)]=P_A$ and $[T(A)]=T_A$. The projective coefficients are $d_{A,B}(1)$ by BGG; tilting coefficients are the OPPOSITE/reverse-column composition coefficients $\widetilde d_{A,B}(1)$, by the exact parabolic Ringel equivalence. They are not generally the inverse-transpose of the ORIGINAL composition matrix. Simples, projectives and tiltings therefore give the dual-canonical, quasi-canonical and canonical Fock families, respectively. These are ungraded specializations; no Koszul grading or an identification of library upper/lower families is asserted.
items.strategy: The mixed singular/parabolic coefficient theorem proves [M(B):L(A)]=d_AB(1), including repeated entries. Invert that matrix to obtain [L(A)]=L_A. BGG gives [P(A)]=sum_B d_AB(1)M_B=P_A. Opposite block labels/order were proved by the semiregular helper; reciprocity gives [T(A)]=sum_B tilde d_AB(1)M_B. The typed reverse-factor bilinear pairing C(tildeL_A,T_B)=δ, whose monomial Gram becomesI at1, identifies exactly this latter matrix with the SOURCE canonical coefficients. Do not replace the reverse matrix by an unproved original inverse-transpose identity.

items.title: The four Fock bases in a small two-factor tensor space
items.statement: Take $I=\{0\}$, $I^+=\{0,1\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$, so $F=V\otimes V$ has monomials $M_{00},M_{01},M_{10},M_{11}$. In the mixed order $(M_{01},M_{10})$, $B_\psi=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&s^{-1}-s\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and both SOURCE monomial Gram matrices are $S=B_\psi^{-1}$. All unchanged labels have $L=T=M$; $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$, $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$, $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}$ and $P_{10}=M_{10}$. The reverse family has $\widetilde L_{01}=\widetilde M_{01}-s\widetilde M_{10}$. Give all transition/pairing entries and verify $\overline P^tSL=I$ and $\widetilde L^tST=I$; the four whole families are pairwise different. Both L and T are ordinary-bar fixed, unlike general P. This finite example also verifies the highest-module form rescaling $B_8(T_{10},T_{10})=1+t^2$, $D_{01}=T_{10}/(s+s^{-1})$ and $G_{\rm up}=sD_{01}$ at $t=s^{-1}$.
items.strategy: Invert the SOURCE B1 parameter before using its tensor-square bar formula. Directly check ψM10=M10+(s^-1−s)M01 and ψ fixes the other monomials. Solve c−bar c=s^-1−s in the two charts: c=−s for L10, c=s^-1 for T10. Invert/transposed d gives P01. The actual pairing definitions force Gram S, and multiplying the displayed4x4 matrices (identities on00/11) proves both delta identities exactly as recorded in the finite-witness JSON. The lower highest vector at the mixed weight is T10; its EF norm is[2]_s and actual5 polarization gives s^-1[2]_s=1+t². This checks the precise upper rescaling/adjointbar without asserting that sourceD itself is libraryupper.

items.title: The canonical and quasi-canonical bases need not coincide
items.statement:
In the four-dimensional model of
[[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]] the canonical and
quasi-canonical Fock families coincide on every label.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The rank-one Fock model with monomials $M_{00},M_{01},M_{10},M_{11}$, the source families $L,T,P$ of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and the computed bar matrix and vectors of [[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]].

[F1] Bar and families ([[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]], [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]): $\psi$ is triangular with $\psi M_{10}=M_{10}+(s^{-1}-s)M_{01}$ and fixes the other monomials; the canonical family is the $s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$-chart and the quasi-canonical family is defined by the inverse transition matrix.

[F2] Highest constituent ([[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], [[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]]): the projection $\pi$, the rectified highest label $01^{\uparrow}=10$, and the rescaling $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on the highest constituent with $a=1$.

## Counterexample

Take $I=\{0\}$, $I^+=\{0,1\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$, and retain the mixed order
$(M_{01},M_{10})$ and the notation of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and
[[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]]. There
$$P_{01}=M_{01}+s\,M_{10}=s\,T_{10},$$
because $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$; but
$$P_{10}=M_{10}\neq M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}=T_{10}$$
over $\mathbb Q(s)$. Hence the canonical and quasi-canonical families are
different, and so are the dual-canonical and monomial families. The
highest-component label rectification is $01^{\uparrow}=10$ with
$a=1$, which exhibits the genuine power and label distinction: the coincidence
$P_{01}=sT_{10}$ happens on the rectified highest label, not by an identity of
the two index sets. At $s=1$ the highest-submodule vectors $P_{01}$ and $T_{10}$
agree after rectification, but the full canonical and quasi-canonical families
are still not interchangeable. This is no claim that every corresponding label
differs at $s=1$.

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The two families at label $10$.** In the mixed order the bar fixes $M_{01}$ and sends $M_{10}$ to $M_{10}+(s^{-1}-s)M_{01}$. A vector $M_{10}+cM_{01}$ is fixed exactly when $c-\bar c=s^{-1}-s$. The positive chart gives $c=-s$ and the negative chart gives $c=s^{-1}$; uniqueness follows because a bar-fixed polynomial in either $s\mathbb Z[s]$ or $s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$ is zero. Thus $L_{01}=T_{01}=M_{01}$, $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$ and $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$. Inverting the $L$ chart gives $M_{10}=L_{10}+sL_{01}$, so the transposed inverse chart is $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}$ and $P_{10}=M_{10}$. Linear independence of the two monomials proves $P_{10}\ne T_{10}$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 **The rectified highest-label coincidence.** At label $01$ the same computations give $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}=sT_{10}$, so the two families do meet at the rectified highest label with the power $a=1$ of [F2]; this is an identity between specific vectors, not an identification of the two labelled families. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Conclusion.** Since $P_{10}\neq T_{10}$, the canonical and quasi-canonical families are different over $\mathbb Q(s)$; the dual-canonical and monomial families differ too, because $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}\neq M_{10}$. The highest-submodule coincidence $P_{01}=sT_{10}$ is exactly the rectified normalization of [F2], and at $s=1$ it does not make the whole families interchangeable. [step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Residue translation on small parabolic category-O standards
items.statement: Take $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$. There is only the residue0. The source crystal has component $00\to01\to11$ and isolated10; categorical residue translates of the simples have the corresponding unique heads/socles. items.title: Opposite-parabolic Ringel duality on a finite ideal
items.statement: Use classical $gl_3$, Levi(2,1), $I=\{0,1\}$ and $\Lambda=\Lambda_1+\Lambda_0$; take the distinct-entry regular block. In target tableau order let $A_0=(1,0|2)$, $A_1=(2,0|1)$, $A_2=(2,1|0)$, with highest weights $(1,1,4),(2,1,3),(2,2,2)$. The target standard/simple matrix is $D=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Reverse readings $(2|1,0),(1|2,0),(0|2,1)$ give opposite highest weights $(2,2,2),(1,3,2),(0,3,3)$ and opposite matrix $N=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Verify the semiregular label shift, $F\bar M(A)=\nabla(A)$, $F\bar P(A)=T(A)$ and tilting-standard ROW matrix $N^t$, distinct from target projective-standard rows $D^t$. On the genuine target lower ideal $\Gamma=\{A_0,A_1\}$ the tilting rows are $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$; its Ringel dual is the opposite highest-weight SERRE QUOTIENT, with standard/simple rows $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Simples/canonical classes in the target ideal are unchanged ambient ones, whereas projective/quasi-canonical classes use the standard-flag truncation of the ambient projectives. This gives the actual three-basis finite-ideal dictionary without a false same-downset opposite restriction.

items.title: The degenerate affine Hecke algebra
items.statement: For d≥0 the degenerate affine Hecke algebra H_d has commuting polynomial generators x_1,…,x_d and the symmetric-group generators s_i, with s_i x_j=x_j s_i outside j=i,i+1 and s_i x_(i+1)=x_i s_i+1, x_(i+1)s_i=s_i x_i+1. Its ordered monomials x_1^r1…x_d^rd w, r_i≥0 and w∈S_d, form a basis. Thus H_0=C and H_1=C[x_1]. The evaluation H_d/(x_1−a)≅C[S_d] sends x_j to a+sum_(k<j)(k j), not to the same scalar for every j. Polynomial degree gives a filtration with gr H_d=C[x_1,…,x_d] semidirect C[S_d]; the inhomogeneous cross relation is not a grading with deg x=1, deg s=0.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Move polynomial generators left using the cross relations; braid and commutation resolve the overlaps. For independence act on rational functions with s_i=permutation_i−(x_i−x_(i+1))^−1(1−permutation_i). The coefficient of each distinct rational-function permutation is triangular with invertible diagonal, so the monomials are independent. Verify the cross and braid identities by clearing denominators in two/three adjacent variables. The Jucys sums satisfy the same relations and the quotient recursion identifies every x_j, giving evaluation. This is the explicit rational-operator proof in the affine-Yangian local note §1.

items.title: Type-A nilpotent orbit closures are normal via chain varieties
items.statement: Assume AC and let e be a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex vector space V. The closure X of its GL(V)-conjugacy orbit has a reduced irreducible NORMAL coordinate domain. The orbit boundary has codimension at least2. This holds for every Jordan type, not only the regular nilpotent cone. A complete proof uses the auxiliary chain equations B_1A_1=0 and B_iA_i=A_(i−1)B_(i−1): their actual scheme is a complete intersection, smooth outside a codimension≥2 subset, reduced/irreducible/normal, and its internal-vertex GL invariant ring is C[X].
items.strategy:
Complete local construction and proof in owner-category-o-batch17-vust-local-proof.md §§2–4. ## 2. Auxiliary chain variety and local rank calculation

For the Jordan partition η of e let t=l, q_1≥...≥q_t>0 its column lengths. Put n_i=q_t+...+q_{t-i+1}, 1≤i≤t, n_0=0, U_i=C^{n_i}. Let
M=product_{i=1}^{t-1}(Hom(U_i,U_{i+1})×Hom(U_{i+1},U_i)).
Write its coordinates (A_i,B_i), and let Z be the actual scheme cut out by
B_1A_1=0, B_iA_i=A_{i-1}B_{i-1} (2≤i<t).
There are c=sum_{i<t}n_i² equations. On Z° where each A_i is injective OR B_i surjective, the differential of these equations is onto: at each stage solve Y_i A_i+B_i X_i=the prescribed residual, using a left inverse of A_i or right inverse of B_i, successively after the earlier variables have been chosen. The actual nonradical Jacobian supplier therefore gives smoothness and dimension D=2sum_{i<t}n_i n_{i+1}−sum_{i<t}n_i² there.

This open set is nonempty. Take U_{t-k}=im(e^k), with inclusions A_i and restrictions B_i=e. Both maps have maximal rank and satisfy the equations. The end map θ=A_{t-1}B_{t-1} has typeη. For t=1 take Z=Spec C, θ=0 and H trivial; the zero orbit is normal directly.

## 3. Complete ab-string dimension and boundary estimate

A nilpotent pair A:U→V,B:V→U is the odd nilpotent operator T on U⊕V. The usual Jordan string construction can be made homogeneous: kernels, images and all successive quotient spaces are Z/2-graded, so choose homogeneous complements/bases at every stage. Its indecomposables are alternating a/b strings. Suppressing the b letters gives the Jordan diagram of BA, suppressing a gives that of AB. This proves the classification and finiteness without a quiver-classification theorem. Injectivity/surjectivity are read from the first/last letters; in the relevant dimU≤dimV case, A injective means every string ends in b, B surjective means every string starts in b.

Let r_j,s_j be the numbers of a,b letters in each string, and let a_k,b_k count odd strings of lengthk starting respectively with a,b. Put Delta=sum_{k odd}a_k b_k. A graded Hom between strings has min(L_i,L_j) possible shifts. For both odd lengths the difference of even/odd Hom dimensions is the product of their endpoint signs. For an odd/even pair the two opposite Hom directions cancel that difference; for two even lengths it is0. Hence the superdimension of the full centralizer is (dimU−dimV)². Subtracting the even centralizer dimension from dimGL(U)×GL(V) proves that the pair orbit has half the dimension of the full GL(U⊕V) nilpotent orbit, rather than importing this half-dimension fact.

Also
min(r_i+s_i,r_j+s_j)=min(r_i,r_j)+min(s_i,s_j)
except for equal odd lengths of opposite endpoint signs, when it is larger by1. Summing ordered pairs gives the correction2Delta. The ordinary Jordan centralizer has dimension sum_{i,j}min(L_i,L_j), since a module map between C[t]/t^{L_i} and C[t]/t^{L_j} has that dimension. Therefore, if the pair orbit projects to ordinary orbits C_alpha,C_beta,
dim X_delta=dimU dimV+(dim C_alpha+dim C_beta)/2−Delta.
All stabilizers here are unit groups of finite-dimensional even endomorphism algebras, principal opens in vector spaces, hence smooth connected irreducible in characteristic zero.

Stratify Z by the finite compatible sequences of these pair diagrams. The pair-orbit maps to their ordinary nilpotent orbits are locally trivial smooth maps with irreducible fibers: locally choose Jordan bases by fixed nonzero rank minors; their stabilizer fibers are quotients of the connected centralizer unit groups just described. Iterating these fiber products proves that each stratum Z_lambda is smooth irreducible and
 dim Z_lambda=sum_{i<t}n_i n_{i+1}+dim C_sigma/2−sum_i Delta_i,
where sigma is the final end-map type. Powers of the end map factor through U_{t-k}, so rank θ^k≤n_{t-k}. Thus sigma is dominated byη (equivalently the conjugate-partition partial-sum rank inequalities). The ordinary orbit formula is N²−sum_j q_j², or N²−sum_i(2i−1)η_i. It implies every distinct dominated type has dimension smaller by an even positive integer.

There is exactly one stratum over typeη: each final b-diagram must be filled internally with the n_{t-1} a letters; there are exactly that many, so every row starts and ends in b. Removing the first column repeats this argument inductively. This stratum lies in Z° and has dimensionD. If the final orbit dimension drops by at least4, the displayed stratum formula already gives dim≤D−2.

For a drop exactly2, the prefix-sum expression for orbit dimension shows that exactly one prefix drops by1, so the diagram moves a box to the NEXT row. Analyze one link and remove the first column. If the receiving row was nonempty, the internal filling uses all available a's and every row starts/ends in b; the lower a-diagram is again this one-box degeneration. If a new one-box row is created, exactly one a remains after internal filling. The condition that the a-diagram be dominated by the prescribed diagram with its first column removed permits it only at either end of the last shortened b-row, at either end of the new b-row, or as a separate a-row. The first four placements make A or B maximal rank and either remove the degeneration or pass it down. The separate a-row makes both maps nonmaximal and contributes Delta_i≥1 (there is an a-only and at least one b-only row; for shortened length1 there can be two b-only rows, so equality1 need not be asserted). Induction down the links proves: every stratum outside Z° has dim≤D−2. This is the full two-case/five-placement argument of KP5.4–5.6, including the short-string corner, not a nominal dimension estimate.

## 4. Complete intersection, normality and the actual invariant quotient

The previous estimate gives dimZ=D and no lower-dimensional component: every component of a scheme cut out by c equations has dimension≥dimM−c=D, while the complement strata have smaller dimension. Thus the c generators have heightc. In the polynomial Cohen–Macaulay ambient ring they form a regular sequence: localize at the homogeneous maximal ideal, use the height bound for each prefix (Krull height gives height(prefix)≥c−remaining=k), extend to a system of parameters and apply the actual CM parameter theorem. Homogeneous localization detects failure of injectivity, so this is global. The quotient is CM, hence S2/S1; it is generically smooth R0. The actual R0+S1 reducedness lemma makes it reduced. The unique irreducible D-dimensional stratum over typeη is dense: every other stratum has smaller dimension, while every component has dimensionD, so a second component would have a nonempty D-dimensional open subset outside that first closure, impossible. Thus the reduced quotient is a domain. Regularity in codimension1 plus S2 now makes this domain normal by the actual Serre criterion. This proves irreducibility before using a domain-only normality supplier. This avoids assuming reducedness before applying the nonradical Jacobian clause.

Let H=product_{i<t}GL(U_i). We prove, rather than quote, that C[Z]^H is generated by the entries of θ. First, for Hom(U,V)×Hom(V,U), polynomial invariants under GL(U) are generated by entries of AB. Scalar weights force equal degrees in A,B; polarize and apply the actual Schur–Weyl centralizer to U^⊗k, whose invariant contractions pair each U with a U* in a permutation. Depolarization gives products of AB entries. No general invariant-theory FFT is imported.

Invariants of a rational polynomial quotient lift. Every vector lies in a finite-dimensional stable subspace (bounded polynomial degree); its scalar torus acts diagonally by integral degree weights. The actual Weyl theorem splits the derived sl modules inside each torus weight. Thus finite-degree rational GL modules are completely reducible and invariant quotient vectors have invariant lifts; integration is checked on elementary unipotents and diagonal matrices, which generate GL. This works also for the needed finite-dimensional coefficient modules. Apply this exact invariant lifting successively at vertices1,...,t−1. At the first vertex the invariant generators are A_1B_1 and all remaining matrix entries; on Z the former equal B_2A_2, so they can be eliminated. Continue, leaving only θ's matrix entries. Consequently C[Z]^H is precisely the coordinate ring of the closure of θ(Z). The unique dense stratum maps onto the conjugacy orbit of e (all Jordan bases are covered), so that closure is its orbit closure.

The invariant subring of a normal domain is normal: an element of Frac(C[Z]^H) integral over that subring is integral over C[Z], hence in C[Z], and remains H-fixed. Thus the desired nilpotent orbit closure has a normal coordinate domain. All its boundary orbits have smaller even dimension by the finite Jordan classification and the orbit formula; the boundary therefore has codimension≥2. Neither rational singularities nor Hochster–Roberts is needed.

items.title: Arakawa-Suzuki Casimir operators on tensor functors
items.statement: For gl_N with trace Casimir Ω=sum E_ij tensor E_ji, on M tensor V^tensor d put x_j=Ω_0j+sum_(k<j)P_kj and s_i=P_(i,i+1). Equivalently x_(j+1)=s_j x_j s_j+s_j; these operators are natural and commute with gl_N. For the sl_N Arakawa–Suzuki normalization, if z=sum E_ii acts on M by z_M, the source generators are y_j=x_j−z_M/N+(N−1)/2 and its transpositions are the same P. The sl_N Casimir is Ω_gl−z tensor z/N. Degree zero omits all x_j. Trivial M gives x_j=sum_(k<j)P_kj, with x_1=0.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Expand the trace dual basis and observe Ω on V tensor V is the flip. Subtract the scalar central summand to pass to sl_N: Ω_0j loses z_M/N, while each Ω_kj loses1/N, which the source's added1/N restores. Its remaining shift is (N−1)/2. Read and compare the actual AS2.2.2, rather than identify x and y without this scalar. The universal formulas make naturality and the recursion immediate.

items.title: Nilpotent-orbit tensor covariants extend and polarize
items.statement: Assume AC, e∈End_C(V) nilpotent and d≥0. Every G_e-fixed B∈End_C(V^⊗d) is the value at e of a GL(V)-equivariant POLYNOMIAL tensor covariant Phi:End(V)→End(V^⊗d). Every such Phi is a sum, with invariant scalar polynomial coefficients, of X↦sigma composed with X^h1⊗...⊗X^hd. The extension is proved on the normal codimension-two orbit closure and lifted using finite rational GL complete reducibility; the covariant formula is proved by polarization and Schur–Weyl permutation contractions, not an imported Procesi FFT.
items.strategy:
Complete local argument in owner-category-o-batch17-vust-local-proof.md §5. ## 5. Extension and polarized tensor covariants

Let X be this normal orbit closure and O its dense orbit. Regular functions on O extend to X. Here is the needed Hartogs argument without an imported intersection theorem. For f∈Frac A regular off codimension≥2, put J={a∈A:af∈A}. At every height-one prime J is the unit ideal. If J were proper choose0≠a∈J. In the normal S2 domain every associated prime of A/(a) has height1, by localization, the actual depth-zero criterion and the regular-element depth shift. Finite prime avoidance supplies b∈J avoiding those primes. Since b(af)=a(bf), regularity of b modulo a implies af∈aA. Cancellation gives f∈A, contradiction. Apply coordinatewise to maps into a finite-dimensional vector representation.

For B∈End(V^⊗d) fixed by G_e, define on O the equivariant map g e g^{-1}↦g^⊗d B(g^{-1})^⊗d. It is well-defined. It is regular: on rank-minor charts of the constant-rank powers choose bases of kerX^k, their image/quotient complements and hence homogeneous Jordan top vectors by Gaussian elimination. The resulting Jordan-basis conjugator g(X) and its inverse are regular where the finitely many chosen minors/determinant do not vanish. These charts coverO and the expressions agree by G_e-invariance. Hartogs extends the map equivariantly to X (equality on the dense orbit gives equality everywhere). Finite-degree GL complete reducibility then lifts it to an equivariant polynomial map Phi:End(V)→End(V^⊗d).

To determine Phi, polarize its degree-k matrix input and pair its output with d independent matrices Y_1,...,Y_d by the nondegenerate trace form. This is a multilinear invariant on End(V)^{k+d}; the actual Schur–Weyl theorem identifies all such invariants with permutation contractions. Each permutation gives products of traces along its cycles, by expansion of matrix indices. Depolarizing the k identical X variables leaves cycles consisting only of X (scalar invariant coefficients) and cycles through the Y's, of the form Tr(X^{a_1}Y_{i_1}...X^{a_r}Y_{i_r}). These latter cycles are exactly the trace pairing of Y_1⊗...⊗Y_d with a place permutation followed by X^{h_1}⊗...⊗X^{h_d}. Nondegeneracy of trace therefore proves that Phi is a sum of these operator covariants with scalar invariant polynomial coefficients. Evaluating at e gives only permutation×individual e powers; powers≥l vanish. This proves the FULL converse centralizer identity for every nilpotent type and every d, independently of stable faithfulness.

items.title: The type-A nilpotent pyramid, good grading and Whittaker character
items.statement: Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$ and let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$. Number the boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left, write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for the row and column of the $i$-th box, let $L(i)$ and $R(i)$ be the numbers of its immediate left and right neighbours (or $\emptyset$ if absent), and define the nilpotent $e=\sum_{i:L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g$, $v_i\mapsto v_{L(i)}$. Declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ and let $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0$, $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r$. Then $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$ (largest Jordan block $l$), $\mathfrak p$ is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor $\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak m$ is the nilradical of the opposite parabolic, $\mathfrak g^{e}$ is the graded subalgebra $\bigoplus_{r\ge0}(\mathfrak g_r\cap\mathfrak g^e)$ generated by the elements $e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k}$ for $s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ (where $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$ for $i\ge j$), Put $I_{box}=\{1,\ldots,N\}$, $J=\{(a,b)\in I_{box}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$ and $K=\{(i,j,r):1\le i,j\le n,\ s_{i,j}\le r<p_j\}$. The map $(a,b)\mapsto(\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b),\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a))$ is a bijection $J\to K$. Its inverse takes $b$ to the rightmost box of row $j$ and $a$ to the box in row $i$ at column $p_j-r$. The finite sum $\xi_{a,b}=\sum_{t=0}^{\mathrm{col}(a)-1}e_{L^t(a),L^t(b)}$ equals $e_{\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b);\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)}$; these elements for $(a,b)\in J$ form the same basis of $\mathfrak g^e$ as the elements indexed by $K$. Finally set $\chi(x)=(x,e)=\mathrm{tr}(xe)$ for $x\in\mathfrak m$; then $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character, i.e. $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$. This grading is the type-A pyramid good grading, not the Dynkin grading of an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple; it is the one used for the finite W-algebra of the higher-level Schur-Weyl duality.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Check [E_ab,E_cd]=delta_bc E_ad−delta_ad E_cb and e v_i=v_L(i). Each row is one Jordan string. For Hom between strings of lengths p_a,p_b, the sl2 decomposition has top grading2(p_b−k)≥0 and bottom−2(p_a−k)≤0, 1≤k≤min(p_a,p_b), under the doubled grading. This proves injectivity/surjectivity of ad e in the negative/nonnegative degrees and the stated centralizer basis, rather than importing the Dynkin grading. The column blocks give the parabolic and opposite radical. Since brackets of negative degrees have degree≤−2 while e has degree1, trace([m,m]e)=0. The undoubled source grading has e degree1; its doubled version has no odd degrees and e degree2. For fixed row labels i,j, the right endpoint b has column p_j. Requiring a at column p_j−r to exist in row i is exactly max(0,p_j−p_i)≤r<p_j, the declared K range. This proves the bijection with J. Successive left shifts terminate after col(a) terms, give every row-pair matrix unit of the same displacement, and commute with e by cancellation of adjacent summands and the right-end boundary. The string calculation gives min(p_i,p_j) independent maps per row pair, so these finite sums are the full centralizer basis. The loop consumers use (i,j,r)∈K and T^(r+1), without confusing box and row indices.

items.title: The Casimir and place-permutation operators satisfy the degenerate affine Hecke relations
items.statement: For every gl_N-module M, these x_j and place permutations give a natural commuting right H_d action on M tensor V^tensor d, using the generator-fixing anti-involution to encode right actions. All Coxeter, polynomial commutation and affine cross relations hold. In particular the x_i commute; this is an essential additional check, not a consequence of the permutation braid alone.
items.strategy:
**Given:** $N\ge1$, a $\mathfrak g$-module $M$ with $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$, the natural module $V$, $d\ge0$, and the operators of [[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]] built from the trace-form Casimir $\Omega=\sum_{i,j}E_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}$.

[F1] The operators $P_{ab}$ are the place permutations of the labelled tensor factors; $P_{ab}^2=1$, and $P_{ab}$ commutes with $P_{cd}$ when $\{a,b\}\cap\{c,d\}=\varnothing$ ([[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]], [[thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products]]).

[F2] On two natural factors $\Omega_{ij}=P_{ij}$; more generally, for any triple of factors $a,b,c$ the element identity $[\Omega_{ab},\Omega_{ac}+\Omega_{bc}]=0$ holds in $U(\mathfrak g)^{\otimes3}$, and $[\Omega_{ab},P_{cd}]=0$ whenever the pairs of labels are disjoint ([[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]], [[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]).

[F3] $[E_{ab},E_{cd}]=\delta_{bc}E_{ad}-\delta_{ad}E_{cb}$ in $\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]).

[F4] The Hecke algebra $H_d$ is presented by the Coxeter relations for the $s_i$ and the cross relations $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$, $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$, together with $x_ix_j=x_jx_i$; the generator-fixing anti-involution $\omega$ of $H_d$ is the anti-automorphism fixing all generators, and a left action $\rho$ of $H_d$ defines a right action by $e\cdot u=\rho(\omega(u))e$ ([[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]).

[F5] The Casimir operator acts as an intertwiner and commutes with the $\mathfrak g$-action; place permutations of natural factors also commute with the $\mathfrak g$-action because the comultiplication is cocommutative ([[lem-the-casimir-operator-is-basis-independent-and-intertwining]], [[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The operators $x_j=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, and the identities of [F1]-[F5].

1.1 The infinitesimal braid identities. For distinct labels $a,b,c$ one has $[\Omega_{ab},\Omega_{ac}+\Omega_{bc}]=0$: expanding $\Omega=\sum E_{uv}\otimes E_{vu}$ and using [F3], the double commutator sum splits into terms $[E_{uv},E_{xy}]\otimes E_{vu}\otimes E_{yx}$ and $E_{uv}\otimes[E_{vu},E_{xy}]\otimes E_{yx}$, and the two resulting sums cancel term by term after relabelling; equivalently, this is the identity $[\Omega_{12},\Omega_{13}+\Omega_{23}]=0$ in $U(\mathfrak g)^{\otimes3}$, which is the derivative of the invariance of $\Omega$ under the diagonal adjoint action. Consequently $[\Omega_{ab},\Omega_{ac}]=-[\Omega_{ab},\Omega_{bc}]=[\Omega_{ac},\Omega_{bc}]$. In particular, for three natural factors this is the identity $[P_{ab},P_{ac}]+[P_{ab},P_{bc}]=0$ for the flips. [F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 The Coxeter relations for $s_i$. $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ is an involution; $s_is_j=s_js_i$ for $|i-j|>1$ because the pairs of interchanged labels are disjoint; and $s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$ because both sides are the permutation operator inducing the same permutation of the three labelled factors. [F1, algebra]

2.1 Cross relations. Conjugation by $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ interchanges the labels $i$ and $i+1$ in any operator supported on those factors, so $s_i\Omega_{0,i+1}=\Omega_{0i}s_i$ and $s_iP_{k,i+1}=P_{ki}s_i$ for $k<i$. Therefore $s_ix_{i+1}=s_i\Omega_{0,i+1}+\sum_{k<i}s_iP_{k,i+1}+s_iP_{i,i+1}=\Omega_{0i}s_i+\sum_{k<i}P_{ki}s_i+1=x_is_i+1$, and symmetrically $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$. For $j<i$, all labels in $x_j$ are disjoint from $\{i,i+1\}$, so $s_i$ commutes with every summand. For $j>i+1$, $\Omega_{0j}$ and the terms $P_{kj}$ with $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$ commute with $s_i$, while conjugation by $s_i$ interchanges $P_{ij}$ and $P_{i+1,j}$. Their sum is invariant, so again $s_ix_j=x_js_i$; the two overlapping summands need not commute individually. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Polynomial commutation. Fix $i<j$. Since $x_i=\Omega_{0i}+\sum_{k<i}P_{ki}$ and $x_j=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{l<j}P_{lj}$, the commutator is $[\Omega_{0i},\Omega_{0j}]+\sum_{l<j}[\Omega_{0i},P_{lj}]+\sum_{k<i}[P_{ki},\Omega_{0j}]+\sum_{k<i}\sum_{l<j}[P_{ki},P_{lj}]$. The second sum reduces to the single term $[\Omega_{0i},P_{ij}]$ (all other $P_{lj}$ are disjoint from the labels $0,i$), and the third sum vanishes (all pairs $\{k,i\}$, $\{0,j\}$ are disjoint since $k<i<j$). In the fourth sum only the terms with $k=l$ or $l=i$ can fail to vanish, so it equals $\sum_{k<i}([P_{ki},P_{kj}]+[P_{ki},P_{ij}])$. Hence $[x_i,x_j]=([\Omega_{0i},\Omega_{0j}]+[\Omega_{0i},P_{ij}])+\sum_{k<i}([P_{ki},P_{kj}]+[P_{ki},P_{ij}])$. The first bracket vanishes by step 1.1 with $a=0$, $b=i$, $c=j$ together with $\Omega_{ij}=P_{ij}$; each summand of the second bracket vanishes by step 1.1 for the three distinct labels $k,i,j$. Therefore $[x_i,x_j]=0$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Naturality, commutation with $\mathfrak g$, and the right action. The place permutations are natural in $M$ and commute with $\mathfrak g$; the Casimir operators are intertwiners by [F5]; hence every $x_j$ and $s_i$ is natural and $\mathfrak g$-linear. The relations established in steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 are exactly the defining relations of $H_d$ [F4], so the assignment $x_j\mapsto x_j$, $s_i\mapsto s_i$ defines a left $H_d$-action. The generator-fixing anti-automorphism $\omega$ of $H_d$ (which preserves each defining relation because the reversed cross relation $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$ is also a defining relation) converts it into a right action by $e\cdot u:=\rho(\omega(u))e$; the anti-automorphism property gives $(e\cdot u)\cdot v=\rho(\omega(v))\rho(\omega(u))e=\rho(\omega(uv))e=e\cdot(uv)$. This proves both assertions. [F4, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- The two cross relations are not symmetric consequences of the braid relation: the summand $+s_i$ has no counterpart in the Coxeter presentation of $S_d$, and it is exactly the term responsible for the inhomogeneous filtration discussed in [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]].

- The computation of step 2.2 uses $\Omega_{ij}=P_{ij}$ only on pairs of natural factors; the identities involving the module label $0$ are the universal commutation identities of the Casimir element and hold for arbitrary $M$.

references.title: Tomoyuki Arakawa and Takeshi Suzuki, Lie algebras and degenerate affine Hecke algebras of type A, J. Algebra 209 (1998) 288-304 (complete 16-page arXiv preprint)
references.locator: Lemma 2.2.1, printed p. 7, and its proof: [y_i,y_j]=0 from [Omega_ij+Omega_jk,Omega_ik]=0 and [Omega_ij,Omega_km]=0 for distinct labels, and the cross relation (2.2.4) from s_iOmega_0j=Omega_0s_i(j)s_i.

references.title: Jonathan Brundan and Alexander Kleshchev, Representations of shifted Yangians and finite W-algebras, Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 196 (2008), no. 918 (complete 109-page arXiv memoir)
references.locator: Section 8.1, (8.15)-(8.23), printed pp. 86-87: the explicit checks x_ix_j=x_jx_i, s_ix_i=x_{i+1}s_i-1, s_ix_j=x_js_i for j not i,i+1, s_i^2=1 and the braid and commutation relations, identified as the defining relations of H_d.

items.title: The type-A finite W-algebra and the Whittaker category
items.statement: Keep the type-A pyramid data $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$ of the preceding item and let $\eta\colon U(\mathfrak p)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ be the algebra automorphism with $\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l)$ for all $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie character of the preceding item (so $I_\chi$ is the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$, $x\in\mathfrak m$) and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates. The type-A finite W-algebra is $W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p): [x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all } x\in\mathfrak m\}$; it is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a $(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule (the right action by $u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\eta(u)}$). The Whittaker category $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of $\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every $x\in\mathfrak m$; for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the Whittaker vectors $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M: xv=\chi(x)v\ \forall x\in\mathfrak m\}$ form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes $W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ (proved below): this is the loop or good filtration, not the Kazhdan filtration.
items.strategy: Show closedness of $W(\lambda)$ under multiplication and $\eta$-equivariance of the defining condition; the bimodule structure on $Q_\chi$ follows because $W(\lambda)$ preserves the left ideal $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ by definition. The $W(\lambda)$-module structure on $\mathrm{Wh}(M)$ follows from $[\mathfrak m,\eta(W(\lambda))]\subseteq U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$: for $m\in\mathfrak m$, $u\in W(\lambda)$ and a Whittaker vector $v$ one has $m(\eta(u)v)=\eta(u)mv+[m,\eta(u)]v=\chi(m)\eta(u)v$. The vanishing statement $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0\Rightarrow M=0$ is proved by the Gan-Ginzburg/Skryabin cohomology argument in the next-but-one item; record it here as part of the categorical interface. The dictionary $\eta$ is the type-A $\rho$-shift of [BKHL, Introduction] and is the one used (with the automorphism $\eta_c$) on tensor space.

references.title: Jonathan Brundan and Alexander Kleshchev, Representations of shifted Yangians and finite W-algebras, Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 196 (2008), no. 918 (complete 109-page arXiv memoir)
references.locator: Chapter 3, (3.6)-(3.8), printed pp. 24-25: the nilpotent e, the character chi(x)=(x,e), the automorphism eta of U(p), the ideal I_chi, and the definition W(pi)={u in U(p): [x,eta(u)] in U(g)I_chi for all x in m}; Chapter 8, printed pp. 88-91, for the Wh model and the Whittaker category.
