items.title: Shifted degrees and Garnir exchanges for standard tableaux
items.statement:
In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and
$r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the
Cartan matrix of the regime.

2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition,
then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$
in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and
$S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A partition $\mu$, standard tableaux $S,T$ of shape $\mu$, and the
degree function of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

[F1] The weak Bruhat arrows, the Garnir belt and tableau, the brick notion and
the terminal alternatives are those of
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]; in particular a
tableau below a Garnir tableau agrees with $t^\mu$ outside the belt.

[F2] The degree $d_A(\mu)$, the codegree recursion, the defect and the identities
$d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$, $d_i(\mu)=(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$,
$\operatorname{def}(\alpha)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)+d_i(\mu)+1$ and
$\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$ are the content of
[[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]], including the brick lemma
$\operatorname{codeg}(S)=\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ for a removed brick.

[F3] The KLR generators, their degrees $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$ and
$\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, and the Cartan coefficients $a_{ij}$ of the
cyclic affine type-$A$ specialization are those of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]] and
[[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]].

[F4] Addable and removable nodes are as declared in
[[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **One edge (1).** Delete entries greater than $r+1$ from both tableaux. These occupy the same nodes and have equal degree-recursion contributions, so they cancel and we may assume $r=d-1$. Write $A$ for the node of $d$ in $T$ and $B$ for the node of $d-1$. In a weak edge $B$ is above $A$, and removing $B$ does not change the boundary counts strictly below $A$. Expanding the two recursions therefore gives $\deg S-\deg T=d_B(\mu)-d_B(\mu\setminus A)$. Removing the $i$-node $A$ changes the addable-minus-removable $j$-node count below $B$ by $a_{ji}$: when $i=j$ one loses a removable node and gains an addable one, giving $2$; at a single edge one loses one addable $j$-node or gains one removable $j$-node, giving $-1$; at $e=2$ the two adjacent colors coincide and the two contributions give $-2$; otherwise it gives zero. Thus $d_B(\mu\setminus A)-d_B(\mu)=a_{ji}$ and the desired difference is $-a_{ji}$. [F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 **Reduced words (2).** The KLR element $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})$ is homogeneous of degree $\sum_l(-a_{j_l,k_l})$, where $(j_l,k_l)$ is the residue pair at the crossing after the generators to its right have acted, and the reduced word moves $t^\mu$ to $T$ by successive weak edges; by step 1.1 each edge changes the degree by the negative of the corresponding Cartan coefficient $a_{i_ri_{r+1}}=\deg\psi_re(i)$ [F3]. Summing over the $m$ edges gives $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu}))$, independent of the word because the degree is a function of $T$ [F2, F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **The Garnir exchange (3).** By [F1], $S$ and $T$ agree outside the belt. The prefix shapes immediately before and after the belt coincide for $S,T$, so the outside-label contributions coincide. For belt labels, the rows strictly above its upper row are fixed. Their contribution to each upper-row addition depends only on that node's column, so the sum over the fixed upper-tail node set is identical. For a lower-row addition, subtract the local signed corners of the upper belt row from the actual above-node count. This leaves a fixed external signed-corner count: if the upper row reaches the length of the preceding row, the lost external removable corner and the suppressed local addable corner have exactly the same residue, so their changes cancel in this difference. The sum of that fixed correction over the lower-prefix node set is therefore identical as well. Thus outer contributions cancel in the codegree difference. Translate the belt row indices and residues to the two-row diagram $(m,b)$ with Garnir node $(1,b)$; the calculations below give these residual codegrees. The initial upper head has entries $1,\ldots,b-1$. The Garnir filling puts $b,\ldots,2b-2$ in the lower prefix, $r=2b-1$ at the upper node $(1,b)$, $r+1=2b$ at the lower node $(2,b)$, and the remaining entries along the upper tail. If $e=0$, the upper-belt contents $b-1,\ldots,m-1$ and lower-belt contents $-1,\ldots,b-2$ are disjoint, with each integer appearing once. Consequently the prescribed residue sequence $i_S=i_{s_rT}$ forces every belt label to occupy exactly its node in $s_rT$. That filling has $r+1$ above $r$ in column $b$, so is not standard. Thus no $S$ in the hypothesis exists for $e=0$; clause (3) is vacuous in that extension, without assigning a codegree to a nonexistent standard tableau. Now let $e\ge2$ be finite, and write $\delta_e(t)=1$ if $e\mid t$ and $0$ otherwise. In any standard two-row filling, a lower-row brick occupying columns $p,\ldots,q$ while the upper row has fixed length $x$ contributes $\sum_{c=p}^q(\delta_e(x-c+2)-\delta_e(x-c+1))=\delta_e(x-p+2)-\delta_e(x-q+1)$ to codegree: the addable upper corner has content $x$, the removable upper corner content $x-1$, and the added lower node content $c-2$. In particular a complete $e$-brick contributes zero, agreeing with [F2]. For $S$, the target belt residue word is the single consecutive run $-1,0,\ldots,m-1$ modulo $e$. Every lower brick starting after an upper brick has first endpoint indicator $1$, by comparing the preceding upper residue $x-1$ with the next lower residue $p-2$. Every lower brick has last endpoint indicator $1$: if followed by an upper brick this follows by comparing $q-2$ with $x$, while if it ends the whole belt then $x=m$, $q=b$, and the final prescribed residue gives $m-b+1\equiv0$. Hence every such brick contributes zero except possibly the initial lower brick, whose first indicator is $\delta_e(b)$ since $x=b-1$ and $p=1$. If $S$ starts instead in the upper row, its first residue forces $b\equiv0$, so the same total follows. Therefore $\operatorname{codeg}(S)=\delta_e(b)-1$. For $T$, the lower-prefix additions at columns $1,\ldots,b-1$ occur with upper length $b-1$ and contribute $\delta_e(b)-\delta_e(1)=\delta_e(b)$; the lower node in column $b$ is then added with upper length $b$, contributing $\delta_e(2)-\delta_e(1)=\delta_e(2)$; all upper additions contribute zero. Thus $\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\delta_e(b)+\delta_e(2)$. The matched residual count table is $$\begin{array}{c|c|r|r|r}e&b\bmod e&\operatorname{codeg}(S)&\operatorname{codeg}(T)&\operatorname{codeg}(T)-\operatorname{codeg}(S)\\\hline e>2&\ne0&-1&0&1\\e>2&0&0&1&1\\e=2&1&-1&1&2\\e=2&0&0&2&2\end{array}.$$ By [F2], degree difference is the reverse codegree difference at fixed shape and content. The vertically adjacent residues at $r,r+1$ are distinct and joined by one edge for $e>2$ and by a double edge for $e=2$; hence every row of the table gives $\deg S-\deg T=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$. All signs are accounted for by the explicit addable-minus-removable endpoint count. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **No choice.** The reductions use the finitely many nodes of the two tableaux, the finite belt and its finitely many bricks, and the finitely many residue comparisons; no family of nonempty sets is selected. Hence no choice is used. [F1, F4, given] ∎

items.title: The graded Specht module has a homogeneous tableau basis
items.statement:
Keep the notation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors
$v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with
$a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of
$S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced
decompositions of the same $w_T$, then
$\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\lhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$;
in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is
independent of the choices.

3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ lie in
the prescribed homogeneous components; when nonzero their degrees satisfy
$$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$
Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis
$\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$;
forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the
resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A partition $\mu$, its cell module $S(\mu)=H^\Lambda_dz_\mu$, the
standard vectors $z_T=T_{w_T}z_\mu$ and $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$, and the degree
function $\deg(T)$.

[F1] The module $S(\mu)$, the elements $z_T$, $v_T$ and the degree recursion
are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the Murphy
cellularity and ordinary dominance-raising Garnir straightening are
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] and
[[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]].

[F2] The weak Bruhat graph, the triangularity of the tableau order and the
Garnir/terminal alternatives are those of
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]; standard tableaux
and reduced words for $w_T$ are those of
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]].

[F3] The degree and codegree identities, including
$\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$ and the brick
lemma, are those of [[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]]; the
shifted-degree formulas for weak edges, reduced words and Garnir exchanges are
those of
[[prop-shifted-degrees-and-garnir-exchanges-for-standard-tableaux]].

[F4] The KLR presentation, its grading and the degrees $\deg e(i)=0$,
$\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ are those of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]] and
[[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Ungraded straightening and triangularity.** The cellular Murphy straightening in [F1], in its left version, expresses $z_U$ for any tableau $U$ as a sum of standard $z_S$ with $w_S\le w_U$; row sorting is passage to the parabolic minimal representative, hence lowers Bruhat order; each Garnir replacement raises prefix dominance, hence strictly lowers Bruhat order by the row-boundary rank-count equivalence proved in [F2]. The standard $z_T=m_{T,t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ are independent because they are distinct surviving cellular basis elements, and they span the cyclic module by that straightening. The initial-vector calculation in the Definition gives $e(i_{t^\mu})z_\mu=z_\mu$ and $y_az_\mu=0$. In the fixed BK presentation, $\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_r(i))Q_r(i)^{-1}e(i)$, where $Q_r(i)$ has invertible constant term. Expand a reduced product and slide dots right using the mixed relations: the result is a sum $T_{r_{a_1}}\cdots T_{r_{a_b}}f(y)z_\mu$ over subwords, and the full-subword coefficient is a product of nonzero constants $Q_r(i)^{-1}(0)$. Rightmost dots evaluate at zero. The Hecke quadratic relation and the Bruhat subword criterion reduce each proper subword to $T_uz_\mu$ with $u<w_T$, so Murphy straightening gives $v_T=a_Tz_T+\sum_{S\lhd T}a_Sz_S$, with $a_T\ne0$ for standard $T$. This proves a basis for each selected reduced-word family and also straightens every nonstandard $v_U$ into standard $v_S$ with $S\unlhd U$. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 **Filtered KLR word calculus before a grading on the module.** A dot moved through a crossing becomes the permuted dot plus a scalar term only for equal residues; moving all dots to the right thus deletes crossings in every scalar error. Two reduced words are connected by Coxeter moves. A distant move is exact; a length-three braid changes the product to a polynomial in dots times the remaining word, deleting the three crossings of that braid. A nonreduced word is shortened by bringing a repeated simple reflection together through these moves and replacing its square by its KLR quadratic polynomial. Induction on word length, using the deletion/subword criterion, therefore writes every error as $\psi_uf(y)e(i_{t^\mu})$ with $u<w_T$ and preserves its algebra degree. Acting on $z_\mu$ kills positive-degree rightmost dot monomials. Combined with step 1.1 this gives, without presupposing module homogeneity: reduced-word changes have only $v_S$ with $S\lhd T$; $y_av_T$ has only $S\lhd T$; and if $a,a+1$ share a row or column, $\psi_av_T$ has only $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=s_ai_T$. For the last assertion first straighten below $s_aT$ and use the exceptional-prefix comparison of [F2] to get $S\unlhd T$; equality is excluded because adjacent same-row or same-column boxes have distinct residues for $e\ge2$. Weight support follows directly from $\psi_ae(i)=e(s_ai)\psi_a$ and commuting dots. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **The simultaneous induction.** Assign degree $\deg T$ to the selected basis $v_T$. Prove together, for $m\ge0$, (a) word-change errors at standard tableaux of length at most $m$ have degree $\deg T$, and (b) all dot and crossing actions at standard tableaux of length at most $m-1$ have their prescribed degrees. The base $m=0$ has the unique length-zero tableau $t^\mu$ and no action assertion. For (a), a nontrivial braid error has at most $m-3$ crossings after step 2.1 and the same algebra degree as the original reduced word. Act on $z_\mu$ successively with the at most $m-3$ crossings of each shortened term, expanding after each action in the ungraded selected standard basis. Step 1.1 bounds every appearing standard-tableau length by the number of crossings so far, and step 2.1 gives the corresponding bound after straightening a nonreduced product. Thus before every action the standard-basis lengths are at most $m-4$, and the already proved action assertion (b) applies. No standardness of an arbitrary subword tableau is assumed. By [F3] the algebra degree plus $\deg(t^\mu)$ is $\deg T$. Strict-order straightening and weight support in step 2.1 therefore give exactly the difference formula (2). A sequence of braid moves gives it for any two words. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Dot actions in the induction.** At $\ell(T)=m-1$ write $v_T=\psi_av_U$ with $\ell(U)=m-2$; word changes only add shorter vectors of the same degree by step 3.1. Slide $y_r$ past $\psi_a$. The main term is $\psi_ay_{s_a(r)}v_U$, and the possible scalar error is $\pm v_U$ at equal crossing colors. The dot action at $U$ is homogeneous by induction and, by step 2.1, is supported on lengths strictly below $m-2$, so applying $\psi_a$ to all its basis terms is covered by induction. The mixed relation is homogeneous, so both the main term and the scalar error have degree $\deg T+2$. When $T=t^\mu$, the dot is zero. This proves every dot assertion at length $m-1$. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 **Crossing actions at standard swaps.** If $s_rT$ is standard and has length $m$, the word $s_rw_T$ is reduced, so the word-change assertion just proved at length $m$ and the weak-edge identity in [F3] give degree $\deg T-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$. If $s_rT$ instead has length $m-2$, write $v_T=\psi_rv_{s_rT}$ up to shorter same-weight same-degree errors. Apply $\psi_r$: the main term becomes $Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})v_{s_rT}$, and the other terms are crossing actions at strictly shorter tableaux. Those actions are covered by induction and the dot polynomial by step 4.1 and induction. Homogeneity of the quadratic relation gives the required degree also for this case. [F2, F3, F4, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **Crossing actions at a horizontal or vertical pair.** The four terminal alternatives of [F2] complete the crossing induction. For a distant terminal edge $t$, write $v_T=\psi_tv_U$ up to shorter homogeneous errors, with $|t-r|>1$. Commute $\psi_r$ past $\psi_t$. The action $\psi_rv_U$ is supported strictly below $U$ by step 2.1 because the horizontal or vertical relation persists, so both successive actions are already covered by induction and their degree is the homogeneous product degree. For a two-edge terminal alternative write $v_T=\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_rv_U$ up to shorter homogeneous errors, where $\ell(U)=m-3$ and $r\pm1,r\pm1+1$ are horizontal or vertical in $U$. The braid relation rewrites $\psi_r\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_rv_U$ as $\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_r\psi_{r\pm1}v_U$ plus the homogeneous dot correction. By step 2.1 the first action on the rewritten word is supported strictly below $U$, so all remaining actions use strictly shorter lengths and induction; step 4.1 handles the dot correction. The horizontal terminal base is $T=t^\mu$: step 2.1 makes $\psi_rv_T=0$. The vertical terminal base is the Garnir tableau. Here step 2.1 gives only $v_S$ with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=s_ri_T$, and the Garnir exchange formula in [F3] gives $\deg S=\deg T-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ for every such term. This proves (b), completing the simultaneous induction without assuming the homogeneity being proved. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 **Grading, character and independence.** The weight identity in step 2.1 and the action degrees established in steps 4.1–6.1 show that the vector-space grading is a module grading. Zero images belong to the stated homogeneous components; a degree is asserted only for a nonzero vector. Step 3.1 makes every change of selected reduced words a unitriangular basis change within each weight and degree, so it preserves the graded subspaces while individual $v_T$ may change. Finally the homogeneous basis yields $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_Tq^{\deg T}i_T$ and the construction used exactly the original ungraded left Murphy cell. Every selection is finite and requires no choice principle. [F1, F4, step 3.1, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

items.axiom_use: None: finite integer PBW, crossing straightening, finite rational kernels and the choice-free regular-trace/finite-root-field head helper.
items.statement:
Fix the level-one type-A integer KLR presentation, charge $0$, and finite quantum characteristic $e\in\{2,3,\ldots\}$. Let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field in the specified Hecke regime, let $\lambda$ be the specified partition, and let $S_K(\lambda)$ be the LEFT graded Murphy cell Specht module with its specified initial cyclic generator $z_K$. Then there is a finite-dimensional graded module $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ for the rational KLR algebra, with a specified homogeneous cyclic vector $z_{\mathbb Q}$, and a graded generator-preserving isomorphism $K\otimes_{\mathbb Q} S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)\cong S_K(\lambda)$. The rational module is explicitly presented by the initial weight, dot and horizontal crossing relations, together with one homogeneous rational relation for each Garnir belt. Each of these relations is the unique vector with Garnir coefficient $1$ in the kernel of a finite matrix with integer entries, obtained from crossing operators in the integer row permutation module. It therefore depends only on the integer presentation, not on a choice of $K$ or of a root of unity.

If the specified normalized simple head $D_K(\lambda)$ is nonzero and absolutely simple, this construction, combined with the local cyclic-head descent lemma, defines its initial-generator image line over $\mathbb Q$ up to scalar. The orbit of that image under the finite integer cyclotomic algebra is a lattice of rank $\dim_K D_K(\lambda)$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] gives the affine KLR PBW basis. Dot slides remove one crossing from correction terms, quadratic moves remove two, and three-term braid corrections remove three. Preferred reduced expressions differ by terms with strictly fewer crossings.

[F2] [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] fixes the integer coefficients and the source BK/BKW crossing convention $\psi=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$. This proof uses that convention directly; it does not identify KMR's reversed-orientation crossing with it.

[F3] [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] supplies the LEFT Murphy cell Specht module's homogeneous standard basis $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_K$ and triangularity: for every tableau $T$, $v_T$ is a combination of standard $v_U$ with $w_U\le w_T$ in strong Bruhat order. Idempotents and grading restrict this expansion to the vector's weight and degree.

[F4] The specified initial vector has weight $i^\lambda$, all dots kill it, and a crossing kills it when its two successive entries occupy the same initial row. These are the initial-generator relations in the reviewed BKW construction, not conditions imposed on an arbitrary vector in a simple.

[F5] [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] proves characteristic-zero radical base change by the regular trace pairing, hence descends a rational cyclic module's normalized simple head and its specified generator image, and proves the lattice rank.

[F6] [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]] gives the finite free integer cyclotomic algebra used in step 5.2. The local PBW straightening used before that quotient is integral: its monic moves have integer coefficients, and independence follows by rational scalar extension of the supplied PBW basis.

## Proof

**Given:** The stated level-one integer presentation, the specified LEFT cell module and its initial generator, and F1–F5. No Axiom of Choice is used.

1.1 Put $\kappa=0$ in the residue formulas below. Work first in the affine content algebra $R_{\mathbb Z}$ before the cyclotomic quotient. For each row of $\lambda$, the successive residue segment has a one-dimensional integral module on which its word idempotent is $1$ and its dots and internal crossings are $0$. The KLR relations hold: successive colours are distinct, their quadratic at zero dots is $0$, and a possible three-strand repeated-endpoint pattern occurs only for $e=2$, where its double-edge braid correction also vanishes at zero dots. Induce the tensor product of these segment modules, and shift its generator $m_0$ to degree $\deg(T_0)$, where $T_0$ is row reading. Denote the result by $M_{\mathbb Z}$. [F2, construct, algebra]

1.2 Let $P$ be the Young row subgroup. Choose reduced expressions compatible with the unique decomposition $w=d p$, with $d$ a minimal representative for $S_d/P$ and $p\in P$, and $\ell(w)=\ell(d)+\ell(p)$. F1 then makes the inducing bimodule free over the row algebra on the minimal-representative words. Tensoring the one-dimensional row modules shows that $M_{\mathbb Z}$ has the integral basis $m_T=\psi_{w_T}m_0$ indexed by all row-strict tableaux $T$. Its cyclic presentation is exactly the initial weight, dot and horizontal-crossing relations. In particular all generator-action matrices on this finite basis have integer entries. Put $M_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes M_{\mathbb Z}$; scalar extension gives $M_K=K\otimes M_{\mathbb Q}$. By F4, there is a surjective graded map $\pi_K:M_K\to S_K(\lambda)$ carrying $m_0$ exactly to $z_K$. [F1, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

1.3 Crossing straightening gives a filtration useful below: a word with at most $N$ crossings applied to $m_0$ is a combination of $m_U$ with $\ell(w_U)\le N$. Move dots right, reduce nonreduced words by quadratic and Coxeter moves, compare reduced words, and split off the right row subgroup as in step 1.2. Positive dot powers kill $m_0$; a nontrivial row factor ends in an internal crossing and also kills $m_0$. Every correction has fewer crossings. In particular if $s_rT$ is row-strict and $\ell(w_{s_rT})=\ell(w_T)+1$, then $\psi_r m_T=m_{s_rT}$ plus terms of strictly smaller crossing length, with leading coefficient exactly $1$. If $s_rT$ is not row-strict, its possible leading term is killed by the right row factor and only shorter terms remain. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 Fix a Garnir node $A=(a,b)$ with $(a+1,b)\in\lambda$. Its belt consists of the row-$a$ suffix $X$ beginning at column $b$ and row-$(a+1)$ prefix $Y$ ending at column $b$. The entries in these nodes in $T_0$ form one consecutive interval $J=\{u,\ldots,v\}$: the suffix ends at the last position of row $a$, immediately followed by the prefix at the beginning of row $a+1$. Let $G_A$ agree with $T_0$ outside the belt and fill $Y$ first, then $X$, increasingly with $J$. It is row-strict and nonstandard. This $G_A$ is the nonstandard belt filling used for the rational-kernel presentation; it is distinct from the maximal STANDARD Garnir tableau in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]. [construct, algebra]

2.2 Among ALL row-strict tableaux agreeing with $T_0$ outside this belt, $G_A$ is the only nonstandard one. For columns $c<b$, the upper entry is an unchanged number less than $u$, hence less than every changed lower entry. For columns $c>b$, the lower entry, if present, is unchanged and greater than $v$, hence greater than every changed upper entry. Comparisons with the row above or the row below have the same strict bounds, and every other column comparison is unchanged. Thus only column $b$ can fail. It fails precisely when the first upper-belt entry exceeds the last lower-belt entry. Since each of the two rows is increasing, this is equivalent to every upper-belt entry exceeding every lower-belt entry, and hence to the unique filling $G_A$. [step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 On $J$, the residue word $i(G_A)$ is one successive-residue segment. Along $Y$ the residues increase by $1$; its final node $(a+1,b)$ has residue $\kappa+b-a-1$. The first node of $X$, $(a,b)$, has residue $\kappa+b-a$, and the rest again increase by $1$. Consequently $i(G_A)_r\ne i(G_A)_{r+1}$ for every $u\le r<v$, including $e=2$. This distinctness, rather than any braid normalization, is essential. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

2.4 Let $\delta_A=\deg(\psi_{w_{G_A}}e(i^\lambda))+\deg(T_0)$ and let $T_A^{\mathbb Q}$ be the span of those integral basis vectors $m_T$ for which $T$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt, has weight $i(G_A)$, and has homogeneous degree $\delta_A$. It includes $m_{G_A}$. The use of the entire weight-degree slice avoids any brick-classification assumption. Write $T_A^K=K\otimes T_A^{\mathbb Q}$. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct]

2.5 The vector $\pi_K(m_{G_A})$ is a combination of images of standard basis vectors in $T_A^K$. Indeed F3 gives standard $U$ with $w_U\le w_{G_A}$. The permutation $w_{G_A}$ belongs to the parabolic subgroup generated by $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$, since it permutes only $J$. Every Bruhat-smaller permutation belongs to this same subgroup: choose a reduced word for $w_{G_A}$ in these generators, and use the defining subword characterization of strong Bruhat order. Hence $U$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt. Weight idempotents discard different words, and homogeneity discards different degrees, leaving exactly the standard vectors in the slice of step 2.4. By step 2.2, every other vector of the slice is standard; by F3 its image is part of the standard Specht basis and is linearly independent. Therefore $\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$ is precisely one-dimensional, including the case where the image of $m_{G_A}$ is zero. [F3, step 2.2, step 2.4, algebra]

3.1 For every $u\le r<v$, the image $\psi_r T_A^K$ in $M_K$ is spanned by standard row-strict belt tableaux. To see the support assertion, choose reduced words for all belt permutations using only $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$. Straightening a crossing supported in this interval never introduces a crossing outside it; factoring a right row permutation also uses only this interval. Thus every resulting row-strict basis tableau agrees outside the belt. The image has fixed weight $s_r i(G_A)$, which differs from $i(G_A)$ by step 2.3. Its support cannot include the sole nonstandard belt tableau $G_A$. Hence the entire image has standard support by step 2.2, and $\pi_K$ is injective on its span by F3. [F1, F3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 2.4, algebra]

3.2 If $x\in\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$, then $\pi_K(\psi_r x)=\psi_r\pi_K(x)=0$. The injectivity in step 3.1 implies $\psi_r x=0$ in $M_K$ for every inside-belt crossing. Thus this one-dimensional Specht-kernel line lies in $B_A^K:=\bigcap_{r=u}^{v-1}\ker(\psi_r:T_A^K\to M_K)$. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]

3.3 The $m_{G_A}$ coefficient map is injective on $B_A^K$. Suppose a nonzero $x\in B_A^K$ has that coefficient zero. Choose a tableau $T$ with nonzero coefficient in $x$ whose crossing length $N=\ell(w_T)$ is maximal. It is standard by step 2.2. Record membership in $X$ or $Y$ for the successive numbers $u,\ldots,v$ as a binary word. Unless this word is all $Y$ then all $X$, it has an adjacent occurrence $XY$; that excluded word is exactly $G_A$. Choose such an occurrence at $r,r+1$. Swapping them preserves row strictness because they lie in different rows and are consecutive numbers; it increases permutation length by $1$, because $r$ is in the earlier row. Its weight becomes $s_r i(G_A)\ne i(G_A)$, so it cannot be $G_A$ and is also standard by step 2.2. By step 1.3, the coefficient of $m_{s_rT}$ in $\psi_r x$ at length $N+1$ is precisely the nonzero coefficient of $m_T$ in $x$. A lower-length input cannot reach length $N+1$; a different equal-length input has a different possible leading tableau because $s_r$ is injective; and its correction terms have smaller length. Therefore $\psi_r x\ne0$, contradicting $x\in B_A^K$. [step 1.3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.2, algebra]

3.4 Consequently $\dim_K B_A^K\le1$, while step 3.2 gives a nonzero line inside it. Thus $B_A^K=\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$. Define $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ using the same intersection of crossing kernels over $\mathbb Q$. These are kernels of a single finite stacked matrix with integer entries on the explicitly selected integral row-strict bases. Row reduction over $\mathbb Q$ commutes with extension to $K$, so $B_A^K=K\otimes B_A^{\mathbb Q}$. It follows that $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ is one-dimensional and has a unique rational vector $h_A$ with coefficient $1$ on $m_{G_A}$. Its scalar extension is exactly the Specht-kernel vector with that normalization. This is an explicit rational linear-system construction of the relation, not an assumption that a chosen vector belongs to a rational form. [step 1.2, step 3.2, step 3.3, algebra]

4.1 Every other row-strict belt tableau has strictly smaller crossing length than $G_A$. Outside the belt there are no inversions involving belt entries because the belt interval is consecutive in row reading and its values form $J$. Inside, inversions are exactly upper/lower pairs with the upper entry larger. The tableau $G_A$ has all $|X||Y|$ such inversions, whereas every other filling loses at least one. Hence $h_A=m_{G_A}+\sum_{U:\,\ell(w_U)<\ell(w_{G_A})}c_U m_U$ with rational $c_U$, and it is homogeneous of degree $\delta_A$ by its definition in the slice. [step 2.1, step 2.4, step 3.4, algebra]

4.2 Put $S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}=M_{\mathbb Q}/\sum_A R_{\mathbb Q}h_A$. We prove standard spanning locally. For any nonstandard row-strict $T$, choose a vertical inversion at $(a,b),(a+1,b)$. All entries in its upper suffix $X$ exceed all entries in its lower prefix $Y$. Its Garnir factor $G_A$ therefore satisfies $T=wG_A$ with $w=w_Tw_{G_A}^{-1}$ and $\ell(w)=\ell(w_T)-\ell(w_{G_A})$: reordering the contiguous belt's one-line list from $X,Y$ to $Y,X$ removes precisely its $|X||Y|$ cross inversions, while preserving within-part and outside comparisons. Reduced-word straightening and the relation $h_A=0$ replace $m_T$ by words with fewer than $\ell(w_T)$ crossings, by step 4.1. The filtration of step 1.3 expresses these as row-strict vectors of strictly smaller length. Induction proves that standard vectors span the quotient. [F1, step 1.3, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

4.3 Scalar extension of the rational quotient presentation gives $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}=K\otimes S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}$. Every $h_A$ lies in $\ker\pi_K$ by step 3.4, so $\pi_K$ induces a surjection $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}\to S_K(\lambda)$ preserving the generator and grading. The source is spanned by the standard vectors by step 4.2, and their images are the linearly independent standard Specht basis by F3. Hence this map is an isomorphism. In particular the rational module is finite-dimensional, has its standard basis, and its generator maps exactly to $z_K$. [F3, step 3.4, step 4.2, algebra]

5.1 The rational module factors through the cyclotomic quotient. Each specified cyclotomic relation acts as zero after extension to $K$, because the module in step 4.3 is the specified cyclotomic Hecke cell Specht module. The matrix of that action on the rational standard basis has rational entries; faithful field extension forces it to be zero already over $\mathbb Q$. Denote this rational cyclotomic module by $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$, with generator $z_{\mathbb Q}$ the class of $m_0$. This identifies the required rational initial cyclic generator, not merely the unpointed module's isomorphism class. [step 4.3, algebra]

5.2 If an integer cyclic quotient is desired for F5, take the saturated generator annihilator $I_{\mathbb Z}=\{a\in A_{\mathbb Z}:a z_{\mathbb Q}=0\}$ in the finite integer cyclotomic algebra of [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]]. It is a homogeneous left ideal, and $A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z}$ identifies with the integral orbit $A_{\mathbb Z}z_{\mathbb Q}\subset S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$. Its rational span is the entire rational module by cyclicity, so $\mathbb Q\otimes(A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z})\cong S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ with the specified generator. Clearing denominators in each $h_A$ is also possible, but no unsaturated integer quotient or integral Specht-freeness theorem is needed. [step 5.1, algebra]

5.3 Apply F5 to this pointed rational form and the supplied absolutely simple normalized head. Its radical-basechange proof gives a rational normalized head with the image of $z_{\mathbb Q}$; absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed head differ only by a scalar. Its integral-algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free, with rational span that head, so its rank is exactly the head's $K$-dimension. This establishes the precise requested initial-generator line and lattice statement over arbitrary characteristic-zero $K$. No three-brick identity, unproved R-matrix formula, arbitrary-vector rational form, or change of the specified generator enters the argument. [F5, step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Graded Specht restriction has the removable-node filtration
items.statement:
Keep the notation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], let $\mu$ be a
partition of $d$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let
$i\in I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$. Let $A_1,\dots,A_c$ be the removable $i$-nodes
of $\mu$ ordered from bottom to top, and let
$\mu^{A_m}=\mu\setminus A_m$. Write $E_i:=E_i^{\rm basic}$ for the restriction
functor $N\mapsto e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)N$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]] (equivalently the
$i$-part of the tower restriction of
[[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]). Then $E_iS(\mu)$ has a
filtration
$$0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_c=E_iS(\mu)$$
of graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-modules with
$V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})\{d_{A_m}(\mu)\}$ for $1\le m\le c$.

Equivalently, the restriction of $S(\mu)$ to the previous rank has the
removable-node filtration of [BKW, Theorem 4.11] over ALL removable nodes, and
$E_i$ selects the removable-$i$-node part. No choice is used.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A partition $\mu$ of $d$ with content $\alpha$, a residue $i$, the
removable $i$-nodes $A_1,\dots,A_c$ ordered bottom to top, and the graded
Specht module $S(\mu)$ with its homogeneous tableau basis.

[F1] The graded Specht module $S(\mu)$, its degree recursion and the standard
vectors $v_T$ are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; by
[[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] the $v_T$ form a
homogeneous basis with $v_T\in e(i_T)S(\mu)$ and
$\deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T)$,
$\deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T)$.

[F2] The restriction functor $E_i$, the idempotent decomposition
$\operatorname{Res}=\bigoplus_iE_i$ and the tower induction/restriction
bimodules are those of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]] and
[[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; the type-$A$ specialization
and its Cartan data are those of
[[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]].

[F3] Tableaux, the weak Bruhat arrows and the removable/addable node
conventions, in particular the bottom-to-top order of removable nodes, are
those of [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]; the
shifted-degree and Garnir-exchange formulas are those of
[[prop-shifted-degrees-and-garnir-exchanges-for-standard-tableaux]].

[F4] Over $\mathcal R=\mathbb Z[u,u^{-1}]$ the left Murphy cell has the
free standard basis $z_T=T_{w_T}z_\mu$ and is compatible with every base
change ([[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Over its fraction
field $\mathcal K=\mathbb Q(u)$ the cell-level JM eigenbasis has
$f_T=z_T+\sum_{S\lhd T}b_Sz_S$. Its adjacent-generator coefficients are
$u$ on a row, $-1$ on a column, and on a standard swap are the two
seminormal coefficients of
[[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]],
clauses (2)–(4). These depend only on the two node contents and the relative
tableau dominance. We use its individual-cell diagonalization and generator
formulas, not a global JM label theorem or a finite-$e$ simple classification.
The right-cell formulas convert to left formulas by star, which fixes $T_r$
and the additive JM elements.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The ordered Murphy subspaces over the universal ring.** First work with the ungraded level-one left Murphy cell $S_{\mathcal R}(\mu)$ at the universal Hecke parameter $u$, where $\mathcal R=\mathbb Z[u,u^{-1}]$. List all removable corners as $B_1,\ldots,B_b$ from bottom to top. Define $W_j^{\mathcal R}$ to be the span of standard $z_T$ with the maximal entry $d$ in $B_1,\ldots,B_j$. Each is a free basis-coordinate subspace, with free quotient. If $S\unlhd T$ in the tableau Bruhat order, its prefix of size $d-1$ dominates the corresponding prefix of $T$ by [F3]. For corners of a fixed partition, $\mu\setminus B$ dominates $\mu\setminus A$ exactly when $B$ is lower than or equal to $A$: subtracting a node from a lower row retains one extra node in every intervening upper-row prefix sum. Thus every standard tableau below $T$ has $d$ in the same or a lower corner. This is the direction needed for the bottom-to-top filtration. [F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 **Prove stability generically and descend exact coefficients.** Extend scalars to $\mathcal K=\mathbb Q(u)$ and use the cell-level triangular eigenbasis of [F4]. Step 1.1 implies $W_j^{\mathcal K}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathcal K}\{f_T:d\text{ in }B_1,\ldots,B_j\}$: the triangular basis change and its inverse preserve each such set. For $1\le r<d-1$, the seminormal formula for $T_r f_T$ involves only $f_T$ and, when standard, $f_{s_rT}$. Both have $d$ in the same node, so every $W_j^{\mathcal K}$ is an $H_{\mathcal K,u}(S_{d-1})$-submodule. The action matrix of $T_r$ on the universal $z$-basis has coefficients in $\mathcal R$ by [F4]. Every coefficient exiting $W_j^{\mathcal R}$ vanishes after the injective extension $\mathcal R\hookrightarrow\mathcal K$, hence is zero already in $\mathcal R$. Therefore $W_j^{\mathcal R}$ is a submodule. This proves only stability of the ordered sums; it makes no claim that individual fixed-corner spans are stable after specialization. [F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Identify the generic corner quotient on its standard vectors.** Fix $j$, put $A=B_j$ and $\nu=\mu\setminus A$, and let $T_A$ be the standard filling with $d$ in $A$ and the remaining entries row-filled in $\nu$. For any standard $T$ with $d$ in $A$, deletion gives $\bar T$ of shape $\nu$. On the eigenbasis quotient $W_j^{\mathcal K}/W_{j-1}^{\mathcal K}$ the map $f_T\mapsto f_{\bar T}$ is an $H_{d-1}$-isomorphism: for every generator $T_r$, $r<d-1$, the two contents, same-row/column alternatives, standardness of the swap and relative prefix dominance are unchanged by deleting $d$; hence the two displayed seminormal action matrices in [F4] are identical. The tableau $T_A$ is dominance-maximal among tableaux with $d$ in $A$, since its deleted tableau is row-filled. Thus the triangular correction to $f_{T_A}$ has only tableaux with $d$ in lower corners, so $f_{T_A}+W_{j-1}^{\mathcal K}=z_{T_A}+W_{j-1}^{\mathcal K}$. The initial eigenvector of $S_{\mathcal K}(\nu)$ is $f_{t^\nu}=z_\nu$. If the row-reading index of $A$ in $\mu$ is $k$, the permutation $w_{T_A}$ sends the initial entry $k$ to $d$ and shifts $k+1,\ldots,d$ down by one, and has length $d-k$. The factorization $w_T=w_{\bar T}w_{T_A}$ is length-additive: the $d-k$ inversions involving $d$ are fixed, and all other inversions are precisely those of $w_{\bar T}$. Therefore $z_T=T_{w_{\bar T}}z_{T_A}$, and the generic isomorphism sends $z_T+W_{j-1}^{\mathcal K}$ exactly to $z_{\bar T}$. This identifies the standardized quotient map, not just an unspecified generic module isomorphism. [F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **The integral and specialized deletion quotient.** Define the $\mathcal R$-linear basis map $W_j^{\mathcal R}/W_{j-1}^{\mathcal R}\to S_{\mathcal R}(\nu)$ by $z_T\mapsto z_{\bar T}$. Both source and target are free with these corresponding bases. For each finite Hecke generator, both action matrices have entries in $\mathcal R$, and step 3.1 makes their difference zero in $\mathcal K$. Injectivity of $\mathcal R\to\mathcal K$ therefore makes that difference zero over $\mathcal R$. This is an integral module isomorphism. Base change $u\mapsto\xi$ gives the exact Murphy restriction filtration and deletion quotients over the original field $F$, including singular finite-$e$ parameters and positive characteristic. Because every inclusion was a basis-coordinate inclusion with free quotient, these scalar extensions preserve the entire filtration and its quotients; no flatness assumption on $F$ is needed and no generic denominator is specialized. [F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 **Pass to the selected homogeneous basis and establish the shift.** Return to the fixed graded Hecke–KLR presentation. Its homogeneous theorem [F1] gives a triangular change $v_T=a_Tz_T+\sum_{S\lhd T}a_Sz_S$, $a_T\ne0$. Step 1.1 therefore identifies every specialized $W_j$ with the span of the selected $v_T$ having $d$ in $B_1,\ldots,B_j$, so $W_j$ is a graded submodule. To verify that the deletion isomorphism of step 4.1 is homogeneous, choose compatible reduced words $w_T=w_{\bar T}w_{T_A}$, which are reduced by step 3.1. The grading is independent of this selected-word change by [F1]. The triangular expansion of $v_{T_A}$ has only lower-corner terms besides its nonzero leading term, so its image under the ungraded deletion quotient is $a_Az_\nu$ for a fixed scalar $a_A\ne0$. The previous-rank generators have the same tower images under the transported KLR presentation: the inclusion keeps $X_r,T_r$ for $r<d$; hence its weight idempotent $e(\mathbf i)$ becomes $\sum_j e(\mathbf i,j)$, since both project onto the generalized eigenspaces of those same first $d-1$ commuting $X$ operators. The defining dot formula and fixed crossing normalizing series use only the same adjacent $X$ operators, so $y_r$ for $r\le d-1$ and $\psi_r$ for $r<d-1$ are unchanged. This is the tower transport in [F2], without assigning any simple-module shape from a JM tuple; consequently the deletion map sends $v_T+W_{j-1}=\psi_{w_{\bar T}}v_{T_A}+W_{j-1}$ to $a_Av_{\bar T}$. Rescaling the quotient map by $a_A^{-1}$ gives the homogeneous-basis correspondence. The degree recursion [F1] gives $\deg T=\deg\bar T+d_A(\mu)$, so $W_j/W_{j-1}\cong S(\nu)\{d_A(\mu)\}$ as graded modules. Other preferred words preserve the same graded subspaces and graded isomorphism by [F1]; no word-independence of the individual vectors is asserted. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **Select the removable-$i$-node filtration.** The residue projector $e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)$ on restriction selects exactly the homogeneous basis vectors whose last residue is $i$ by [F1, F2]. Apply this exact idempotent summand to the all-corner filtration of step 5.1. A quotient for a corner $B_j$ of residue different from $i$ becomes zero, while a quotient for an $i$-corner remains $S(\mu\setminus B_j)\{d_{B_j}(\mu)\}$. Removing the repeated zero steps leaves precisely the bottom-to-top sequence $A_1,\ldots,A_c$ of the Statement, with $V_m$ spanned by the selected $v_T$ whose last node is among $A_1,\ldots,A_m$. This proves the asserted filtration and all graded quotients. If there are no removable $i$-nodes the selected module is zero and the filtration is empty; rank zero has no restriction assertion. The entire argument uses finite bases, finite spectra and explicit scalar extension, so no choice principle or cellular head classification is used. [F1, F2, step 5.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Graded Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
items.statement:
In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], let
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$ be
the transported identification of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]], and let
$S_\mu:=\pi(M_\mu)$ be the standard monomial image of the standard Fock vector
$M_\mu$ of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]] under
the projection to the basic module. Then for every partition $\mu$ with content
$\alpha$,
$$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}\bigl([S(\mu)]\bigr)=S_\mu .$$
In other words, the class of the graded Specht module of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] is the standard
Fock vector in the fixed level-one convention. This holds in both branches (C0)
and (CP). No choice beyond the inherited suppliers is used.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The nondegenerate level-one regime, the transported identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$, the graded Specht modules $S(\mu)$ with their
homogeneous standard-tableau bases, and the symmetric level-one Fock model
with its standard vectors $M_\mu$ and projection $\pi$.

[F1] The homogeneous basis theorem gives
$\operatorname{gdim}e(\mathbf i)S(\mu)=\sum_{T:i_T=\mathbf i}q^{\deg T}$
([[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]]). The transported
projective map sends $P(\mathbf i):=R^\Lambda_\alpha e(\mathbf i)$ to
$F_{i_d}\cdots F_{i_1}v_{\Lambda_0}$, since successive basic inductions append
strands, and the canonical restricted-dual map is defined by the bilinear
tensor pairing $\Psi_{\rm can}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$
([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]]).

[F2] The Fock model has nodes with residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for
all partitions, and node action formulas satisfying the quantum affine
relations ([[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]],
[[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]],
[[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]],
[[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]]); the
projection $\pi$ onto the basic module commutes with the field quantum action
and satisfies $E_iM_\mu=\sum_Aq^{-d^A(\mu\setminus A)}M_{\mu\setminus A}$, where
$d^A$ is the number of addable $i$-nodes strictly above $A$ minus the number of
removable $i$-nodes strictly above $A$, computed in $\mu\setminus A$
([[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]]).

[F3] The integral highest weight module $V_A(\Lambda_0)$ and its dual are
irreducible over $\mathbb Q(q)$, with generated highest-weight submodules
determined by the highest vector
([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); the normalized contravariant form satisfies
$B(F_ix,y)=B(x,q^{-1}K_iE_iy)$
([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]); the
transported identification $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ intertwines the
canonical $E_i$ with the Fock node action
([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]).

[F4] The degree identities $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu\setminus A)=h_i(\alpha)+1$ and
$d_i(\mu)=(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$ are the content of
[[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]] in the level-one convention.

[C1] Choice is inherited only through the declared global-basis interfaces
used to identify the integral dual lattice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Evaluate on projective words.** For a residue word $\mathbf i=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ of content $\alpha$, put $P(\mathbf i)=R^\Lambda_\alpha e(\mathbf i)$ and transport it to the Hecke block. Appending the strands successively realizes it as $F_{i_d}^{\rm basic}\cdots F_{i_1}^{\rm basic}$ of the vacuum projective, so [F1] sends its class to $F_{i_d}\cdots F_{i_1}v_{\Lambda_0}$. The generator-fixing anti-involution identifies $P(\mathbf i)^\psi$ with the right ideal $e(\mathbf i)R^\Lambda_\alpha$, and multiplication gives $e(\mathbf i)R^\Lambda_\alpha\otimes_{R^\Lambda_\alpha}S(\mu)\cong e(\mathbf i)S(\mu)$. Thus the defining bilinear tensor pairing, without any Hom-pairing bar on a shifted first argument, gives $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([S(\mu)])(F_{i_d}\cdots F_{i_1}v_{\Lambda_0})=\sum_{T:i_T=\mathbf i}q^{\deg T}$. [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 **The identical standard-coordinate evaluation.** If $A$ is a removable $i$-node of $\mu$ and $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, the Fock formula [F2] gives its removal coefficient $q^{-d^A(\mu\setminus A)}$. The operator $K_i$ on the resulting weight $\Lambda_0-\alpha+\alpha_i$ multiplies by $q^{h_i(\alpha)+2}$. Contravariance of [F3] therefore gives the coefficient of $M_\mu$ in $F_iM_{\mu\setminus A}$ as $q^{h_i(\alpha)+1-d^A(\mu\setminus A)}=q^{d_A(\mu)}$, by [F4]. Iterating additions from the vacuum enumerates precisely the standard tableaux of shape $\mu$ with successive residues $\mathbf i$: at each stage the occupied nodes form a partition, and conversely its increasing filling records the addition path. The product of the node factors is $q^{\sum_A d_A}=q^{\deg T}$ by the degree recursion. Hence the coordinate functional $\operatorname{Std}_\mu(x)=B(x,M_\mu)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Std}_\mu(F_{i_d}\cdots F_{i_1}v_{\Lambda_0})=\sum_{T:i_T=\mathbf i}q^{\deg T}$, exactly step 1.1. [F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 **Equality in the restricted integral dual.** The basic highest-weight module over $\mathbb Q(q)$ is generated from the vacuum by the negative generators, so its vectors $F_{i_d}\cdots F_{i_1}v_{\Lambda_0}$ span every weight space; no assertion that ordinary words alone span the divided-power lattice over $A$ is needed. Steps 1.1–2.1 make the two functionals equal on this field spanning family. Both lie in the restricted integral weight dual by [F1] and the coordinate-functional construction of [F2]; their field equality therefore is equality in that lattice. Under the nondegenerate contravariant form, $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ is represented by $S_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)$, giving the stated equation. It holds in both field-characteristic branches because the homogeneous basis and integral categorical pairing do, and uses no cellular head classification or characteristic-zero based theorem. Choice is precisely the inherited [C1]. [C1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Ariki's canonical basis theorem in characteristic zero
items.statement:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the normalized
self-dual simples $D(\lambda)$ and their normalized projective covers
$Y(\lambda)$ labelled by the crystal $B(\Lambda_0)=RP$ as in
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4):

1. the transported isomorphism
$\phi^{\rm Hecke}:K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)$ sends the class
of the normalized self-dual indecomposable projective $Y(\lambda)$ to the lower
global basis vector $G(\lambda)$ for every $\lambda\in RP$;

2. the transported identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$
sends $[D(\lambda)]$ to the upper global basis vector $G^*(\lambda)$, form-dual
to $G(\lambda)$ under the highest-weight contravariant form;

3. equivalently the lower global basis is the canonical basis of the basic
module $V_A(\Lambda_0)$ and corresponds to projective indecomposables, while
the upper global basis is the dual-canonical basis and corresponds to simple
classes, and the labels are those of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4): the
crystal $B(\Lambda_0)=RP$, with a simple and its projective cover carrying the
same label. The passage from these crystal labels to the
cellular/Dipper--James parametrization of the simple modules is not asserted
here; it is established with the head classification later on this page;

4. specializing the grading $q=1$ via the forgetful maps $\zeta$ of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]
recovers Ariki's ungraded canonical-basis statement, and combined with the
graded decomposition theorem later on this page it gives his ungraded
decomposition-number theorem.

Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers; no choice is
introduced by the transport or by the label comparison.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Branch (C0) of the nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized
self-dual simples and projective covers, and the transported identifications.

[F1] The QG-8 transport identifies the KLR-side canonical data with the
Hecke-side groups: clause (1) transports $\phi$ to $\phi^{\rm Hecke}$, clause
(2) transports $\Psi_{\rm can}$ to $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$, and clause (4)
identifies the transported normalized self-dual projectives with the lower
global basis, the transported normalized self-dual simples with the upper
global basis, and the transported crystals with the $B(\Lambda_0)$-crystals
labelled in $RP$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]).

[F2] The lower and upper global bases, their duality
$B(G(\lambda),G^*(\lambda'))=\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$ under the contravariant
form, and their crystal compatibility are those of
[[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]],
[[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] and
[[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; the KLR
side conclusions are
`thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis`
and `thm-self-dual-simple-cyclotomic-klr-modules-give-the-upper-global-basis`.

[F3] The transport of the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups, its
Cartan and forgetful maps and its dualities along the blockwise graded
isomorphism is the content of
[[lem-graded-algebra-isomorphism-transports-the-graded-module-category]]; the
forgetful maps satisfy $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).

[F4] The Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]), with the
restricted coordinate functionals and the transition polynomials of
[[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]] and
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]].

[C1] Choice is inherited through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Projectives to the lower basis (1).** By [F1] the transported isomorphism $\phi^{\rm Hecke}$ is the QG-8 transport of the KLR-side identification, under which the normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives correspond bijectively to the lower global basis; the transport preserves the classes of the underlying modules and internal shifts, so the class of $Y(\lambda)$ is sent to $G(\lambda)$ for every restricted label $\lambda$ [F1, F2]. [F1, F2]

1.2 **Simples to the upper basis (2).** The same clause identifies the transported normalized self-dual simples with the upper global basis, and the upper family is form-dual to the lower family under the contravariant form by [F2]; hence $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([D(\lambda)])=G^*(\lambda)$ with $B(G(\lambda),G^*(\lambda'))=\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$ [F1, F2]. [F1, F2]

1.3 **Labels and non-assertion (3).** On the KLR side the crystals are constructed from the one-step socle and head operators and identified with $B(\Lambda_0)$; the transport preserves the crystal structure, so each transported class carries its intrinsic label in $RP$ and no permutation of labels is left open [F1]. The identification of these crystal labels with the cellular or Dipper--James head labels is deliberately not asserted here; only the transported identifications of clauses (1) and (2) are claimed [F1, F4]. [F1, F4]

1.4 **The ungraded specialization (4).** The forgetful maps satisfy $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$ and specialize $q$ to $1$ [F3]; a graded composition series of a finite-dimensional graded module specializes to an ungraded composition series with the same multiplicities, and the transported identifications therefore specialize to the ungraded statement that the self-dual projective classes are the canonical basis and the simple classes the dual-canonical basis of the basic module, which is Ariki's ungraded canonical-basis statement [F1, F3]. Combining this specialization with the graded decomposition theorem of this page gives the ungraded decomposition-number statement; that combination is recorded as the pointer in clause (4) and is not used in the present proofs [F3, F4]. [F1, F3, F4]

2.1 **Choice.** The transport functor, the label comparison and the specialization are explicit finite constructions on finite-dimensional blocks; the only choice is inherited through the global-basis suppliers, as recorded in [C1]. [C1, F1, given] ∎

items.title: Graded decomposition numbers equal canonical-basis coefficients in characteristic zero
items.statement:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition
$\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded
composition multiplicity satisfies
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$
where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in
$G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless
$\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded
decomposition-number theorem
$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the
QG-8 global-basis suppliers.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Branch (C0) of the regime, a partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$,
the graded Specht module $S(\mu)$, and the transported identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$.

[F1] The transported identification sends $[S(\mu)]$ to the standard Fock
vector $S_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)$
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]); and
$S_\mu=\sum_\lambda d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ over the restricted
labels, with the same coefficients as the lower expansion, by
[[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]].

[F2] In branch (C0) the transported normalized self-dual simples $D(\lambda)$
map to the upper global basis vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ under
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2)), and the
simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$
([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)).

[F3] The transition polynomials have off-diagonal entries in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ and are supported
on $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ with diagonal $1$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]);
the graded module group is the restricted direct sum of the blockwise groups
with forgetful maps $\zeta$ satisfying $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).

[F4] The graded Specht module and its basis are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the regime is
branch (C0) of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]].

[C1] Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis and Fock suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Transport the Specht class.** Applying $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ to $[S(\mu)]$ gives $S_\mu$ by [F1], and the expansion of the standard vector in the upper family is $S_\mu=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ by [F1]; the coefficients are the transition polynomials of [F3]. [F1, F3]

2.1 **Replace the upper basis by the simple classes.** By [F2] the vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ are the images of the simple classes $[D(\lambda)]$ under the same isomorphism; applying $(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}$ to step 1.1 therefore gives the expansion $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda}d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ [F1, F2]. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 **Read off multiplicities and support.** Since the simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ by [F2], the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in the expansion of step 2.1 is the graded composition multiplicity $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q$, and it equals $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)$; the support statement $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ is the triangularity of [F3]. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 **The ungraded specialization.** The forgetful map $\zeta$ specializes $q$ to $1$ and sends a graded composition series to an ungraded one with the same multiplicities [F3]; applying $\zeta$ to the expansion of step 2.1 gives $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(1)$, Ariki's ungraded decomposition-number theorem. No new choice is made: [C1] is inherited. [C1, F3, F4, given] ∎

items.title: Graded Specht heads classify the graded simple modules
items.statement:
In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for
$\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ the graded Specht module $S(\lambda)$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] has irreducible
head, denoted $\dot D(\lambda)$, and
$\dot D(\lambda)^\circledast\cong\dot D(\lambda)$. Moreover:

1. the modules $\{\dot D(\lambda)\langle m\rangle:\lambda\in RP_\alpha,\ m\in\mathbb Z\}$
are a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic graded simple
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules (equivalently, of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with the
transported grading);

2. in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ one has
$[S(\lambda)]=[\dot D(\lambda)]+(\ast)$ if $\lambda$ is restricted and
$[S(\lambda)]=(\ast)$ otherwise, where $(\ast)$ is an $A$-linear combination of
$[\dot D(\mu)]$'s with $\mu\lhd\lambda$; consequently
$[S(\mu):\dot D(\lambda)]_q\ne0$ implies $\lambda\unlhd\mu$, and
$[S(\lambda):\dot D(\lambda)]_q=1$;

3. in branch (C0), $\dot D(\lambda)\cong D(\lambda)$, the normalized simple
with crystal label $\lambda$ of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4);
separately, after forgetting the grading and converting the ordinary right
modules through star, $\dot D(\lambda)\cong(D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'})^{\theta}$ by
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`. Thus the
conjugate $e$-regular ordinary label occurs with the explicit
sign-automorphism pullback, which reflects residue content and is not an
untwisted same-block identification. The ordinary module dictionary and radical
comparison hold in both field branches; the crystal-label comparison in this
part is the stated (C0) assertion.

Parts (1) and (2) hold in both branches (C0) and (CP); part (3) is stated in
branch (C0), the branch of the decomposition theorem it consumes. The branch
(CP) analogue of (3) is the identification [BK 2009, Theorem 5.18] and is NOT
asserted here. Choice is inherited only through the cited transported
global-basis suppliers, as recorded in the contract.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The nondegenerate level-one regime in either field branch, its
finite-dimensional graded block $B=R^\Lambda_\alpha$ (or the transported Hecke
block), the graded left Murphy cells $S(\mu)$ and dominance order.

[F1] The ungraded cells are the Murphy cells, their form quotients are
absolutely simple exactly at the restricted labels, and these quotients exhaust
the ungraded simples over every stated field
([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]).
Every proper submodule of a nonzero-form cell lies in its form radical;
$[S(\mu):D_\lambda]\ne0$ forces $\lambda\unlhd\mu$, and
$[S(\lambda):D_\lambda]=1$
([[lem-finite-cellular-nonzero-form-heads-purity-and-shared-factor-linkage]]).
The left version is obtained through cellular star.

[F2] The homogeneous tableau basis supplies precisely the grading on these
same ungraded cells
([[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]],
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]).
The restricted labels and order are
[[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]] and
[[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]].

[F3] In both branches the canonical restricted-dual identification sends
$[S(\mu)]$ to the standard coordinate functional $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]).
The restricted coordinate functionals form an $A$-basis and satisfy
$\operatorname{Std}_\mu=\sum_\nu d_{(\nu,\mu)}(q)G^*(\nu)$ with dominance support
and restricted diagonal $1$
([[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]],
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]).
Here the upper bar is the adjoint of lower bar and fixes $G^*(\nu)$.

[F4] In (C0) only, the crystal-labelled normalized simple classes are the
upper global vectors and their multiplicities are $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)$
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]],
[[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]],
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]).

[F5] The ordinary signed-conjugate module and unit-scaled form dictionary are
[[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]],
[[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]] and
[[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]].

[F6] In both branches each graded simple shift orbit has a unique
$D_\psi$-self-dual representative, independently of any characteristic-zero
global-basis theorem
([[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]],
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]]).
On the Hecke side the transported anti-involution is
$\rho\psi\rho^{-1}$; it is not identified with raw Murphy star
([[lem-graded-algebra-isomorphism-transports-the-graded-module-category]]).
Write $\circledast=D_\psi$ and use the shifts of
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

[F7] The projective map sends the word projective $Be(\mathbf i)$ to the
corresponding negative-generator word on the vacuum; these words span the
highest-weight module over $\mathbb Q(q)$. The module map is defined by
$\Psi(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$, where $T$ is the bilinear tensor pairing and
$h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ is the first-bar-sesquilinear Hom pairing
([[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]],
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]).

[C1] Choice is inherited through the quantum highest-weight and global-basis
suppliers; the finite grading and pairing arguments add none
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The intrinsic radical is homogeneous.** For restricted $\lambda$, let $R_\lambda$ be the ungraded cell-form radical in $S(\lambda)$. By [F1] it is the unique maximal proper submodule, and the same is true after scalar extension to the infinite field $K=F(u)$: the Gram kernel extends to $K\otimes_F R_\lambda$ and the quotient remains simple. The same argument also works over an infinite algebraic closure; using $F(u)$ requires no algebraic-closure choice. For $t\in K^\times$ define $s_t(a)=t^ja$ on $B_j$ and $g_t(v)=t^kv$ on $S(\lambda)_k$. The grading gives $g_t(av)=s_t(a)g_t(v)$, so $g_t$ takes submodules to submodules and preserves the unique maximal one. If $v=\sum_{k\in E}v_k$ belongs to this radical, all $\sum_k t^kv_k$ do. The distinct Laurent monomials $t^k$ are linearly independent as functions on the infinite field: multiply a vanishing relation by a large power of $t$ and use the root bound for a polynomial. Thus one can select $|E|$ values of $t$ with invertible evaluation matrix, and solve for each $v_k$ in the radical. It is homogeneous over $K$, hence over $F$, since $v_k\otimes1\in K\otimes R_\lambda$ implies $v_k\in R_\lambda$. Therefore the quotient $\dot D(\lambda)=S(\lambda)/R_\lambda$ has its actual quotient grading and is irreducible even after forgetting that grading. No homogeneity or degree of the cellular form has been assumed. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 **Categorical duality transports to the adjoint upper bar in both branches.** The projective $Be(\mathbf i)$ is $\#$-self-dual: evaluation sends $\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be(\mathbf i),B)$ to $e(\mathbf i)B$, and twisting by the generator-fixing $\psi$ gives $Be(\mathbf i)$ with no shift. Under [F7] its image is a word $F_{i_d}\cdots F_{i_1}v_{\Lambda_0}$, which lower bar fixes since it fixes the vacuum and every $F_i$. These words span each rational weight space. Thus the semilinear projective duality transported by $\phi$ equals lower bar over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and hence on the integral lattice as well; ordinary words need not generate that lattice integrally. Evaluation of a tensor functional gives $D(P^\psi\otimes_BM)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi M)$, so $\overline{T(P,M)}=h(P,D_\psi M)=T(P^\#,D_\psi M)$. Consequently $\Psi(D_\psi M)(x)=\overline{\Psi(M)(\overline{x})}$, the adjoint upper bar on the restricted dual. This uses only [F6, F7], so holds in (CP) as well as (C0), without identifying positive-characteristic simples with a global basis. [F6, F7, algebra]

2.1 **Completeness of the graded list and uniqueness of shifts.** Let $M$ be any finite-dimensional graded simple $B$-module. Its underlying module has a simple submodule, which is isomorphic to the underlying $\dot D(\lambda)$ for some restricted $\lambda$ by [F1]. An ungraded embedding $f:\dot D(\lambda)\to M$ decomposes into finitely many homogeneous maps $f_r$: for homogeneous $a,v$, comparing degree components in $f(av)=af(v)$ gives $f_r(av)=af_r(v)$. A nonzero $f_r$ has zero kernel since its source is ungraded simple, and its image is a nonzero graded submodule, hence all of $M$. It is therefore a graded isomorphism from the suitable shift of $\dot D(\lambda)$. The same decomposition applied to an ungraded isomorphism between two graded lifts proves that they differ by a shift. Distinct labels cannot become isomorphic by [F1]; a nonzero finite-dimensional graded vector space cannot equal a nonzero shift of itself because its finite degree support would have to be invariant under a nonzero translation. Thus the list in (1) is complete and pairwise distinct. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 **The standard-class bar difference is strictly lower.** By [F3], for restricted $\lambda$ the upper expansion is $\operatorname{Std}_\lambda=G^*(\lambda)+\sum_{\nu\lhd\lambda}d_{(\nu,\lambda)}G^*(\nu)$. Upper bar fixes every $G^*(\nu)$ and reverses coefficients, so its difference from $\operatorname{Std}_\lambda$ is a combination of strictly smaller upper vectors. The finite dominance-unitriangular restricted matrix has a triangular inverse over $A$; hence each smaller upper vector is itself a combination of restricted $\operatorname{Std}_\eta$ with $\eta\unlhd\nu\lhd\lambda$. Applying [F3] and step 1.2 gives $[S(\lambda)^\circledast]-[S(\lambda)]\in\sum_{\eta\lhd\lambda}A[S(\eta)]$. This is a statement in the upper integral dual lattice, not in an asserted self-dual lower lattice. [F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **The actual graded triangular expansion.** A finite graded composition series exists by repeatedly taking a proper graded submodule of maximal dimension. By step 2.1 its factors, after forgetting grading, are the absolutely simple heads of [F1]. Their ungraded multiplicities and dominance support therefore give $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\unlhd\mu}c_{\lambda\mu}(q)[\dot D(\lambda)]$. If $\mu$ is unrestricted, every such restricted $\lambda$ is strictly smaller. If $\mu$ is restricted, the actual quotient map in step 1.1 has degree zero and supplies $\dot D(\mu)$ once; ungraded diagonal multiplicity $1$ in [F1] excludes all further shifts of that label, so $c_{\mu\mu}=1$. This proves every clause of (2), without extracting labels or grading shifts from a Grothendieck-group rank count. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **The intrinsic head has zero duality shift.** By [F6] the orbit of $\dot D(\lambda)$ contains a $D_\psi$-self-dual representative $L$. Write $\dot D(\lambda)\cong L\langle r\rangle$, so $\dot D(\lambda)^\circledast\cong\dot D(\lambda)\langle-2r\rangle$; denote this integer shift by $m$. This uses the separately proved normalization supplier, not an inference about a homogeneous cell form or its half-degree. Applying exact duality to the expansion in step 3.1 preserves every smaller label's orbit by the same [F6]. Thus the coefficient of $[\dot D(\lambda)]$ in $[S(\lambda)^\circledast]-[S(\lambda)]$ is $q^m-1$, while step 2.2 and the triangular expansions in step 3.1 make it zero. The simple shift-orbit classes are a free $A$-basis (graded Jordan--Hölder, step 2.1), so $q^m=1$ in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, forcing $m=0$. This proves the asserted self-duality in both branches and finishes (1). [F6, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

5.1 **The (C0) crystal label is the intrinsic head label.** In (C0), [F4] gives $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\unlhd\mu}d_{(\lambda,\mu)}[D(\lambda)]$ with diagonal $1$. Both the intrinsic heads of step 4.1 and the $D(\lambda)$ are normalized self-dual representatives of the same simple orbits, so their bases differ by a permutation, with no shifts. Induct through a finite linear extension of dominance: after the strictly smaller labels have been identified, subtract their terms from the two expansions of $S(\lambda)$. The remaining leading class is both $[\dot D(\lambda)]$ and $[D(\lambda)]$, proving equality and hence graded isomorphism. This establishes only the (C0) crystal-label clause of (3). [F4, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **The ordinary dictionary and Choice.** Independently, the intrinsic nondegenerate form on the ungraded cell head gives its raw-Murphy-star duality by $v\mapsto\langle v,-\rangle$. The Laurent-unit form identity of [F5] identifies the cell radicals and quotients, including the zero case, after every stated field specialization. Through the right-to-left star conversion and involutive sign pullback this gives the ungraded identification $\dot D(\lambda)\cong(D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'})^\theta$ in both branches, with the reflected ordinary residue content described in the Statement. This raw cellular-star comparison is separate from the transported $\psi$ duality used in the categorical duality argument; no equality of those anti-involutions has been inferred. The (CP) crystal-label assertion remains unasserted. All new grading and interpolation arguments are finite; Choice is precisely inherited through [C1]. [F5, F6, C1, step 5.1] ∎
