items.title: Reduction of characteristic-zero simple modules modulo p
items.strategy: Apply [[lem-rational-garnir-annihilator-lines-present-the-specified-specht-generator]] to the specified LEFT Murphy cell module and its initial homogeneous cyclic generator. Its finite integral row-permutation crossing matrices define a rational simultaneous Garnir-annihilator line; the strict crossing filtration proves standard spanning, and the actual homogeneous standard basis proves generator-preserving scalar-extension equality. It factors through the finite integer cyclotomic algebra by faithful rational scalar extension. Then [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] identifies the radical by the regular trace pairing, proves rational radical base change, and descends the specified simple head and initial-generator image. Absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed normalized head differ only by a scalar. Thus the special vector lies in a scalar multiple of this proved rational form. No arbitrary-vector rational descent, KMR brick identity, or ordinary DJ comparison is used in this lattice step. The integer algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free by the integral algebra theorem, spans the rational head by cyclicity, and is homogeneous; hence it is a full lattice of rank equal to the K-dimension. Word idempotents give graded direct summands, whose ranks survive tensoring with F, proving equality of graded word characters. Any other full homogeneous stable lattice has those same word-component ranks; the actual extremal-word character lemma proves G0 injectivity, so its reduction has the same G0 class. No assertion that all arbitrary K-lattices are literally commensurable without a rational/scalar identification is needed. Finally the restricted Specht classes are an A-basis of the UPPER dual lattice, have field-independent characters, and map under the corrected canonical identification to the same pi(M_mu). Character injectivity therefore shows that modules of equal characters over the two fields have equal images under Psi_can. Apply this to J(lambda) and the normalized characteristic-zero simple and invoke the characteristic-zero upper-basis theorem, proving part(3). No new choice beyond the declared sources.

items.title: Positive-characteristic Specht head and cyclotomic crystal labels agree
items.statement: In the positive-characteristic nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized cellular head dotD(lambda) for each restricted partition lambda is isomorphic, with shift zero, to the normalized simple of the same right crystal label lambda. The reduction J(lambda) of the characteristic-zero normalized simple contains that crystal-labelled simple once, and has no constituents with cellular labels not dominated by lambda. Its G0 class is invariant under finite-module diagram duality. This proves the CP label comparison needed for the crystal-labelled adjustment matrix; it is not a positive-characteristic global-basis identification.
items.strategy:
Now let J(lambda) be the reduction of the characteristic-zero normalized simple of crystal label lambda, constructed using a rational Specht-generator lattice. Its graded word character equals that of the characteristic-zero simple. Choose an extremal word of this common character. In characteristic zero the reconstruction label is lambda; in positive characteristic the same word gives the same canonical B(Lambda) label. The displayed quotient is1 for the characteristic-zero simple, hence [J(lambda):D_crystal(lambda)]_q=1 in positive characteristic.

Independently, the corrected canonical Fock comparison and the upper expansion identify [J(lambda)] with the inverse image of the characteristic-zero upper vector. The restricted upper-transition minor is dominance-unitriangular. Invert it over Z[q,q^{-1}] and use the ACTUAL positive-characteristic cellular-head triangular expansion of restricted Specht classes. This gives [J(lambda)]=[D_cell(lambda)]+sum_{nu<lambda}a_nu(q)[D_cell(nu)]. These coefficients are the actual composition multiplicities because J(lambda) is a module; there is no asserted positivity from matrix inversion alone. Induct over a finite dominance refinement in the fixed root degree. Assume D_cell(nu)=D_crystal(nu) for the smaller labels. Since different crystal labels give different simple orbits, D_crystal(lambda) cannot be any smaller D_cell(nu). Its occurrence in J(lambda) therefore forces D_cell(lambda)=D_crystal(lambda). The coefficient1 forces shift0 as both chosen representatives are self-dual. This proves the CP label comparison before defining adjustment polynomials in the crystal-labelled basis.

The characteristic-zero simple D(lambda) is normalized for finite vector duality, so each word component e(nu)D(lambda) has a symmetric graded dimension: its Laurent polynomial is unchanged by v -> v^{-1}. The constructed J(lambda) has exactly the same graded word character. The descended generator-fixing anti-involution fixes every word idempotent; hence e(nu)D_psi J(lambda) is the graded vector dual of e(nu)J(lambda), and its graded dimension is the same symmetric polynomial. Therefore D_psi J(lambda) and J(lambda) have identical word characters. The completed local extremal-word character detection proves G0 character injectivity over the actual positive-characteristic field, so [D_psi J(lambda)]=[J(lambda)]. This proves bar invariance of its CLASS; no self-dual stable integral lattice is asserted.

items.title: The graded adjustment polynomials in positive characteristic
items.statement:
In branch (CP) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the reduced modules $J(
u)$ of [[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]] and the normalized simples $D(\lambda)$ with crystal label $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ of the general-field normalization/crystal clauses of [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] and [[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]] (in branch (C0) these are the heads of the graded Specht modules by [[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (3)), define the **graded adjustment polynomials** $a_{\lambda,
u}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ for $\lambda,
u\in RP_\alpha$ by $$[J(
u)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,
u}(q)[D(\lambda)]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad a_{\lambda,
u}(q)=[J(
u):D(\lambda)]_q .$$ Then the matrix $(a_{\lambda,
u})$ is the graded adjustment matrix; its entries are bar-invariant, have nonnegative integer coefficients, satisfy $a_{
u,
u}(q)=1$ and vanish unless $\lambda\unlhd
u$ (dominance); equivalently $a_{\lambda,
u}$ is the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in $(\Psi_{m can}^{m Hecke})^{-1}(D_
u)$.

**Source comparison (recorded, not used).** For level one and $\xi=1$ the source states that this adjustment matrix specializes at $q=1$ to the adjustment matrix of James; that degenerate comparison lies outside the nondegenerate branch of this page and is deferred (see the batch coverage record). No choice is used in the definition.
items.strategy: Expand the actual finite-dimensional J(nu) in the shift-orbit basis of normalized positive-characteristic simples; this uniquely defines the Laurent coefficients and makes their coefficients nonnegative integers. The general-field cover/duality/crystal suppliers normalize these simples; the local CP head/crystal lemma identifies their labels with the cellular-head labels, without using the characteristic-zero-only global theorem in CP. The local CP comparison proves J(nu)=D(nu)+terms with smaller labels, giving diagonal1 and dominance support. Bar invariance follows from WORD CHARACTERS: the characteristic-zero normalized simple is finite-dual self-dual, so each word graded dimension is symmetric in q. J(nu) has this same character, and D_psi J(nu) has the inverted character, hence the same one. The actual extremal-word character detection implies equality of their G0 classes. Applying duality to the expansion fixes every normalized simple and inverts q, so uniqueness gives a(q)=a(q^-1). No self-dual stable integral lattice, field-bar compatibility of an unspecified form, or positive-characteristic global-basis theorem is assumed. The source's degenerate comparison remains recorded outside this page's parameter branch. No new choice.

items.title: Canonical bases do not solve arbitrary positive-characteristic decomposition numbers
items.statement: The characteristic-zero theorems of this page ([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]) compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization [[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]] reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the boundary recorded in [[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]] and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
items.strategy: Compare exactly what the two cited results determine: the characteristic-zero identifications compute $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q$ as $d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$, while the positive-characteristic factorization leaves the adjustment coefficients $a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)$ undetermined beyond bar-invariance, nonnegativity, unitriangularity and the dominance support of [[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]. The source's announced specialization to James's matrix concerns the degenerate parameter and is outside this page's regime (recorded in the coverage). No claim of a general positive-characteristic formula is made. Provenance: statement literature-derived; the remark is not consumed to prove any replacement.

items.title: Projective and simple Grothendieck classes in a small non-semisimple block
items.statement: Take $F=\mathbb C$, $\xi=-1$ (so $e=2$), level one $\Lambda_0$ and $d=2$. Then $H^\Lambda_2=H_{\mathbb C,-1}(S_2)$ with $T_1^2=-2T_1-1$, i.e. $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra is $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ with $t=T_1+1$, a local algebra whose unique simple is $D=\mathbb C$ with $t$ acting as $0$, and whose regular module is the unique indecomposable projective $P=H^\Lambda_2$. Both partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$ convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$; its transported grading has $\deg t=2$ (the KLR block is the rank-two $e=2$ block $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg y_2=2$). The graded Specht modules are the one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is $0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so $$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$ The restricted label is $(1,1)$ (since $(1,1)$ is $2$-restricted and $(2)$ is not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and $\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence under the transported identifications of [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] $$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$ The graded Cartan pairing of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] has $h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$, while the graded composition multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ (ungraded value $2$). Thus the projective class $[P]$ is not a simple class, and the two bases are dual to each other under $h$ without being equal as classes. All computations are finite and explicit; choice is inherited only through the transported identifications cited.
items.strategy: Compute in the algebra: $T_1^2=(\xi-1)T_1+\xi=-2T_1-1$ gives $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ is local with radical $(t)$ and unique simple $D=\mathbb C$, and the regular module is the unique indecomposable projective because a local algebra has a unique simple and its regular module is projective; the graded composition series follows from $tP\cong D\{2\}$ (multiplication by $t$ shifts degree by $2$) and $P\cong D\oplus tP$ as graded vector spaces. The block statement uses the residue-content computation: nodes of $(2)$ have residues $0,1$ and nodes of $(1,1)$ have residues $0,-1\equiv1$, so both lie in the block of content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1=\alpha_1+\alpha_0$; the transported grading is [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock identities are the explicit $e=2$ computation of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] (its recorded $e=2$ example), the graded Specht degrees are read from the degree recursion of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] (the unique tableau of $(2)$ has degree $d_A(2)=1$: the addable $1$-node $(2,1)$ lies strictly below the removable node $(1,2)$, and there is no removable $1$-node below it), and the projective/simple identifications are [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]. The pairing values are read from $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,D)=\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,P)=1+q^2$ (endomorphisms are the identity and multiplication by $t$, of degree $2$). No choice.

items.title: Specializing the grading variable to one forgets graded decomposition information
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the Fock/global-basis and graded-decomposition identifications used below; the explicit finite block and polynomial calculations make no additional choices.

The claim under refutation is that specializing the grading variable $q$ to
$1$ determines the graded decomposition data: that the forgetful map is
injective on the graded Grothendieck classes of the block, or equivalently that
the graded transition polynomials, graded Cartan entries and shift classes are
recovered from their values at $q=1$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume the inherited AC above. Use the example's field $\mathbb C$, Hecke parameter $\xi=-1$, level-one weight $\Lambda_0$ and rank $2$, so $e=2$ and the block has content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$. The symbol $q$ is the formal grading variable, distinct from the numerical Hecke parameter $\xi$.

[F1] In the example's block $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$, $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, with the graded Cartan pairing and shift action there recorded
([[ex-projective-versus-simple-grothendieck-classes-in-a-small-block]]).

[F2] The level-one transition polynomials in the $e=2$ case are $d_{(1,1),(1,1)}(q)=1$ and $d_{(1,1),(2)}(q)=q$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]).

[F3] The graded decomposition theorem identifies the graded multiplicities with the transition polynomials
([[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]).

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The polynomials and the class $[P]$.** In $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ the elements $1+q^2$ and $2$ differ (their difference $q^2-1$ is nonzero) while $(1+q^2)|_{q=1}=2$; multiplying by the nonzero class $[D]$ gives distinct classes $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$ and $2[D]$ in the free $A$-module $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1})$, whose images under the forgetful map $\zeta$ (which satisfies $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$) both equal $2[D]$ [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] [F1]. [F1]

1.2 **The Specht classes and the transition polynomials.** The example computes $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, which are distinct because $q\ne1$; the forgetful map sends both to $[D]$. The corresponding transition polynomials are $d_{(1,1),(1,1)}(q)=1$ and $d_{(1,1),(2)}(q)=q$ in the recorded $e=2$ Fock computation, distinct in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and equal at $q=1$ ([[ex-projective-versus-simple-grothendieck-classes-in-a-small-block]], [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]) [F2]. [F1, F2]

2.1 **Conclusion.** By the graded decomposition theorem the classes are read through the transition polynomials, so the failure above is exactly the statement that the specialization $q\mapsto1$ loses the graded multiplicities and shift data ([[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]). The displayed finite block and polynomial computations introduce no new choice; AC is inherited only through the invoked Fock/global-basis and graded-decomposition identifications. [F1, F2, F3] ∎

title: Kronecker Coefficients and Internal Products

items.title: Kronecker coefficients and the internal tensor product
items.statement: Fix n >= 0 and work over C. For partitions lambda, mu, nu of n the diagonal tensor product S^lambda (x) S^mu is a finite-dimensional complex S_n-module; by Maschke's theorem it is completely reducible, and by the classification of complex irreducibles of S_n the Specht modules S^nu (nu |- n) are a complete set of pairwise inequivalent irreducibles. Let (S^lambda (x) S^mu)_{(S^nu)} be the isotypic component of type S^nu and put g(lambda,mu,nu) := dim (S^lambda (x) S^mu)_{(S^nu)} / dim S^nu; equivalently g(lambda,mu,nu) is the multiplicity of S^nu in S^lambda (x) S^mu. Call (lambda,mu) -> S^lambda (x) S^mu the internal (Kronecker) product of S_n-representations. Unlike the outer induction product this operation keeps the rank: both inputs and the output are S_n-modules of the same degree n, and it is never the same operation as Ind_{S_a x S_b}^{S_{a+b}}.
items.strategy: Complete reducibility comes from complex Maschke applied to the finite-dimensional S_n-module S^lambda (x) S^mu; the classification and pairwise inequivalence of the S^nu make the isotypic component decomposition available. Well-definedness of the multiplicity is canonical: the isotypic component of a completely reducible module is defined as the sum of all irreducible submodules equivalent to S^nu, so it does not depend on a chosen decomposition, and dim S^nu > 0 because S^nu is irreducible. The contrast with the outer product is prose only and creates no logical dependency; the outer induction product is not used.
items.axiom_use: None: the argument is finite-dimensional complex representation theory of a finite group and is choice-free (complex Maschke and the Specht classification are choice-free in the cited suppliers).

items.title: Complex Specht modules are self-dual with real-valued characters
items.statement: For every lambda |- n the complex Specht module S^lambda carries a nondegenerate symmetric S_n-invariant bilinear form b(x,y) = sum_T x_T y_T (coefficientwise product in the tabloid basis), so v -> b(v,-) is an isomorphism of C S_n-modules S^lambda -> (S^lambda)^*; equivalently S^lambda is self-dual. Consequently chi^lambda(g^{-1}) = chi^lambda(g), i.e. every irreducible character of S_n is real-valued.
items.strategy: The coefficientwise product b is symmetric, bilinear and invariant because S_n permutes the tabloid basis. It is nondegenerate on the tabloid module M^lambda. Every polytabloid has integer tabloid coefficients and is fixed by coefficientwise conjugation; conjugating an arbitrary complex linear combination of these generators gives another such combination, so S^lambda is stable under conjugation; writing H(x,y) = sum_T conj(x_T) y_T for the published invariant Hermitian form (which the previous item proves to be nondegenerate on S^lambda), we have b(x,y) = H(conj(x), y) for x,y in S^lambda, and conj(S^lambda) = S^lambda. For nonzero x in S^lambda, conj(x) is also a nonzero vector of S^lambda, so nondegeneracy of H supplies y in S^lambda with H(conj(x),y) != 0; hence b is nondegenerate on S^lambda. Invariance of b gives equivariance of v -> b(v,-) with the dual action (g.f)(w) = f(g^{-1}w); nondegeneracy plus finite dimension makes it an isomorphism. Finally chi_{(S^lambda)^*}(g) = conj(chi^lambda(g)) by the tensor/dual character theorem, so chi^lambda(g) = chi^lambda(g^{-1}) = conj(chi^lambda(g)) is real.
items.axiom_use: None: the tabloid form, conjugation in the tabloid basis and the character comparison are finite-dimensional and choice-free.

items.title: The Kronecker coefficient is a three-character inner product
items.statement: For all lambda,mu,nu |- n, g(lambda,mu,nu) = <chi^lambda chi^mu, chi^nu> = (1/n!) sum_{sigma in S_n} chi^lambda(sigma) chi^mu(sigma) chi^nu(sigma), where the sum uses the real-valuedness of the irreducible characters (no conjugation on the third factor).
items.strategy: The character of a tensor product is the pointwise product, so S^lambda (x) S^mu has character chi^lambda chi^mu. For a finite-dimensional completely reducible module with character phi the multiplicity of the irreducible character chi^nu equals <phi, chi^nu>, computed by the intertwiner-dimension formula together with the orthonormality of irreducible characters on S_n. Finally chi^nu(g^{-1}) = conj(chi^nu(g)) by the dual-character formula and chi^nu(g^{-1}) = chi^nu(g) by self-duality, so the inner product can be written as the plain average of the triple product.
items.axiom_use: None: finite-dimensional character theory over C.

items.title: Kronecker coefficients are nonnegative integers with full S_3 and conjugation symmetries
items.statement: For all lambda,mu,nu |- n: (a) g(lambda,mu,nu) is a nonnegative integer; (b) g(lambda,mu,nu) is invariant under every permutation of lambda,mu,nu; (c) conjugating exactly two of the three partitions preserves the coefficient: g(lambda,mu,nu) = g(lambda',mu',nu) = g(lambda',mu,nu') = g(lambda,mu',nu'). No positive combinatorial rule is asserted.
items.strategy: (a) is the multiplicity definition; the character formula expresses it as a nonnegative integer. (b) follows from the symmetric form of the three-character average together with commutativity of pointwise multiplication and real-valuedness of the three characters. (c) uses S^{lambda'} = S^lambda (x) sgn from the sign-twist/omega item: S^{lambda'} (x) S^{mu'} = (S^lambda (x) S^mu) (x) (sgn (x) sgn) and sgn (x) sgn is the trivial representation, so the tensor product is unchanged; the multiplicity of S^{nu'} (respectively S^nu) in it equals that of S^nu (respectively S^{nu'}) because sgn is one-dimensional, giving the three displayed equalities.
items.axiom_use: None.

items.title: The internal (Kronecker) product on symmetric functions
items.statement: Let ch: R_S -> Lambda be the Frobenius characteristic, a degree-preserving ring isomorphism from the graded character ring of the symmetric groups onto the stable symmetric-function ring. For f in Lambda^m and g in Lambda^n define f * g := ch( ch^{-1}(f) . ch^{-1}(g) ) if m = n, where the dot is the pointwise (internal tensor) product of class functions, and f * g := 0 if m != n; extend bilinearly. Then * is a degree-preserving, commutative, associative, bilinear product on Lambda with degreewise unit h_n = s_(n) = ch(trivial character of S_n) on Lambda^n (h_0 = 1); the direct sum Lambda has no global unit for *, and for partitions lambda,mu of n, s_lambda * s_mu = sum_nu g(lambda,mu,nu) s_nu.
items.strategy: Closure of R(S_n) under the pointwise product: honest characters of S_n multiply to the character of the tensor product of the corresponding representations, and virtual characters are integral combinations, so the product of two elements of R(S_n) lies in R(S_n). Hence the transport through the graded isomorphism ch is well defined and inherits bilinearity, commutativity and associativity from pointwise multiplication. The Schur expansion follows from ch(chi^lambda) = s_lambda and the definition of g. On Lambda^n the trivial character is the unit for pointwise multiplication, so its characteristic h_n = s_(n) is the internal-product unit. Every element of the graded direct sum has finite degree support; for a degree n outside that support its internal product with the nonzero h_n is zero, so it cannot be a global unit. In particular the ordinary-product unit 1 in degree zero is not a unit for * on positive degrees.
items.axiom_use: None: the transport uses the choice-free Frobenius characteristic isomorphism.

items.title: Power sums diagonalize the internal product
items.statement: For partitions rho,sigma of n one has p_rho * p_sigma = delta_{rho,sigma} z_rho p_rho, where z_rho = prod_i i^{m_i(rho)} m_i(rho)!; consequently s_lambda * s_mu = sum_{nu |- n} g(lambda,mu,nu) s_nu. The internal product of symmetric functions is therefore diagonal in the power-sum basis and has integer structure constants (the Kronecker coefficients) in the Schur basis.
items.strategy: Let 1_rho denote the class function that is 1 on the conjugacy class of cycle type rho and 0 elsewhere. The characteristic map gives ch(1_rho) = p_rho / z_rho, and class functions multiply pointwise: 1_rho . 1_sigma = delta_{rho,sigma} 1_rho. Transporting through the internal product of symmetric functions gives (p_rho/z_rho)*(p_sigma/z_sigma) = delta_{rho,sigma} p_rho/z_rho, and bilinearity gives p_rho * p_sigma = delta_{rho,sigma} z_rho p_rho. The Schur form is the definition of g together with ch(chi^lambda) = s_lambda.
items.axiom_use: None.

items.title: First-row padding of a partition
items.statement: For a partition alpha and an integer n, define alpha[n] := (n - |alpha|, alpha_1, alpha_2, ...) whenever n >= |alpha| + alpha_1; the displayed sequence is then a partition of n, and below the threshold it is not a partition (the first part is smaller than the second, or negative). The threshold |alpha| + alpha_1 is exact. This notation is neutral: it records no constancy and is shared with the FI-module and representation-stability developments.
items.strategy: Weak decrease of (n - |alpha|, alpha_1, alpha_2, ...) is equivalent to n - |alpha| >= alpha_1, i.e. n >= |alpha| + alpha_1, because alpha itself is weakly decreasing; conversely n < |alpha| + alpha_1 makes the first entry smaller than alpha_1 (when alpha is nonempty) so the sequence is not a partition. The empty partition case alpha = empty gives alpha[n] = (n).
items.axiom_use: None: finite arithmetic with partitions.

items.title: Padded Kronecker coefficient sequences
items.statement: Let alpha,beta,gamma be partitions and let n_0 := max{|alpha|+alpha_1, |beta|+beta_1, |gamma|+gamma_1}. For integers n >= n_0 all three padded sequences alpha[n], beta[n], gamma[n] are partitions of n, and one defines g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) := g(alpha[n], beta[n], gamma[n]). Below n_0 the notation is undefined because at least one padded sequence is not a partition. This definition asserts no eventual constancy; Murnaghan stability is a theorem about this sequence proved elsewhere.
items.strategy: On the common domain each alpha[n] is a partition of n by the preceding item, so g_n is the already-defined Kronecker coefficient of three partitions of n; the maximum threshold is exactly where the common domain starts. No well-definedness beyond this is claimed and no limit is taken.
items.axiom_use: None.

items.title: Littlewood's identity - the internal product against an outer product
items.statement: For partitions lambda |- n, tau |- r and theta |- n - r, Littlewood's identity holds in Lambda^n: s_lambda * (s_tau s_theta) = sum_{alpha |- r, beta |- n-r} c^lambda_{alpha,beta} (s_alpha * s_tau)(s_beta * s_theta), with c^lambda_{alpha,beta} the Littlewood-Richardson coefficient. Both sides have degree n and the sum is finite.
items.strategy: Work with class functions and pass to symmetric functions only at the end. Let H <= S_n be the two-block subgroup S_r x S_{n-r}. By the outer Littlewood-Richardson rule, Ind_H^{S_n}(S^alpha (x) S^beta) = sum_lambda c^lambda_{alpha,beta} S^lambda, so Frobenius reciprocity gives the restriction multiplicity [Res_H chi^lambda : chi^alpha (x) chi^beta] = c^lambda_{alpha,beta}. Frobenius' formula writes the induced character chi^tau o chi^theta at sigma as a sum over cosets of the values at x^{-1} sigma x, and chi^lambda(sigma) = chi^lambda(x^{-1} sigma x) because chi^lambda is a class function. Multiplying pointwise and using the restriction expansion of chi^lambda at every coset term that lies in H turns the product into sum_{alpha,beta} c^lambda_{alpha,beta} Ind_H^{S_n}((chi^alpha . chi^tau) (x) (chi^beta . chi^theta)). Applying the characteristic map, which preserves outer products and sends chi^mu to s_mu, and using that * is defined by transporting pointwise products gives the stated identity.
items.axiom_use: None: induction, Frobenius reciprocity and the outer LR rule are choice-free in the cited suppliers.

items.title: The Kronecker reduction lemma of Pak and Panova
items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge0$, and let $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n$ have lengths at most $\ell$. Read missing parts as zero and put $s:=n-\nu_1$, with $\nu_1=0$ for the empty partition.

**(i)** If $|\lambda_i-\mu_i|>s$ for some $i\le\ell$, then $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=0$.

**(ii)** Otherwise put $\rho:=\lambda\cap\mu$, $\omega:=\lambda\cup\mu$, $\omega_{\ell+1}:=0$, and define
$$\delta_i:=\max\{0,\rho_i-\omega_{i+1}-2s\},\qquad D_j:=\sum_{i=j}^{\ell}\delta_i,\qquad \varphi(\theta)_j:=\theta_j-D_j\quad(1\le j\le\ell).$$
For every partition $\theta$ with at most $\ell$ parts satisfying $\rho_j-s\le\theta_j\le\omega_j$ for each $j$, the image $\varphi(\theta)$ is a partition after deletion of zero parts. In particular $\varphi(\lambda)$ and $\varphi(\mu)$ have a common size $r$, and $\varphi(\nu):=(r-s,\nu_2,\nu_3,\ldots)$ is a partition of $r$. Then
$$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=g(\varphi(\lambda),\varphi(\mu),\varphi(\nu)),\qquad r\le2s\ell^2.$$

This is a corrected reduction map for the bounded-reduction conclusion of Pak–Panova. It retains their Littlewood–Richardson/Jacobi–Trudi proof route and the same size bound; the map is not the block formula printed in their papers.
items.strategy: Use Littlewood internal/outer compatibility to obtain the finite LR coefficient identity, expand the third Schur function along the first Jacobi–Trudi row, and prove small-skew LR and inverse-index invariance under Phi(theta)=theta-D with delta_i=max(0,rho_i-omega_(i+1)-2s); prove output partitions and the original r<=2s ell^2 bound separately for ell=1, ell=2 and ell>=3. The printed block map is refuted by a coefficient-changing triple even when all its images are partitions.
items.axiom_use: None intended: the argument uses Littlewood's identity, LR/Pieri expansions of symmetric functions, the Jacobi-Trudi identity and finite tableau combinatorics. The authoring stage must confirm that no cited supplier silently assumes the Axiom of Choice.

items.title: Row-gap reduction and conditional k-stability of Kronecker coefficients
items.statement:
Fix $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n$ and an integer $k\ge1$. Write $(t^k)$ for $k$ parts equal to $t$ and $(tk)$ for the one-part partition of size $tk$, and read missing parts as zero. Put $s:=n-\nu_1$, with $\nu_1=0$ if $n=0$.

**(i)** Suppose $\lambda_1\le\mu_1\le\nu_1$ and
$$\min\{\lambda_k,\mu_k\}\ge\max\{\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1}\}+s.$$
Then for every integer $t\ge0$,
$$g(\lambda+(t^k),\mu+(t^k),\nu+(tk))=g(\lambda,\mu,\nu).$$
All shifted arguments are partitions of $n+tk$. For $k=1$, this is the first-row padding of the three tails to size $n+t$ ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]).

**(ii)** For arbitrary $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n$ and $k\ge1$, the sequence $G_k(t):=g(\lambda+(t^k),\mu+(t^k),\nu+(tk))$ is eventually constant. More precisely, it is constant for every integer $t\ge t_0$, where
$$t_0:=\max\{0,\ s+\max\{\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1}\}-\min\{\lambda_k,\mu_k\}\}.$$
The proof of the row-gap identity does not require first-part ordering, so the threshold also covers $k=1$ when $\nu_1<\max\{\lambda_1,\mu_1\}$. No monotonicity is asserted.
items.strategy: Use the locally proved finite LR coefficient identity and first-row Jacobi–Trudi expansion of the reduction lemma directly at the k-row cut. Map alpha to alpha+(t^k), prove the inverse partition and both LR tableau bijections using the sharp s-gap, and compare unchanged small coefficients and tail cofactors. Apply the ordering-free proved identity at t0=max(0,s+max(next rows)-min(kth rows)) to obtain eventual constancy for all k including k=1.
items.axiom_use: None intended: the proof is a direct application of the local reduction lemma and finite ordering of the shifted triple. Re-verify supplier AC status at authoring.

items.title: No general positive combinatorial rule for Kronecker coefficients is known
items.statement: The character formula, the reduction lemma and k-stability of this page do not supply a general positive combinatorial rule: it remains a well-known open problem to give a combinatorial interpretation of, or a positive formula for, all Kronecker coefficients g(lambda,mu,nu). In particular this page claims no such rule, no polynomial-time algorithm and no general positivity criterion. Provenance: literature-derived statement, no proof section.
items.strategy: No proof section. Quote the exact source boundary (Pak-Panova, Bounds, Introduction and Section 7.3: the coefficients themselves are integer and nonnegative by definition but lack a combinatorial interpretation or any meaningful positive formula) and keep the page's claim boundary explicit.

title: Kronecker Coefficients and Internal Products — Examples

items.title: The complete internal product table for S_3
items.statement: For S_3 the three irreducibles are S^(3) (trivial), S^(2,1) (standard, dim 2) and S^(1,1,1) (sign). The character values on cycle types (1^3),(2,1),(3) are (1,1,1), (2,0,-1), (1,-1,1) respectively; consequently the complete internal product table is: S^(3) (x) X = X for every irreducible X; S^(2,1) (x) S^(2,1) = S^(3) + S^(2,1) + S^(1,1,1); S^(2,1) (x) S^(1,1,1) = S^(2,1); S^(1,1,1) (x) S^(1,1,1) = S^(3). Equivalently all Kronecker coefficients g(lambda,mu,nu) for n=3 are 0 or 1 and the table is invariant under all permutations of the three arguments.
items.strategy: Compute the character table from the Frobenius dictionary: ch(chi^lambda) = s_lambda, and h_3, h_2h_1 - h_3, e_3 expand in power sums with the complete-homogeneous expansion, giving the character values displayed. Multiply the three characters pointwise and decompose the products with the three-character inner product (the previous proposition), using the class sizes 1, 3, 2 for the three cycle types of S_3. Verify each resulting coefficient against the S_3 symmetry from the corollary. All computations are finite and explicit; the S_3 character table is recomputed here rather than imported from an examples page.

items.title: First-row padding below the threshold is undefined
items.statement: For alpha = (2,1) the padded sequence alpha[n] = (n-3,2,1) is a partition exactly when n >= 5. In particular alpha[3] = (0,2,1) and alpha[4] = (1,2,1) are not partitions, so the padded family and the padded Kronecker coefficient g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) are undefined below the stated threshold; the stable family for this shape begins only at n = 5.
items.strategy: By the definition of first-row padding, alpha[n] is a partition exactly when n >= |alpha| + alpha_1 = 3 + 2 = 5. For n = 3 the first entry n - 3 = 0 is not a positive part and (0,2,1) is not weakly decreasing; for n = 4 the first entry 1 is smaller than the second entry 2, so (1,2,1) is not a partition. For n = 5 the padded partition is (2,2,1).

items.title: Row padding need not preserve a Kronecker coefficient before stability
items.statement: With lambda = mu = (2,2) and nu = (3,1) (n = 4, k = 1) one has g((2,2),(2,2),(3,1)) = 0, whereas g((2+t,2),(2+t,2),(3+t,1)) = 1 for every t >= 1. Thus adding (t^k) does not preserve the coefficient from t = 0 on: the separation hypothesis of the row-gap theorem fails at t = 0, since min{lambda_1,mu_1} = 2 < max{lambda_2,mu_2} + (n - nu_1) = 2 + 1 = 3. Eventual constancy is not immediacy.
items.strategy: Compute the coefficients with characters. For t = 0: V_(2,2) (x) V_(2,2) = Sym^2 V_(2,2) + Lambda^2 V_(2,2) = (trivial + V_(2,2)) + sign, and V_(3,1) does not occur, so g((2,2),(2,2),(3,1)) = 0. For t = 1: the triple ((3,2),(3,2),(4,1)) satisfies the conditions of the row-gap theorem with k = 1 (3 <= 3 <= 4, s = n - nu_1 = 1, and min{3,3} = 3 >= max{2,2} + 1 = 3), so the theorem gives g((3+t',2),(3+t',2),(4+t',1)) = g((3,2),(3,2),(4,1)) for all t' >= 0; substituting t = t' + 1 identifies the sequence in the statement. The single value needed is g((3,2),(3,2),(4,1)) = 1: compute the character of S^(3,2) from the permutation module M^(3,2) = S^(5) + S^(4,1) + S^(3,2) (Young's rule; the character of M^(3,2) at sigma counts the 3-element unions of cycles), with chi^(4,1) = chi(M^(4,1)) - chi^(5) (the standard representation), and use the dictionary to get the S_5 character table; the inner product (1/120) sum over the seven cycle types of S_5 gives 120/120 = 1.

items.title: The category FI and FI-modules over a commutative ring
items.statement: Let $FI$ be the category whose objects are the finite sets and whose morphisms are the injections ([[def-category]]); it is equivalent to the full subcategory on the objects $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, $n\ge0$, so that $\operatorname{End}_{FI}([n])\cong S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]). An **FI-module over a commutative ring $k$** ([[def-commutative-ring]]) is a covariant functor $V\colon FI\to k\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], [[def-left-and-right-modules]]); write $V_S=V(S)$, $V_n=V([n])$ and $f_*=V(f)$ for a morphism $f$. Since $\operatorname{End}_{FI}([n])=S_n$, the maps $V_n\to V_n$ induced by permutations make $V_n$ a left $kS_n$-module ([[def-group-ring]]), and each $f_*\colon V_m\to V_n$ is equivariant for the conjugation homomorphism $S_m\to S_n$ determined by $f$. A **sub-FI-module** of $V$ is a subfunctor of $V$ ([[def-submodule]]), a **map of FI-modules** is a natural transformation, and kernels, images and cokernels are computed pointwise, so the FI-modules over $k$ inherit an abelian-category structure from $k\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-quotient-module]]). An **FB-module** over $k$ is a functor from the groupoid $FB$ of finite sets and bijections to $k\text{-Mod}$; an FB-module is determined up to isomorphism by the $kS_n$-modules $W_n$ and carries no transition maps.
items.strategy: Definition pack: spell out that the equivalence $FI\simeq\{[n]\}$ fixes the endomorphism groups as the symmetric groups, that a functor sends each injection to a $k$-linear map with $V(g\circ f)=V(g)\circ V(f)$ and $V(\mathrm{id}_S)=\mathrm{id}_{V_S}$, and that pointwise kernels and cokernels satisfy the functor axioms because $k\text{-Mod}$ is abelian. No naturality properties beyond the functor axioms are asserted; natural transformations are only named, not used here.

items.title: Span, finite generation and generation degree of an FI-module
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ and let $\Sigma\subseteq\bigsqcup_S V_S$ be a set of elements. The **sub-FI-module generated by $\Sigma$**, written $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$, is the intersection of all sub-FI-modules of $V$ containing $\Sigma$; it is the smallest such sub-FI-module and consists of all finite $k$-linear combinations of elements $f_*(v)$ with $v\in\Sigma$ and $f$ a morphism of $FI$. Call $V$ **finitely generated** when $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)=V$ for some finite $\Sigma$, and **generated in degree $\le d$** when $\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le d})=V$, where $V_{\le d}=\bigsqcup_{|S|\le d}V_S$; the **generation degree** is the least such $d$, and $\infty$ when no such $d$ exists ([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]). Finite generation of $V$ and pointwise finite generation of the $k$-modules $V_S$ are different conditions: the latter is implied by the former ([[lem-generated-in-degree-d-is-a-quotient-of-free-fi-modules]]) but does not imply it, and no pointwise finite-dimensionality is built into either notion ([[def-submodule]] for the span).
items.strategy: Define the intersection as in the generated-submodule construction, verify it is a subfunctor and that it is exactly the set of finite combinations of images of generators (the finite-combination set is itself a subfunctor containing $\Sigma$), and record that a degree bound on generators is an additional structure, not a consequence of finite generation. Separate the two finite-generation notions in prose; no arithmetic claim is made here.

items.title: The coinvariant functors $\Phi_a$ and the transition maps $T$
items.statement: A **graded $k[T]$-module** consists of $k$-modules $U_n$, $n\ge0$, together with $k$-linear maps $T\colon U_n\to U_{n+1}$ for all $n$. Fix $a\ge0$, a set $\mathbf a$ of cardinality $a$ and a functorial disjoint union. For an FI-module $V$ over $k$ and $n\ge0$ put $$\Phi_a(V)_n:=(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n})_{S_n},$$ the coinvariants of the $kS_n$-module $V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ ([[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]], [[def-quotient-module]]). Any injection $f\colon n\to n+1$ gives an injection $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f\colon\mathbf a\sqcup n\to\mathbf a\sqcup n+1$ and an induced map $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$; postcomposition by $S_{n+1}$ shows that this map depends only on $f$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}$, because any two injections $n\to n+1$ differ by an element of $S_{n+1}$. Writing $T$ for it, $(\Phi_a(V),T)$ is a graded $k[T]$-module, and $\Phi_a$ is a functor from FI-modules to graded $k[T]$-modules. Each $\Phi_a$ is right exact in every degree, and is exact when $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$, since averaging over the finite groups $S_n$ splits the coinvariant quotient; in that case $\Phi_a(W)\subseteq\Phi_a(V)$ for every sub-FI-module $W\subseteq V$.
items.strategy: Choice-independence of $T$: the two injections differ by a permutation of $n+1$, and coinvariants identify the images. Functoriality and right exactness are pointwise from the right-exact coinvariant functor; left exactness over a $\mathbb Q$-algebra follows because $(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n})_{S_n}\to V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ is split by the averaging map $v\mapsto\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\sigma v$, which is defined when $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$ and is natural ([[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]], [[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]]).

items.title: Injectivity, surjectivity and stability degree
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. The **injectivity degree** $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)$ (respectively the **surjectivity degree** $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$) is the least $s\ge0$ such that for every $a\ge0$ the transition map $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective (respectively surjective) for all $n\ge s$; the **stability degree** is $$\operatorname{stab-deg}(V):=\max\bigl(\operatorname{inj-deg}(V),\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\bigr).$$ Each of the three is $+\infty$ when no such $s$ exists. Equivalently, $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is an isomorphism for all $a\ge0$ and all $n\ge\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. The three bounds are kept distinct: stability degree is the max, and injectivity and surjectivity degree need not agree in examples.
items.strategy: Unwrap the definitions ($\max$ of two extended nonnegative integers), and record the equivalent indexing statement as a reformulation: $T$ is an isomorphism iff it is both injective and surjective, and each of the two stated bounds is the least threshold controlling the corresponding property. No claim of finiteness is made; $\infty$ is allowed throughout.

items.title: Specht modules classify the irreducibles over every field of characteristic zero
items.statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $n\ge0$. The field-valued Specht modules $S^\lambda_F$, $\lambda\vdash n$, of [[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]] are nonzero, irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic, and every irreducible $F S_n$-module is isomorphic to exactly one of them; consequently, by Maschke, every finite-dimensional $F S_n$-module is a direct sum of copies of the $S^\lambda_F$, so the irreducible $F S_n$-modules are indexed by the partitions of $n$ and the $S^\lambda_F$ form a complete irredundant list. This is the constituent convention used throughout the pair: over $F=\mathbb C$ it specialises to the published complex classification, and over a general characteristic-zero field F it is proved using rational Specht models and extension Q -> F, not a scalar extension from C to F.
items.strategy: Use the rational Specht models, then extend from the prime field, never from an arbitrary field to C. The integral standard basis gives explicit matrices with rational entries on S^lambda_Q and an isomorphism F tensor_Q S^lambda_Q = S^lambda_F for every characteristic-zero field F. Over Q, a proper nonzero invariant subspace would remain proper and nonzero under the explicit finite-dimensional extension Q -> C, contradicting complex irreducibility. For finite-dimensional rational representations, equivariant Hom spaces are kernels of finite rational matrices; matrix ranks are unchanged on extension to C. Thus End_QSn(S^lambda_Q)=Q and Hom_QSn(S^lambda_Q,S^mu_Q)=0 for lambda!=mu. Any simple QSn-module W is finite-dimensional (a nonzero w generates it as a quotient of QSn); its complex extension has a Specht constituent, and the same Hom-rank comparison descends a nonzero map S^lambda_Q -> W, proving completeness over Q. Maschke therefore decomposes the finite regular module QSn as a finite sum of rational Specht modules. Extend this finite decomposition along Q -> F. The same rational Hom-matrix ranks give End_FSn(S^lambda_F)=F and zero Hom between distinct shapes; Maschke implies each S^lambda_F is irreducible, since a proper summand would give a non-scalar projection. Every simple FSn-module is a quotient of the regular module, so the extended decomposition proves completeness over F. All scalar extensions and rank comparisons concern explicit finite-dimensional matrices, not an embedding F -> C. No arbitrary-index choice is used.

items.title: Weight of an FI-module over a field of characteristic zero
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). For a partition $\lambda$ and $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ put $\lambda[n]:=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$, the first-row padding ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), and let $V(\lambda)_n$ denote the irreducible $kS_n$-module indexed by the partition $\lambda[n]$, i.e. $k\otimes_{\mathbb Q}S^{\lambda[n]}_{\mathbb Q}$, the scalar extension of its rational Specht model ([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]], [[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]). The **weight** of $V$ is $$\operatorname{weight}(V):=\sup\{|\lambda|:V(\lambda)_n\text{ occurs as a constituent of }V_n\text{ for some }n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1\},$$ the supremum over all pairs $(\lambda,n)$ as displayed; it is $0$ for $V=0$ and $+\infty$ when the set is unbounded. If $W$ is a subquotient of $V$ then $\operatorname{weight}(W)\le\operatorname{weight}(V)$.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: every partition of $n$ is uniquely $\lambda[n]$ for a partition $\lambda$ (the boxes below the first row form a partition), so the constituent labels are well defined and the supremum is over a set of nonnegative integers. The subquotient inequality is immediate since constituents of a subquotient are constituents of $V$. The item records the convention that $k$ may be any characteristic-zero field via the absolute irreducibility supplied by the classification lemma; no finiteness of $\operatorname{weight}(V)$ is asserted. Constituent tests require no basis or global decomposition for infinite-dimensional values: every vector has a finite-dimensional orbit span under the finite group, and finite-dimensional Maschke applies there. A finite-dimensional submodule of a quotient can be lifted into a finite-dimensional orbit-stable subspace using finitely many vector lifts; this gives the stated subquotient monotonicity without infinite choices.

items.title: The free FI-module $M(W)$ generated by an $S_m$-module
items.statement: Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$, i.e. a family of $kS_m$-modules $W_m$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). The **free FI-module** $M(W)$ is the FI-module with $$M(W)_S:=\bigoplus_{T\subseteq S}W_T,$$ where $W_T$ denotes $W_{|T|}$ transported along a bijection $T\to[|T|]$ (well defined up to canonical isomorphism), and on an injection $f\colon S\to S'$ the map $M(W)_S\to M(W)_{S'}$ is the sum of the maps $W_T\to W_{f(T)}$ induced by $f|_T$ ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). $M(-)$ is the left adjoint of the forgetful functor from FI-modules to FB-modules, so $$\operatorname{Hom}_{FI\text{-}Mod}(M(W),V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{FB\text{-}Mod}(W,\pi V)$$ naturally in $V$; the unit sends $W_S$ to the summand $W_S$ of $M(W)_S$. As an $S_n$-module, $$M(W)_n\cong\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}\bigl(W_a\boxtimes k\bigr),$$ with $\boxtimes$ the external tensor product of modules for the direct factors and $\operatorname{Ind}$ the induced module built from $H$-covariant functions ([[def-induced-r-linear-g-module-by-h-covariant-functions]], [[def-outer-induction-product-for-symmetric-group-characters]], [[lem-character-ring-of-a-direct-product-is-the-tensor-product]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]). For $m\ge0$, $M(m):=M(k[S_m])$ has as a $k$-basis the injections $m\to S$; for a partition $\lambda$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, $M(\lambda):=M(S^\lambda_k)$.
items.strategy: Existence and functoriality of $M(W)$: the summands $W_T$ depend on $T$ only up to the canonical transport along the unique bijection between two $|T|$-element sets, and $f$ sends $T$ to $f(T)$, giving compatible maps; the adjunction is checked on the unit and co-unit (evaluate at $S=\emptyset$ and at singletons). The $S_n$-module identification is the orbit decomposition of the sum over subsets, each orbit contributing $\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}(W_a\boxtimes k)$. No choice beyond finite transport data is used.

items.title: Generation in bounded degree presents an FI-module as a quotient of free FI-modules
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. (a) For $v\in V_m$ the FI-module map $M(m)\to V$ sending the basis element $\mathrm{id}_m\in M(m)_m$ to $v$ has image $\operatorname{span}_V(v)$; more generally, for any $\Sigma\subseteq\bigsqcup_S V_S$ the canonical map $\bigoplus_{s\in\Sigma}M(|S_s|)\to V$ has image $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$. (b) $V$ is finitely generated if and only if there is a finite family $m_1,\dots,m_k\ge0$ with a surjection $M(m_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus M(m_k)\twoheadrightarrow V$; $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$ if and only if there is a surjection $\bigoplus_{i\in I}M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ with $m_i\le d$ for all $i$. In particular, if $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$ then the evaluation map $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)\to V$ is surjective, where $V_m$ is regarded as an FB-module. (c) If $V$ is finitely generated, then $V_S$ is a finitely generated $k$-module for every finite set $S$.
items.strategy: For (a), the image of $M(m)\to V$ is spanned by the elements $f_*(v)$, and every sub-FI-module containing $v$ contains these elements; the general $\Sigma$ case is the same computation on a direct sum. For (b), a finite generating set defines a map from a finite sum of free modules by (a), which is surjective by definition of generation; conversely the images of the canonical generators $\mathrm{id}_{m_i}\in M(m_i)_{m_i}$ generate the image ([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]). Taking the generating set $V_{\le d}$ gives the evaluation map. For (c), a surjection $\bigoplus_i M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ restricts at $S$ to a surjection of $k$-modules onto $V_S$ from a finite direct sum of free $k$-modules, which is a finitely generated $k$-module.

items.title: Branching rule for Specht modules: adding or removing boxes in distinct columns
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $S^\lambda_F$ be the corresponding Specht module. (i) For every $k\ge0$ there is an isomorphism of $F S_{n+k}$-modules $$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_n	imes S_k}^{S_{n+k}} igl(S^\lambda_F oxtimes F igr)\cong igoplus_{\mu}S^\mu_F,$$ summed over the partitions $\mu\vdash n+k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one box to each of $k$ different columns. (ii) For every $k\le n$ there is an isomorphism of $F S_{n-k}$-modules $$ igl(\operatorname{Res}^{S_n}_{S_{n-k}	imes S_k}S^\lambda_F igr)_{S_k}\cong igoplus_{
u}S^
u_F,$$ summed over the partitions $
u\vdash n-k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by removing one box from each of $k$ different columns. All multiplicities are $0$ or $1$.
items.strategy:
Part (i) is the outer Pieri rule with trivial factors ([[cor-outer-pieri-rules-for-trivial-and-sign-factors]]) read off in the Specht basis supplied by [[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]. For (ii), Frobenius reciprocity for complex characters ([[cor-frobenius-reciprocity-for-complex-characters]]) identifies the multiplicity of $S^
u_F$ in the $S_k$-coinvariants of the restriction with the multiplicity of $S^\lambda_F$ in $\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{n-k}	imes S_k}^{S_n}(S^
u_F oxtimes F)$, which is $1$ exactly when $\lambda/
u$ is a horizontal $k$-strip by (i); the coinvariant quotient is semisimple over $F$ of characteristic $0$ by Maschke, so multiplicities determine the module. No other summands occur because (i) lists exactly the horizontal-strip shapes. The character calculation is made first over C and descends to Q by the finite rational Hom-matrix rank comparison in the classification lemma. Averaging over the finite subgroup identifies invariants and coinvariants by an explicit rational idempotent, whose finite-matrix rank is likewise unchanged under Q -> F. Extending the finite rational decomposition therefore proves the displayed formulas over every characteristic-zero field F.

items.title: Free FI-modules have computable stability degree and weight
items.statement: Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$. Then $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(W))=0$, and if $W_i=0$ for $i>m$ then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(W))\le m$; in particular $M(m)=M(k[S_m])$ has $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(m))=0$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(m))=m$. If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $\lambda$ is a partition, then $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=|\lambda|$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$.
items.strategy: The displayed computation of $\Phi_aM(W)$ as $\bigoplus_{U\subseteq\mathbf a,0\le j\le n}\Phi_{|U|}(W)_j$ shows that $T$ preserves the summands and acts as the identity on each, giving injectivity degree $0$; when $W$ vanishes above $m$ the $j$-range is exhausted for $n\ge m$, giving surjectivity degree $\le m$, and $\Phi_0(k[S_m])_m\cong k$ gives the exact value $m$ for $M(m)$. For M(lambda), branching for Ind_{S_m x S_{n-m}}^{S_n}(S^lambda x k) gives full shapes nu obtained by adding n-m boxes in distinct columns. Hence nu_1>=n-m, so the padding-tail size n-nu_1 is at most m; equality is attained for the padded shape lambda[n] when n>=m+lambda_1. For exact stability, Phi_a M(S^lambda)_n decomposes into factors (S^lambda)_{S_j}, indexed by subsets U of [a] with |U|+j=m and j<=n. Transition T is the identity on existing factors. By branching, (S^lambda)_{S_j}=0 for j>lambda_1, so no new nonzero factor appears after n=lambda_1; the factor j=lambda_1 is nonzero, and with a=m-lambda_1 and U=[a] it first appears there. Thus T fails surjectivity at n=lambda_1-1 if lambda_1>0, proving stability degree exactly lambda_1; for the empty partition it is zero.

items.title: Bounded generation degree bounds surjectivity degree and weight
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. (a) Every quotient $V\twoheadrightarrow W$ satisfies $\operatorname{surj-deg}(W)\le\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$. (b) If $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le d$. (c) If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, then $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le d$.
items.strategy: (a) $\Phi_a$ is right exact, so $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(W)_n$ is surjective in every degree and a surjective $T$ remains surjective on the quotient. (b) By the presentation lemma $V$ is a quotient of $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)$, and each summand is an $M(W)$ with $W$ supported in degrees $\le d$, so it has surjectivity degree $\le d$; a finite direct sum has surjectivity degree the maximum, and (a) passes the bound to the quotient $V$. (c) The same presentation exhibits $V$ as a quotient of $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)$, each $M(V_m)$ has weight $\le m\le d$ by the free-module bound, and weight is monotone under subquotients, so $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le d$. For (c), no finite-dimensionality of V_m is assumed: every finite collection of vectors in V_m lies in a finite-dimensional S_m-stable orbit span. In M(V_m)_n each vector involves only finitely many such coefficients and injections, so it lies in the induction of one finite-dimensional coefficient subrepresentation. Finite-dimensional Maschke and the branching lemma bound every simple constituent by m; finite sums and quotients preserve this bound. A finite-dimensional simple submodule of a quotient is lifted using finitely many basis vectors and their finite S_n-orbits, so no infinite-dimensional decomposition or choice of an infinite basis is needed.

items.title: Tensor products of finitely generated FI-modules are finitely generated
items.statement: Let $V$ and $W$ be finitely generated FI-modules over $k$, with pointwise tensor product $(V\otimes W)_S=V_S\otimes_k W_S$. Then $V\otimes W$ is finitely generated. More precisely, if $V$ is generated in degree $\le m_1$ and $W$ in degree $\le m_2$, then $V\otimes W$ is generated in degree $\le m_1+m_2$.
items.strategy: By the presentation lemma it suffices to treat $U=M(m_1)\otimes M(m_2)$: a $k$-basis of $U_S$ is given by pairs $(f_1\colon m_1\to S, f_2\colon m_2\to S)$, and each basis element lies in the image of $U_T$ for $T=\mathrm{im}(f_1)\cup\mathrm{im}(f_2)$ with $|T|\le m_1+m_2$; hence $U$ is generated in degree $\le m_1+m_2$. For general $V,W$ choose surjections $\bigoplus_i M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ and $\bigoplus_j M(n_j)\twoheadrightarrow W$ with all $m_i\le m_1$, $n_j\le m_2$; tensor products preserve surjections and distribute over finite direct sums ([[thm-right-exactness-of-tensor-products]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), so $V\otimes W$ is a quotient of a finite sum of $M(m_i)\otimes M(n_j)$, each generated in degree $\le m_i+n_j\le m_1+m_2$; quotients do not increase generation degree.

items.title: Coinvariants detect vanishing of subquotients of bounded weight, and padded irreducibles stabilise
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\mu\vdash n$ and write $\mu=\lambda[n]$ as in the padding definition. (i) For $a\le n$, with $k_0:=n-a$, the $S_a$-representation $(V_\mu)_{S_{k_0}}$ is zero if and only if $n-a>\mu_1$, equivalently $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$ if and only if $a<|\lambda|$. (ii) If $n-a=\mu_1$ (that is, $a=|\lambda|$), then $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong V_\lambda$ as $S_{|\lambda|}$-modules. (iii) For fixed $\lambda$ and $a\ge|\lambda|$, the $S_a$-module $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}$ is independent of $n$ once $n\ge a+\lambda_1$; in fact $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{|\lambda|}\times S_{a-|\lambda|}}^{S_a}(V_\lambda\boxtimes k)$ throughout that range. (iv) If $V$ is an FI-module over $k$ with $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le a$, then every subquotient $W_n$ of the $S_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies $W_n=0\iff(W_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$.
items.strategy: Apply the branching lemma part (ii) with $S^\lambda_F = V_\mu$: $(V_\mu)_{S_{n-a}}$ is the sum of the irreducibles $V_\nu$ over partitions $\nu\vdash a$ obtained from $\mu$ by removing one box from each of $n-a$ different columns; such a removal is possible iff $n-a\le\mu_1$, and when $n-a=\mu_1$ it is possible only by removing every column's bottom box, leaving $\lambda$; this gives (i) and (ii). For (iii), write m=|lambda| and mu=lambda[n]=(n-m,lambda_1,...). A partition nu of a occurs on the left precisely when mu_i>=nu_i>=mu_{i+1} for every i, by horizontal-strip removal. On the right, Pieri gives exactly nu_i>=lambda_i>=nu_{i+1}. These are the same inequalities except for nu_1<=n-m; the latter is automatic because |nu|-|lambda|=a-m gives nu_1<=lambda_1+a-m<=n-m in the stated range n>=a+lambda_1. Thus both sides have exactly the same constituents, each with multiplicity one, proving the displayed isomorphism independent of n. For (iv), if $W_n$ is nonzero, fix a nonzero vector and its finite-dimensional $S_n$-orbit span. Finite-dimensional Maschke supplies a simple submodule $V(\lambda)_n$ with $|\lambda|\le a$. By (i) its $S_{n-a}$-coinvariants are nonzero. Coinvariants over a characteristic-zero field are exact: the finite averaging operator identifies the quotient with invariants and preserves injections. Hence $(W_n)_{S_{n-a}}$ is nonzero. The reverse direction is immediate. This proves the claim even when $W_n$ is infinite-dimensional, without choosing an infinite basis or decomposition.

items.title: A stability degree bounds the first row of every padding tail
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, with $s:=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)<\infty$. Then for every $n\ge0$ every irreducible constituent $V(\lambda)_n$ of the $S_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies $\lambda_1\le s$; equivalently, the second row of the full Specht diagram has length at most s, since the first row of the padding tail is the second row of the full diagram.
items.strategy:
Filter $V$ by $F^mV:=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le m})$, so that $V= igcup_mF^mV$ and each $F^mV$ is generated in degree $\le m$. It suffices to prove the bound for every constituent of every quotient $F^mV/F^{m-1}V$. Fix $m$ and let $\overline V:=V/F^{m-1}V$; then $\overline V_n=0$ for $n<m$ and $\overline V_m\cong H_m:=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le m})/\operatorname{span}(V_{<m})$ is its degree-$m$ part. If $m\le s$ then any $\mu\vdash m$ has $\mu_1\le m\le s$; for $m\ge s+1$ the index $a_0:=m-s-1$ is nonnegative: since $\overline V$ is a quotient of $V$, part (a) of the generation lemma gives $\operatorname{surj-deg}(\overline V)\le s$, so $T\colon\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_s	o\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_{s+1}$ is surjective; its domain is a quotient of $\overline V_{m-1}=0$, hence $0$; but $\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_{s+1}=(\overline V_m)_{S_{s+1}}$, so $(H_m)_{S_{s+1}}=0$, and the coinvariant lemma (i) with subgroup size $s+1$ (retained rank $m-s-1$) gives $\mu_1\le s$ for every constituent $V_\mu$ of $H_m$. Next, $F^mV/F^{m-1}V$ is generated in degree $\le m$ with vanishing values below $m$, so the presentation lemma gives a surjection $M(H_m)	woheadrightarrow F^mV/F^{m-1}V$; by the free-module description every constituent of $M(H_m)_n$ is obtained from a constituent $H_\mu$ of $H_m$ by adding boxes in different columns, giving a full diagram $
u$ with $
u_2\le\mu_1\le s$ by horizontal-strip interlacing; if $
u=\lambda[n]$, then $\lambda_1=
u_2$; a quotient of $M(H_m)_n$ has no other constituents. Passing along the filtration gives the claim for $V_n$. All constituent arguments can be made in finite-dimensional orbit spans; any constituent vector in the exhaustive filtration already occurs at a finite stage. The bound concerns the tail, not the growing first row of lambda[n].

items.title: FI-modules over a Noetherian $\mathbb Q$-algebra form a Noetherian category
items.statement: Let $k$ be a commutative Noetherian ring containing $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-noetherian-ring]]), and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ ([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]]). Then every sub-FI-module $W\subseteq V$ is finitely generated; that is, the category of FI-modules over $k$ is Noetherian. The hypothesis that $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$ is used only through the exactness of the functors $\Phi_a$ and through restriction of scalars to $\mathbb Q$.
items.strategy: Let $V$ be generated in degree $\le a$ and let $W\subseteq V$. First, $V_n$ is a finitely generated $k$-module for every $n$ (presentation lemma (c)), and the graded $k[T]$-module $\Phi_a(V)$ is finitely generated: $T$ is surjective in degrees $\ge a$ by the generation-degree bound (b), so $\Phi_a(V)$ is generated over $k[T]$ by the finitely many components $\Phi_a(V)_0,\dots,\Phi_a(V)_a$, each a finitely generated $k$-module as a quotient of $V_{a+i}$. Since $k[T]$ is Noetherian ([[thm-hilbert-basis-theorem]], [[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and a finitely generated module over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian ([[thm-finitely-generated-modules-over-noetherian-rings-are-noetherian]], [[def-noetherian-module]]), the submodule $\Phi_a(W)\subseteq\Phi_a(V)$ is a finitely generated graded $k[T]$-module; take a finite generating set and replace each generator by its finitely many homogeneous components (the submodule is graded), obtaining homogeneous generators $x_1,\dots,x_r$, lift each $x_i\in\Phi_a(W)_{n_i}$ to $w_i\in W_{a+n_i}$, and let $\widetilde W\subseteq W$ be generated by the $w_i$ together with finite generating sets of $W_0,\dots,W_{a-1}$. Then $\Phi_a(\widetilde W)=\Phi_a(W)$, and exactness of $\Phi_a$ over $\mathbb Q$-algebras gives $\Phi_a(W/\widetilde W)=0$. It remains to show $U:=W/\widetilde W=0$. Restrict scalars from k to Q, as in the complete proof of CEF Theorem 1.3; no map k -> C is used. The evaluation surjection direct_sum_{m<=a} M_k(V_m) -> V stays surjective on restriction, and M_k(V_m)_Q = M_Q((V_m)_Q): free k-modules on finite injection sets become the same finite direct sums of rational coefficient spaces, and the S_m-balanced relations agree because the actions are k-linear. Thus V_Q is generated in degree <=a over Q, although its values can be infinite-dimensional. The generation-degree/weight supplier now proves this case through finite orbit-stable subspaces of the coefficient modules, so weight(V_Q)<=a. U_Q is a subquotient and has the same bound. Restriction commutes with coinvariants: the k-submodule generated by hv-v is exactly its Q-linear span, since c(hv-v)=h(cv)-cv for c in k. Therefore Phi_a(U_Q)=0. For every n>=a, apply the vanishing-detection supplier to U_Q,n, with averaging over the finite group S_{n-a}. Its proof uses only a finite-dimensional cyclic submodule if U_Q,n is nonzero, not a decomposition of the whole rational space. It follows that U_Q,n=0, hence U_n=0. For n<a, the chosen finite generators of W_n already give tilde W_n=W_n. Consequently W=tilde W is finitely generated. All Noetherian-module uses and all generator/lift selections are finite; the Hilbert citation uses only its explicitly choice-free ideal implication.

items.title: Uniform representation stability for consistent sequences of $S_n$-modules
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$. A **consistent sequence** is a sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ in which $V_n$ is a finite-dimensional $kS_n$-module and $\varphi_n\colon V_n\to V_{n+1}$ is $S_n$-equivariant, $V_{n+1}$ being regarded as an $S_n$-module by restriction along the standard inclusion $S_n\hookrightarrow S_{n+1}$; an FI-module $V$ with finite-dimensional values determines the consistent sequence $(V_n,f_*)$ for the standard inclusions. The sequence is **uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge N$** when (I) $\varphi_n$ is injective for all $n\ge N$; (II) the $S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is all of $V_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge N$; and (III) writing $V_n\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda}c_{\lambda,n}V(\lambda)_n$ with padded irreducibles $V(\lambda)_n$ ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), the multiplicity $c_{\lambda,n}$ is independent of $n$ for every fixed $\lambda$ and all $n\ge N$. The sequence is uniformly representation stable when it is so for some $N$. All three conditions are part of the definition; (II) is not implied by (I) and (III).
items.strategy: State the three clauses and the padding convention used in (III), and verify that an FI-module's standard-inclusion maps $f_*$ are $S_n$-equivariant by functoriality and the conjugation action. Record the known non-example (the consistent sequence of regular representations is not uniformly stable, and indeed does not come from an FI-module) only as a warning that consistency alone is weaker; no claim of it is needed here.

items.title: Weight and stability degree give a uniform representation-stability range
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d=\operatorname{weight}(V)$ and stability degree $s=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. Then the consistent sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge d+s$.
items.strategy: Set $K_n=\ker\varphi_n\subseteq V_n$ and let $C_{n+1}$ be the cokernel of the $S_{n+1}$-map $\operatorname{Ind}^{S_{n+1}}_{S_n}\varphi_n\colon\operatorname{Ind}^{S_{n+1}}_{S_n}V_n\to V_{n+1}$; conditions (I) and (II) are exactly $K_n=0$ and $C_{n+1}=0$. Since $K_n$ is a subrepresentation of $V_n$ and $C_{n+1}$ a quotient of $V_{n+1}$, the coinvariant lemma (iv) reduces both to the vanishing of $(K_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ and $(C_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}$ for $n\ge d$. Exactness of $S_a$-coinvariants in characteristic $0$ identifies $(K_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ with the kernel of $(\varphi_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ and $(C_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}$ with the cokernel of $(\operatorname{Ind}\varphi_n)_{S_{n+1-d}}$, and the transition map $T\colon\Phi_d(V)_{n-d}\to\Phi_d(V)_{n+1-d}$ factors through both, so it is the composite in the two ways displayed in the source. For $n-d\ge s$, $T$ is an isomorphism, so $(\varphi_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ is injective and $(\operatorname{Ind}\varphi_n)_{S_{n+1-d}}$ is surjective; hence $K_n=0$ and $C_{n+1}=0$ for $n\ge s+d$. For (III), fix $m\le d$ and induct on $m=|\lambda|$: in the range $n\ge s+d$, decompose $(V_n)_{S_{n-m}}$ into constituents and use the coinvariant lemma (i) to see that only $|\lambda|\le m$ contribute, (iii) to see that the contributions of $|\lambda|<m$ are independent of $n$, and the induction hypothesis to see that their multiplicities are constant; the remaining summand is a direct sum of $\lambda$'s of size $m$ with multiplicity $c_{\lambda,n}$ by (ii), so constancy of the total forces constancy of each $c_{\lambda,n}$. Here the range hypothesis enters twice: $\lambda_1\le s$ for every occurring constituent by the first-row bound, so $n\ge s+d\ge\lambda_1+m$ puts all constituents in the range where the coinvariant lemma applies, and the isomorphism statement of the stability degree applies at $n-m\ge s$.

items.title: Finite generation is equivalent to uniform representation stability
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values. Then $V$ is finitely generated if and only if the consistent sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable.
items.strategy: ($\Rightarrow$) If $V$ is generated in degree $\le g$, then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le g$ by the generation-degree lemma (b), and the presentation lemma gives a surjection $M:=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{g}M(i)^{\oplus b_i}\twoheadrightarrow V$ with kernel $K$; by the Noetherian theorem $K$ is finitely generated, say in degree $\le r$. Exactness of $\Phi_a$ over $\mathbb Q$ writes $\Phi_a(V)\cong\Phi_a(M)/\Phi_a(K)$; the free summands have injectivity degree $0$ and $\operatorname{surj-deg}(K)\le r$, so $T$ is injective on $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ for $n\ge r$; hence $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)\le r$, $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)\le\max(g,r)$ and the weight is finite. The preceding proposition then gives uniform representation stability in degrees $\ge\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)+\operatorname{weight}(V)$. ($\Leftarrow$) If the sequence is uniformly representation stable for $n\ge N$, then for $n\ge N$ the $S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is all of $V_{n+1}$, so the images of the finitely many $F I$-maps $V_n\to V_{n+1}$ span $V_{n+1}$; by induction $V=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le N})$, and since each $V_{\le N}$ is finite-dimensional by hypothesis, $V$ is finitely generated.

items.title: Character polynomials in the cycle counts $X_i$
items.statement: For $i\ge1$ and $n\ge0$ let $X_i\colon S_n\to\mathbb N$ be the class function sending a permutation to the number of its $i$-cycles ([[def-permutation-support-disjoint-cycles-and-cycle-type]]); thus $X_1(\sigma)$ is the number of fixed points. A **character polynomial** is a polynomial $P\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ in finitely many of the variables $X_i$, its **weighted degree** being defined by $\deg X_i:=i$ ([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Since the class functions on $S_n$ form a $\mathbb Q$-algebra under pointwise multiplication ([[def-class-function-and-the-space-of-complex-class-functions]]), every character polynomial $P$ defines a class function $P\colon S_n\to\mathbb Q$ for every $n\ge0$. The expression is not unique on a single $S_n$, since $X_i$ vanishes identically for $i>n$; it is unique in the limit: if $P$ and $Q$ agree as functions on $S_n$ for infinitely many $n$, then $P=Q$. A sequence $(\chi_n)$ of class functions with $\chi_n$ a class function on $S_n$ is **eventually polynomial** when there are $N$ and a character polynomial $P$ with $\chi_n(\sigma)=P(\sigma)$ for all $n\ge N$ and all $\sigma\in S_n$.
items.strategy: Define the $X_i$ as class functions (they are constant on conjugacy classes because cycle type is a conjugacy invariant), define evaluation and weighted degree, and prove uniqueness by evaluating at permutations that fix all but a fixed finite set: for a monomial of top weighted degree $\le M$, the substitutions $X_1\mapsto n-c$, $X_r\mapsto X_r(\rho)$ for $r\ge2$ produce a polynomial in $n$; vanishing for infinitely many $n$ forces the coefficient of the top $X_1$-power to vanish on all fixed-point-free cycle types, and descending on the $X_1$-degree gives $P=0$. No representation theory is used in this definition.

items.title: Padded irreducible characters are eventually given by character polynomials
items.statement: For every partition $\lambda$ there is a character polynomial $P_\lambda\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of weighted degree at most $|\lambda|$ such that for every $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$ $$\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=P_\lambda(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots),$$ where $\chi^{\lambda[n]}$ is the character of the irreducible Specht module $S^{\lambda[n]}$.
items.strategy: Classical route of Macdonald's Example I.7.14. Fix $\lambda\vdash m$ and write $N:=n-m\ge\lambda_1$. By the published character-value formula ([[cor-irreducible-symmetric-group-character-values-are-power-sum-coefficients]]) $\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=\langle s_{\lambda[n]},p_{\rho(\sigma)}\rangle$, and the Frobenius coefficient formula applied with the $n+1$ variables $x_0,x_1,\dots,x_n$ exhibits the value as a coefficient in $\Delta\prod_rp_r^{X_r(\sigma)}$; the product is homogeneous, so the $x_0$-exponent is forced by the other exponents and the substitution $x_0=1$ removes $N$ from the extraction: $\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=\langle E\cdot P(\sigma),s_\lambda\rangle$ with $E=\prod_i(1-x_i)$ and $P(\sigma)=\prod_{r\ge1}(1+p_r)^{X_r(\sigma)}$ in the completed stable ring, the inner product being the Hall form ([[def-hall-inner-product-on-symmetric-functions]], [[def-stable-schur-function-by-bialternants]], [[def-power-sum-and-complete-homogeneous-symmetric-polynomials]]). Since $s_\lambda$ has degree $m$, only the total-degree-$m$ component of $E\cdot P(\sigma)$ contributes; expanding $E=\sum_j(-1)^je_j$ and $P(\sigma)=\prod_r\sum_{k_r}\binom{X_r(\sigma)}{k_r}p_r^{k_r}$ shows that this component is a finite $\mathbb Q$-linear combination of products $e_jp_{r_1}^{k_1}\cdots p_{r_s}^{k_s}$ with $j+\sum r_ik_i=m$, and the Hall inner product with $s_\lambda$ of each such product is a rational constant; hence $\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=\sum_{j+\sum r_ik_i=m}c_{j,k}s_{\lambda}\prod_r\binom{X_r(\sigma)}{k_r}$, a polynomial in the cycle counts of weighted degree $\le m$, independent of $N$. Uniqueness of the polynomial is the injectivity of the cycle-count evaluation for infinitely many $n$ recorded in the definition.

items.title: Finitely generated FI-modules have eventual character polynomials
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d=\operatorname{weight}(V)$ and stability degree $s=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. Then there is a unique character polynomial $P_V\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of weighted degree at most $d$ such that $$\chi_{V_n}(\sigma)=P_V(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots)$$ for every $n\ge s+d$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$; here $\chi_{V_n}$ is the character of the $kS_n$-module $V_n$, and $\mathbb Q\subseteq k$ is the prime field.
items.strategy: By the stability-range proposition applied to $V$, there are constants $c_\lambda\ge0$ with $V_n\cong\bigoplus_\lambda c_\lambda V(\lambda)_n$ for all $n\ge s+d$, the sum over the finitely many $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|\le d$. For each such $\lambda$, $\lambda_1\le s$ by the first-row bound, so $n\ge s+d\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ and the padded character polynomial lemma gives $\chi_{V(\lambda)_n}=P_\lambda$ of degree $\le|\lambda|$ on that range; additivity of characters gives $\chi_{V_n}=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda P_\lambda$, a character polynomial of weighted degree at most $d$ and with rational coefficients, as a function on all $S_n$ with $n\ge s+d$. Uniqueness: if two polynomials of weighted degree $\le d$ agree on $S_n$ for all $n\ge s+d$, then by the uniqueness statement of the character-polynomial definition they are equal.

references.title: Thomas Church, Jordan S. Ellenberg and Benson Farb, “FI-modules and stability for representations of symmetric groups”, arXiv:1204.4533v4 (2014); published in Duke Math. J. 164 (2015) 1833–1910
