items.title: Formal adjoints of differential operators on metric vector bundles
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, $\mu$ a smooth positive density on $M$, and $E,F\to M$ finite-rank smooth vector bundles over $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ with smooth bundle metrics, Hermitian (first-variable-linear) in the complex case, with the conventions of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]. Let $P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(F)$ be a linear differential operator of order at most two (the target-$F$ version of the local description in [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]).

Then there is a unique linear differential operator $P^\star:\Gamma(F)\to\Gamma(E)$ of order at most two such that
$$\int_M\langle Pu,v\rangle_F\,d\mu=\int_M\langle u,P^\star v\rangle_E\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $u\in\Gamma_c(E)$ and $v\in\Gamma_c(F)$; it is the **formal adjoint** of $P$. It is given locally as follows: in a chart with coordinates $x$, with density coefficient $\gamma>0$ defined by $\mu=\gamma\,|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$ ([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), with orthonormal frames of $E$ and $F$, and with local coefficients $Pu=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}a_\alpha D^\alpha u$,
$$P^\star v=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\gamma^{-1}D^\alpha\bigl(\gamma\,a_\alpha^*v\bigr),$$
where $a_\alpha^*$ is the fibre adjoint. Consequently:
1. if $P$ has order $\delta\in\{0,1,2\}$, with principal symbol defined on a chart by $\sigma_\delta(P)(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=\delta}a_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha$, then $\sigma_\delta(P^\star)=(-1)^\delta\sigma_\delta(P)^*$; thus a Laplace-type operator has a Laplace-type formal adjoint with the same principal form;
2. $(P^\star)^\star=P$;
3. if $E=F$, then $P$ is formally symmetric in the sense of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] exactly when $P=P^\star$.
items.strategy: Local construction. In a chart with orthonormal frames and density coefficient $\gamma$, integrate the product $(Pu)_\lambda\overline{v}_\lambda\gamma$ by parts $|\alpha|$ times; each step cancels the boundary term because $u$ and $v$ have compact support ([[lem-euclidean-stokes-for-a-compactly-supported-form]] applied to the compactly supported $(n-1)$-forms built from the products), and the derivatives falling on $\gamma$ and on $a_\alpha$ produce exactly the displayed formula. Uniqueness on an open set: if a smooth operator $Q$ satisfies $\int\langle Pu,v\rangle=\int\langle u,Qv\rangle$ for all compactly supported smooth $u,v$ in a chart, then for fixed $v$ the section $Qv$ vanishes wherever it is nonzero-free: if a component of $Qv$ were nonzero at a point, a compactly supported $u$ equal to a nonnegative cutoff times that component near the point would make the integral nonzero, a contradiction. Gluing: over an overlap of two charts, the two locally constructed operators both satisfy the adjoint identity against tests supported in the overlap, so their difference $R$ satisfies $\int\langle u,Rv\rangle=0$ for all such tests and hence vanishes there by the previous paragraph; the local operators therefore agree on overlaps and patch to one global smooth operator $P^\star$, which is unique by the same argument. The local formula shows that $P^\star$ has order at most that of $P$ and gives the symbol identity in (1), since the top-order part of $\gamma^{-1}D^\alpha(\gamma a_\alpha^*v)$ is $(-1)^{|\alpha|}a_\alpha^*D^\alpha v$. Applying the defining identity twice and using uniqueness gives $(P^\star)^\star=P$, and (3) is the defining identity itself. The construction is made over the given atlas and uses no choice, no partition of unity and no global pseudodifferential calculus.
items.axiom_use: None: finite chart constructions, glued by uniqueness; the Euclidean compact-support Stokes lemma is choice-free.

items.title: Complex manifolds, holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian metrics
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$. A **chart** on a topological space $X$ is a homeomorphism $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)$ from an open set $U\subseteq X$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb C^m$ with its usual topology ([[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]]); two charts $\varphi,\psi$ are **holomorphically compatible** when the transition maps $\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$ and $\varphi\circ\psi^{-1}$ are holomorphic on the open sets where they are defined ([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). A **holomorphic atlas** is a family of pairwise compatible charts whose domains cover $X$. A **complex manifold of dimension $m$** is a nonempty Hausdorff ([[def-hausdorff-space]]) second-countable ([[def-second-countable-space]]) topological space carrying a holomorphic atlas; exactly as for [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]] one passes to the maximal atlas and calls its members holomorphic charts, and for connected $X$ the case $m=1$ recovers Riemann surfaces ([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]).

A **holomorphic map** $f:X\to Y$ between complex manifolds is a continuous map whose expression in every pair of holomorphic charts is holomorphic ([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]); equivalently, composition with $f$ preserves holomorphic functions.

**Induced smooth structure and complex structure.** Holomorphic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C^m$ are smooth ([[cor-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables-are-smooth]]), so every holomorphic atlas is a smooth atlas ([[def-smooth-atlas]]) and $X$ is a smooth manifold of real dimension $2m$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) whose smooth charts include the holomorphic ones. In holomorphic coordinates $z_k=x_k+iy_k$ the **complex structure** is the endomorphism field $J$ of the tangent bundle determined by $J\partial_{x_k}=\partial_{y_k}$ and $J\partial_{y_k}=-\partial_{x_k}$; it satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$ and is independent of the holomorphic chart because holomorphic transition maps have complex-linear differentials ([[thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables]], [[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]). A **Hermitian metric** on $X$ is a Riemannian metric $g$ ([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying $g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors; its Riemannian volume density is written $\mu_g$ ([[def-riemannian-volume-density]]).

**Holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian bundle metrics.** A **holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r$** on $X$ is a smooth complex vector bundle $\pi:E\to X$ of rank $r$ ([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]], [[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]) together with an open cover $(V_\alpha)$ of $X$ and smooth local trivializations $\theta_\alpha:E|_{V_\alpha}\to V_\alpha\times\mathbb C^r$ whose transition matrices $g_{\alpha\beta}:V_\alpha\cap V_\beta\to\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$, defined by $\theta_\alpha\theta_\beta^{-1}(p,v)=(p,g_{\alpha\beta}(p)v)$, are holomorphic. A **holomorphic frame** over an open set $V$ is such a trivialization. A **Hermitian metric** $h$ on $E$ is a smooth bundle metric ([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]) whose fibre pairings are positive definite Hermitian forms, linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second.
items.strategy: Maximal atlas: the argument of [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]] applies verbatim with $\mathbb C^m$ in place of $\mathbb C$; pairwise compatibility of a family of charts means all transition maps are holomorphic, and the union of a holomorphic atlas with all charts compatible with it is again a holomorphic atlas, giving the unique maximal atlas. Holomorphic functions of several variables are of class $C^\infty$ ([[cor-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables-are-smooth]]), so each transition map is a smooth diffeomorphism between open subsets of $\mathbb R^{2m}$ and the maximal holomorphic atlas is a smooth atlas; the induced smooth structure is the one used for tangent vectors, densities and smooth sections ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Complex structure: on the overlap of two holomorphic charts the transition differential is complex-linear ([[thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables]] and the complex Jacobian of [[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]), so it intertwines the two local definitions of $J$, which is therefore a globally defined smooth endomorphism field with $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$; the tangent bundle is thereby a smooth complex vector bundle in the sense of [[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]. Holomorphic bundle: the transition matrices of a holomorphic bundle are holomorphic functions with values in $\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$; conversely the given data produce a smooth complex vector bundle by [[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]] and the cocycle identities, and changing holomorphic frame multiplies a local section by a holomorphic matrix. Hermitian bundle metric: the fibrewise positive definite Hermitian forms vary smoothly in the sense of [[def-smooth-bundle-metric]], and the condition is independent of the chosen trivializations because the only gauge freedom is conjugation by a pointwise invertible matrix. All statements are local verifications; no choice is used and no existence of metrics is asserted.
items.axiom_use: None: the structures are supplied data; the maximal-atlas and gluing verifications are local and choice-free. Existence of compatible or Hermitian metrics is not asserted here.

items.title: E-valued Dolbeault operators and their L2 structure
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold of dimension $m\ge1$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with a Hermitian metric $g$, and let $E\to X$ be a holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r$ with a Hermitian metric $h$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). Fix integers $p,q\ge0$. In a holomorphic chart with coordinates $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_m)$ and a holomorphic frame of $E$, an **$E$-valued $(p,q)$-form** is an expression
$$s=\sum_{|I|=p}\sum_{|J|=q}s_{IJ}\otimes dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J,$$
with $s_{IJ}$ smooth local sections of $E$ and increasing multi-indices $I,J$ ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]); such expressions agree on overlaps because holomorphic changes of coordinates preserve bidegree and holomorphic frame changes are complex-linear. The resulting smooth global sections of the bundle $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E$ are denoted $\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$.

The **Dolbeault operator** is the first-order operator
$$\bar\partial_E:\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)\to\mathcal A^{p,q+1}(X,E),\qquad \bar\partial_E s=\sum_{I,J}\sum_{k=1}^m \bar\partial_{z_k}s_{IJ}\otimes d\bar z_k\wedge dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J,$$
with the Wirtinger operators $\bar\partial_{z_k}$ ([[def-wirtinger-operators-in-several-complex-variables]], [[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]) acting componentwise on the local sections $s_{IJ}$. It is independent of the holomorphic chart and frame, and $\bar\partial_E^2=0$ ([[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]]).

Equip $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E$ with the Hermitian metric induced by $g$ and $h$ ([[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]] and [[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). For compactly supported smooth $s,t\in\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$ the **$L^2$ pairing**
$$\langle s,t\rangle_{L^2}=\int_X\langle s,t\rangle\,d\mu_g$$
uses the Riemannian volume density $\mu_g$ ([[def-riemannian-volume-density]], [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]) and is a complex inner product in the first-variable-linear convention ([[def-complex-l-two-inner-product]]); its completion $L^2(X,\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E)$ is a complex Hilbert space ([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]]). By [[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]] the operator $\bar\partial_E$ has a **formal adjoint** $\bar\partial_E^*:\mathcal A^{p,q+1}(X,E)\to\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$, the unique smooth first-order operator with
$$\langle\bar\partial_Es,t\rangle_{L^2}=\langle s,\bar\partial_E^*t\rangle_{L^2}$$
for all compactly supported smooth forms.

The **Dolbeault Laplacian** $\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$ is a formally symmetric Laplace-type second-order operator ([[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]) preserving each bidegree $(p,q)$, with
$$\langle\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}s,s\rangle_{L^2}=\|\bar\partial_Es\|_2^2+\|\bar\partial_E^*s\|_2^2\ge0$$
for compactly supported smooth $s$. Its principal symbol is $\sigma_2(\Delta_{\bar\partial_E})(x,\xi)=|\xi^{0,1}|_g^2\,\mathrm{id}$, where $\xi^{0,1}$ is the $(0,1)$-part of $\xi\in T_x^*X$; in particular the principal form is smooth, and it is positive definite on nonzero real covectors.
items.strategy: Well-definedness of $\bar\partial_E$: if $\theta_\alpha,\theta_\beta$ are holomorphic frames with transition matrix $g_{\alpha\beta}$, then $\bar\partial(g_{\alpha\beta}s^\beta)=\bar\partial g_{\alpha\beta}\wedge s^\beta+g_{\alpha\beta}\bar\partial s^\beta=g_{\alpha\beta}\bar\partial s^\beta$, because $g_{\alpha\beta}$ is holomorphic; hence the local $(p,q+1)$-forms glue to a global form. A holomorphic change of coordinates has complex-linear Jacobian ([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]) and preserves the bidegree decomposition and commutes with $\bar\partial$ ([[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]], [[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]), so the definition does not depend on the chart. The square vanishes by the coordinate identity $\bar\partial^2=0$ of [[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]] plus the same gluing argument. Formal adjoint: $\bar\partial_E$ is a smooth first-order operator between metric bundles over the manifold $X$ with the positive density $\mu_g$, so [[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]] applies and supplies existence, uniqueness and the local formula for $\bar\partial_E^*$. Formal symmetry of the Laplacian: for compactly supported smooth $s,t$, $\langle\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*s,t\rangle+\langle\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_Es,t\rangle=\langle\bar\partial_E^*s,\bar\partial_E^*t\rangle+\langle\bar\partial_Es,\bar\partial_Et\rangle$, and each summand is conjugate-symmetric in $s,t$, giving $\langle\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}s,t\rangle=\langle s,\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}t\rangle$; the energy identity is the same expansion with $s=t$. Principal symbol: in a holomorphic chart the operator $D=\bar\partial$ is, on the $(p,q)$-bundle, exterior multiplication by the $(0,1)$-form $\bar\partial z_k\otimes\cdot$ followed by coefficient differentiation, with principal symbol $i\varepsilon(\xi^{0,1})$ in the convention of [[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]] and [[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]]; its adjoint has symbol $-i\varepsilon(\xi^{0,1})^*$. The elementary identity $\varepsilon(\eta)\varepsilon(\eta)^*+\varepsilon(\eta)^*\varepsilon(\eta)=|\eta|^2\mathrm{id}$, checked on wedge monomials by deleting each factor with its alternating sign, gives $\sigma_2(DD^*+D^*D)(x,\xi)=|\xi^{0,1}|^2\mathrm{id}$, which is smooth in $(x,\xi)$; for a nonzero real covector the $(0,1)$-part is nonzero, so the form is positive definite. Bidegree preservation and nonnegativity follow because $\bar\partial_E$ raises $q$ by one and $\bar\partial_E^*$ lowers it by one. The metric on $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X$ is the complex-linear extension of the metric induced on exterior bundles by the compatible Riemannian metric $g$ ([[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]); the completion statement is ordinary $L^2$ completeness of a metric bundle over a Riemannian manifold with the density measure, obtained from the cited scalar Hilbert-space items on a finite trivializing cover.
items.axiom_use: None beyond the cited Hilbert-space and integration interfaces (which are choice-free at this level): the constructions are local and glued by uniqueness. No existence of Hermitian metrics is asserted.

items.title: Compact Laplace-type bundle operators: regularity and shifted parametrices
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a Laplace-type second-order differential operator on $E$ in the sense of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] — smooth coefficients, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm{id}_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors; thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$ ([[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.
items.strategy:
Chart norms (1): choose finitely many relatively compact bundle charts and a subordinate smooth partition of unity ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]], under AC). Coefficient transformation between charts is multiplication by a smooth invertible matrix followed by a smooth coordinate change with bounded derivatives and inverse derivatives on the compact overlaps; the repeated chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) expresses each derivative of order at most $k$ of a transformed coefficient as a finite sum of bounded coefficients times derivatives of order at most $k$ of the original, and integrable change of variables ([[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]]) bounds the integrals; approximate compactly supported Sobolev coefficients by smooth ones ([[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]]) and pass the bounds to the limit. This gives equivalent norms on different choices and $H^0=L^2$; completeness is checked componentwise, and smooth density follows by localizing, mollifying and summing. Compactness of $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ and the $C^r$ bound follow by applying Rellich compactness and the higher-order Sobolev embedding on finitely many fixed Euclidean balls to the finitely many localized coefficients ([[thm-rellich-compactness-from-w-one-p-to-lp-on-an-extension-domain]], [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]]); the Hilbert-space facts are [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]] and [[lem-w-one-two-is-a-hilbert-space]].

Weak $H^1$-to-$H^2$ regularity (2, $k=0$): in a precompact chart write each component of $Pu=f$ as $-\partial_i(a^{ij}\partial_ju_\alpha)=f_\alpha-\widetilde B^j_{\alpha\beta}\partial_ju_\beta-C_{\alpha\beta}u_\beta$, where the adjusted first-order coefficients absorb the derivatives of $a$; for $u\in H^1$ the right side is locally $L^2$ and bounded by $C(\|f\|_2+\|u\|_{H^1})$ on an outer patch, so the weak scalar interior $H^2$ regularity theorem ([[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]]) gives all components in $H^2$ on an inner patch. Cover $M$ by finitely many inner patches inside larger outer patches to get $\|u\|_{H^2}\le C(\|f\|_{L^2}+\|u\|_{H^1})$. Interpolation ([[lem-interpolation-absorbs-lower-order-sobolev-terms-in-elliptic-estimates]]) gives $\|u\|_{H^1}\le\varepsilon\|u\|_{H^2}+C_\varepsilon\|u\|_2$; absorbing the small term yields the stated $k=0$ estimate. Higher order: differentiate the scalar principal equation $k$ times on nested patches; for every multi-index $\alpha$ of length $k$, $w=\partial^\alpha u_\beta\in H^1$ satisfies the same scalar equation with source $\partial^\alpha f_\beta$ plus terms involving at most $k+1$ derivatives of $u$ (the commutator with the principal term always has at least one derivative on $a$), all $L^2$ and bounded by $C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{H^{k+1}})$; apply the scalar theorem on successively smaller patches, sum, and absorb the $H^{k+1}$ norm by interpolation again. Smooth data therefore give smooth weak solutions.

Coercivity and the shifted inverse (3): the form $a(u,v)$ obtained from $(Pu,v)_{L^2}$ by integrating the principal term once is bounded on $H^1\times H^1$ with at most one derivative in either argument; formal symmetry and smooth density give $a(u,v)=\overline{a(v,u)}$. With real smooth cutoffs $\chi_i$ supported in charts and $\sum_i\chi_i^2=1$, positivity of $a^{ij}$ and of the bundle metric bounds $a(\chi_iu,\chi_iu)$ below by $c\|\partial(\chi_iu)\|_2^2$ minus lower terms; summing and absorbing gives $a(u,u)\ge c\|u\|_{H^1}^2-C\|u\|_2^2$, extended by density. For $\lambda>C+1$, $a_\lambda=a+\lambda(\cdot,\cdot)_2$ is coercive, so Lax-Milgram ([[thm-lax-milgram]]) gives a unique $Bf\in H^1$ with $a_\lambda(Bf,v)=(f,v)_2$ and a bound; the $H^2$ part gives $Bf\in H^2$ and $\|Bf\|_{H^2}\le C\|f\|_2$. The inverse identities $PB=I-\lambda B$ and $BP=I-\lambda B$ follow by testing; symmetry of $a_\lambda$ makes $B$ bounded selfadjoint; its range contains all smooth sections, hence is dense, and $Bf=0$ forces $f=0$. Compactness follows from the bounded $H^2$ range and $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$ compact. Selfadjointness of the unbounded $P$ with domain exactly $H^2=\operatorname{ran}B$: for $A=P+\lambda$, $y\in\operatorname{dom}A^*$ gives $(f,y)_2=(Bf,A^*y)_2=(f,BA^*y)_2$ for all $f$, so $y=BA^*y\in H^2$ and $Ay=A^*y$; conversely symmetry puts $H^2\subseteq\operatorname{dom}A^*$. The $H^k\to H^{k+2}$ boundedness and smooth preservation of $B$ follow from the higher regularity estimate applied to $Pu=f-\lambda u$.

Parametrices (4): the inverse identities give $PB=I-\lambda B$ on $L^2$ and $BP=I-\lambda B$ on $H^2$; the error is compact on $L^2$ by the compactness of $B$, and on $H^2$ because $B:H^2\to H^4$ is bounded and $H^4\hookrightarrow H^2$ is compact. The Axiom of Choice supplies the countable-choice consequences used through the cited Rellich, Sobolev-embedding, partition and Lax-Milgram interfaces ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).
items.axiom_use: Full AC is assumed; it is used through the cited interfaces for smooth partitions of unity, Rellich compactness, higher-order Sobolev embedding and Lax-Milgram (countable choice), declared via def-axiom-of-choice and thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice. The statement is not choice-free.

items.title: Compact Laplace-type operators: smooth kernel, closed range and Green inverse
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]). There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.
items.strategy: Kernel: every $h\in\mathcal H$ lies in $H^2$, and the higher weak regularity of the preceding theorem at all orders makes $h$ smooth with $\|h\|_{H^2}\le C\|h\|_2$; the kernel is closed in $L^2$ because that estimate makes an $L^2$-convergent sequence Cauchy in $H^2$. If $\mathcal H$ were infinite dimensional, AC permits choosing successively an orthonormal sequence in it; the sequence is bounded in $H^2$, so $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$ compactness gives an $L^2$-convergent subsequence, contradicting the distance $\sqrt2$ between distinct orthonormal vectors. Closed range and complement: there is $c>0$ with $\|u\|_2\le c\|Pu\|_2$ on $H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$; otherwise a sequence with $\|u_j\|_2=1$ and $\|Pu_j\|_2<1/j$ is bounded in $H^2$ by the elliptic estimate, a subsequence converges in $L^2$, the estimate applied to differences makes it Cauchy in $H^2$, and its limit would be a nonzero element of $\mathcal H\cap\mathcal H^\perp$, a contradiction. Combining with the elliptic estimate gives $\|u\|_{H^2}\le C'\|Pu\|_2$ on that complement, hence closed range: a convergent sequence $Pu_j$ can be corrected by the $\Pi$-projections (which do not change $Pu_j$), made Cauchy in $H^2$ and passed to the limit. A vector orthogonal to the range is exactly an element of $\operatorname{dom}P^*$ with $P^*y=0$, which by selfadjointness is $\mathcal H$; the closed-subspace orthogonal decomposition ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]) gives $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ and the $L^2$ splitting. Green operator: for $f\in\mathcal H^\perp$ choose a preimage in $H^2$ and subtract its harmonic projection; the result is the unique preimage in $H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$, and setting $Gf$ equal to it and $G=0$ on $\mathcal H$ gives linearity, the bounds and the two inverse identities; compactness follows from the $H^2$ bound and the compact inclusion, selfadjointness from symmetry of $P$ (harmonic cross terms vanish), and $G\Pi=\Pi G=0$ is immediate. Smoothing projection: a finite $L^2$-orthonormal basis $e_1,\dots,e_N$ of the finite-dimensional smooth space $\mathcal H$ gives $\Pi f=\sum_j(f,e_j)_2e_j$, so $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le\sum_j\|f\|_2\|e_j\|_2\|e_j\|_{C^r}$. The $H^k\to H^{k+2}$ bounds follow from $PGf=f-\Pi f$ and the preceding regularity estimate, and give smooth preservation; the decompositions $H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2})$ are then the inverse identities read at order $k$. Nonnegativity: if $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ on smooth $u$, density and continuity extend it to $H^2$, and $(Gf,f)_2=(u,Pu)_2\ge0$ for $f\in\mathcal H^\perp$, $u=Gf$; finiteness and smoothing of the remainder give the parametrix statement.
items.axiom_use: Full AC as declared; used for the orthonormal-sequence choice in the finite-dimensionality argument and inherited through the orthogonal-decomposition and elliptic interfaces.

items.title: Harmonic representatives for compact de Rham and Dolbeault complexes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, of real dimension at least two ([[def-smooth-manifold]], [[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]). Its metric defines the $L^2$ pairing on forms by the Riemannian density ([[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]], [[def-riemannian-volume-density]], [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]); orientation is unnecessary. Let $d^*$ denote the formal adjoint of $d$ ([[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]]), and $\Delta=dd^*+d^*d$ on total real forms, or on their complexification. With domain $H^2$ the operator is nonnegative and selfadjoint. Its degreewise smooth kernels $\mathcal H^k$ are finite dimensional, and there is an orthogonal smooth decomposition
$$\Omega^k(M)=\mathcal H^k\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d\Omega^{k-1}(M)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d^*\Omega^{k+1}(M).$$
The map $h\mapsto[h]$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal H^k\to H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)$ ([[def-de-rham-cohomology]]), over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ as appropriate.

More generally let $X$ be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension $m\ge1$ with a smooth Hermitian metric ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). Let $E$ be a holomorphic bundle of finite rank with a smooth Hermitian metric ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). On $E$-valued $(p,q)$ forms let $\bar\partial_E$ be the Dolbeault operator of [[def-e-valued-dolbeault-operators-and-ltwo-structure]] and let $\bar\partial_E^*$ be its formal adjoint; for each fixed $p$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$ on the sum over $q$ is nonnegative and selfadjoint on $H^2$; its smooth harmonic spaces $\mathcal H_E^{p,q}$ are finite dimensional and
$$\Omega^{p,q}(X,E)=\mathcal H_E^{p,q}\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E\Omega^{p,q-1}(X,E)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E^*\Omega^{p,q+1}(X,E).$$
In particular harmonic forms represent the smooth Dolbeault quotient
$$H_{\bar\partial}^{p,q}(X,E):=\ker\bar\partial_E/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_E$$
uniquely. Terms outside the degree range are zero. This asserts smooth Dolbeault cohomology; an identification with sheaf cohomology requires a separate Dolbeault-resolution comparison theorem.

For either complex write $D=d$ or $D=\bar\partial_E$, $P=DD^*+D^*D$, and let $\Pi,G$ be the preceding Green projection and inverse. They preserve degree, $G$ preserves smooth forms, and on smooth forms
$$DG=GD,\qquad D^*G=GD^*,\qquad D\Pi=\Pi D=D^*\Pi=\Pi D^*=0.$$
Every closed smooth $u$ satisfies $u=\Pi u+D(D^*Gu)$.
items.strategy: Formal adjoint: in a chart, integrate each coefficient derivative of $D$ once, transpose-conjugate its matrix and include the derivatives of the bundle metric and of the density; the local expressions have smooth coefficients of order at most one and satisfy the adjoint identity, and the partition-free construction and gluing of [[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]] make them global. Uniqueness follows by testing the difference against all compactly supported smooth sections, so the local expressions agree on overlaps. Hence $D^*$ exists as a smooth differential operator, $P=DD^*+D^*D$ is formally symmetric with $(Pu,u)_2=\|Du\|_2^2+\|D^*u\|_2^2\ge0$, and it is Laplace type: for $d$, the positive-frequency principal symbol is $i\varepsilon(\xi)$, that of $d^*$ is $-i\iota(\xi^\sharp)$, and the contraction product rule $\iota(\xi^\sharp)(\xi\wedge v)=|\xi|^2v-\xi\wedge\iota(\xi^\sharp)v$, checked on wedge monomials by deleting each factor with its alternating sign, gives $\varepsilon(\xi)\iota(\xi^\sharp)+\iota(\xi^\sharp)\varepsilon(\xi)=|\xi|^2I$, hence $\sigma_2(P)=|\xi|^2I$. For $\bar\partial_E$, in a holomorphic frame the coefficients transform by holomorphic matrices ([[def-e-valued-dolbeault-operators-and-ltwo-structure]]), and the same unitary wedge-basis identity gives $\sigma_2(P)=\frac12|\xi|^2I$ (equivalently $|\xi^{0,1}|^2I$), a smooth positive-definite scalar quadratic form; the general theory of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] applies with the bundle $\Lambda^kT^*M$ or $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E$. Applying [[thm-sobolev-compactness-and-elliptic-estimates-give-fredholm-hodge-decomposition]] to $P$ gives a finite-dimensional smooth kernel $\mathcal H$, closed range $\mathcal H^\perp$ and the Green pair $\Pi,G$ with $PG=GP=I-\Pi$; smoothness of harmonic elements and the $H^k$-bounds hold in every degree, and degree preservation follows because $D$ and $D^*$ change degree by $\pm1$ and $P$ preserves it. Commutation: for smooth $u$, $P(DGu)=D(PGu)=D(u-\Pi u)=Du$; both $DGu$ and $Du$ are orthogonal to $\mathcal H$, so uniqueness of the orthogonal solution gives $DG=GD$, and the same argument gives $D^*G=GD^*$; orthogonality of the images gives $D\Pi=\Pi D=D^*\Pi=\Pi D^*=0$. Decomposition and representatives: the Green identity $u=\Pi u+DD^*Gu+D^*DGu$ is an orthogonal sum (the harmonic term is orthogonal to both images, and $(Da,D^*b)_2=(D^2a,b)_2=0$), and conversely every harmonic or image form lies in the displayed ambient space; so $\Omega^k=\mathcal H^k\oplus d\Omega^{k-1}\oplus d^*\Omega^{k+1}$, with the analogous bidegree statement for $\bar\partial_E$. If $Du=0$, then $DGu=GDu=0$, so $u=\Pi u+D(D^*Gu)$; harmonic forms are closed, giving surjectivity of $h\mapsto[h]$ onto the smooth closed/exact quotient, while a harmonic exact form $h=Dv$ has $\|h\|_2^2=(Dv,h)_2=(v,D^*h)_2=0$, giving injectivity and uniqueness. Finite dimensionality is that of $\mathcal H$. Endpoint degrees are handled by interpreting the out-of-range operators as zero. The trivial line bundle on the de Rham side and the case $p=q=0$ on the Dolbeault side are included; no sheaf comparison is used or asserted ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]], [[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]]).
items.axiom_use: Full AC as declared, inherited from the Fredholm/Green theorem and the density-integration interfaces; no separate choice principle is introduced.

title: Compact Laplace Type Operators And Hodge Representatives Examples

items.title: Flat torus harmonic forms are constant-coefficient forms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and $n\ge2$. On $T^n=\mathbb R^n/\mathbb Z^n$ with its flat metric, the forms $dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$, $i_1<\cdots<i_k$, form a basis of $\mathcal H^k$. Every real de Rham class therefore has a unique constant-coefficient representative, and $\dim H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(T^n)=\binom nk$.
items.strategy: The flat metric, the global coframe and the local isometry $q:\mathbb R^n\to T^n$ are those of [[prop-flat-torus-model-geometry]]. Write a smooth $k$-form uniquely as $u=\sum_Iu_I\,dx^I$ with periodic smooth coefficients on $\mathbb R^n$ ([[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]): uniqueness of the coefficient functions is the coordinate basis expansion, and periodicity follows by comparing the form with its pullbacks along the deck translations. On the flat torus $d=\sum_j\varepsilon(dx^j)\partial_j$ and, because a formal adjoint is determined by the identity $\int\langle du,v\rangle d\mu=\int\langle u,d^*v\rangle d\mu$ against compactly supported smooth forms and the boundary terms cancel by periodicity, $d^*=-\sum_j\iota(\partial_j)\partial_j$ ([[thm-hodge-laplacian-kernel-represents-de-rham-and-dolbeault-cohomology]] supplies $d^*$ and the Laplacian $\Delta=dd^*+d^*d$). The elementary anticommutator identity $\varepsilon(dx^j)\iota(\partial_k)+\iota(\partial_k)\varepsilon(dx^j)=\delta_{jk}\,\mathrm{id}$, checked on wedge monomials by deleting each factor with its alternating sign, cancels the mixed second derivatives in $dd^*+d^*d$ and gives $\Delta u=-\sum_I\sum_j\partial_j^2u_I\,dx^I$. Integrating over the unit cube and cancelling opposite-face terms by periodicity gives $(\Delta u,u)_{L^2}=\sum_{I,j}\int_{[0,1]^n}|\partial_ju_I|^2\,dx\ge0$. If $u$ is harmonic this sum of nonnegative continuous integrals vanishes, so each $\partial_ju_I$ vanishes identically and each coefficient $u_I$ is constant; conversely constant coefficients give $\Delta u=0$ by the same identity. The increasing wedge monomials with constant coefficients are linearly independent and there are $\binom nk$ of them; the isomorphism $h\mapsto[h]$ of [[thm-hodge-laplacian-kernel-represents-de-rham-and-dolbeault-cohomology]] identifies this space with $H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(T^n)$, giving the unique representative and the dimension. Full AC is inherited from the cited Hodge theorem.
items.axiom_use: Full AC inherited from the Hodge theorem [[thm-hodge-laplacian-kernel-represents-de-rham-and-dolbeault-cohomology]]; the flat-torus geometry uses only countable choice.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry; Ch. VI §3.3, (3.15)–(3.16), printed pp. 294–295: the harmonic decomposition whose flat-torus instance is computed here; Ch. VI §7.1, printed pp. 309–310: the corresponding Dolbeault statement used only as context

title: Compact Support Sheaf Calculus

items.title: Support of a section of a sheaf
items.statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of $k$-vector spaces (or of abelian groups) on $X$, let $U\subseteq X$ be open and let $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. The support of $s$ is $$\operatorname{Supp}(s):=\{\,x\in U: s_x\neq 0\,\}\subseteq U,$$ where $s_x$ denotes the germ of $s$ at $x$ in the stalk $\mathcal F_x$. A section $s\in\mathcal F(X)$ is compactly supported when its support is a compact subspace of $X$. For a subspace $Z\subseteq X$ and a presheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Z$, the support of $t\in\mathcal G(Z)$ is defined by the same condition using the stalks of $\mathcal G$. When $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces the following hold: (1) $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is closed in $U$; (2) $\operatorname{Supp}(s)=\varnothing$ if and only if $s=0$; (3) $\operatorname{Supp}(s|_V)=\operatorname{Supp}(s)\cap V$ for every open $V\subseteq U$. The support is not assumed closed in $X$ nor compact.
items.strategy: Definition plus the three standard consistency facts. (1) If $x\notin\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ then $s_x=0$, and two germs are equal exactly when the sections agree on a common open neighbourhood of $x$ (def-germ-of-section, def-stalk-of-presheaf); hence $s$ vanishes on an open neighbourhood of every point of $U\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(s)$, so that complement is open in $U$. (2) If $\operatorname{Supp}(s)=\varnothing$ then every germ of $s$ is zero, so locality of a sheaf applied to the cover of $U$ by all its open subsets gives $s=0$ (lem-section-zero-if-all-germs-zero); the converse is immediate. (3) Restriction is compatible with the germ maps, so $(s|_V)_x=s_x$ for $x\in V$. Compactly supported sections are exactly the sections whose support is contained in some compact set; the empty section has empty support. No choice is used anywhere.
items.axiom_use: None: germs, stalks, supports and restrictions are elementary and choice-free.

items.title: Sections on a compact set extend to a neighbourhood
items.statement: Let $K\subseteq X$ be a compact subset of a locally compact Hausdorff space, let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ and let $i:K\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion. Then the canonical map $$\varinjlim_{U\supseteq K,\ U\ \text{open}}\mathcal F(U)\longrightarrow\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)=(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K)$$ is an isomorphism. Moreover, for pairwise disjoint compact subsets $K_1,\dots,K_m\subseteq X$ and sections $s_j$ of $\mathcal F$ over open neighbourhoods $U_j$ of the respective $K_j$, there is a single section $s$ of $\mathcal F$ over a neighbourhood of $K_1\cup\dots\cup K_m$ which restricts to $s_j$ near $K_j$ for every $j$; in particular the zero section can be prescribed on any compact set disjoint from $K$.
items.strategy: Surjectivity: a class in $\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)$ is locally represented by ambient sections. Compactness of $K$ supplies finitely many compact subsets $C_1,\dots,C_m$ covering $K$ with ambient representatives on opens $U_j\supseteq C_j$ (finite shrinking in the compact Hausdorff space $K$, using thm-locally-compact-hausdorff-basics). On $C_i\cap C_j$ the two representatives agree as germs, hence on an open $W_{ij}\supseteq C_i\cap C_j$ (finitely many points, each with a common neighbourhood). Two-set shrinking: in a relatively compact open neighbourhood of $C_i\cup C_j$, separate the disjoint compact sets $C_i\setminus W_{ij}$ and $C_j$ by disjoint open sets (compact Hausdorff normality, thm-a-compact-hausdorff-space-is-regular-and-normal) and define new domains around $C_i,C_j$ contained in $W_{ij}$ on their overlap; after finitely many pairs the representatives glue over a neighbourhood of $K$. Injectivity: representatives with the same image agree as germs at every point of $K$, hence agree on a neighbourhood of each point; finitely many such neighbourhoods cover a neighbourhood of $K$, and locality of the sheaf gives equality there. The disjoint-family gluing is the same argument applied to the finite family $s_1,\dots,s_m$, using that pairwise disjoint compact subsets of a Hausdorff space have pairwise disjoint open neighbourhoods. All constructions are $k$-linear and natural; no cohomology and no choice are used.
items.axiom_use: None: compactness, normality and the sheaf axioms; only finite choices are made.

references.title: Pierre Schapira, An Introduction to Categories and Sheaves, lecture notes, 2023
references.locator: §10.1, printed pp. 175-176: for a subset Z with inclusion i_Z one sets F|Z = i_Z^{-1}F and Gamma(Z;F) = Gamma(Z; i_Z^{-1}F), and the natural morphism colim_{U contains Z} Gamma(U;F) -> Gamma(Z;F) of (10.1.2) is injective in general; Proposition 10.1.2(ii): it is an isomorphism whenever Z is a relatively Hausdorff compact subset of X, proved by induction on a finite cover of Z with the two-set gluing step

items.title: c-soft sheaves
items.statement: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$. Then $\mathcal F$ is c-soft (soft for compact supports) if for every compact subset $K\subseteq X$ the restriction map $$\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F),\qquad s\longmapsto s|_K,$$ is surjective, that is: every section of $\mathcal F$ over a compact subset extends to a global section. By lem-sections-near-a-compact-set-are-sections-on-that-set, this is equivalent to requiring that every section of $\mathcal F$ over an open neighbourhood of a compact set $K$ agrees near $K$ with a global section. C-softness is a property of the pair $(X,\mathcal F)$; a flasque sheaf on a locally compact Hausdorff space is c-soft.
items.strategy: This is a definition. The only mathematical content is the stated equivalence of the two formulations, which is the isomorphism $\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)\cong\varinjlim_{U\supseteq K}\mathcal F(U)$ of lem-sections-near-a-compact-set-are-sections-on-that-set, and the final remark: for flasque $\mathcal F$ a class in $\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)$ is represented by a section over an open neighbourhood of $K$, which flasqueness extends to $X$ (def-flasque-sheaf). Local compactness and the Hausdorff property ensure that compact subsets are closed and compact sets admit neighbourhood bases and separation, which the later arguments use. The terminology matches the literature (sheaves 'mous pour les compacts').
items.axiom_use: None.

references.title: Pierre Schapira, An Introduction to Categories and Sheaves, lecture notes, 2023

items.title: Compactly supported global sections and their right derived functors
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$. The compactly supported global sections of $\mathcal F$ are $$\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=\{\,s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F):\operatorname{Supp}(s)\ \text{is compact}\,\}\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal F).$$ A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ induces $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ by restriction of $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$, so $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is an additive functor with values in $k$-vector spaces, and it is left exact: for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ the sequence $0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$ is exact. Fix the supplied functorial injective resolution datum $\mathcal F\mapsto I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$ on the abelian category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces and define $$H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=H^q\bigl(\Gamma_c(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr)\quad(q\ge0),\qquad H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=0\ (q<0).$$ These groups are independent of the supplied resolution datum up to canonical natural isomorphism, and they are the right derived functors of $\Gamma_c(X,-)$, which therefore form a cohomological delta functor with connecting maps and long exact sequences. When $X$ is compact, $\Gamma_c(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ and $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(X,\mathcal F)$.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: supports of sections are closed in $X$ (def-support-of-a-sheaf-section), so the support of $\varphi(s)$ is contained in that of $s$ and the functor is well defined; left exactness holds because a section mapping to zero in $\mathcal F''$ lies in the image of $\mathcal F'$, and a section of $\mathcal F'$ inside a compactly supported section is compactly supported. Sheaves of $k$-vector spaces are modules over the constant sheaf $k_X$, so the ringed-space lemma supplies a functorial injective resolution datum (lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives), and the derived objects and their independence of the datum follow the pattern of def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections with the published comparison theorem; the delta-functor statement, hence the long exact sequences, is thm-right-derived-functors-form-a-cohomological-delta-functor. Compactness gives $\Gamma_c=\Gamma$. The Axiom of Choice is used exactly for the resolution datum; the derived-functor comparison uses dependent choice, which follows from AC.
items.axiom_use: AC: the functorial injective resolution datum on sheaves of $k$-vector spaces, obtained from the Grothendieck injective embedding theorem; the comparison and delta-functor statements use DC, which follows from AC. No other choice is used.

items.title: Compact-support acyclicity of c-soft sheaves
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$. Then: (1) if $\mathcal F$ is c-soft, every section of $\mathcal F$ over a compact subset $K\subseteq X$ extends to a compactly supported global section whose support is contained in any prescribed open neighbourhood of $K$; (2) every injective sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ is c-soft; (3) if $\mathcal F$ is c-soft, then $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>0$ (when $X$ is compact this is vanishing of ordinary sheaf cohomology); (4) c-softness is preserved by restriction to open subsets, by restriction to closed subsets, by extension by zero along an open inclusion, by arbitrary direct sums, and by tensor product with a constant $k$-vector space; (5) if $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ is a short exact sequence of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces and $\mathcal F'$ is c-soft, then every section of $\mathcal F''$ over a compact subset lifts to a section of $\mathcal F$ over an open neighbourhood of it, and the induced sequence $0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')\to0$ is exact whenever $\mathcal F$ is also c-soft; if $\mathcal F'$ and $\mathcal F$ are c-soft then $\mathcal F''$ is c-soft.
items.strategy: (1) Put $K$ inside an open $W$ with compact closure and choose a smaller open $W_0$ with $K\subseteq W_0\subseteq\overline{W_0}\subseteq W$ (thm-locally-compact-hausdorff-basics). Extend the section prescribed near $K$ to a global section by c-softness, prescribe the zero section on the compact collar $\overline W\setminus W_0$ (disjoint from $K$), glue the two prescriptions over the disjoint compact sets (lem-sections-near-a-compact-set-are-sections-on-that-set), apply c-softness again to the resulting section over a compact neighbourhood of $K\cup(\overline W\setminus W_0)$, restrict to $W$ and glue with zero across the cover $\{W, X\setminus\overline{W_0}\}$; the result is supported in $\overline{W_0}$, hence compact, and agrees with the given germs near $K$. The same construction with a prescribed neighbourhood gives the support control. (2) For open $U\subseteq X$ the canonical map $j_!k_U\to k_X$ of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces is a monomorphism (extension by zero is exact, thm-extension-by-zero-adjunction-exactness), so an injective $\mathcal I$ makes $\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\mathcal I)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I)\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_!k_U,\mathcal I)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal I)$ surjective; combined with the representation of sections over compact sets on neighbourhoods (item 1) this says that every section over a compact set extends to $X$. (3) Resolve $\mathcal F$ by injectives; each term is c-soft by (2); the successive quotients are c-soft by (5); the short exact sequences of the resolution are sequences of c-soft sheaves, so applying $\Gamma_c$ keeps them exact by (5); the acyclic-resolution theorem identifies $R^q\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ with the positive cohomology of the $\Gamma_c$-image of the resolution, which vanishes. On a compact space $\Gamma_c=\Gamma$. (4) Open and closed restrictions follow from the support-controlled extension; $j_!$ preserves c-softness by the same argument (a compactly supported section of $j_!\mathcal F$ restricts to a compactly supported section of $\mathcal F$ on the open part); direct sums are handled by covering a compact set by finitely many domains on which only finitely many summands are nonzero; the tensor clause follows after choosing a basis of the constant vector space, so that the tensor product is a direct sum of copies of $\mathcal F$. (5) Choose finitely many local lifts of the section over a compact shrinking of $K$ and patch them inductively: the difference of two lifts over a compact intersection lies in $\mathcal F'$ and is corrected by a support-controlled extension of $\mathcal F'$ (1). The compact-support exactness is proved by the same patching including the zero lift on a compact collar, and the middle-quotient statement follows because a global section of $\mathcal F''$ over a compact set lifts over a neighbourhood, which c-softness of $\mathcal F$ extends off a relatively compact model of that neighbourhood; restricting and gluing zero gives the extension for $\mathcal F''$.
items.axiom_use: AC: enough injectives and the functorial injective resolution datum for sheaves of $k$-vector spaces; basis selection in the tensor-product clause. The patching arguments are finite and use no further choice.

items.title: Compact-support calculus along open and closed embeddings
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace with closed complement $Z=X\setminus U$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the closed inclusion. (1) For every sheaf $\mathcal A$ of $k$-vector spaces on $U$ the canonical map $\Gamma_c(X,j_!\mathcal A)\to\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal A)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal A$, and $j_!$ carries c-soft sheaves on $U$ to c-soft sheaves on $X$; consequently there are natural isomorphisms $R^q\Gamma_c(X,j_!\mathcal A)\cong R^q\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal A)$ for all $q\ge0$. (2) For every sheaf $\mathcal B$ of $k$-vector spaces on $Z$ the canonical map $\Gamma_c(X,i_*\mathcal B)\to\Gamma_c(Z,\mathcal B)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal B$, $i_*$ carries c-soft sheaves on $Z$ to c-soft sheaves on $X$, and there are natural isomorphisms $R^q\Gamma_c(X,i_*\mathcal B)\cong R^q\Gamma_c(Z,\mathcal B)$ for all $q\ge0$. (3) If $Z$ is compact, then $\Gamma_c(X,i_*\mathcal B)\cong\Gamma(Z,\mathcal B)$ and $R^q\Gamma_c(X,i_*\mathcal B)\cong H^q(Z,\mathcal B)$ for all $q$.
items.strategy: (1) By def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf, $(j_!\mathcal A)(X)$ consists of the sections of $\mathcal A$ over $U$ whose support is closed in $X$; a compactly supported section of $\mathcal A$ over $U$ has compact, hence closed, support in $X$, and conversely a compactly supported global section of $j_!\mathcal A$ is a compactly supported section of $\mathcal A$ over $U$. This gives the $q=0$ isomorphism. For c-softness: given a compact $L\subseteq X$ and a section of $j_!\mathcal A$ on a neighbourhood, it is a section of $\mathcal A$ over the open part with support closed in that neighbourhood; the part of the support over $L\cap U$ is compact, and c-softness of $\mathcal A$ on $U$ extends it to a compactly supported section of $\mathcal A$ on $U$, which is a global section of $j_!\mathcal A$ agreeing near $L$ (points of $L\setminus U$ have zero germs). For the derived statement, take an injective resolution of $\mathcal A$ on $U$; its terms are c-soft on $U$ by the acyclicity lemma, $j_!$ is exact and preserves c-softness, so $j_!$ of the resolution is a resolution of $j_!\mathcal A$ by c-soft, hence $\Gamma_c(X)$-acyclic, sheaves; the acyclic-resolution theorem gives the natural isomorphisms. (2) The $q=0$ statement is the support computation: global sections of $i_*\mathcal B$ have support contained in the closed set $Z$, and compact support in $X$ is the same as compact support in $Z$; $i_*$ is exact on closed inclusions (stalks: $(i_*\mathcal B)_x=\mathcal B_x$ for $x\in Z$, $0$ otherwise) and the injective resolution of $\mathcal B$ on $Z$ is carried to a resolution by c-soft sheaves on $X$ by the same compact-neighbourhood argument as in the acyclicity lemma; the acyclic-resolution theorem then identifies the derived functors. (3) For compact $Z$, $\Gamma_c(Z,-)=\Gamma(Z,-)$ by the definition of compact support.
items.axiom_use: AC: injective resolutions on $U$ and $Z$ and the acyclic-resolution theorem (via DC, implied by AC). No further choice is used.

items.title: Vanishing compactly supported first cohomology on opens characterises c-softness
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and let $\mathcal E$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ satisfying $H^1_c(V,\mathcal E|_V)=0$ for every open subspace $V\subseteq X$. Then $\mathcal E$ is c-soft; more precisely, every section of $\mathcal E$ over a compact subset $K\subseteq X$ extends to a compactly supported global section of $\mathcal E$. Conversely, if $\mathcal E$ is c-soft then $H^q_c(V,\mathcal E|_V)=0$ for every $q>0$ and every open $V\subseteq X$, so c-softness of $\mathcal E$ is equivalent to $R\Gamma_c(V,\mathcal E|_V)$ being concentrated in degree $0$ for every open $V\subseteq X$.
items.strategy: Fix a compact $K\subseteq X$. By lem-extension-by-zero-short-exact-sequence applied to $\mathcal F=\mathcal E$ and the open complement $X\setminus K$ of the closed (compact) set $K$, there is a short exact sequence of sheaves on $X$ $$0\to j_!(\mathcal E|_{X\setminus K})\to\mathcal E\to i_*(\mathcal E|_K)\to0.$$ Apply the long exact sequence of the right derived functors of $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ (thm-right-derived-functors-form-a-cohomological-delta-functor). By the calculus of extension by zero and closed pushforward, $H^0_c(X,j_!(\mathcal E|_{X\setminus K}))=\Gamma_c(X\setminus K,\mathcal E)$ and $H^1_c(X,j_!(\mathcal E|_{X\setminus K}))=H^1_c(X\setminus K,\mathcal E)=0$ by hypothesis, while $H^0_c(X,i_*(\mathcal E|_K))=\Gamma_c(K,\mathcal E|_K)=\Gamma(K,\mathcal E|_K)$ because $K$ is compact. Exactness gives that $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal E)\to\Gamma(K,\mathcal E|_K)$ is surjective, that is, every section over $K$ extends to a compactly supported global section; this is the c-softness requirement of def-c-soft-sheaf. For the converse, restriction of a c-soft sheaf to an open subspace is c-soft and c-soft sheaves are $\Gamma_c$-acyclic (both from the acyclicity lemma), so all positive compactly supported cohomology on opens vanishes, giving the stated equivalence.
items.axiom_use: AC: the injective-resolution long exact sequences of compactly supported cohomology and the derived identities along open and closed embeddings; no further choice.

items.title: A refinement compatible with tuple-indexed coverings
items.statement: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space, let $I$ be a finite set, and let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be an open cover of $X$. Fix an integer $p\ge0$ and suppose that for every $(p+1)$-tuple $(i_0,\dots,i_p)$ of elements of $I$ a family $(W_{i_0\dots i_p,k})_k$ of open subsets of $U_{i_0}\cap\dots\cap U_{i_p}$ is given which covers it. Then there are a finite set $J$, a map $\alpha:J\to I$ and an open cover $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ of $X$ with $V_j\subseteq U_{\alpha(j)}$ for all $j$, such that every $V_{j_0}\cap\dots\cap V_{j_p}$ is contained in some $W_{\alpha(j_0)\dots\alpha(j_p),k}$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Induction on p with a shrinking lemma for finite covers of a normal space. The base case p=0 is a finite subcover of the family of all W_{i,k}. In the induction step the p-tuple-indexed covers are the meet families over all (p+1)-tuples with the same underlying set, which makes every tuple whose alpha-values have a repetition automatically compatible; the remaining failing tuples are then removed one at a time by splitting one cover member V_{j_0} into the open pieces V_{j_0} cap W_{i,k} (k in a finite subcover of a compact closed piece) and V_{j_0} minus the closed union of the members whose alpha-values lie in {i_1,...,i_p}. The counts N(i) of failing tuples decrease strictly under each fix-up and never increase, so the descent terminates. All selections are finite; no AC.
items.axiom_use: None: compactness provides finite subcovers, the shrinking uses normality, and only finitely many choices are made.

items.title: Refinement-limit Cech cohomology computes sheaf cohomology on compact Hausdorff spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space. For every sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and every $p\ge0$, the canonical comparison map $$\varphi^p_X:\check H^p(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^p(X,\mathcal F)$$ from the refinement-limit Cech cohomology of $X$ (taken over all open covers, equivalently over finite open covers because $X$ is compact) to sheaf cohomology is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal F$; these isomorphisms form an isomorphism of cohomological delta functors extending the identity in degree $0$ and hence commute with the connecting homomorphisms of short exact sequences. Consequently, if a cofinal family of open covers of $X$ has $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $p>d$, then $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $p>d$.
items.strategy: The comparison map is the filtered colimit, over the directed preorder of open covers, of the fixed-cover comparison maps of thm-cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-comparison; naturality in $\mathcal F$ and compatibility with refinement maps are parts of that theorem (with thm-refinement-map-independent-on-cohomology making the refinement maps well defined). Finite covers are cofinal because a compact space is quasi-compact. Isomorphism: (i) the functors $\check H^p(X,-)$ form a cohomological delta functor on abelian sheaves extending $\Gamma$: degree $0$ is lem-cech-h0-global-sections together with thm-zero-sheaf-cohomology-global-sections; the connecting maps are constructed on the limit by lifting a cocycle to a cochain of $\mathcal G$ over a common refinement on which the epimorphism $\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ is locally split, taking the Cech differential of the lift, and verifying well-definedness using common refinements and the alternating prism homotopy (thm-refinement-map-independent-on-cohomology); exactness of the long sequences follows from the fixed-cover exact sequences and exactness of filtered colimits; this is the boundary construction of Stacks 09V2. (ii) Effaceability: embed $\mathcal F$ in an injective $\mathcal I$; injective sheaves are flasque (lem-injective-sheaves-flasque) and every cover is $\mathcal I$-acyclic (thm-flasque-sheaves-acyclic with def-acyclic-cover-for-sheaf), so the fixed-cover comparison is an isomorphism (lem-acyclic-rows-and-columns-of-cech-double-complex, clause 3) onto $H^p(X,\mathcal I)=0$, whence $\check H^p(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for $p>0$. (iii) By universality of effaceable cohomological delta functors (thm-effaceable-cohomological-delta-functors-are-universal) and uniqueness of the extension of the degree-zero identity (cor-universal-delta-functors-extending-the-same-degree-zero-functor-are-uniquely-isomorphic), applied to the derived-functor delta functor $H^\bullet(X,-)$ (thm-derived-functors-are-universal-delta-functors, prop-positive-right-derived-functors-are-effaceable-by-injectives), the canonical comparison is the unique delta-functor isomorphism extending the identity in degree $0$; hence it is an isomorphism in every degree. The cofinal-family corollary is immediate from the definition of the colimit and the isomorphism. No acyclic cover of $\mathcal F$ is assumed.
items.axiom_use: AC: enough injectives for abelian sheaves, the chosen refinement data in def-global-cech-cohomology-directed-limit, and dependent choice (from AC) for the derived-functor comparison theorems.

items.title: A polyhedral dimension bound for every sheaf
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $P=|K|$ be the realization of a finite abstract simplicial complex $K$ of dimension $d$ (a finite compact polyhedron of dimension $d$), and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $P$. Then: (1) $H^q(P,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>d$; (2) for every open subspace $U\subseteq P$ and every sheaf $\mathcal E$ of abelian groups on $U$, $H^q_c(U,\mathcal E)=0$ for every $q>d$; (3) more generally, the same conclusions hold for every compact topological space in which every open cover admits a finite open refinement of order at most $d+1$, and for every open subspace of such a space. These bounds concern arbitrary sheaves, not merely cellular, constructible or coherent ones. If $L\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex, then $|L|$ is closed in $P$, the complement $P\setminus|L|$ is open, and every open subspace of $P\setminus|L|$ is an open subspace of $P$; this is the fibre model on which the bound is applied.
items.strategy: (1) By lem-refinement-limit-cech-cohomology-agrees-with-sheaf-cohomology it suffices to prove $\check H^q(P,\mathcal F)=0$ for $q>d$ in the refinement limit. The realization $|K|$ is compact and Hausdorff (prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization), and the barycentric identification carries the weak topology to the Euclidean one (lem-finite-simplicial-weak-topology-agrees-with-euclidean-topology), so $P$ is a compact metric space. For an open cover $\mathcal U$ of $P$, choose a Lebesgue number (thm-lebesgue-number-lemma) and, using that the mesh of iterated barycentric subdivisions tends to zero (lem-mesh-of-iterated-simplicial-barycentric-subdivision-tends-to-zero, with def-metric-bounded-diameter), a subdivision $r$ so fine that each open vertex star has diameter below that number; the open stars of $\mathrm{sd}^rK$ (def-open-and-closed-stars-in-a-subdivision) then form a finite open cover refining $\mathcal U$. Every point of a star cover lies in at most $d+1$ members: the vertices of $\mathrm{sd}^rK$ meeting at a point span a simplex of $\mathrm{sd}^rK$, which has dimension at most $d$. Hence the ordered Cech complex of the star cover (def-cech-cochain-complex-open-cover) has $C^p=0$ for $p>d$, so $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for $p>d$ on that cover. Star covers of all sufficiently fine subdivisions are cofinal among finite covers and finite covers are cofinal in the refinement limit (def-global-cech-cohomology-directed-limit), so $\check H^q(P,\mathcal F)=0$ for $q>d$; the comparison gives (1). (2) For the open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow P$ the functors $\Gamma_c(U,-)$ and $\Gamma(P,j_!(-))$ agree and have naturally isomorphic right derived functors by lem-compact-support-calculus-of-extension-by-zero-and-closed-pushforward, so $R\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal E)\cong R\Gamma(P,j_!\mathcal E)$; applying (1) to the sheaf $j_!\mathcal E$ on the compact space $P$ gives the vanishing. (3) The same proof with the order bound used directly: each open cover of the space admits a finite refinement of order at most $d+1$, so its Cech complex vanishes above $d$, and these refinements are cofinal; the compact-support clause follows as in (2). A subcomplex $L$ is a finite union of simplices, hence $|L|$ is closed in $P$; open subsets of the open subspace $P\setminus|L|$ are open in $P$ by the definition of the subspace topology.
items.axiom_use: AC: enough injectives for abelian sheaves and the Cech refinement data; dependent choice (from AC) for the comparison and for choosing Lebesgue numbers and subdivisions in compact metric spaces.

items.title: Bounded fibrewise-soft resolutions from a uniform all-sheaf dimension bound
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map between locally compact Hausdorff spaces and let $d\ge0$ be an integer such that $$H^q_c(V,\mathcal F)=0\qquad(q>d)$$ for every open subspace $V$ of every fibre of $f$ and every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $k$-vector spaces on $V$. Then every sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ has a bounded resolution whose terms are c-soft on every fibre: for every sheaf $\mathcal A$ on $X$ there is an exact sequence $$0\longrightarrow\mathcal A\longrightarrow\mathcal K^0\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal K^d\longrightarrow0$$ in which each $\mathcal K^j$ restricts to a c-soft sheaf on every fibre $f^{-1}(y)$; for $d=0$ this says that $\mathcal A$ is already c-soft on every fibre. Every bounded complex of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ admits a bounded resolution by complexes whose terms are fibrewise c-soft, obtained by totalising these termwise resolutions over the bounded index range. In particular the constant sheaf $k_X$ has such a resolution. The hypothesis is the uniform fibrewise form of finite all-sheaf compact-support dimension; in the geometric applications it is supplied by finite triangulations of fibre compactifications of dimension at most $d$.
items.strategy: The fibres of $f$ are closed subspaces of the locally compact Hausdorff space $X$, hence locally compact Hausdorff. Resolve $\mathcal A$ by injective sheaves on $X$ (lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives with AC). Each injective term is c-soft on $X$ and its restriction to each closed fibre is c-soft on that fibre (the acyclicity lemma, clauses (2) and (4)). Let $\mathcal Q$ be the cokernel after $d$ steps, so that $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal I^0\to\cdots\to\mathcal I^{d-1}\to\mathcal Q\to0$ is exact. Restricting to an open subspace $V$ of a fibre preserves exactness and keeps the $\mathcal I^j|_V$ c-soft, hence $\Gamma_c(V,-)$-acyclic (acyclicity lemma, clause (3)); the long exact sequence of compactly supported cohomology (thm-right-derived-functors-form-a-cohomological-delta-functor) therefore gives dimension shifting $H^q_c(V,\mathcal Q|_V)\cong H^{q+d}_c(V,\mathcal A|_V)$ for $q>0$. The right-hand side vanishes because $q+d>d$, so $\mathcal Q$ is c-soft on every fibre by lem-vanishing-compactly-supported-h1-on-opens-implies-c-soft. Truncating gives the displayed resolution of length $d$ with fibrewise c-soft terms; the same construction applies to $k_X$. For a bounded complex, resolve each term by such a fibrewise c-soft resolution and totalise over the bounded index range; the uniform length $d$ makes every total-degree diagonal finite, so the total complexes form a bounded resolution with the required fibrewise c-softness.
items.axiom_use: AC: injective resolutions on $X$ and dependent choice for the long exact sequences and derived-functor comparisons; no other choice.

title: Compact Support Sheaf Calculus Examples

items.title: Compact support and softness on a finite discrete space
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a finite set with the discrete topology and let $k$ be a field. A sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ is the same thing as a family $(V_x)_{x\in X}$ of $k$-vector spaces, its stalks, with $\mathcal V(U)=\prod_{x\in U}V_x$ for open $U\subseteq X$. Then: (1) every sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ is c-soft; (2) $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal V)=\bigoplus_{x\in X}V_x$ and $H^q_c(X,\mathcal V)=0$ for every $q>0$, so the derived object $R\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal V)$ is concentrated in degree zero with value $\bigoplus_{x\in X}V_x$; (3) for a $k$-vector space $W$ let $W_X$ be the constant sheaf with stalk $W$; then the functor $W\mapsto W_X$ is right adjoint to $\Gamma_c(X,-)$, that is, there is a natural bijection $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)}(\mathcal V,W_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k\Big(\bigoplus_{x\in X}V_x,\,W\Big)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal V),W).$$ This is the discrete case of the exceptional inverse image along the terminal map $X\to\mathrm{pt}$.
items.strategy: (1) A compact subset of a finite discrete space is a finite set, and a section on it is a finite tuple, which extends by zero; so every sheaf is c-soft directly. (2) $X$ is compact, so $\Gamma_c(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ and, since every sheaf is c-soft, the compact-support acyclicity lemma gives $H^q_c(X,\mathcal V)=0$ for $q>0$ and $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal V)=\prod_{x\in X}V_x=\bigoplus_{x\in X}V_x$ (a finite product of vector spaces is their direct sum). (3) Since $X$ is discrete, a morphism $\mathcal V\to W_X$ is exactly a family of $k$-linear maps $V_x\to W$, one for each $x$; the components compose with the canonical embeddings $V_x\to\bigoplus_xV_x$, and this correspondence is a natural bijection by the universal property of the direct sum of vector spaces: a family of linear maps out of the summands is the same as one linear map out of the sum. Hence $W\mapsto W_X$ is right adjoint to $\Gamma_c(X,-)$. Equivalently the direct sum of the stalks is exact as a functor, so its higher derived functors vanish with no choice; on this finite space the displayed acyclicity has therefore a choice-free proof as well.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the cited compact-support acyclicity lemma (injective resolutions); the finite discrete case has a direct choice-free proof because finite products and direct sums are exact and $X$ is compact.

items.title: Truncation functors, t-cohomology, amplitude and bounded t-structures
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$ with translation $[1]$ ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]], [[def-triangulated-category]]), and set $\mathcal T^{\le n}:=\mathcal T^{\le0}[-n]$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n}:=\mathcal T^{\ge0}[-n]$ for $n\in\mathbb Z$; thus $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ exactly when $X[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$, and $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ exactly when $X[n]\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$.

For $X\in\mathcal T$ and $n\in\mathbb Z$, the t-structure axiom applied to the translate $X[n]$ and then shifted by $[-n]$ produces a distinguished triangle
$$\tau_{\le n}X\longrightarrow X\longrightarrow\tau_{\ge n+1}X\longrightarrow\tau_{\le n}X[1]$$
with $\tau_{\le n}X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\tau_{\ge n+1}X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$; such a triangle is a **truncation triangle** of $X$ at $n$. Truncation triangles of the same $X$ at the same $n$ are canonically isomorphic over $X$, so the objects and maps occurring in them are determined up to unique compatible isomorphism ([[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]]); one writes $\tau_{\le n}$ and $\tau_{\ge n}$ for the resulting **truncation functors**.

The **t-cohomology** of $X$ is
$$H^n_t(X):=(\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\ge n}X)[n],$$
an object of the heart $\mathcal C=\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ ([[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]]). The **amplitude** of $X$ is the set of $n$ with $H^n_t(X)\not\cong0$; it is *contained in* an interval $[a,b]$ when $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n\notin[a,b]$. The t-structure is **bounded** when every object of $\mathcal T$ lies in $\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ for some integer $n$ depending on the object.

This item fixes notation and conventions only; existence, essential uniqueness and all algebraic properties of $\tau_{\le n}$, $\tau_{\ge n}$ and $H^n_t$ are proved in the two immediately following lemmas.
items.strategy: Definition pack. Apply the t-structure axiom (condition (iii) of [[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) to $X[n]$: it gives a distinguished triangle $A\to X[n]\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$ and $B\in\mathcal T^{\ge1}$; translating by $[-n]$ and using $\mathcal T^{\le0}[-n]=\mathcal T^{\le n}$ together with $\mathcal T^{\ge1}[-n]=\mathcal T^{\ge0}[-(n+1)]=\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ gives the displayed truncation triangle. The membership and uniqueness assertions are exactly the content of the following lemma, which also shows that a different choice of the axiom triangle changes $\tau_{\le n}X$, $\tau_{\ge n+1}X$ and the connecting map only by the unique compatible isomorphism; nothing else is proved here.

items.title: Truncation triangles are essentially unique and give adjoint truncation functors
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$, with truncations as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]].

(i) *Essential uniqueness.* For every $X$ and $n$, every distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $B\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ is isomorphic to the truncation triangle $\tau_{\le n}X\to X\to\tau_{\ge n+1}X\to\tau_{\le n}X[1]$ by an isomorphism of triangles whose middle component is the identity of $X$; this isomorphism is unique.

(ii) *Adjunction and orthogonality.* The assignment $X\mapsto\tau_{\le n}X$ is a functor and for $T\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}(T,\tau_{\le n}X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)$, $f\mapsto(\tau_{\le n}X\to X)\circ f$, is a bijection natural in $X$; dually $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau_{\ge n}X,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,T)$ is a bijection for $T\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$. Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n},\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$ for every $n$.

(iii) *Aisle criteria.* $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ if and only if $\tau_{\le n}X\to X$ is an isomorphism, if and only if $\tau_{\ge n+1}X=0$, if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$; dually $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ if and only if $X\to\tau_{\ge n}X$ is an isomorphism, if and only if $\tau_{\le n-1}X=0$, if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n-1},X)=0$.

(iv) *Extensions, direct sums and iteration.* If in a distinguished triangle two of the three vertices lie in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ (respectively $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$), then so does the third; a finite direct sum lies in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ (respectively $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$) if and only if each summand does. For $m\le n$ there are canonical isomorphisms $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\le n}\cong\tau_{\le m}$, $\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\le m}\cong\tau_{\le m}$, $\tau_{\ge n}\tau_{\ge m}\cong\tau_{\ge n}$ and $\tau_{\ge m}\tau_{\ge n}\cong\tau_{\ge n}$ compatible with the truncation maps, and $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge n}=0$ when $m<n$.
items.strategy:
Existence is the t-structure axiom; the work is uniqueness, adjunction, functoriality and the closure properties.
(1) Orthogonality for all shifts: the axiom gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge1})=0$, and the shift criteria of [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] turn this into $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n},\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$ for every $n$: a map from $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ to $Y\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ is a map $X[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le0}\to Y[n]\in\mathcal T^{\ge1}$.
(2) Uniqueness: let $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ be distinguished with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$, $B\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$. For $T\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the long exact Hom sequence of [[thm-long-exact-hom-sequences-of-a-distinguished-triangle]] gives an exact sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(T,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,B)$, and the last term vanishes by step (1) (also after shifting $T$), so the first map is a bijection. Applying this with $T=\tau_{\le n}X$ and with $T=A$ produces mutually inverse maps $\tau_{\le n}X\leftrightarrow A$ compatible with the maps to $X$; comparing the two triangles through the third components with [[cor-triangulated-five-lemma]] (via [[prop-distinguished-triangles-are-closed-under-shifts-and-both-rotations]]) yields the unique isomorphism of triangles over $X$. The same argument applied to two truncation triangles proves that even the truncation triangle itself is unique up to unique isomorphism over $X$.
(3) Adjunction and functoriality: the bijection in (ii) is step (2)'s sequence with $B=\tau_{\ge n+1}X$. For $f:X\to Y$ the composite $\tau_{\le n}X\to X\to Y$ factors uniquely through $\tau_{\le n}Y\to Y$ because $\tau_{\le n}Y\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$; this defines $\tau_{\le n}f$, and the uniqueness makes the assignment compatible with identities and composition. Additivity follows because for a finite biproduct the universal property identifies $\tau_{\le n}(X\oplus Y)$ with $\tau_{\le n}X\oplus\tau_{\le n}Y$; the dual statements give $\tau_{\ge n}$.
(4) Criteria (iii): if $\tau_{\ge n+1}X=0$, the truncation triangle makes $\tau_{\le n}X\to X$ an isomorphism, so $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$; conversely if $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the triangle $X\xrightarrow{1}X\to0\to X[1]$ is a decomposition triangle, so essential uniqueness identifies its third vertex with $\tau_{\ge n+1}X=0$. For the Hom formulation, if $\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$ then the truncation map $X\to\tau_{\ge n+1}X$ is zero; the rotated triangle has zero first map, so [[prop-a-distinguished-triangle-with-zero-first-map-is-split]] makes it split and $\tau_{\ge n+1}X$, being a direct summand of $X$ whose projection is zero, vanishes; hence $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$. Conversely $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ kills $\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})$ by the orthogonality of step (1), and the dual formulation is identical.
(5) Closures and iteration: if two vertices of a distinguished triangle lie in $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$, the long exact $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n},-)$ sequence and (iii) put the third there as well; the other aisle is dual, and direct sums are immediate from the orthogonality description. For $m\le n$, $\tau_{\le m}X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}\subseteq\mathcal T^{\le n}$ so (iii) identifies $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\le n}X$ and $\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\le m}X$ with $\tau_{\le m}X$; the remaining identities are dual, and for $m<n$ the composite $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge n}$ vanishes because $\tau_{\ge n}X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$, so $\tau_{\le n-1}\tau_{\ge n}X=0$ by (iii), and then $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge n}X=\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\le n-1}\tau_{\ge n}X=0$ by the iteration identities since $m\le n-1$.
