items.title: t-cohomology is functorial, additive, shift-compatible and detects amplitude
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$, with truncations and t-cohomology as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] and [[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]], and let $\mathcal C=\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ be the heart.

(i) Each $H^n_t$ is a functor from $\mathcal T$ to $\mathcal C$: for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ the induced map $H^n_t(f)$ is the unique map compatible with $f$ under the truncations, and values lie in the heart.

(ii) *Shifts.* $H^n_t(X[m])\cong H^{n+m}_t(X)$ for all $m,n\in\mathbb Z$, naturally in $X$.

(iii) *Additivity.* For a finite biproduct $X\oplus Y$ with injections $i_X,i_Y$ and projections $p_X,p_Y$, the maps $(H^n_t(i_X),H^n_t(i_Y)):H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)\to H^n_t(X\oplus Y)$ and $(H^n_t(p_X),H^n_t(p_Y)):H^n_t(X\oplus Y)\to H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)$ are mutually inverse isomorphisms; in particular $H^n_t(X\oplus Y)\cong H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)$ naturally.

(iv) *Amplitude detection.* If $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ then $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n>m$, and if $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$ then $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n<m$. If the t-structure is bounded ([[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]]), the converses hold: $H^n_t(X)=0$ for all $n>m$ implies $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$, and $H^n_t(X)=0$ for all $n<m$ implies $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$.

(v) *Concentration and its consequences.* If $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ then $\tau_{\ge m}X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$, and if $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$ then $\tau_{\le m}X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$; if $X$ lies in both aisles then the canonical map gives $X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$. If $X$ and $Y$ both have $H^n_t=0$ for every $n\ne m$, then $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H^m_t(X),H^m_t(Y))$, $f\mapsto H^m_t(f)$, is a bijection under these canonical identifications.
items.strategy:
(i) $H^n_t$ is the composite $\tau_{\le n}\circ\tau_{\ge n}\circ[n]$ of functors from the previous lemma, so it is functorial; its values lie in the heart because $\tau_{\ge n}X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$, the truncation $\tau_{\le n}$ of an object of $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ again lies in $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ (closure under extensions in (iv) of [[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]]), and $Z\in\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ is equivalent to $Z[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ by the shift criteria of the definition.
(ii) Truncation commutes with shift: for every $a$, $\tau_{\le m}(X[a])\cong(\tau_{\le m+a}X)[a]$ and dually, because both sides satisfy the same universal property with respect to the aisle $\mathcal T^{\le m}$ (or, directly, because the shifted truncation triangle is a decomposition triangle for $X[a]$ at $m$). Hence $H^n_t(X[m])=\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\ge n}(X[m])[n]\cong\tau_{\le n+m}\tau_{\ge n+m}X[n+m]\cong H^{n+m}_t(X)$, naturally.
(iii) Additive functors preserve finite biproducts; explicitly, the injections and projections of $X\oplus Y$ satisfy the biproduct identities ([[def-biproduct]]), and applying the functorial $H^n_t$ to those identities exhibits the stated mutually inverse maps.
(iv) If $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ and $n>m$, then $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n-1}$, hence $\tau_{\ge n}X=0$ by the aisle criterion and $H^n_t(X)=0$; the other aisle is dual. For the converses assume the t-structure is bounded, so choose $N\ge m$ with $X\in\mathcal T^{\le N}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -N}$. If $H^n_t(X)=0$ for all $n>m$, then for $k=N,N-1,\dots,m+1$ downwards: $X\in\mathcal T^{\le k}$ and the concentration identity proved in (v) below gives $\tau_{\ge k}X\cong H^k_t(X)[-k]=0$, so $X\cong\tau_{\le k-1}X\in\mathcal T^{\le k-1}$; after finitely many steps $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$. The lower bound is dual; the two arguments are independent and may be applied in either order.
(v) The identity $H^m_t(X)[-m]=\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge m}X$ is the definition. If $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$ then $\tau_{\ge m}X\cong X$ and the first identity follows; if $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ then $X\to\tau_{\ge m}X$ is the truncation and $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge m}X\cong\tau_{\ge m}X$, giving the second identity; both aisles force $X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$. For the map detection: the concentration identities provide canonical isomorphisms $X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$ and $Y\cong H^m_t(Y)[-m]$, and the composite $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H^m_t(X),H^m_t(Y))$ with those isomorphisms and the shift identification is exactly the map induced by the functor $H^m_t$, hence a bijection.

references.title: A. A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein and P. Deligne, «Faisceaux pervers», Astérisque 100 (1982), Société Mathématique de France (complete numdam PDF)

items.title: Hard Lefschetz splits a bounded t-structure complex
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with a bounded t-structure, with truncation functors and t-cohomology as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] and [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]]. Let $K\in\mathcal T$ and let $L:K\to K[2]$ be a morphism such that for every integer $j\ge0$ the map
$$H^{-j}_t(L^j):H^{-j}_t(K)\longrightarrow H^{-j}_t(K[2j])\cong H^j_t(K)$$
is an isomorphism, where the identification is the shift isomorphism $H^{j}_t(K)\cong H^{-j}_t(K[2j])$ of that lemma. Then there is an isomorphism
$$K\cong\bigoplus_j H^j_t(K)[-j]$$
in $\mathcal T$; the sum is finite because the t-structure is bounded. The isomorphism is not asserted to be canonical, and no compatibility with primitive lifts is claimed: this is the abstract splitting criterion, not the stronger primitive-compatible decomposition used in the Hodge theory of projective maps. The degenerate case in which $H^{-n}_t(K)$ and $H^n_t(K)$ are both zero (they vanish together because $H^{-n}_t(L^n)$ is an isomorphism) is covered by the same formulas, all of which are then the zero maps between zero objects.
items.strategy:
Proof by induction on the amplitude. Fix $K,L$ and use the boundedness of the t-structure to choose $n\ge0$ with $K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ ([[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]]); by amplitude detection (iv) of [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]] this is equivalent to $H^j_t(K)=0$ for $|j|>n$. We prove for every $n\ge0$ the statement: every $K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ admitting such an $L$ satisfies the conclusion.
Base $n=0$: $K$ lies in the heart, so the concentration identity (v) gives $K\cong H^0_t(K)$ and the sum has the single term $j=0$.
Induction step $n\ge1$. Put $A=H^{-n}_t(K)$ and $B=H^n_t(K)$. Let $a:A[n]\to K$ be the truncation map $\tau_{\le -n}K\to K$, identified with $A[n]\to K$ by the concentration identity for $K\in\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$, and let $b:K\to B[-n]$ be the truncation map $K\to\tau_{\ge n}K$, identified with $K\to B[-n]$ by the concentration identity for $K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$. Then $ba=0$, because $A[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le -n}$, $B[-n]\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le -n},\mathcal T^{\ge n})=0$ for $n\ge1$ ([[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]]).
Let $h=H^{-n}_t(L^n):A\to B$ be the isomorphism supplied by the hypothesis and define two morphisms by the truncated composites
$$c:=L^n[-2n]\circ a[-2n]\circ h^{-1}[-n]:B[-n]\to K,\qquad r:=h^{-1}[n]\circ b[2n]\circ L^n:K\to A[n].$$
Then $bc=1$ and $ra=1$: the first composites induce $1_B$ resp. $1_A$ on $H^n_t$ resp. $H^{-n}_t$, because $H^{-n}_t(L^n)=h$, the truncation maps $a$ and $b$ induce the canonical identifications on the extreme t-cohomology, and $H$ is functorial; since $B[-n]$ and $A[n]$ are concentrated in single degrees, map detection (v) of [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]] promotes these cohomological identities to the displayed identities of morphisms. Put $r':=r-(rc)b$. Then $r'a=1-(rc)(ba)=1$ and $r'c=rc-(rc)(bc)=0$, while $ba=0$ and $bc=1$; hence $(r',b)\circ(a,c)$ is the identity of $A[n]\oplus B[-n]$ with respect to the biproduct structure.
Complete $(a,c):A[n]\oplus B[-n]\to K$ to a distinguished triangle and let $K_0$ be its third vertex. The left inverse $(r',b)$ makes the triangle split by [[prop-a-distinguished-triangle-splits-exactly-when-one-connecting-map-vanishes]], so $K\cong A[n]\oplus K_0\oplus B[-n]$ with $i:K_0\to K$ the remaining inclusion and $p:K\to K_0$ the remaining projection, $pi=1$.
The summands $A[n]\cong H^{-n}_t(K)[n]$ and $B[-n]$ are concentrated in the extreme degrees, so additivity (iii) of the t-cohomology lemma applied to this biproduct gives $H^{-n}_t(K)\cong A\oplus H^{-n}_t(K_0)$ and $H^n_t(K)\cong H^n_t(K_0)\oplus B$, whence $H^{\pm n}_t(K_0)=0$. Since $K_0$ is a direct summand of $K$, it lies in $\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ (closure of the aisles under direct summands, (iv) of the truncation-triangle lemma). From $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ and $H^{-n}_t(K_0)=0$, the concentration identity (v) gives $\tau_{\le -n}K_0=0$, hence $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\ge -n+1}$ by the aisle criterion (iii) of the truncation-triangle lemma; dually $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $H^n_t(K_0)=0$ give $\tau_{\ge n}K_0=0$ and $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\le n-1}$.
Define $L_0:=p[2]\circ L\circ i:K_0\to K_0[2]$. For $0\le j<n$ one has $L_0^j=p[2j]L^ji$, so by functoriality $H^{-j}_t(L_0^j)=H^{-j}_t(p[2j])\circ H^{-j}_t(L^j)\circ H^{-j}_t(i)$. The outer maps are isomorphisms: $H^{-j}_t(i)$ is an isomorphism because $H^{-j}_t(K)\cong H^{-j}_t(K_0)$ for $-n<j<n$ by additivity and the concentration of $A[n]$ and $B[-n]$, and $H^{-j}_t(p[2j])$ has the inverse $H^{-j}_t(i[2j])$ because $pi=1$. Hence $H^{-j}_t(L_0^j)$ is an isomorphism whenever $H^{-j}_t(L^j)$ is; for $j\ge n$ both sides vanish. Thus $L_0$ satisfies the hard Lefschetz hypothesis on $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\le n-1}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -(n-1)}$ and the induction hypothesis decomposes $K_0$. Combining with $K\cong A[n]\oplus K_0\oplus B[-n]$, $A[n]=H^{-n}_t(K)[n]$ and $B[-n]=H^n_t(K)[-n]$ gives the asserted finite direct sum for $K$.

items.title: Graded hard Lefschetz has a canonical primitive decomposition
items.statement:
Let $H^j$ be objects of an abelian category, zero for all but finitely many integers $j$, and let $L:H^j\to H^{j+2}$ be morphisms whose iterates give isomorphisms $L^r:H^{-r}\to H^r$ for every $r\ge0$. Put $P^{-r}:=\ker\bigl(L^{r+1}:H^{-r}\to H^{r+2}\bigr)$ for $r\ge0$, and $P^{-r}=0$ for $r<0$. Then for every $r\ge0$ the powers of $L$ induce finite direct sum decompositions
$$H^{-r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^jP^{-r-2j},\qquad H^{r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^{r+j}P^{-r-2j},$$
each displayed power $L^j$ or $L^{r+j}$ restricts to a monomorphism on its primitive source, and both decompositions are natural for morphisms commuting with $L$. This is a decomposition statement for graded objects in an abelian category; it does not identify primitive objects with classes annihilated by an untruncated map on a derived splitting of a complex.
items.strategy: Fix $r\ge0$. The restriction of $L^{r+1}:H^{-r}\to H^{r+2}$ to $\operatorname{im}(L:H^{-r-2}\to H^{-r})$ is the composite $L^{r+2}=L^{r+1}L$, which is an isomorphism by hypothesis; hence the kernel of $L^{r+1}$ meets $\operatorname{im}L$ trivially and $L^{r+1}$ is an epimorphism, with the explicit right inverse $s=L\circ(L^{r+2})^{-1}:H^{r+2}\to H^{-r}$ (here $(L^{r+2})^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of the isomorphism). The sequence $0\to P^{-r}\to H^{-r}\xrightarrow{L^{r+1}}H^{r+2}\to0$ is therefore short exact ([[def-exact-sequence-and-short-exact-sequence-in-an-abelian-category]]), and the splitting lemma ([[thm-splitting-lemma-in-an-abelian-category]], [[def-split-short-exact-sequence-in-an-abelian-category]]) gives a biproduct decomposition $H^{-r}\cong P^{-r}\oplus H^{r+2}$ whose second inclusion is $s$. Since $L^{r+2}=L^{r+1}L$ is an isomorphism, the map $L$ on $H^{-r-2}$ is a split monomorphism, and its image equals $\operatorname{im}s$: indeed $s=L(L^{r+2})^{-1}$ lands in $\operatorname{im}L$, and $Ly=s(L^{r+2}y)$, so every element of $\operatorname{im}L$ is in $\operatorname{im}s$. Hence $H^{-r}=P^{-r}\oplus LH^{-r-2}$ with explicit projection the idempotent $L(L^{r+2})^{-1}L^{r+1}$ ([[def-image-and-coimage-in-a-category-with-kernels-and-cokernels]] for kernels and images). Iterating this decomposition through $H^{-r-2},H^{-r-4},\dots$ terminates because the graded family is finite: since $L$ is a monomorphism on each $H^{-m}$ with $m\ge1$, it carries the direct sum $H^{-r-2}=P^{-r-2}\oplus LH^{-r-4}$ to the direct sum $LH^{-r-2}=LP^{-r-2}\oplus L^2H^{-r-4}$, and continuing gives $H^{-r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^jP^{-r-2j}$. Each displayed power restricts to a composite of the split monomorphisms $L$ on the intermediate $H^{-m}$, $m\ge1$, hence is a monomorphism on its primitive source. Applying the isomorphism $L^r:H^{-r}\to H^r$ to the first decomposition and using $L^rL^j=L^{r+j}$ gives the second. Naturality: a morphism of graded objects commuting with $L$ commutes with the isomorphisms $L^{r+2}$ and their inverses, with the kernels $P^{-r}$, with the explicit projections and injections, and hence with the whole finite construction; the same argument applies at each induction step. Degenerate cases (a zero $H^{-r}$, or a finite family ending before the induction does) are covered by the same split maps.

items.title: The nilpotent Lefschetz filtration is canonical and self-dual
items.statement:
Let $N$ be a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space $H$ over a field. There is a unique increasing finite filtration $W$ of $H$ such that $NW_i\subset W_{i-2}$ for all $i$ and $N^r:\operatorname{Gr}^W_rH\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-r}H$ is an isomorphism for every $r\ge0$. It is given intrinsically by
$$W_i=\sum_{a,b\ge0,\ a-b=i}\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b.$$
If in addition $S$ is a nondegenerate bilinear form on $H$ with $S(Nv,w)+S(v,Nw)=0$ for all $v,w$, then $(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$ for every $i$, and consequently $S$ induces a perfect pairing between $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}H$; moreover for $i\ge0$ the form $S_i([v],[w]):=S(v,N^iw)$ on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH$ is well defined and nondegenerate.
items.strategy:
Existence and the intrinsic formula. Use a Jordan-string basis of $N$ ([[thm-nilpotent-jordan-string-basis]]): in a chain $v_0,\dots,v_{l-1}$ with $Nv_t=v_{t-1}$, $Nv_0=0$, assign $v_t$ the weight $2t-l+1$. The resulting filtration satisfies $NW_i\subset W_{i-2}$ and pairs the graded pieces symmetrically; on each chain, $\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b$ is the span of the $v_t$ with $t\le\min(a,l-1-b)$, and under $a-b=i$ the largest such index is $\lfloor(i+l-1)/2\rfloor$, with negative values giving $0$ and values beyond $l-1$ giving the whole chain. Kernels and images decompose chainwise, so the intrinsic formula holds for this filtration, independently of the chosen Jordan basis.
Uniqueness and hard Lefschetz. For a filtration satisfying the two conditions, apply the graded hard Lefschetz lemma ([[lem-graded-hard-lefschetz-has-a-canonical-primitive-decomposition]]) with degrees reversed to the graded maps $N:\operatorname{Gr}^W_t\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{t-2}$: this gives, for every $q\ge0$ and $t\le -q$, the surjectivity of $N^q:\operatorname{Gr}^W_{t+2q}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_t$ used below (composite of an isomorphism with its inverse factor). Choose a basis of each primitive graded piece of weight $r\ge0$, lift a primitive class to $v\in W_r$; its primitivity makes $N^{r+1}v\in W_{-r-3}$. The surjectivity just recorded, iterated downward through the finite filtration, produces $u\in W_{r-1}$ with $N^{r+1}u=N^{r+1}v$: correct the error successively at decreasing weights, which terminates because $W_i=0$ for $i\ll0$. Replace $v$ by $v-u$, so that $N^{r+1}v=0$ while the primitive graded class is unchanged. The strings $v,Nv,\dots,N^rv$ obtained from all primitive graded basis classes have independent associated graded classes, hence form a basis of $H$ by dimension count. Since each $N^iv$ lies in $W_{r-2i}$ with nonzero graded class, the span of those basis vectors of $W$-weight at most $i$ is exactly $W_i$; computing that span chainwise as in the first paragraph shows that the given $W$ equals the intrinsic formula $W_i=\sum_{a-b=i}\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b$. That formula depends only on $N$, so $W$ is unique.
Self-duality. Assume $S(Nv,w)+S(v,Nw)=0$ and put $W'_i:=(W_{-i-1})^\perp$. The skew-adjointness gives $NW'_i\subset W'_{i-2}$: test $Nv$ against $w\in W_{-i+1}$, for which $Nw\in W_{-i-1}$. The associated graded objects of $W'$ are the duals of those of $W$ in opposite degrees, and the induced maps $N^r$ on them are, up to the sign $(-1)^r$, the transposes of the hard Lefschetz isomorphisms for $W$; hence $W'$ satisfies the same two defining conditions. Uniqueness forces $W'=W$, i.e. $(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$. (The orthogonal complement is computed with respect to a nondegenerate bilinear form: $B^\flat$ is an isomorphism and $U^\perp=(B^\flat)^{-1}(\operatorname{ann}U)$ as in [[thm-bilinear-forms-correspond-to-linear-maps-into-the-dual]], [[def-annihilators-under-the-evaluation-pairing]] and [[thm-double-annihilator-and-annihilator-dimension]], so that $U^{\perp\perp}=U$ and $\dim U+\dim U^\perp=\dim H$ by [[thm-rank-nullity]], [[thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace]] and [[cor-dimension-of-a-direct-sum]].)
Descent of the form. The self-duality identity makes $S$ descend to a perfect pairing between opposite graded pieces (their radicals are exactly the lower filtration terms). Composing with the isomorphism $N^i:\operatorname{Gr}^W_i\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}$ for $i\ge0$ yields the form $S_i([v],[w])=S(v,N^iw)$ on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH$: independence of representatives holds because an error in $W_{i-1}$ is orthogonal to $W_{-i}$, and $N^i$ carries an error in $W_{i-1}$ into $W_{-i-1}$, orthogonal to $W_i$; nondegeneracy follows because $N^ia$ orthogonal to $W_i$ implies $a$ orthogonal to $N^iW_i$, i.e. $N^ia\in(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$, which forces $a\in W_{i-1}$ by injectivity of $N^i$ on the graded piece.

title: Lefschetz Splitting In Bounded Triangulated Categories Examples

items.title: Hard Lefschetz splitting for a three-degree complex
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal T=D^b(\mathbf{vect}^{fd}_k)$ be the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces with its canonical t-structure. Take
$$K=k[2]\oplus k\oplus k[-2]\in\mathcal T,$$
and let $L:K\to K[2]$ identify the first summand $k[2]$ with the shifted second summand $k[2]$ of $K[2]$, the second summand $k$ with the shifted third summand $k$ of $K[2]$, and the third summand $k[-2]$ with $0$. Its nonzero t-cohomology objects are
$$H^{-2}_t(K)=k,\qquad H^0_t(K)=k,\qquad H^2_t(K)=k,$$
and for every $j\ge0$ the map $H^{-j}_t(L^j)$ is an isomorphism: $j=0$ and $j=2$ are the two Lefschetz steps, while for $j=1$ and for $j\ge3$ both sides are zero. Consequently the splitting of [[lem-hard-lefschetz-splits-a-bounded-t-structure-complex]] returns exactly
$$K\cong H^{-2}_t(K)[2]\oplus H^0_t(K)\oplus H^2_t(K)[-2]=k[2]\oplus k\oplus k[-2].$$
This example tests the abstract splitting on the simplest complex with two hard Lefschetz steps; it does not test primitive-lift compatibility.
items.strategy: The finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces form a full abelian subcategory of the category of $k$-modules, closed under kernels, cokernels and finite direct sums ([[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]], [[thm-rank-nullity]], [[thm-first-isomorphism-theorem-in-an-abelian-category]], [[cor-dimension-of-a-direct-sum]]); it is essentially small, so the derived-category construction of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]] applies and $\mathcal T$ is triangulated ([[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]]) with the canonical bounded t-structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]], [[thm-the-canonical-pair-is-a-t-structure]]). In this t-structure the truncation triangles are supplied by the canonical truncations of complexes ([[lem-canonical-truncation-is-a-complex-and-has-the-claimed-cohomology]], [[thm-canonical-truncations-fit-a-distinguished-triangle]]), so by the essential uniqueness and amplitude detection of [[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]] and [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]] the abstract $H^j_t$ of a bounded complex is its usual $j$-th cohomology object. The displayed $K$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of $k$, so $H^{-2}_t(K)=H^0_t(K)=H^2_t(K)=k$ by the shift rule of the t-cohomology lemma, and all other $H^j_t(K)$ vanish. On the first summand $L$ is the canonical isomorphism $k[2]\cong k[2]$, on the second the canonical isomorphism $k\cong k$; hence $H^{-2}_t(L)$ is the identity of $k$, $H^0_t(L)$ the identity of $k$, and $H^{-2}_t(L^2)$ and the higher iterates pair the first with the third summand and vanish afterwards, again isomorphisms; the remaining maps $H^{-j}_t(L^j)$ involve a zero source or target. The hard Lefschetz hypothesis of the splitting lemma is therefore satisfied, with amplitude in $[-2,2]$, and the lemma's conclusion is the displayed finite direct sum; both extreme terms are $k[2]$ and $k[-2]$ and the middle term is $k$.

title: Mixed Hodge Structures And Strictness

items.title: Rational mixed Hodge structures
items.statement: A rational mixed Hodge structure is a finite-dimensional rational vector space $H$ together with a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the weight filtration, and a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of $H_{\mathbb C}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the Hodge filtration, such that for every integer $n$ the filtrations induced by $F$ and by its complex conjugate $\bar F$ on the graded piece $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ are $n$-opposed: writing $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ for the image of $F^p\cap W_n$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ and $H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$, one has $$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n,\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n.$$ A morphism of rational mixed Hodge structures is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $f\colon H\to K$ with $f(W_nH)\subseteq W_nK$ and $f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $n,p$. A pure structure of weight $n$ is the special case $W_{n-1}H=0$, $W_nH=H$. A substructure or quotient carries the induced or quotient filtrations; that the kernel, image and cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is proved in the strictness lemma below and is not part of the definition. The Tate structure $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the pure structure of weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type $(-r,-r)$. The tensor conventions are $W_n(H\otimes K)=\sum_{a+b=n}W_aH\otimes W_bK$ and $F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{a+b=p}F^aH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^bK_{\mathbb C}$, and the dual conventions are $W_n(H^*)=\{u:u(W_{-n-1}H)=0\}$ and $F^p(H^*_{\mathbb C})=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}$. A pure rational Hodge structure is polarizable if it carries a rational bilinear form of the parity of its weight that pairs only complementary Hodge types and whose Weil-operator Hermitian form is positive definite. No mixed structure is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb Q$.
items.strategy: Definition only, so no proof section. Well-definedness: the $n$-opposition is a condition imposed on the given data, and the displayed decomposition defines the summands $H^{p,q}_n$ rather than asserting an identity beyond that axiom; both filtrations are finite and $H$ is finite dimensional, so all sums over $p,q$ in the statement are finite. The clauses on substructures and quotients, on the tensor and dual formulas, and the Tate and polarizability conventions record the structures the later pages use; the definition asserts no existence theorem for them and this batch's proofs use none of them. The forward mention of kernel and image is explanatory only and creates no dependency: the existence statement is the strictness lemma. Choice-free: finite-dimensional linear algebra over $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb C$, no index set is chosen.
items.axiom_use: None: the definition quantifies only over finite filtrations of a finite-dimensional space.

items.title: The Deligne splitting of a mixed Hodge structure
items.statement:
Let $(H,W,F)$ be a rational mixed Hodge structure
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]) with complex conjugation $\sigma$ on
$H_{\mathbb C}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, and write
$\bar F^a=\sigma(F^a)$ for the conjugate Hodge filtration; all weight spaces
below are the complexifications $W_aH_{\mathbb C}$. For integers $p,q$ put
$m=p+q$ and
$$I^{p,q}=\bigl(F^p\cap W_m\bigr)\cap\Bigl(\bigl(\bar F^q\cap W_m\bigr)+\sum_{j\ge1}\bigl(\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
the intersections and the sum taken in $H_{\mathbb C}$. Then:

(a) $I^{p,q}\subseteq W_m\cap F^p$, the intersection $I^{p,q}\cap W_{m-1}$ is
zero, and the projection $W_m\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH_{\mathbb C}$ maps
$I^{p,q}$ isomorphically onto the summand $H^{p,q}_m$ of the mixed Hodge
definition;

(b) $W_mH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}$,
$F^aH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}$ for all integers $a,m$; in
particular $H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p,q}I^{p,q}$;

(c) every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(I^{p,q}(H))\subseteq I^{p,q}(K)$.

The construction satisfies
$I^{p,q}+W_{m-2}=\sigma(I^{q,p})+W_{m-2}$ inside $W_m$.
It need not satisfy $\sigma(I^{p,q})=I^{q,p}$, and the same splitting need
not split $\bar F$: its conjugate gives
$\bar F^bH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{q\ge b}\sigma(I^{q,p})$. The splitting is
the one pinned down in the sources by the displayed formula, not an arbitrary
direct-sum decomposition.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A rational mixed Hodge structure $(H,W,F)$ with conjugation
$\sigma(h\otimes z)=h\otimes\bar z$ and conjugate filtration
$\bar F=\sigma(F)$, as in [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]; the
complexified weight filtration $W_aH_{\mathbb C}=(W_aH)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$
is again written $W_a$.

[F1] On each $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ the induced filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$ are $n$-opposed, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n$ with $H^{p,q}_n=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$, where $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is the image of $F^p\cap W_n$ and $\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ the image of $\bar F^q\cap W_n$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], [[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]]).

[F2] $W$ is finite: $W_a=0$ for all sufficiently negative $a$ and $W_a=H_{\mathbb C}$ for all sufficiently positive $a$; $F$ and $\bar F$ are finite decreasing filtrations, so also the induced filtrations on each $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ are finite ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

[F3] A finite sum of vectors lying in pairwise independent subspaces vanishes only if every summand vanishes; equivalently, the sum map from a finite direct sum of subspaces is injective ([[def-internal-direct-sum]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Two-filtration lemma, spanning and partial sums.) Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector space with finite decreasing filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$ such that $V=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}(F^pV\cap\bar F^qV)$ for an integer $n$. Then (i) $F^aV+\bar F^{n+1-a}V=V$ for every $a$, and (ii) $F^aV=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$, with the conjugate formula $\bar F^bV=\bigoplus_{q\ge b}(F^{n-q}V\cap\bar F^qV)$. For (i), write $v=\sum_{p+q=n}v_{p,q}$; the terms with $p\ge a$ sum into $F^aV$, and each remaining term has $p<a$, hence $q=n-p>n-a$, that is $q\ge n+1-a$, so their sum lies in $\bar F^{n+1-a}V$. For (ii), prove $F^aV\subseteq\sum_{p\ge a}(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$ by descending induction on $a$: the claim is trivial when $F^aV=0$, and otherwise (i) with $a+1$ gives $V=F^{a+1}V+\bar F^{n-a}V$, so the modular law applied to $F^{a+1}V\subseteq F^aV\subseteq V$ yields $F^aV=F^{a+1}V+(F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V)$, in which the induction hypothesis places $F^{a+1}V$ inside $\sum_{p\ge a+1}(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$ while $F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V$ is the term with $p=a$; the reverse inclusion is clear, and the sum is direct because the pieces $F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V$ are independent by the decomposition hypothesis, which is symmetric in the two filtrations, so the same argument with $F$ and $\bar F$ interchanged gives the formula for $\bar F^bV$. [given, algebra]

2.1 (Two-filtration lemma, vanishing.) Under the hypothesis of step 1.1, $F^aV\cap\bar F^bV=0$ whenever $a+b>n$. Indeed, let $x\in F^aV\cap\bar F^bV$ and let $x=\sum_{p+q=n}x_{p,q}$ be its unique decomposition with $x_{p,q}\in F^pV\cap\bar F^qV$. Since $x\in F^aV$, its decomposition lies in $\bigoplus_{p\ge a}(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$ by step 1.1 (ii), so $x_{p,n-p}=0$ for every $p<a$; since $x\in\bar F^bV$, the conjugate half of step 1.1 (ii) gives $x_{n-q,q}=0$ for every $q<b$. If $x\ne0$, some $x_{p,n-p}$ is nonzero, and it satisfies $p\ge a$ and $n-p\ge b$, whence $n=p+(n-p)\ge a+b>n$, a contradiction; so $x=0$. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 (Lifting.) Let $m=p+q$. Every $d\in W_{m-1}$ can be written as $d=z+g$ with $z\in F^p\cap W_{m-1}$ and $g\in(\bar F^q\cap W_{m-1})+\sum_{j\ge1}(\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1})$. To see this, construct elements $d_1,d_2,\dots$ and vectors $f_j,g_j$ as follows. Put $d_1=d$, and suppose $d_j\in W_{m-j}$ has been constructed for some $j\ge1$. By [F1] the induced filtrations on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m-j}$ are $(m-j)$-opposed, and step 1.1 (i) applied there with the pair $(p,q-j+1)$, whose indices sum to $m-j+1$, shows that the images of $F^p\cap W_{m-j}$ and $\bar F^{q-j+1}\cap W_{m-j}$ generate $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m-j}$; choose $f_j\in F^p\cap W_{m-j}$ and $g_j\in\bar F^{q-j+1}\cap W_{m-j}$ whose classes sum to the class of $d_j$, and put $d_{j+1}:=d_j-f_j-g_j\in W_{m-j-1}$. By [F2] there is $J$ with $W_{m-J}=0$; the recursion stops there, and summing the identities $d_{j+1}=d_j-f_j-g_j$ gives $d=\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}(f_j+g_j)$. Each $f_j$ lies in $F^p\cap W_{m-j}\subseteq F^p\cap W_{m-1}$; $g_1$ lies in $\bar F^q\cap W_{m-1}$ and, for $j\ge2$, $g_j$ lies in $\bar F^{q-(j-1)}\cap W_{m-(j-1)-1}$. Hence $z:=\sum_jf_j$ and $g:=\sum_jg_j$ have the required properties. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 (Surjectivity onto the graded summand.) Let $\xi\in H^{p,q}_m$. Since $H^{p,q}_m\subseteq F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ is the image of $F^p\cap W_m$, choose $x_0\in F^p\cap W_m$ representing $\xi$; since $H^{p,q}_m\subseteq\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ is the image of $\bar F^q\cap W_m$, choose $y_0\in\bar F^q\cap W_m$ also representing $\xi$. Then $d:=x_0-y_0$ lies in $W_{m-1}$, so step 2.2 gives $d=z+g$ with $z\in F^p\cap W_{m-1}$ and $g$ in the displayed sum. Put $x:=x_0-z=y_0+g$. Then $x\in F^p\cap W_m$, and $x\in(\bar F^q\cap W_m)+\sum_{j\ge1}(\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1})$ because $y_0$ lies in the first summand and $g$ in the sum; so $x\in I^{p,q}$. Finally $x-x_0=-z\in W_{m-1}$, so $x$ and $x_0$ have the same class $\xi$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$. Hence the projection maps $I^{p,q}$ onto $H^{p,q}_m$, and $I^{p,q}\subseteq W_m\cap F^p$ holds by definition. [F1, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 (Injectivity modulo the lower weight.) Suppose $0\ne x\in I^{p,q}\cap W_{m-1}$, and choose its least weight index $r$, so $x\in W_r\setminus W_{r-1}$ and $r<m$. Write $x=y+\sum_{j\ge1}g_j$ as in the defining formula, with $y\in\bar F^q\cap W_m$ and $g_j\in\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1}$; only finitely many terms are needed because $W$ is finite. Put $J=m-r-1\ge0$. The sum $\sum_{j>J}g_j$ lies in $W_{r-1}$, while $h:=y+\sum_{1\le j\le J}g_j$ lies in $\bar F^{q-J}$ and also in $W_r$, because $h=x-\sum_{j>J}g_j$. Thus the nonzero class of $x$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_r$ belongs to $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_r\cap\bar F^{q-J}\operatorname{Gr}^W_r$. But $p+q-J=r+1>r$, so step 2.1 makes that intersection zero, a contradiction. Together with step 3.1 this proves the projection isomorphism in (a). [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 (The weight decomposition and the direct-sum identity.) For every $m$ the projection restricts to an isomorphism $\bigoplus_{p+q=m}I^{p,q}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH_{\mathbb C}$: by steps 3.1 and 4.1 each $I^{p,q}$ maps isomorphically onto $H^{p,q}_m$, and by [F1] the summands $H^{p,q}_m$ are independent with sum $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$. In particular $\dim I^{p,q}=\dim H^{p,q}_m$, so $\sum_{p+q=m}\dim I^{p,q}=\dim\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ for every $m$. The sum map $\psi_m\colon\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}\to W_m$ is injective: if a finite sum $\sum_{m'\le m}\sum_{p+q=m'}x_{p,q}$ vanishes, its class in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ is the sum of the classes of the top pieces $x_{p,m-p}$, which vanishes only if each of those pieces is zero because the restricted projection is an isomorphism; subtracting them leaves a vanishing sum over $m'\le m-1$, and induction on $m$ (with $W_m=0$ for all sufficiently negative $m$) finishes the argument. Its image therefore has dimension $\sum_{m'\le m}\dim\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m'}=\dim W_m$, the finite telescoping identity for the finite filtration $W$; an injective map between spaces of equal dimension is an isomorphism, so $W_mH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}$. Taking $m$ large gives $H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p,q}I^{p,q}$. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 4.1, F3, algebra]

5.2 (Conjugation modulo lower weights.) Work in $U=W_m/W_{m-2}$ with the images of $F^p\cap W_m$ and $\bar F^q\cap W_m$. Their intersection $T$ maps injectively to $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$: its intersection with $W_{m-1}/W_{m-2}$ is $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m-1}\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m-1}=0$ by step 2.1, since $p+q=m>m-1$. The formula for $I^{p,q}$ shows its image in $U$ lies in $T$, since every tail term has weight at most $m-2$. Step 3.1 shows this image maps onto $H^{p,q}_m$; the image of $T$ also lies in $H^{p,q}_m$, so injectivity makes the image of $I^{p,q}$ exactly $T$. Conjugating the same argument for $I^{q,p}$ shows that $\sigma(I^{q,p})$ has this same image $T$ in $U$. Therefore $I^{p,q}+W_{m-2}=\sigma(I^{q,p})+W_{m-2}$. [F1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 (The Hodge decomposition.) For all $a,m$ one has $F^a\cap W_m=\bigoplus_{p\ge a,\ p+q\le m}I^{p,q}$. Indeed, decompose $x\in F^a\cap W_m$ by step 5.1. Its class in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ lies in $\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,m-p}_m$ by step 1.1, so its top components with $p<a$ vanish by the projection isomorphism. Subtracting the remaining top components leaves an element of $F^a\cap W_{m-1}$, and induction through the finite $W$ proves the assertion. Taking $m$ large proves $F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}$. Conjugating this identity gives $\bar F^b=\bigoplus_{q\ge b}\sigma(I^{q,p})$; it does not assert a decomposition of $\bar F$ by the original $I^{p,q}$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 (Functoriality.) Let $f\colon H\to K$ be a morphism of rational mixed Hodge structures. Since $f$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$, $f_{\mathbb C}$ commutes with the conjugations, so $f_{\mathbb C}(\bar F^qH_{\mathbb C})=\overline{f_{\mathbb C}(F^qH_{\mathbb C})}\subseteq\bar F^qK_{\mathbb C}$; it also satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ and $f_{\mathbb C}(W_aH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq W_aK_{\mathbb C}$ by definition. Applying $f_{\mathbb C}$ to the two intersections and the sum defining $I^{p,q}(H)$ therefore produces an element of the corresponding intersection of $F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ with the sum of the $\bar F$-terms for $K$, and $W$-membership is preserved term by term; hence $f_{\mathbb C}(I^{p,q}(H))\subseteq I^{p,q}(K)$. [given, algebra] ∎
items.axiom_use: None: the argument is finite-dimensional linear algebra with finite filtrations; no basis or complement is chosen from an infinite family.

items.title: Strictness of mixed Hodge morphisms
items.statement: Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for $W$ and for $F$: $$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$ for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is $W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has pure image of weight $n$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]); the complexified map is written
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$ and commutes with the conjugations because
$f$ is rational.

[F1] The Deligne splitting of [[lem-deligne-splitting-of-a-mixed-hodge-structure]]: $H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p,q}I^{p,q}(H)$ with $W_mH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}(H)$, $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}(H)$, the projection of $I^{p,q}(H)$ onto $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{p+q}H_{\mathbb C}$ being an isomorphism onto $H^{p,q}_{p+q}$, and $f_{\mathbb C}(I^{p,q}(H))\subseteq I^{p,q}(K)$. The conjugation formula is only $I^{p,q}+W_{p+q-2}=\sigma(I^{q,p})+W_{p+q-2}$; no exact $\bar F$ partial-sum formula by the same pieces is used.

[F2] On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ one has $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n$ with $H^{p,q}_n=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Weight strictness.) Let $y=f(x)\in f(H)\cap W_nK$ and decompose $x=\sum_{p,q}x^{p,q}$ along the splitting of $H_{\mathbb C}$; then $y=\sum_{p,q}f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ with $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})\in I^{p,q}(K)$ by [F1]. Since $y\in W_nK=\bigoplus_{p+q\le n}I^{p,q}(K)$ and the sum is direct, all components with $p+q>n$ vanish: $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$ whenever $p+q>n$. Hence $x':=\sum_{p+q\le n}x^{p,q}$ lies in $W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ and satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(x')=y$, so $y\in f_{\mathbb C}(W_nH_{\mathbb C})$. The reverse inclusion $f(W_nH)\subseteq f(H)\cap W_nK$ is the preservation of $W$ by $f$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 (Hodge strictness.) The same computation with the condition $p<a$ instead of $p+q>n$: if $y=f_{\mathbb C}(x)\in f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^aK_{\mathbb C}$, decompose $x$ and use $F^aK_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}(K)$ to conclude that $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$ for $p<a$, so $x'=\sum_{p\ge a}x^{p,q}$ lies in $F^aH_{\mathbb C}$ and maps to $y$. [F1, algebra]

2.1 (Rational descent.) Step 1.1 gives equality of the complexifications of the rational subspaces $A=f(W_nH)$ and $B=f(H)\cap W_nK$. Images and intersections commute with extension from $\mathbb Q$ to $\mathbb C$: in finite rational coordinates they are kernels or images of matrices, whose rank is unchanged on extension since the same nonzero rational minors remain nonzero. To descend $A_{\mathbb C}=B_{\mathbb C}$, map $A$ into the rational quotient $K/B$. Its complexification is zero, hence the rational map is zero (a nonzero rational coordinate remains nonzero over $\mathbb C$), so $A\subseteq B$; interchanging them gives equality. Together with step 1.2 this proves the stated rational $W$ strictness and complex $F$ strictness. Complex conjugation fixes the real scalar extension of a rational space and is not used to recover rational vectors. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 (Exactness of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$.) Let $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to 0$ be a short exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures. By [F1] the splitting identifies $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nA$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nB$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nC$ with $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}I^{p,q}(A)$ and its analogues, and the maps $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n i$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n p$ with the direct sums of the maps induced by $i$ and $p$ between the pieces $I^{p,q}$. Each piecewise sequence $0\to I^{p,q}(A)\to I^{p,q}(B)\to I^{p,q}(C)\to 0$ is exact: the middle arrows are the restrictions of the injective $i$ and of the surjective $p$, and an element $b\in I^{p,q}(B)$ lies in $\ker p$ precisely when $b=i(a)$ for some $a\in A$, and decomposing $a$ into its $I$-pieces shows that all other pieces map to zero; since $i$ is injective, they vanish and $a\in I^{p,q}(A)$. A direct sum of short exact sequences is short exact, so $0\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nA\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nB\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nC\to0$ is exact; a morphism is strict for $W$ precisely when it induces such exact sequences, so this recovers step 1.1 independently. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 (Kernel, image and cokernel.) The functorial splitting [F1] makes $f_{\mathbb C}$ a direct sum of maps $I^{p,q}(H)\to I^{p,q}(K)$. Thus its kernel, image and cokernel decompose into the respective kernels, images and cokernels of these maps, and their induced or quotient $W$ and $F$ are the partial sums by $p+q\le n$ and $p\ge a$. The projection isomorphisms in [F1] identify their weight-$n$ pieces, with these induced $F$ filtrations, with the kernel, image and cokernel of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n f$, computed componentwise in the pure decompositions $H^{p,q}_n,K^{p,q}_n$. These identifications are the canonical rational graded maps: for a kernel this follows from $W$ strictness, since if $f(x)\in W_{n-1}K$ with $x\in W_nH$, choose $y\in W_{n-1}H$ with $f(y)=f(x)$ and replace $x$ by $x-y$; the image and cokernel follow by the same induced/quotient description. The graded rational map commutes with conjugation and preserves $F$, hence also $\bar F$; between equal-weight pure structures it preserves each type $F^p\cap\bar F^q$ with $p+q=n$. Consequently its pure kernels, images and cokernels have conjugation exchanging their $(p,q)$ and $(q,p)$ pieces. Their $F$ partial sums and their conjugates are therefore $n$-opposed. Every weight-graded piece of the three rational filtered spaces satisfies the mixed Hodge axiom, proving the claim. This argument requires no exact conjugate decomposition on the mixed vector space. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 (Pure image.) Now suppose $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nK=K$. By step 3.1 the image is a mixed Hodge structure with the induced filtration, and step 1.1 gives $W_{n-1}(\operatorname{im}f)=f(W_{n-1}H)=0$ and $W_n(\operatorname{im}f)=f(H)\cap W_nK=f(H)=\operatorname{im}f$; hence the image is pure of weight $n$. [step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Cohomological mixed Hodge complexes
items.statement: A rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex consists of: (a) a bounded-below cochain complex $K_{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces with a finite increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes, finite on each cochain group; (b) a cochain complex $K_{\mathbb C}$ of $\mathbb C$-vector spaces with a finite increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes and a finite decreasing filtration $F$ by subcomplexes, again finite on each cochain group; (c) a filtered comparison morphism $K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$ which is a quasi-isomorphism; subject to the axiom: for every integer $w$ the weight-graded complex $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its induced differential is strict for the induced filtration $F$, and for every $r$ the induced filtration $F$ on $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, together with the induced rational comparison, is a pure Hodge structure of weight $r+w$. The weight filtration on $H^n(K)$ is the shifted filtration $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K)\bigr)$; this shift is essential and pole-count weight on a logarithmic complex is not the weight on its cohomology. The same definitions apply to bounded-below complexes of sheaves on a space when the complexes are replaced by derived global sections and the required resolutions preserve the graded pieces; the existence of such resolutions for the concrete complexes used later is proved where those complexes are constructed, not here.
items.strategy: Definition only, so no proof section. The axiom is a condition on the data (Deligne III (8.1.5) together with (8.1.1)-(8.1.2)); the displayed shift is the convention of (1.1.2), and it is what makes the axiom's weight $r+w$ compatible with the weight of $H^n$; the statement records this rather than proving it. The strictness requirement on the differentials of the graded complexes is exactly axiom (GH1); the standard equivalent formulation, that the $F$-spectral sequence of the graded complex degenerates at its first page, is recorded in the sources but is neither asserted nor used here, so no degeneration theorem enters the dependencies. Biregularity (finiteness on each cochain group) is what the filtered-complex comparison needs in the following lemma; it holds for the complexes occurring in this run. The sheaf clause is applied by resolving the graded pieces separately; a Godement resolution of a complex of sheaves has exact terms and successive cokernels, so it preserves the graded pieces, but the proof of that statement belongs to the pages that construct the sheaves. Choice-free at this level: no family of nonempty sets is selected.
items.axiom_use: None in the definition itself; the later pages that build sheaf resolutions must declare their own choice use.

items.title: Mixed Hodge complex cohomology and simplicial weights
items.statement: (i) Let $K$ be a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex. Then for every $n$ the vector space $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ carries a mixed Hodge structure whose weight filtration is the shifted image filtration $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$ and whose Hodge filtration is the image filtration $F^pH^n(K_{\mathbb C})=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK_{\mathbb C})\to H^n(K_{\mathbb C}))$. In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$ one has $E_1^{p,q}$ pure of weight $q$, the sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ compatibly with the Hodge filtrations. A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces, on every $H^n$, a morphism of the resulting mixed Hodge structures. (ii) Let $K^\bullet$ be a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes concentrated in nonnegative cohomological degrees, i.e. cochain complexes $K^{p,q}$ with coface maps and an internal differential satisfying the cosimplicial identities, with $K^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, and with $H^q(K^p)$ a pure Hodge structure of weight $q$ for all $p,q$. Form its simple complex $sK$ with the standard total differential and the increasing filtration $L$ by cosimplicial degree, $L_{-p}sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}K^{i,n-i}$. Then $sK$ is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for the filtration $L$ and the Hodge filtrations of the $K^p$, the cosimplicial spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(sK)$ degenerates at $E_2$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$; consequently all weights of $H^n(sK)$ are at most $n$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex $K$ with its axiom: for
every $w$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its
differential is strict for the induced $F$, and $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK)$
with its induced $F$ and rational comparison is a pure Hodge structure of
weight $r+w$ ([[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]).

[F1] The cohomological filtered complex construction: for a cochain complex with a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes, degreewise finite, $E_1^{p,q}\cong H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK)$ and the sequence naturally abuts to the decreasing image filtration with $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}(K)$; a filtered chain map induces compatible maps on all pages and on the abutments ([[thm-the-cohomological-filtered-complex-construction]]).

[F2] Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, their kernels, images and cokernels with induced or quotient filtrations are mixed Hodge structures, and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $q$ to one of weights at most $q'<q$ is zero: strictness gives $W_{q-1}$ of its image equal to zero and $W_{q'}$ of its image equal to the whole image, and $q'\le q-1$ forces the image to vanish ([[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]).

[F3] A cochain complex has $d^{n+1}d^n=0$, so its differentials preserve every subcomplex filtration used below ([[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], [[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (First page and pure strictness.) Put $G^p=W_{-p}$ and apply [F1] over $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb C$. Then $E_0^{p,q}=\operatorname{Gr}^p_GK^{p+q}$, $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$ and $E_\infty^{p,q}=\operatorname{Gr}^p_GH^{p+q}(K)$ for the image filtration. The axiom gives $E_1^{p,q}$ a pure rational Hodge structure of weight $q$. We will use the following explicit pure case of [F2]: a rational map preserving $F$ also preserves $\bar F$; between pure structures of the same weight it therefore preserves each type $F^a\cap\bar F^b$, so it is strict for $F$, and its kernels, images and cokernels have the induced pure structures. If the source has weight $q$ and the target has weight $q'<q$, it is zero: a source vector of type $(a,b)$ with $a+b=q$ maps into $F^a\cap\bar F^b$ of the target, which is zero because no target type of total $q'$ has both indices at least $a,b$. Thus no mixed Hodge structure on the abutment is being assumed. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 (Strict representative correction.) For a complex $C$ with decreasing filtration $T$ by subcomplexes and $T$-strict differential, the sequence $0\to H^n(T^aC)\to H^n(C)\to H^n(C/T^aC)\to0$ is exact for every $a,n$. For injectivity, a cycle $x\in T^aC$ that is a boundary $dy$ in $C$ equals $dy'$ for some $y'\in T^aC$ by strictness. For surjectivity, a quotient cycle lifts to $x\in C$ with $dx\in T^aC$; strictness gives $y\in T^aC$ with $dy=dx$, so $x-y$ is a cycle with the same quotient class. If a cycle maps to a quotient boundary, subtract a lift of that boundary to obtain a cycle in $T^aC$, proving exactness at the middle. In particular $H(T^aC)$ identifies with the filtration induced on $H(C)$ by $T^a$. These corrections use only strictness of the differential on $C$. [F3, construct, algebra]

2.1 (Exact filtered pages through $E_2$.) Fix a Hodge index $a$, and apply [F1] with the intersection and quotient $G$ filtrations to $A=F^aK_{\mathbb C}$, $B=K_{\mathbb C}$ and $C=B/A$. Their $E_0$ complexes form a short exact sequence $0\to E_0(A)\to E_0(B)\to E_0(C)\to0$: the first image in $G^pB/G^{p+1}B$ is $(F^aB\cap G^pB+G^{p+1}B)/G^{p+1}B$, exactly $F^aE_0(B)$, and the last term is its quotient. The mixed Hodge complex axiom says $d_0$ on $E_0(B)=\operatorname{Gr}^GK_{\mathbb C}$ is $F$-strict. Step 1.2 therefore gives a short exact sequence on $E_1$, with first image exactly $F^aE_1(B)$. Naturality of the page maps shows $d_1$ preserves this image for every $a$; its rational form then makes $d_1:E_1^{p,q}\to E_1^{p+1,q}$ a map of pure Hodge structures of weight $q$, strict by step 1.1. Apply step 1.2 again to the $E_1$ complexes to obtain exactness on $E_2$, with $E_2(A)$ identifying with the filtration induced on $E_2(B)=H(E_1(B),d_1)$. Denote this recursively induced filtration by $F_{\mathrm{rec}}$. The pure type decomposition of $E_1$ descends through its type-preserving $d_1$, so $E_2^{p,q}(B)$ with $F_{\mathrm{rec}}$ is pure of weight $q$. [F1, given, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 (Higher differentials and exact stable pages.) Suppose the three page complexes are exact at page $r\ge2$, with $E_r(A)$ identifying with $F^a_{\mathrm{rec}}E_r(B)$ for every $a$, and $E_r^{p,q}(B)$ pure of weight $q$. Naturality shows $d_r$ preserves these images, hence $F_{\mathrm{rec}}$; it also preserves the rational structures. Its target $E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$ has lower weight, so step 1.1 forces $d_r=0$. This zero map is strict, and step 1.2 applied to the exact triple of $E_r$ complexes gives exactness at $E_{r+1}$ and the recursive filtration identification. Since $d_r(B)=0$, injectivity of $E_r(A)\to E_r(B)$ and surjectivity onto $E_r(C)$ also give $d_r(A)=d_r(C)=0$. Starting from step 2.1 proves this induction for all $r\ge2$. Thus the weight sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and the three sequences for $A,B,C$ stabilize there; $E_\infty^{p,q}(B)=E_2^{p,q}(B)$ is pure of weight $q$ for the recurrent filtration. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 (Recurrent filtration equals the abutment filtration.) By convergence and naturality [F1], the injective stable-page map $E_\infty(A)\to E_\infty(B)$ is $\operatorname{Gr}_G H(A)\to\operatorname{Gr}_G H(B)$ for the image $G$ filtrations on cohomology. A filtered linear map between finite filtered spaces whose graded map is injective is injective and strict: for any nonzero $x$, choose its largest decreasing-filtration index $p$; its nonzero graded class has nonzero image, so the image has this same index. This proves injectivity and, if the image of $x$ belongs to $G^p$, forces $x\in G^p$, which is strictness. The cohomology $G$ filtrations here are finite in each degree because $G$ is finite on the degree-$n$ cochain group, so the argument applies to $H^n(F^aK)\to H^n(K)$. Consequently its graded image is the induced filtration of the subspace $F^aH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^aK)\to H^n(K))$ on $\operatorname{Gr}_GH^n(K)$: in filtration degree $p$ the numerator is $(F^aH^n(K)\cap G^pH^n(K))+G^{p+1}H^n(K)$. By steps 2.1 and 3.1 that same image on $E_\infty$ is $F^a_{\mathrm{rec}}$. This proves exactly the recurrent-to-abutment comparison needed here, with the strict representative correction supplied in step 1.2. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 (Mixed Hodge structure and shifted weights.) Write $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$. Substitution $p=n-m$, $q=m$ in [F1] and step 3.1 gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{Gr}^{n-m}_GH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$. Step 4.1 makes this identification compatible with the Hodge filtration induced by $F$ on cohomology; the right side is pure of weight $m$ by step 2.1. The rational comparison is an isomorphism on $E_1$ by the graded quasi-isomorphism axiom and hence on the stable pages; finite filtered leading-term descent makes it an isomorphism on cohomology as well. The finitely many nonzero stable terms in degree $n$ are finite-dimensional, so $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ is finite-dimensional. The induced $W$ and $F$ are finite, and every $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ with its induced $F$ is pure of weight $m$, precisely the mixed Hodge axiom. [F1, given, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 (Functoriality.) A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces rational and complex cohomology maps compatible with the comparisons. It maps $W_{m-n}K$ to $W_{m-n}L$ and $F^aK_{\mathbb C}$ to $F^aL_{\mathbb C}$, hence preserves the cohomology image filtrations $W_m$ and $F^a$. These maps are therefore morphisms of the mixed Hodge structures of step 5.1. Naturality of [F1] and of the exact-page construction makes the graded-piece identifications compatible with these maps and their Hodge filtrations. [F1, given, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 (The cosimplicial case.) Form $sK^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}K^{p,q}$ with the standard total differential. The cosimplicial identities, commutation with the internal differential and the usual total sign give $d^2=0$. The filtration $L_\ell sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge-\ell}K^{i,n-i}$ is increasing, by subcomplexes, and finite on each degree because $0\le i\le n$. Its graded piece is $\operatorname{Gr}^L_\ell sK\cong K^{-\ell}[\ell]$, so $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^L_\ell sK)=H^{r+\ell}(K^{-\ell})$ is pure of weight $r+\ell$, and its internal differential is strict for $F$ by the Hodge complex hypothesis. Levelwise rational comparisons and filtration-preserving coface maps assemble to the total comparison, which is a graded quasi-isomorphism; the total complex is bounded below and its $F$ filtration is degreewise finite because each diagonal is finite. Thus $sK$ is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for $L$. Applying steps 1.1-6.1 gives $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^L_{-p}sK)=H^q(K^p)$, degeneration at $E_2$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)=\operatorname{Gr}^L_{q-n}H^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$, with its induced Hodge filtration and functorial mixed structure. Here $W_qH^n=L_{q-n}H^n$ is the shifted cohomology filtration, not the unshifted $L$. [F1, given, construct, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1]

8.1 (Weights at most the degree.) Since the cosimplicial degree is nonnegative, $E_1^{p,q}=0$ for $p<0$, hence $E_2^{n-q,q}=0$ when $q>n$. Step 7.1 gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)=0$ for all $q>n$; finiteness of the weight filtration then gives $W_nH^n(sK)=H^n(sK)$, proving the stated bound. [step 5.1, step 7.1, algebra] ∎
items.axiom_use: None intended: the published filtered-complex spectral sequence construction is algebraic and choice-free, and Steps 1-5 use finite-dimensional linear algebra. The Step-3 author must re-verify the AC status of the spectral-sequence and double-complex suppliers, none of which states a choice principle.

items.title: A mixed Hodge extension without a rational splitting
items.statement: A rational mixed Hodge structure can be an extension of two pure structures and still admit no splitting over $\mathbb Q$. On $H=\mathbb Q e_0\oplus\mathbb Q e_1$ put $W_{-3}=0$, $W_{-2}=W_{-1}=\mathbb Q e_1$, $W_0=H$, and $F^1=0$, $F^0=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$, $F^{-1}=H_{\mathbb C}$. This is a mixed Hodge structure sitting in a short exact sequence $0\to\mathbb Q(1)\to H\to\mathbb Q(0)\to0$ which has no splitting in the category of rational mixed Hodge structures.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The rational vector space $H=\mathbb Q e_0\oplus\mathbb Q e_1$
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), the increasing filtration
$W_{-3}=0$, $W_{-2}=W_{-1}=\mathbb Q e_1$, $W_0=H$ and the decreasing
filtration $F^1H_{\mathbb C}=0$, $F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$,
$F^{-1}H_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$, with $i\in\mathbb C$ satisfying
$i^2=-1$ and conjugation $\sigma(z)=\bar z$
([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]).

[F1] A rational mixed Hodge structure is the datum of a finite increasing $W$ and a finite decreasing $F$ such that on every $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ the induced filtrations are $n$-opposed, i.e. split into the pieces $H^{p,q}_n$ with $\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$; a morphism preserves $W$ and $F$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

[F2] The Tate structure $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the pure structure of weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type $(-r,-r)$; in particular $\mathbb Q(1)$ has weight $-2$ and type $(-1,-1)$, while $\mathbb Q(0)$ has weight $0$ and type $(0,0)$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

[F3] On a graded piece $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ the induced filtration $F$ is the image of $F\cap W_n$ and $\bar F=\sigma(F)$; the summands are $H^{p,q}_n=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The weight filtration is finite with $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}=\mathbb Q e_1$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-1}=0$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0=H/\mathbb Q e_1\cong\mathbb Q e_0$. On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}$ the induced $F$ has $F^0=0$ and $F^{-1}=\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}$, since $F^0\cap W_{-2}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)\cap\mathbb C e_1=0$; the conjugate filtration satisfies $\bar F^{-1}=\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}$ and $\bar F^0=0$ for the same reason, so the pieces are $H^{-1,-1}=\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}$ and nothing else, and $H^{-1,-1}$ is spanned by the image of $e_1$, which is rational. On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0$ the image of $F^0\cap W_0=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$ is all of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0$ because $e_0+ie_1\mapsto e_0\ne0$, and $F^1=0$; the conjugate $\bar F^0=\sigma(F^0)=\mathbb C(e_0-ie_1)$ likewise has image all of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0$, so the pieces are $H^{0,0}=\operatorname{Gr}^W_0$ and nothing else. Both graded pieces are therefore $n$-opposed, with the rational structure of $e_1$ and $e_0$ respectively, so $(H,W,F)$ is a rational mixed Hodge structure; its graded pieces are $\mathbb Q(1)$ and $\mathbb Q(0)$ in the convention [F2]. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Let $\iota\colon\mathbb Q(1)\to H$ be the inclusion $\mathbb C\to H_{\mathbb C}$ sending $1$ to $e_1$ and let $\pi\colon H\to\mathbb Q(0)$ be the $\mathbb Q$-linear map $e_0\mapsto1$, $e_1\mapsto0$. Both preserve the filtrations: $\iota$ sends the weight-$(-2)$ structure into $W_{-2}H=\mathbb Q e_1$ and $F^{-1}\mathbb Q(1)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ into $F^{-1}H_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$, while $F^0\mathbb Q(1)_{\mathbb C}=0$; and $\pi$ satisfies $\pi(W_{-1}H)=0=W_{-1}\mathbb Q(0)$ and $\pi(W_0H)=\mathbb Q(0)=W_0\mathbb Q(0)$, $\pi(F^0H_{\mathbb C})\subseteq\mathbb C=F^0\mathbb Q(0)_{\mathbb C}$ and $\pi(F^1H_{\mathbb C})=0$. Hence $0\to\mathbb Q(1)\xrightarrow{\iota}H\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathbb Q(0)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of rational mixed Hodge structures, with $\ker\pi=\mathbb Q e_1$. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Every $\mathbb Q$-linear section $s$ of $\pi$ satisfies $s(1)=e_0+q e_1$ with $q\in\mathbb Q$, because $\pi(e_0+q e_1)=1$ and $\pi(e_1)=0$. If $s$ were a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, it would satisfy $s_{\mathbb C}(F^0\mathbb Q(0)_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$; since $F^0\mathbb Q(0)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ and $s_{\mathbb C}(1)=e_0+qe_1$, there would be $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ with $e_0+qe_1=\lambda(e_0+ie_1)$. Comparing the coefficients of $e_0$ and $e_1$ in the basis $(e_0,e_1)$ gives $\lambda=1$ and $q=i$, which is impossible for $q\in\mathbb Q$. Hence the extension does not split in the category of rational mixed Hodge structures. The obstruction is visible directly in the $(0,0)$-direction: $F^0H_{\mathbb C}\cap\bar F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)\cap\mathbb C(e_0-ie_1)=0$, while a rational section must send $1$ into a rational vector of $F^0$, which is then also fixed by conjugation and hence would have to lie in this zero intersection. [given, F1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

title: Compact Kahler Hodge Foundations

items.title: Compact Kähler and rational Hodge polarization conventions
items.statement:
Assume AC, the standing convention of this page: the analytic and cohomological suppliers invoked below assume full AC. A **Kähler manifold** is a complex manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n\ge1$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with a Hermitian metric $g$ whose real fundamental form $\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ is closed, $d\omega=0$, and positive, $\omega(v,Jv)>0$ for $v\ne0$; it is **compact Kähler** when $X$ is compact. The complex structure orients $X$, $(e_1,Je_1,\dots,e_n,Je_n)$ being positive for every complex frame. Normalize the metric so that in an oriented orthonormal real coframe $(e_1,f_1,\dots,e_n,f_n)$ one has $\omega=\sum_{j=1}^n e_j\wedge f_j$ and $dV=\omega^n/n!$. For $n=0$, $X$ is a finite set of points with its unique complex structure, all operators below are zero, and $dV$ is the counting measure.

Complex-valued differential forms use the complex-linear extension of the Hodge star of [[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] and the integral inner product $\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle=\int_X\alpha\wedge*\bar\beta$, complex-linear in the first variable. In holomorphic charts the complex-valued $k$-forms split as $\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\Omega^{p,q}(X)$ and $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ with $\partial,\bar\partial$ of bidegree $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Put $L=\omega\wedge$, let $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ be the formal adjoints of $L,\partial,\bar\partial,d$ ([[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]]), and $\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d$, $\Delta_\partial=\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\partial$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial$; write $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$.

A **rational pure Hodge structure of weight $k$** is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space $V$ with $V_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}V^{p,q}$ and $\overline{V^{p,q}}=V^{q,p}$. Its **Weil operator** $C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $V^{p,q}$. A **polarization** is a rational nondegenerate bilinear form $Q$ with $Q(y,x)=(-1)^kQ(x,y)$, with $Q(V^{p,q},V^{a,b})=0$ unless $(a,b)=(q,p)$, and with $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ positive definite Hermitian. A **rational sub-Hodge structure** is a rational subspace $U$ with $U_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(U_{\mathbb C}\cap V^{p,q})$, and the **Tate shift** $V(-r)$ keeps the underlying rational space with bidegrees $(p+r,q+r)$ and weight $k+2r$.
items.strategy: Definition and conventions, so no proof section. Well-definedness: the bidegree splitting and $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ are chart-local and glue because holomorphic chart transitions are complex-linear and preserve bidegree ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]], [[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]); the complex orientation is frame-independent because a complex change of basis has positive real determinant; the complex-linear star and the metric on exterior powers are [[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] and [[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]; $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ exist uniquely by [[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]]; every sum over $p,q$ is finite. AC: the definitional content is choice-free; the first sentence records the page-wide convention and declares [[def-axiom-of-choice]] so that the items invoking the analytic suppliers (whose statements assume AC) carry the assumption explicitly to their own consumers. Sources: Schnell classes 16-18 (operators $L,\Lambda,H$ for an orthonormal coframe, the star and the sign $\epsilon(k)$), Demailly VI §5.1-5.2 (complex Hodge star, $d=d'+d''$, adjoint operators, $L$ and $\Lambda=\star^{-1}L\star$), Deligne II (2.1.10)-(2.1.17) (Hodge structures of weight $n$, the Tate twist, polarizations) and (2.1.14) (the orientation $\mathrm{or}_i(X)$ of a complex manifold). The source-review caveat that the class-17 two-plane table contains typographical slips is recorded on the pointwise Lefschetz item, not here.

items.title: Rational cohomology scalar comparison on compact smooth manifolds
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact smooth manifold $X$, the natural coefficient maps induce isomorphisms $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}F\cong H^k(X;F)$ for every characteristic-zero field $F$, finite-dimensional in each degree. For $F=\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ these identify singular cohomology with the real or complex de Rham cohomology. They preserve cup products and are natural for maps between such manifolds. No ordered-field or positivity structure is asserted for a general $F$.
items.strategy: Use the finite CW homotopy model of $X$ ([[lem-compact-smooth-manifolds-have-finite-cw-models-under-countable-choice]], stated under AC_ω, derived here from AC by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) to get finite-dimensional $H_k(X;\mathbb Q)$ and finite generation of all $H_k(X;\mathbb Z)$; [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]] converts the model into singular homology without extra choice. Step 1: choose, using full AC, direct complements $Z_k=B_k\oplus A_k$ and $C_k=Z_k\oplus T_k$ in the singular rational chain complex; the boundary bijects $T_k$ onto $B_{k-1}$, and tensoring with a characteristic-zero field $F$ preserves the splittings and the bijection, so $H_k(X;F)=H_k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes F$ via the canonical coefficient map (checked on cycles). Step 2: the field universal coefficient theorem ([[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]) has $\operatorname{Ext}^1_F=0$, so evaluation is a canonical isomorphism $H^k(X;F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_F(H_k(X;F),F)$; with finite-dimensional $H_k(X;\mathbb Q)$ the natural map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H_k(X;\mathbb Q),\mathbb Q)\otimes F\to\operatorname{Hom}_F(H_k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes F,F)$ is an isomorphism (it is the identity on a finite basis), identifying $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes F$ with $H^k(X;F)$. Cup products commute with coefficient inclusion by the front/back formula and the construction is natural by precomposition on cochains. Step 3: for $F=\mathbb R$ the identification with de Rham cohomology is [[thm-de-rham-theorem]]; complex forms split uniquely into real and imaginary parts, so kernels, images and quotients complexify, giving $F=\mathbb C$. The strategy explicitly avoids choosing bases of infinite-dimensional spaces outside Step 1, so the only full-AC step is the complement decomposition there.
items.axiom_use: Full AC: direct-complement choices in the singular rational chain complex in Step 1. Its countable consequences are used through the finite-CW-model lemma, the de Rham theorem and the universal coefficient theorem; [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] supplies AC_ω from AC. The construction is not choice-free.

items.title: Top de Rham integration equals fundamental-class evaluation
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact oriented smooth boundaryless $m$-manifold $M$ and a smooth real or complex top form $\alpha$, the natural de Rham comparison satisfies $\langle J_M[\alpha],[M]\rangle=\int_M\alpha$. Thus rational cup products that become top de Rham forms integrate to their rational fundamental-class evaluation.
items.strategy: Use the de Rham comparison $J_M$ of [[thm-de-rham-theorem]] as the composition of integration of forms over smooth simplices with the inverse of smooth-to-continuous singular restriction. Step 1: fix a smooth singular cycle $z=\sum_{j=1}^Na_j\sigma_j$ representing the fundamental class $[M]$ ([[thm-smooth-singular-chains-compute-singular-homology]], [[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]]), so $\langle J_M[\alpha],[M]\rangle=\sum_j a_j\int_{\Delta^m}\sigma_j^*\alpha$ by the defining integration cocycle. Step 2: extend each $\sigma_j$ smoothly near its simplex and apply Sard in coordinate charts ([[thm-morse-sard-for-euclidean-maps]]); critical values together with the images of the $(m-1)$-dimensional faces form a null set, a finite union of null sets remaining null. Outside it each preimage of $y\in M$ is interior and regular, and there are finitely many: an infinite set would have an accumulation point by compactness, which can lie neither on a face nor at a regular point. Excising disjoint inverse-image balls ([[thm-excision-for-singular-homology]]) and using the local-orientation characterization of the fundamental class identifies the weighted multiplicity $\sum_j a_j\sum_{x\in\sigma_j^{-1}(y)}\operatorname{sgn}\det D\sigma_j(x)$ with $1$ at every such $y$. Step 3: on the regular locus choose a countable locally finite partition subordinate to precompact inverse-function neighbourhoods, apply the oriented change of variables ([[thm-change-of-variables-for-oriented-manifold-diffeomorphisms]]) on each injective chart, and use monotone convergence ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]) on the pullback of the absolute density to justify summing the absolutely convergent integrals; the critical set contributes zero because its pulled-back top form has vanishing Jacobian and the faces have measure zero. Hence $\sum_j a_j\int_{\sigma_j}\sigma_j^*\alpha=\int_M\alpha$. Real and imaginary parts give complex $\alpha$, and cup compatibility of $J_M$ gives the last sentence. The dimension-zero case is the finite signed point sum and is handled directly. The proof consumes only AC_ω; full AC is recorded as the page convention and AC_ω is obtained from it by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]].
items.axiom_use: Full AC as the page convention; the argument consumes only AC_ω, through smooth-singular comparison, the de Rham theorem and smooth partitions of unity. [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] supplies AC_ω. Sard, change of variables, excision and monotone convergence are choice-free.

items.title: Hermitian exterior Lefschetz decomposition and Weil star identity
items.statement: Let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $2n$ with a positive-definite inner product $g$, a compatible complex structure $J$ ($g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$, $J^2=-1$), fundamental form $\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ and the orientation in which $(e_1,Je_1,\dots,e_n,Je_n)$ is positive, with the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]. On the complexified exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet V_{\mathbb C}$ the operators $L=\omega\wedge$, $\Lambda=L^*$ and $H=[L,\Lambda]$ satisfy $[L,\Lambda]=H$, $H|_{\Lambda^k}=(k-n)I$, $[H,L]=2L$ and $[H,\Lambda]=-2\Lambda$. Every degree-$k$ element has a unique decomposition $\sum_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^ru_r$ with $\Lambda u_r=0$ and $\deg u_r=k-2r$. For primitive $u$ of degree $t$, $L^{n-t+1}u=0$ and $$\Lambda^sL^ru=\frac{r!}{(r-s)!}\frac{(n-t-r+s)!}{(n-t-r)!}L^{r-s}u\qquad(0\le s\le r\le n-t);$$ no nonzero primitive element has $t>n$. Hence $L^{n-k}:\Lambda^k\to\Lambda^{2n-k}$ is an isomorphism for $k\le n$, and primitive degree $k$ is equivalently $L^{n-k+1}u=0$. With $J=i^{p-q}$ on type $(p,q)$ and $W=\exp L\exp(-\Lambda)\exp L$ one has $W|_{\Lambda^k}=\epsilon(k)J*$; in particular, if $u$ is primitive of type $(p,q)$ and $k=p+q$, then $$*u=\frac{\epsilon(k)i^{q-p}}{(n-k)!}L^{n-k}u.$$ All decomposition projections are rational polynomials in $L,\Lambda$ on each fixed degree.
items.strategy: Pointwise Hermitian linear algebra; in-run dependencies are the conventions item and the published Hodge-star items. Sources: Schnell class 16 (Lemma 16.1, Propositions 16.2 and 16.4), Schnell class 17 (Lefschetz decomposition, Lemma 17.1, Proposition 17.3 with its two-plane induction), Demailly VI §5.2-5.3 ((5.9)-(5.17)). Step 1: on an oriented orthonormal two-plane $e,f$ with $Je=f$, $L$ sends $1$ to $e\wedge f$ and kills $e,f$, while $\Lambda=L^*$ sends $e\wedge f$ to $1$ and kills $e,f$; hence $[L,\Lambda]$ has eigenvalues $-1,0,0,1$ in degrees $0,1,1,2$. Summing over orthogonal two-planes (distinct factors commute) gives $[L,\Lambda]=H$, $H|_{\Lambda^k}=(k-n)I$ and the other two relations. Repeated commutation of $\Lambda$ through $L$ gives $\Lambda L^ru=r(n-t-r+1)L^{r-1}u$ for primitive $u$ of degree $t$; iterating gives the displayed coefficient formula and the norm identity $\|L^ru\|^2=r(n-t-r+1)\|L^{r-1}u\|^2$, whose positivity through $r=n-t$ and vanishing at $r=n-t+1$ shows the string is nonzero exactly for $0\le r\le n-t$ and that no nonzero primitive has $t>n$. Step 2: $\ker\Lambda=(\operatorname{im}L)^\perp$ in each degree; subtracting from a vector the top $\Lambda$-power of a multiple of $L$ iteratively splits it as $\sum L^ru_r$ with $\Lambda u_r=0$, and applying $\Lambda^s$ at the largest surviving index to a vanishing sum gives uniqueness and the rational-polynomial projectors (choose the highest lowering power, divide by its displayed nonzero integer coefficient, repeat). The string computation gives $L^{n-k}:\Lambda^k\to\Lambda^{2n-k}$ invertible for $k\le n$ and $\Lambda u=0\iff L^{n-k+1}u=0$. Step 3: $W=\exp L\exp(-\Lambda)\exp L$ satisfies $W=\epsilon(k)J*$ on $\Lambda^k$ by two-plane induction: on a two-plane multiplication of the three exponentials gives $W(1)=e\wedge f$, $W(e)=e$, $W(f)=f$, $W(e\wedge f)=-1$, matching $\epsilon(\deg)J*$; both sides multiply over wedges of orthogonal even-dimensional factors with $*(a\wedge b)=(-1)^{\deg a\deg b}(*a)\wedge(*b)$ and $\epsilon(a+b)=(-1)^{\deg a\deg b}\epsilon(a)\epsilon(b)$. Step 4: model a primitive string of length $m=n-k$ by $L^ru/r!\leftrightarrow\binom mrx^{m-r}y^r$ so that $L=y\partial_x$ and $\Lambda=x\partial_y$; the three exponentials compose to the substitution $x\mapsto y$, $y\mapsto-x$, hence $Wu=L^mu/m!$, and $J$ is the constant $i^{q-p}$ along the string, giving $*u=\epsilon(k)i^{q-p}L^mu/m!$. Source-review warning retained: Schnell's class-17 two-plane table has typographical slips (a duplicated $J*e_2$ entry and a $k\le0$ range); the signs above are re-derived from the star characterization of [[def-hodge-star-on-an-oriented-inner-product-space]] and must be re-checked independently rather than copied.
items.axiom_use: None: finite-dimensional real exterior algebra with canonical orthogonal decompositions and integer coefficients; no basis or complement is chosen from an infinite family.
