items.title: A noncompact algebraic line needs a deleted boundary triangulation
items.statement: The analytic complex affine line $\mathbb A^1(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C$ cannot be homeomorphic to the realization of a finite simplicial complex. It is homeomorphic to a finite triangulated compactification with one boundary vertex deleted. Thus "finite triangulation" for noncompact varieties must allow a deleted subcomplex or another equivalent noncompact finite-cell convention.
items.strategy: (1) The increasing open disks $\{|z|<n\}$ cover $\mathbb C$ but no finite subfamily does, so $\mathbb C$ is not compact; since finite simplicial realizations are compact ([[prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization]]), no finite realization is homeomorphic to $\mathbb C$. (2) The boundary complex $K$ of the octahedron realizes the $\ell^1$-sphere in $\mathbb R^3$; radial normalization and its inverse identify $|K|$ with $S^2$, and deleting the vertex $e_3$ gives $S^2\setminus\{e_3\}$. (3) The stereographic formula $(a,b)\mapsto(2a,2b,a^2+b^2-1)/(a^2+b^2+1)$ is a homeomorphism $\mathbb C\to S^2\setminus\{e_3\}$ with inverse $u\mapsto(u_1,u_2)/(1-u_3)$. Hence $\mathbb C$ is a finite complex with one vertex deleted, which is the compactification convention used by the finite triangulation statements on the companion page.

items.title: SNC projective compactifications of smooth quasiprojective varieties
items.statement: Assume AC. Every smooth quasiprojective complex variety $U$ admits a smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with reduced boundary a simple normal crossings divisor $D$. Given finitely many such compactifications, there is another dominating all of them and restricting to the identity on $U$. A morphism of smooth quasiprojective varieties extends to a morphism of such compactifications after modifying the source compactification outside its open variety.
items.strategy:
Route (Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, 3.2.1 and its quasiprojective remark: the smooth completion of a quasiprojective variety may be chosen projective with SNC boundary; constructive inputs are the published resolution/principalization development of run frontier-40-geometry-braids-rep-27, sourced from Włodarczyk and Hauser).
Step 1 (projective ambient). A smooth quasiprojective complex variety $U$ is a separated finite-type $\mathbb C$-scheme embeddable as a locally closed subscheme of a projective space; take the reduced closure $\bar U$ of $U$ in $\mathbb P^N$, componentwise when $U$ has several components (a finite disjoint union of projective varieties is projective). Then $\bar U$ is projective, $U\subseteq\bar U$ is dense open, and $U$ lies in the smooth locus of $\bar U$ because $U$ is smooth and open in $\bar U$.
Step 2 (embedded desingularization in a single projective ambient). Apply [[thm-weak-embedded-desingularization]] to the reduced closed subscheme $\bar U$ of the smooth projective ambient $\mathbb P^N$. Its statement gives one global sequence $\mathbb P^N=X_0\leftarrow X_1\leftarrow\dots\leftarrow X_r$ of blowups of regular centers $C_{i-1}\subseteq X_{i-1}$ in this single smooth ambient (not a chartwise glued sequence), whose strict transform $\widetilde U$ of $\bar U$ is smooth and has SNC with the exceptional divisor $E_r$, and whose induced morphism $\widetilde U\to\bar U$ is proper, birational and the identity over the smooth locus of $\bar U$, hence over $U$.
Step 3 (projectivity). Every $X_i$ is projective: $X_0=\mathbb P^N$ is, and for a coherent center ideal $\mathcal J$ on a projective integral $X_{i-1}$ with an ample invertible sheaf $\mathcal O(1)$, [[lem-eventual-global-generation-coherent-twists]] makes $\mathcal J(m)=\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal O(m)$ globally generated for $m\gg0$, while [[cor-rational-map-to-projective-space-resolved-by-base-ideal-blowup]] exhibits $\mathrm{Bl}_{\mathcal J}X_{i-1}=\mathrm{Proj}(\bigoplus_d\mathcal J^d)$ as a closed subscheme of $X_{i-1}\times\mathbb P^n$ over $X_{i-1}$. Closing this under the Segre embedding of the product with $\mathbb P^N$ gives projectivity over $\mathbb C$; hence the strict transform $\widetilde U$, a closed subscheme of $X_r$, is smooth projective. This two-supplier argument is the load-bearing step: [[thm-blowup-projective]] is not invoked for it, since in general it gives only local H-projectivity with properness.
Step 4 (SNC boundary). Let $\mathcal I$ be the ideal sheaf of the reduced boundary closed subscheme $\widetilde U\setminus U$ of the smooth projective $\widetilde U$; it is not identically zero on any component because $U$ is dense. Apply [[thm-principalization-of-ideals]] to $\mathcal I$ on $\widetilde U$: a sequence $\widetilde U=X'_0\leftarrow X'_1\leftarrow\dots\leftarrow X'_s=X$ of blowups of regular centers, with $\sigma^*\mathcal I$ the ideal of an effective Cartier divisor $\widetilde E$ with SNC support; projectivity of every $X'_i$ is again Step 3. Let $D$ be the support of $\widetilde E$ with reduced structure: a reduced effective Cartier divisor with SNC support ([[def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors]]), so $X$ is a smooth projective compactification of $U$ with reduced SNC boundary $D$.
Step 5 (identity over $U$). The principalization centers are contained in the supports of the successive transforms of $(\mathcal I,\varnothing,1)$ ([[prop-canonical-resolution-of-marked-ideals]], condition (2)), and those supports map into $\mathrm{supp}(\mathcal I)=\widetilde U\setminus U$ because $\sigma_i^*\mathcal I=\mathcal O(-D_i)\cdot\mathcal I_i$ at each step. Hence every blowup is an isomorphism over $\widetilde U\setminus\mathrm{supp}(\mathcal I)$ and the composite $\sigma$ is the identity there; combined with Step 2 it is the identity over $U$, so $X\setminus D\cong U$ and $j$ is the resulting open immersion.
Step 6 (common domination). For finitely many compactifications $X_1,\dots,X_m$ of $U$, apply Steps 1-5 to the reduced closure of the diagonal image of $U$ in the smooth projective product $X_1\times_{\mathbb C}\dots\times_{\mathbb C}X_m$; the projections of the resulting $X$ dominate each $X_i$ and restrict to the identity over $U$.
Step 7 (morphisms). For $\varphi:U\to V$ and chosen compactifications $\bar U\supseteq U$, $\bar V\supseteq V$, apply Steps 1-5 to the reduced closure of the graph $\Gamma_\varphi\subseteq\bar U\times\bar V$ (a smooth projective ambient); the projection to $\bar V$ extends $\varphi$ after modifying the source outside $U$. Applying Step 6 to two such extensions makes the two resulting pullback maps agree on $U$.
Obligations and caveats for the Step-3 author. (a) The proof must supply the projectivity argument of Step 3 in full, including that a blowup of a projective integral scheme along a coherent ideal embeds in a product with projective space (Serre twist plus graph-closure; the composition with the Segre embedding may be written inline as closed immersions compose). The declared [[thm-resolution-of-singularities-in-characteristic-zero]] states a proper birational resolution constructed on affine charts; it must not be used by itself to conclude that the compactification or the principalization is projective. (b) It is used for its iso-over-the-smooth-locus clause, which Step 5 needs alongside the embedded Step 2. (c) The design's second clause is used by consumers ([[lem-smooth-projective-modification-preserves-open-cohomology-images]]-style domination and the logarithmic theorem) for arbitrary smooth projective compactifications, not only SNC ones: the same Steps 1-5 applied to the given compactification, or the diagonal construction of Step 6 with one factor, provide that domination, and this stronger reading must be written into the proof explicitly. (d) Statements are scheme-theoretic over $\mathbb C$; the author must fix the classical-variety convention used in the statement and its standard comparison, and treat components separately for reducible $U$. (e) AC is consumed through the resolution, principalization and Serre-generation suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); gluing and divisor bookkeeping are choice-free.

The projectivity and divisor bookkeeping, the diagonal and graph closures, and the gluing/identity-over-U argument are otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Modification preserves open cohomology images
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $p:X'\to X$ be a proper morphism between smooth projective complex varieties of equal pure dimension, restricting to the identity on a common open variety $U$. Then $H^n(X,\mathbb Q)$ and $H^n(X',\mathbb Q)$ have the same image in $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ for every $n$. Consequently the compactification-image formula of logarithmic weights extends from an SNC compactification to every smooth projective compactification.
items.strategy:
Route (Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, 3.2.16-3.2.18; the duality computation is rewritten for the library's published duality, field-coefficient and cap-projection suppliers).
Step 1 (the pushforward). Both $X$ and $X'$ are compact oriented real $2d$-manifolds and $p$ is proper, so [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]] gives cap-duality isomorphisms and, on a compact manifold, $D_M(a)=a\cap[M]$. Define $p_!:=D_X^{-1}\circ p_*\circ D_{X'}:H^n(X')\to H^n(X)$.
Step 2 (adjoint identity). For $a\in H^n(X')$ and $b\in H^{2d-n}(X)$, the cap projection formula ([[prop-cap-product-naturality-and-projection-formula]]) and $p_*[X']=[X]$ (a proper birational map of equal-dimensional smooth projective varieties is degree one) give $\langle p_!a,b\rangle_X=\langle a,p^*b\rangle_{X'}$.
Step 3 (extension of compact supports). For the open immersions $U\hookrightarrow X$ and $U\hookrightarrow X'$ write $e_X,e_{X'}$ for extension of compact supports, the colimit structure maps of [[def-compactly-supported-singular-cohomology-of-a-locally-compact-space]]; [[thm-excision-for-singular-cohomology]] identifies the relative groups along the open inclusion. If $c\in H_c^{2d-n}(U)$ has a representative supported in a compact $K\subseteq U$, then $p^{-1}(K)=K$ because $p$ is the identity over $U$, so $p^*(e_Xc)=e_{X'}c$.
Step 4 (detection). [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]] identifies $H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$ with the full linear dual of $H_n(U;\mathbb Q)$, and Poincaré duality identifies $H_c^{2d-n}(U;\mathbb Q)$ with the dual of $H_n(U;\mathbb Q)$; the Kronecker pairing against compactly supported classes therefore detects every class of $H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$.
Step 5 (image equality). Restriction of $p^*a$ to $U$ is $a|_U$, giving $\operatorname{im}(H^n(X))\subseteq\operatorname{im}(H^n(X'))$. Conversely Steps 2-4 give $(p_!a)|_U=a|_U$ for every $a\in H^n(X')$, hence the reverse inclusion and equality of the two images.
Step 6 (arbitrary smooth projective compactifications). Given one smooth projective compactification $X$ of $U$ whose boundary need not be SNC, the diagonal/graph construction of [[lem-smooth-quasiprojective-varieties-admit-snc-projective-compactifications]] (applied to the single given compactification, without assuming its boundary is SNC) dominates it by an SNC smooth projective modification $X'\to X$ that is the identity over $U$. Steps 1-5 then identify the image of $H^n(X)$ with the image of the SNC compactification, so the image subgroup is the same subgroup that the SNC compactification supplies; the last sentence of the statement records exactly this independence, while its identification with the weight filtration is the companion logarithmic theorem's assertion.
Obligations and caveats for the Step-3 author. The identification $p_*[X']=[X]$ (a degree-one/duality argument) and the compact-support pullback identity $p^*(e_Xc)=e_{X'}c$ of Step 3 must be written out from the cited definitions rather than asserted; the equal-image statement does not need $U$ connected and does not need $X,X'$ irreducible. The domination clause of the previous lemma must be stated for an arbitrary smooth projective compactification, as noted in that lemma's obligations. AC enters only through the duality and universal-coefficient suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). No Hodge theory or strictness is used.

items.title: Logarithmic construction of smooth-open mixed Hodge structures
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, and choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, boundary $D$. The logarithmic de Rham complex with Hodge filtration by degree and pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$, independent of the compactification. Its weights are at least $n$, and
$$W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^n(U,\mathbb Q)).$$
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice; a smooth quasiprojective complex variety $U$ of pure dimension $d$; an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with reduced boundary $D$ a simple normal crossings divisor ([[def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors]], [[lem-smooth-quasiprojective-varieties-admit-snc-projective-compactifications]]); the irreducible components $D_1,\dots,D_r$ of $D$ and, for $a\ge0$, the closed subvariety $D^{[a]}\subseteq X$ equal to $X$ for $a=0$ and to the disjoint union of the $a$-fold intersections $D_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap D_{i_a}$ for $a\ge1$. Cohomology is singular cohomology of the analytic spaces on the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]].

[F1] Analytification ([[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]], [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]). $X$ is a compact complex manifold of dimension $d$ with a canonical orientation, $D$ is a reduced divisor with normal crossings, and near every point of $D$ there are holomorphic coordinates $z_1,\dots,z_d$ in which $D$ is $\{z_1\cdots z_r=0\}$ for some $r=r(p)$; each $D^{[a]}$ is a smooth projective complex variety of pure dimension $d-a$ (empty for $a>r$), a morphism of complex varieties induces a holomorphic map, and $U=X\setminus D$ is an open complex submanifold of dimension $d$. Complex-valued smooth forms, the bidegree decomposition, $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ and type are those of [[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]], and holomorphic functions on polydiscs are those of [[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]].

[F2] The de Rham comparison ([[thm-de-rham-theorem]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). For every finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$, integration of smooth forms on smooth simplices is a natural isomorphism $H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)\cong H^*_{\mathrm{sing}}(M;\mathbb R)$ under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, which AC supplies. It applies to the real manifolds underlying $X$, the strata $D^{[a]}$ and $U$, and is compatible with the coefficient extension to $\mathbb C$.

[F3] Hodge theory of the compact strata ([[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]], [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]], [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]). Let $V$ be a smooth projective complex variety of pure dimension $m$. Then $H^k(V;\mathbb Q)$ carries a functorial rational pure Hodge structure of weight $k$, whose Hodge filtration is the filtration induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration $\Omega^{\ge p}_V$ of the holomorphic de Rham complex; there is a Hodge decomposition $H^k(V;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(V)$ with $H^{p,q}(V)\cong H^q(V,\Omega^p_V)$; the Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$; and pullback along a morphism and cup product preserve type. In particular $H^k(V;\mathbb Q)$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$.

[F4] Local analytic inputs ([[thm-dolbeault-lemma-polydisc]], [[thm-cohomological-kunneth-isomorphism-under-finite-free-hypotheses]], [[cor-homology-of-spheres]], [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]], [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]]). On a polydisc $P\subseteq\mathbb C^m$, every $\bar\partial$-closed smooth $(p,q)$-form with $q\ge1$ is $\bar\partial$-exact on every smaller relatively compact polydisc. For a product of circles the Kunneth theorem computes the cohomology as the exterior algebra on the degree-one generators, with each factor contributing one generator because the homology of the circle is $\mathbb Q$ in degrees $0$ and $1$; over the field $\mathbb Q$ the Kronecker evaluation identifies a cohomology group with the full dual of homology, so the classes are detected by their values on the torus cycles.

[F5] Mixed Hodge machinery ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], [[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]], [[lem-mixed-hodge-complexes-give-functorial-cohomology-and-simplicial-weights]], [[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]). A rational mixed Hodge structure is a $\mathbb Q$-vector space with a finite increasing weight filtration $W$ and a finite decreasing Hodge filtration $F$ on the complexification, opposed on every weight-graded piece; a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex is a filtered pair $(K_{\mathbb Q},(K_{\mathbb C},W))$ with a comparison whose graded pieces are quasi-isomorphisms and whose weight-graded complexes have finite-dimensional cohomology with strict differentials and pure Hodge cohomology of weight $r+w$; a morphism of such complexes induces morphisms of the resulting structures; morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for $W$ and $F$, and the image of a morphism is both a sub- and a quotient structure.

[F6] Sheaves and derived global sections ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]], [[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]], [[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]]). Sheaf cohomology is the right derived global-sections functor computed from a supplied functorial injective resolution datum, independent of the datum up to natural isomorphism; for a bounded-below complex of sheaves the same construction is applied to a filtered injective resolution and computes the hypercohomology. On a metric space with a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets, constant-sheaf cohomology agrees with singular cohomology on every open subset.

[F7] Compactification and modification ([[lem-smooth-quasiprojective-varieties-admit-snc-projective-compactifications]], [[lem-smooth-projective-modification-preserves-open-cohomology-images]]). Any finite family of smooth projective compactifications of $U$ is dominated by a smooth projective compactification with reduced SNC boundary restricting to the identity over $U$; a proper morphism of smooth projective varieties of equal pure dimension that is the identity over $U$ does not change the image of $H^n(-;\mathbb Q)$ in $H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$.

[A1] AC is assumed in the statement and is consumed through [F1] (analytification and orientation), [F2] (the de Rham comparison and its $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), [F3] (the compact Kaehler machine), [F4] (the polydisc Dolbeault transform), [F6] (injective resolution data) and [F7] (resolution, principalization and the duality comparison of the modification lemma). The residue, filtration and spectral-sequence bookkeeping below is otherwise choice-free. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Compactification and strata.) By [F7] choose the SNC smooth projective compactification; the constructions below apply separately to its finitely many smooth connected components when dimensions differ. Order the finitely many boundary components to fix residue signs. Their $a$-fold intersections and disjoint unions $D^{[a]}$ are smooth projective by [F1], so [F3] applies to each component. Empty strata contribute zero. [F1, F3, F7, given, construct]

1.2 (Logarithmic forms and the pole filtration.) Put $e_i=dz_i/z_i$ for the $s$ local boundary coordinates. The logarithmic complex $L=\Omega_X^\bullet(\log D)$ is locally generated by $e_1,\ldots,e_s,dz_{s+1},\ldots,dz_d$ over holomorphic functions; regular normal differentials are included because $dz_i=z_ie_i$. Define in degree $k$ the pole-count filtration by $W_aL^k=\sum_{|I|\le a}e_I\wedge\Omega_X^{k-|I|}$, with arbitrary regular holomorphic forms in the second factor, not merely tangential forms. Thus $W_0L=\Omega_X^\bullet$, $W_aL=0$ for $a<0$, and $W_dL=L$. Changing a boundary equation by a unit adds a regular $d\log u$, so this definition is intrinsic. Since $de_i=0$ and differentiating a regular coefficient produces a regular form, $d$ preserves $W$. The degree filtration $F^pL=\Omega_X^{\ge p}(\log D)$ is also a finite filtration by subcomplexes. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 (Residues, signs and the Hodge shift.) For each ordered set $I$ of $a$ distinct components, write a term of $W_aL^k$ as $e_I\wedge\eta_I$ with $\eta_I$ regular, and restrict $\eta_I$ to $D_I$. These are separate residue coordinates on the separate summands of $D^{[a]}$. Terms with fewer poles restrict to zero in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_a$; a regular normal differential restricts to zero, and a coefficient vanishing on $D_I$ lies in the ideal generated by its normal coordinates, each factor $z_i$ converting $e_i$ to the regular form $dz_i$ and reducing the pole count. These observations prove that the kernel of the residue map on $W_a$ is exactly $W_{a-1}$. Conversely every regular stratum form extends locally in the normal coordinates and lifts as $e_I\wedge\eta_I$, proving surjectivity. Changes of local equations add only lower-pole terms, so these maps glue. The differential is $d(e_I\wedge\eta_I)=(-1)^a e_I\wedge d\eta_I$, agreeing with the differential of the shifted complex $[-a]$. Hence $\operatorname{Gr}^W_aL\cong i_{a*}\Omega_{D^{[a]}}^\bullet[-a]$, and $F^p$ corresponds to the stratum degree filtration $F^{p-a}$, the shift appropriate to a Tate twist $(-a)$. [F1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

2.2 (A pole-preserving local contraction.) Work on a smaller polydisc centered at a boundary point with $s$ normal coordinates. Contract the ordinary tangential coordinates by the holomorphic radial homotopy: integration of contraction with the radial vector field over $t\in[0,1]$ gives $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}-\mathrm{ev}_0$ on their de Rham complex. This preserves every pole level, since it affects only regular tangential forms. What remains is the normal logarithmic complex with holomorphic coefficients $f(z)=\sum_{\nu\in\mathbb N^s}c_\nu z^\nu$ and differential $d(z^\nu e_I)=z^\nu(\sum_i\nu_i e_i)\wedge e_I$. For a nonzero multiindex $\nu$, choose the first index $i$ with $\nu_i>0$ and put $h_\nu=\nu_i^{-1}\iota_i$, contraction of the exterior algebra with the $i$-th basis vector. The identity $(\sum_j\nu_je_j)\wedge h_\nu+h_\nu(\sum_j\nu_je_j)\wedge=\mathrm{id}$ contracts that entire monomial summand. This also preserves $W$: in an $e_I$ monomial a logarithmic index with $\nu_i>0$ can be written as a regular differential by factoring $z_i$, so its effective pole count is precisely the number of indices $j\in I$ with $\nu_j=0$; $h_\nu$ removes only a positive-exponent index. Partitioning the series into the finitely many sectors specified by this first positive index and dividing coefficients by $\nu_i\ge1$ preserves normal convergence on each smaller polydisc, so these operators define a holomorphic homotopy. The single all-zero multiindex is left unchanged: its surviving complex is the exterior algebra on the $e_i$, with zero differential and $W_a$ equal to the span of wedges of degree at most $a$. This handles every pattern of simultaneous zero exponents and proves $\mathcal H^q(W_aL)_p=\bigwedge^q\mathbb C^s$ for $0\le q\le a$, and zero otherwise; inclusion $W_aL\to L$ induces the identity on these spaces. [F1, F4, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 (Every canonical truncation and the rational normalization.) Inclusion of holomorphic logarithmic forms into the pushed-forward smooth de Rham resolution on $U$ compares $L$ to $Rj_*\mathbb C_U$. On the polydiscs of step 2.2 the target stalk cohomology is the cohomology of $(\Delta^*)^s\times\Delta^{d-s}$, the exterior algebra on meridians by [F4]. Integration gives $\int_{\gamma_i}e_j=2\pi i\delta_{ij}$, so the comparison is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. Let $\tau_{\le a}$ denote the canonical truncation, with degree $a$ equal to the kernel of the next differential. Since every degree-$k$ logarithmic form has at most $k$ poles, the identity gives a genuine chain inclusion $\tau_{\le a}L\to W_aL$. By step 2.2 it induces an isomorphism in degrees at most $a$ and both sides have no cohomology above $a$, hence is a quasi-isomorphism for every $a$. These inclusions commute with the maps as $a$ increases. We therefore have the filtered comparison zigzag $(Rj_*\mathbb Q_U\otimes\mathbb C,\tau)\to(Rj_*\mathbb C_U,\tau)\leftarrow(L,\tau)\to(L,W)$, all arrows graded quasi-isomorphisms; exact scalar extension and the local finite torus cohomology establish the first arrow. On each graded sheaf the rational meridian wedge corresponds to $(2\pi i)^{-a}e_I$, which pairs by $1$ with the degree-$a$ meridian torus, not a degree-$2a$ class. Ordered residues thus identify $R^aj_*\mathbb Q_U$ with $i_{a*}\mathbb Q_{D^{[a]}}$ and place its comparison lattice in $(2\pi i)^{-a}\mathbb Q$, exactly the rational Tate normalization $(-a)$. [F2, F4, F6, step 2.1, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 (Actual filtered global-section models and a single comparison.) The sheaf comparison in step 3.1 is a zigzag, so it must not be treated as a nonexistent direct sheaf map in the opposite direction. Resolve the complexes and their filtrations by the exact Godement construction: $C^0(A)(V)=\prod_{x\in V}A_x$, with the natural embedding and successive cokernels. Stalks and products are exact for vector spaces under AC. Moreover $C^0(A)=\prod_{x\in X}i_{x*}A_x$ is an injective sheaf of field-vector spaces: each $A_x$ is injective over its field by extension of linear maps along a chosen complement, the exact stalk functor is left adjoint to $i_{x*}$, and a product of injectives is injective because the component extension maps can be chosen simultaneously under AC. The successive cokernel construction therefore gives an actual injective resolution. Exactness of $C^0$ and the short exact augmentation sequences give exactness of each successive cokernel functor by the snake lemma, so the resulting functorial resolution is exact on filtration levels, their finite intersections and both associated gradings; its global-section total computes derived global sections. Apply it to $L$ with $W,F$ and to the other weight-filtered models in the zigzag. Replace the rational and comparison models by $\tau_{\le d}$ first; their cohomology sheaves above $d$ vanish by the local torus calculation, so this is a quasi-isomorphism and leaves a finite weight range $0\le a\le d$. After resolution and global sections the complex-coefficient arrows in the zigzag are maps of weight-filtered vector-space complexes with graded quasi-isomorphisms. For the rational scalar-extension arrow, the global graded comparison is the isomorphism $H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)\otimes\mathbb C\to H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb C)$ from [F3], with the normalization of step 3.1; this proves it is a graded quasi-isomorphism without interchanging tensor product with an infinite product of stalks. Such a map admits a weight-filtered homotopy inverse: its cone has acyclic weight-graded complexes; a cycle in $W_a$ has a leading graded preimage, and subtracting its differential lowers the cycle to $W_{a-1}$, so finite induction supplies a preimage in $W_a$. Thus the cone is acyclic with a $W$-strict differential. Choose filtration-compatible complements of its cycles and right inverses of its differential; the resulting degree-minus-one homotopy contracts the cone and preserves $W$, and the cone homotopy equations give a $W$-filtered homotopy inverse of the original map. AC permits these linear complements. Inverting the leftward comparison in step 3.1 and composing the remaining arrows gives an actual $W$-filtered chain map $K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$, with $K_{\mathbb C}=\Gamma(X,C^\bullet(L))$ carrying the original $W,F$. Its graded maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Different inverse choices are filtered-homotopic, so their induced comparison and image filtrations on cohomology agree. These are bounded-below degreewise-finite filtered models of the type required in [F5]. [F6, A1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 (Strictness on the weight-graded global models.) Exactness of the resolution and step 2.1 identify $\operatorname{Gr}^W_aK_{\mathbb C}$ with a global-section resolution of $\Omega_{D^{[a]}}^\bullet[-a]$, with its degree Hodge filtration shifted by $a$. Its Hodge spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ by [F3]. This implies strictness of the differential of this actual filtered vector-space complex: if $dx$ belongs to $F^p$, take the leading $F$ index $b<p$ of $x$; its class in the associated-graded complex is a cycle. Degeneration means this $E_1$ class lifts to an actual cycle $y\in F^b$, up to an element of $F^{b+1}$ and a boundary in $F^b$. Subtract that cycle and boundary from $x$, preserving $dx$ and raising the filtration index of the preimage. Repeat through the finite filtration until a preimage of $dx$ lies in $F^p$. Thus $\operatorname{im}d\cap F^p=d(F^p)$. Moreover its degree-$r$ cohomology is $H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)(-a)$ under the comparison of step 3.1, with the induced $F$, pure of weight $r-a+2a=r+a$ and finite-dimensional by [F3]. Hence the global comparison models of step 4.1 satisfy every graded axiom of a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex, including strictness and the full induced Hodge filtration. [F3, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 (The mixed structure and its spectral sequence.) Apply the full conclusion of [F5] to the proved mixed Hodge complex of step 5.1. Its cohomology is $H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$ by steps 3.1-5.1 and [F6], and it carries the image Hodge filtration and shifted weight filtration $W_mH^n(U)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$. The weight spectral sequence is $E_1^{-a,q}=H^{q-2a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)(-a)$, pure of weight $q$, degenerates at $E_2$, and gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(U)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ with its induced Hodge filtration. In particular this step uses the supplied recurrent-to-image-filtration proof, not an assumption that higher differentials preserve the desired filtration. [F5, F6, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 (Lower weight bound and compactification image.) The pole index $a$ is nonnegative, so a term contributing to total degree $n=q-a$ has weight $q=n+a\ge n$. Hence step 6.1 gives $W_{n-1}H^n(U)=0$. Also $W_nH^n(U)$ is the image of $H^n(W_0K)$. On the complex side $W_0L=\Omega_X^\bullet$ by step 1.2; on the rational side $\tau_{\le0}Rj_*\mathbb Q_U=\mathbb Q_X$, since a punctured-coordinate polydisc is connected. Its map to $Rj_*\mathbb Q_U$ is restriction. Thus both sides identify $W_nH^n(U)$ with the actual image of $j^*:H^n(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$, compatibly with the rational comparison and Hodge filtration. [F2, F3, F6, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 (Functoriality and independence.) A compactified extension $f:(X,D)\to(Y,E)$ of an open morphism satisfies $f^{-1}(E)\subseteq D$. Locally a target boundary equation pulls back to a unit times a product of source boundary equations with nonnegative integer exponents, so $f^*d\log t=d\log u+\sum_i m_i d\log z_i$. Wedges preserve pole count and degree, hence $f^*$ preserves $W,F$ on the logarithmic complexes and is compatible with the rational meridian comparison. The functorial resolutions and filtered comparison homotopies of step 4.1 produce the same natural pullback on cohomology; [F5] therefore makes it a mixed Hodge morphism. The graph-extension construction in [F7] supplies such compactified extensions after modifying the source. For two SNC compactifications of one $U$, a common SNC domination gives pullback comparison maps between their logarithmic mixed Hodge structures on $H^n(U)$, whose underlying rational maps are the identity. Strictness in [F5] makes these identity maps isomorphisms for both filtrations, proving independence. For any smooth projective compactification with arbitrary boundary, the modification-image clause of [F7] identifies its restriction image with the SNC one, so the formula of step 7.1 holds for it too. [F5, F7, step 4.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, construct, algebra]

9.1 (Choice and boundary cases.) AC is inherited through the typed suppliers in [A1] and is also used exactly in step 4.1 for exact products in the Godement resolution and filtration-compatible vector-space complements to strictify the comparison zigzag. The monomial contractions, residues, rational meridian normalization, finite filtrations and weight bookkeeping are otherwise choice-free. With empty boundary $L=\Omega_X^\bullet$ and $W_0=L$, recovering the pure projective structure; empty $U$ may be represented by empty compactification and has zero cohomology, while the SNC compactification hypotheses already require density on every nonempty component. Components of differing dimensions are handled separately, empty strata vanish, and degrees outside the cohomological range give zero groups. This completes the retained full mixed Hodge, functoriality, independence, lower-weight and image claims. [A1, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, algebra] ∎

title: Logarithmic Hodge Complexes And Smooth Open Weights Examples

items.title: The punctured line has a weight-two logarithmic class
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For $U=\mathbb C^\times\subset\mathbb P^1$, $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q(-1)$, of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$. In particular its weight is strictly larger than its cohomological degree.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice; the smooth quasiprojective curve $U=\mathbb C^\times=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\setminus\{0,\infty\}$ with its SNC compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X=\mathbb P^1$, boundary $D=\{0\}\sqcup\{\infty\}$ ([[def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors]]).

[F1] The strata of the compactification. $D^{[0]}=X=\mathbb P^1$, $D^{[1]}=D$ is the disjoint union of the two points $0$ and $\infty$, and $D^{[a]}=\varnothing$ for $a\ge2$; all are smooth projective complex varieties of pure dimensions $1$ and $0$. The underlying analytic space of $\mathbb P^1$ is the Riemann sphere $S^2$, and $U$ retracts onto the unit circle $S^1$ by $z\mapsto z/|z|$. [given, construct]

[F2] Cohomology of spheres ([[cor-homology-of-spheres]], [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]]). Over $\mathbb Q$, $H_0(S^1)=H_1(S^1)=\mathbb Q$ and $H_n(S^1)=0$ otherwise, and the same pattern holds for $S^2$ in degrees $0$ and $2$; over the field $\mathbb Q$ evaluation identifies $H^n(-;\mathbb Q)$ with the full linear dual of $H_n(-;\mathbb Q)$. Hence $H^0(S^1;\mathbb Q)=H^1(S^1;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ with higher groups zero, and $H^0(S^2;\mathbb Q)=H^2(S^2;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ with $H^1(S^2;\mathbb Q)=0$; a point and a two-point space have cohomology $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb Q^2$ in degree $0$ and zero in positive degrees.

[F3] The logarithmic mixed Hodge structure ([[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]]). For the SNC compactification of [F1] the logarithmic complex endows $H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$ with its weight filtration $W$, of weights at least $n$, satisfying $W_nH^n(U;\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^n(U;\mathbb Q))$, with weight spectral sequence $E_1^{-a,q}=H^{q-2a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)(-a)\Rightarrow H^{q-a}(U;\mathbb Q)$ degenerating at $E_2$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(U;\mathbb Q)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$; the local residue normalization of that construction assigns to the closed logarithmic form $dz/z$ on $U$ the rational class $(2\pi i)^{-1}dz/z\in H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$, whose normalized rational residue coordinates at $0$ and at $\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$; the ordinary analytic residue of the normalized form is $(2\pi i)^{-1}$ times the corresponding coordinate.

[F4] Tate twist and type ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]). The Tate structure $\mathbb Q(-1)$ is the pure rational Hodge structure of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$, concentrated in $H^{1,1}$; a mixed Hodge structure whose weight-graded pieces are $\operatorname{Gr}^W_2=\mathbb Q(-1)$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m=0$ for $m\ne2$ is pure of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$.

[A1] AC is assumed and is consumed only through [F3] and its suppliers; the finite computations below are choice-free. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct: compute both sides of the weight spectral sequence of the logarithmic complex for $\mathbb P^1$ and identify the surviving degree-one term with the Tate twist.

1.1 The two cohomologies. By [F1] and [F2], $H^0(X;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$, $H^1(X;\mathbb Q)=0$, $H^2(X;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$; $H^0(D^{[1]};\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q^2$ and $H^1(D^{[1]};\mathbb Q)=0$; and $H^0(U;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$, $H^1(U;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$, $H^2(U;\mathbb Q)=0$, the generator being the meridian class dual to the circle. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The logarithmic generator. By the residue normalization of [F3] the class $(2\pi i)^{-1}dz/z$ is a nonzero rational class in $H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$ pairing by $1$ with the positively oriented meridian, so it generates the one-dimensional space $H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$ of step 1.1; its normalized rational residue coordinates at $0$ and $\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, because in the coordinate $w=1/z$ at infinity the form $dz/z$ equals $-dw/w$. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The weight spectral sequence. Only $a=0,1$ contribute. The $a=0$ column has $E_1^{0,0}=\mathbb Q(0)$, $E_1^{0,1}=0$, $E_1^{0,2}=H^2(\mathbb P^1;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q(-1)$, pure of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$; the $a=1$ column has $E_1^{-1,2}=\mathbb Q(-1)^2$ and is otherwise zero. The sole possible nonzero differential is $d_1:E_1^{-1,2}\to E_1^{0,2}$, a pure Hodge morphism. Since the sequence degenerates at $E_2$ and $H^2(U)=0$ by step 1.1, its cokernel is zero, so its rank is one. The global closed logarithmic form of step 2.1 has normalized residue vector $(1,-1)$, which must survive this differential because it represents an actual cohomology class; hence this vector lies in its kernel. A rank-one map from a two-dimensional space has one-dimensional kernel, so $\ker d_1=\mathbb Q(1,-1)\cong\mathbb Q(-1)$. Equivalently, in a rational target generator normalized to the nonzero image of $(1,0)$, $d_1(r_0,r_\infty)=r_0+r_\infty$. Thus $E_2^{-1,2}=\mathbb Q(-1)$, $E_2^{0,2}=0$, $E_2^{0,0}=\mathbb Q(0)$, and all remaining terms vanish. This computes the required weight-graded piece without assuming an unproved Gysin normalization. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The mixed Hodge structure on $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)$. By [F3] the weight-graded piece $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^1(U;\mathbb Q)$ is $E_2^{1-m,m}$, so by step 3.1 it is $\mathbb Q(-1)$ for $m=2$ and vanishes for every other $m$; in particular $W_1H^1(U;\mathbb Q)=0$ and $W_2H^1(U;\mathbb Q)=H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$, which also agrees with the weights-at-least-$1$ and image formulas of [F3] and with $H^1(X;\mathbb Q)=0$ from step 1.1. By [F4] the class supported in weight $2$ with $\operatorname{Gr}^W_2=\mathbb Q(-1)$ makes $H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$ pure of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$, so $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q(-1)$; the classical generator $(2\pi i)^{-1}dz/z$ of step 2.1 is a rational class of this structure. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Conclusion and boundaries. The weight of $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)$ is $2$, strictly larger than the cohomological degree $1$, and the only nonzero Hodge number is $h^{1,1}=1$. The space $U$ is nonempty and disconnected cases do not arise; $H^0$ and $H^2$ of $U$ are handled by step 1.1 and carry weights $0$ and at most $2$; the two residue coordinates are the two components of $D$, and the kernel computation is finite linear algebra over $\mathbb Q$; no choice beyond [A1] is used. [A1, F4, step 2.1, step 4.1, given] ∎

items.title: Smooth projective analytifications have rational Kähler forms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the Jacobian-criterion, embedding and Chern-form suppliers below. Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme of pure dimension $n$. Then the closed points of $X$ carry a structure of **compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold** $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ of complex dimension $n$, its analytification, such that: every standard smooth algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and every morphism of smooth complex schemes $X\to Y$ induces a holomorphic map $X^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$. Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham class is the real image of the topological first Chern class $c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$: $$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$ where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$.
items.strategy:
Assume AC. Route: build the analytic charts from the relative Jacobian criterion and the holomorphic implicit function theorem, get compactness from a projective embedding into $\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$, and build the form from the Fubini-Study metric; sources: Serre, GAGA, §1 n°5 and §2 n°5-7 (Lemme 1, Proposition 2, Corollaire 3, Proposition 6, printed pp. 8-12), and Demailly, Chapter V §12 (12.2)-(12.8), §13 (13.2)-(13.4), §15.B (15.8) and Theorem (15.10), Chapter VI §4 (4.4)-(4.6). Step 1 (charts). The morphism $X	o\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ is locally of finite presentation, so at a closed point $x$ the relative Jacobian criterion [[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]] gives a standard smooth presentation $C_h\cong(\mathbb C[t_1,\dots,t_m]/(f_1,\dots,f_r))_g$ in which some $r	imes r$ minor of the Jacobian is invertible at $x$; the chart is flat over $\mathbb C$ with geometrically regular fibres of dimension $m-r$, and pure dimension $n$ of $X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ gives $m-r=n$. On complex points the minor remains invertible on a Euclidean neighbourhood, and the holomorphic implicit function theorem [[thm-holomorphic-implicit-function-theorem]] presents the common zero set of $f_1,\dots,f_r$ as a holomorphic graph over $n$ coordinates, a chart of a complex manifold of dimension $n$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). Two such charts are related by isomorphisms of localized standard smooth $\mathbb C$-algebras; their coordinate functions are rational functions with nonvanishing denominators near the point, hence holomorphic, and the inverse transition is holomorphic by the holomorphic inverse function theorem in several variables [[thm-holomorphic-inverse-function-theorem-several-variables]]. The charts glue on their overlaps, and morphisms of smooth complex schemes become holomorphic because their chart expressions are regular. Step 2 (compactness and topology). By [[thm-ample-powers-very-ample-proper-base]] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ (Noetherian), $X$ proper of finite type over $S$ and $A$ ample, some $A^{\otimes d}$ is closed $H$-very ample relative to $S$: there is a closed immersion $j:X	o\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ with $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong A^{\otimes d}$. The complex points $\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$ are a compact Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold [[def-complex-projective-space-and-holomorphic-charts]]; the defining homogeneous equations of $j$ have full-rank holomorphic Jacobian along $X(\mathbb C)$, so by Step 1's graph presentation $j^{\mathrm{an}}$ identifies the manifold topology of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ with the subspace topology of a closed subset of $\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$; that subset is closed (it is a common zero locus of polynomials) and hence compact. Closed subspaces of second-countable Hausdorff spaces are second-countable Hausdorff, and the local dimension is $n$. Step 3 (the form). Put $\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}= rac{i}{2\pi}\partial ar\partial\log(1+|z|^2)$ on the standard chart of $\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$; chart changes add $\log|g|^2$ for a nonvanishing holomorphic $g$, whose $\partial ar\partial$ vanishes, so the local forms glue to a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form whose Hermitian matrix $ igl((1+|z|^2)\delta_{jk}- ar z_jz_k igr)/ igl(2\pi(1+|z|^2)^2 igr)$ is positive definite by Cauchy-Schwarz ([[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]). Give $\mathcal O(1)$ its Fubini-Study Hermitian metric of local weight $(1+|z|^2)^{-1}$; its Chern connection is characterised by $
abla''= ar\partial$ and metric compatibility and satisfies $
abla'(fe)=(d'f+f\,\psi^{-1}d'\psi)\otimes e$ in a holomorphic frame of metric weight $\psi$, with curvature $\Theta_
abla= -\partial ar\partial\log\psi=\partial ar\partial\log(1+|z|^2)$ ([[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]], [[def-curvature-of-a-vector-bundle-connection]]); hence $-\Theta_
abla/(2\pi i)=\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}$ and, by [[lem-first-chern-form-agrees-with-the-topological-line-class]], $[\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}]$ is the real image of $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$, whose class generates $H^2(\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C);\mathbb Z)$. Pulling back along the holomorphic immersion $j^{\mathrm{an}}$ gives the smooth positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $j^*\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}$ with $[j^*\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}]=ho(c_1(A^{\otimes d}))$, and the additivity clause of [[prop-first-chern-class-of-tensor-dual-and-conjugate-lines]] gives $c_1(A^{\otimes d})=d\,c_1(A)$; the real and integral structures compared here are those of [[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]. Then $\eta_A:=j^*\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}/d$ is the required form, since positivity and closedness are preserved by the positive scale factor $1/d$.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is stated on the item and declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; it is consumed through [[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]], [[thm-ample-powers-very-ample-proper-base]], [[lem-first-chern-form-agrees-with-the-topological-line-class]] and [[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]. The chart construction and the Fubini-Study computation are elementary.

items.title: Kähler identities give Lefschetz sl-two and hard Lefschetz
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold with Kähler form $\omega$, in the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], and put $L=[\omega]\smile(-)$ on cohomology. Then $L^{n-k}:H^k(X;\mathbb R)\to H^{2n-k}(X;\mathbb R)$ is an isomorphism for $0\le k\le n$. Harmonic representatives transport $(L,\Lambda,H)$ to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action: here $\Lambda$ on cohomology means applying $\Lambda$ to the harmonic representative, not to an arbitrary closed form, and $H$ acts by $\deg-n$. Primitive cohomology is $P^k=\ker L^{n-k+1}$, and $$H^k(X;\mathbb R)=\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^rP^{k-2r},$$ with the type decomposition inherited from forms: a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$. If $[\omega]$ is the real image of a rational class $\ell$, all these decompositions and $L$-isomorphisms are rational, and they remain isomorphisms after extension to every characteristic-zero field.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: transport the pointwise Hermitian-exterior algebra through the Hodge isomorphism; sources: Schnell, Class 18, Theorem 18.13 with Corollary 18.14 and the sl2 discussion, printed pp. 4-5; Demailly, Chapter VI §8.3 (8.13)-(8.17), printed p. 313; the pointwise input is [[lem-hermitian-exterior-lefschetz-decomposition-and-weil-star-identity]]. Step 1 (operators on cohomology). The Kähler commutators [[lem-kahler-commutators-and-laplacian-type-preservation]] give $[\Delta,L]=[\Delta,\Lambda]=0$, so $L$ and $\Lambda$ carry harmonic forms to harmonic forms. By the Hodge theorem [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] every de Rham class has a unique harmonic representative; define $L,\Lambda,H$ on $H^*(X;\mathbb R)$ by applying the corresponding operator to that representative. On closed forms $L$ is wedge with $\omega$, which descends on cohomology to cup product with $[\omega]$; the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations and $H=(\deg-n)$ hold on forms, hence on harmonic forms by commutation with $\Delta$, and pass to cohomology. Note that $\Lambda$ does not preserve closed forms in general, which is why it is transported through the harmonic representative. Step 2 (primitive decomposition and hard Lefschetz). By the unique primitive decomposition of [[lem-hermitian-exterior-lefschetz-decomposition-and-weil-star-identity]], every harmonic form $u$ of degree $k$ is uniquely $\sum_rL^ru_r$ with $u_r$ primitive harmonic of degree $k-2r$; the projections are polynomials in $L,\Lambda$, and the string formulas give $\Lambda^sL^ru=\frac{r!}{(r-s)!}\cdot\frac{(n-k-r+s)!}{(n-k-r)!}L^{r-s}u$ for $0\le s\le r\le n-k$ and $L^{n-k+1}u=0$ for primitive $u$ of degree $k$, while $L^ru\ne0$ for $0\le r\le n-k$. Hence $L^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ is bijective for $k\le n$ (on each string it maps the lowest vector to the highest), the kernel of $L^{n-k+1}$ is exactly $P^k$, and the displayed direct sum follows by taking harmonic representatives summand by summand. As $L$ has bidegree $(1,1)$ and $\Lambda$ has bidegree $(-1,-1)$, a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$. Step 3 (rationality). Suppose $[\omega]=\rho(\ell)$ with $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$. In rational bases the matrix of $L^{n-k}:H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^{2n-k}(X;\mathbb Q)$ is rational; it becomes invertible over $\mathbb R$, so its determinant is a nonzero rational number and it is already invertible over $\mathbb Q$, remaining invertible after scalar extension to any characteristic-zero field $F$ under the comparison $H^*(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes F\cong H^*(X;F)$, which preserves cup products ([[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]). The kernels $P^k=\ker L^{n-k+1}$ are then rational, and downward induction on $k$ shows that the rational matrix of the direct-sum map $\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^rP^{k-2r}\to H^k$ is invertible over $\mathbb Q$ because it becomes the isomorphism of Step 2 over $\mathbb R$; hence the decomposition is rational. Finally, the lowering operator reconstructed on a string by $\Lambda L^ru=r(n-k-r+1)L^{r-1}u$ has rational coefficients and coincides over $\mathbb R$ with the transported harmonic $\Lambda$ by uniqueness of the primitive decomposition.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is stated on the item and declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; it is consumed through the Kähler-commutator, Hodge-decomposition and rational-comparison suppliers.

items.title: Morphisms, polarizability and simplicity of rational Hodge structures
items.statement: With the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], all structures in this item are rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight $k$. A **morphism of Hodge structures** $f:(V,\{V^{p,q}\})\to(W,\{W^{p,q}\})$ is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $f:V\to W$ whose $\mathbb C$-linear extension satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(V^{p,q})\subseteq W^{p,q}$ for all $p+q=k$. **Kernels and images** are again rational sub-Hodge structures: a bidegree-preserving map sends the bidegree components of a vector into the matching components, so $\ker(f_{\mathbb C})=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\bigl(\ker(f_{\mathbb C})\cap V^{p,q}\bigr)$ and $\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\bigl(\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})\cap W^{p,q}\bigr)$, the second sum being direct because the target bidegrees $W^{p,q}$ are distinct. The **direct sum** is $(V\oplus W)^{p,q}=V^{p,q}\oplus W^{p,q}$, with the inclusions and projections as morphisms. A **short exact sequence** $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{\pi}W\to 0$ of weight-$k$ Hodge structures consists of morphisms that are exact as a sequence of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces; it **splits** in the category of Hodge structures if $\pi$ admits a morphism $s:W\to V$ with $\pi\circ s=\operatorname{id}_W$. A Hodge structure is **polarizable** if it admits a polarization, and **simple** if it has no nonzero proper rational sub-Hodge structure.
items.strategy: This item records the vocabulary invoked below on this page — the orthogonal splitting of polarized Hodge structures and the absolute projective Hodge package — as the pure weight-$k$ case of the morphisms of $\mathbb Q$-Hodge structures of Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.1.11)-(2.1.12), printed pp. 26-27. It is deliberately not routed through the mixed Hodge structures of a different page of this run, which lie outside this page's declared prerequisite closure. The only assertions to check are the componentwise closure claims recorded in the statement: if $x=\sum x^{p,q}$ and $f_{\mathbb C}(x)=0$, then $0=\sum f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ with $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})\in W^{p,q}$, so every $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$; and $\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})=\sum_{p+q=k}f_{\mathbb C}(V^{p,q})$ is direct because the target bidegrees are distinct. No proof phase applies to a definition, and no choice principle is used.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the item fixes definitions and verifies componentwise linear algebra; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Polarized rational Hodge structures split orthogonally
items.statement: Let $(V,Q)$ be a polarized rational pure Hodge structure and $U\subseteq V$ a rational sub-Hodge structure, with the notions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] and [[def-morphisms-and-polarizability-of-rational-hodge-structures]]. Then $Q|_U$ is a polarization of $U$, and $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$ is an orthogonal direct sum of rational Hodge structures in which the complement is polarized. Every short exact sequence of polarizable rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight splits in the category of Hodge structures, and every polarizable rational pure Hodge structure is a finite direct sum of simple Hodge structures. These are claims about rational Hodge substructures; they do not assert a splitting for an arbitrary local system. Every rational splitting persists after extension of scalars to any characteristic-zero field; no positivity or ordered-field structure on that field is asserted, and a subobject over an extension field need not be defined over $\mathbb Q$.
items.strategy: Choice-free finite-dimensional linear algebra. Route: Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.1.15)-(2.1.17), printed pp. 26-27, and Lemme (4.2.3) with its proof, printed p. 44. Step 1 (the restriction is a polarization). The Weil operator $C$ and complex conjugation preserve $U_{\mathbb C}$, because $U$ is a rational sub-Hodge structure. The form $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ restricts from $V$ to $U$, is positive definite there, and $Q|_U$ inherits rationality, $(-1)^k$-symmetry and type orthogonality from $Q$. If $u\in U$ lies in the radical of $Q|_U$, then $Cu$ does too: type orthogonality gives $Q(Cx,y)=Q(x,C^{-1}y)$ for all $x,y$, since both sides select the same $(p,q)$-$(q,p)$ components, so $Q(Cu,U)=Q(u,C^{-1}U)=0$. Then $h(u,u)=Q(Cu,\bar u)=0$, and positive definiteness forces $u=0$; hence $Q|_U$ is nondegenerate and is a polarization of $U$. Step 2 (the orthogonal complement). As $Q|_U$ is nondegenerate, the rational equations $Q(x,U)=0$ define a rational complement $U^{\perp_Q}$ with $\dim U^{\perp_Q}=\dim V-\dim U$ and $U\cap U^{\perp_Q}=0$, so $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$. If $x=\sum x^{p,q}\in U^{\perp_Q}_{\mathbb C}$ and $v\in U^{q,p}$, then $0=Q(x,v)=\sum_{r,s}Q(x^{r,s},v)=Q(x^{q,p},v)$, because $Q$ pairs $V^{r,s}$ nontrivially only with $V^{s,r}$; as $x^{q,p}$ pairs nontrivially only with type $(q,p)$, it is orthogonal to all of $U$. Thus each $x^{p,q}\in U^{\perp_Q}$, which is therefore a rational sub-Hodge structure, and the restriction of $h$ to it is positive definite; by Step 1 the restricted $Q$ is a polarization of the complement. Step 3 (splitting, semisimplicity, scalar extension). In a short exact sequence $0\to U\to V\to W\to 0$ of polarizable structures the middle term $V$ is polarizable; identify $U$ with its image, a rational sub-Hodge structure because a bidegree-preserving map has bidegree-preserving image and kernel, and fix a polarization $Q$ of $V$. By Step 2, $\pi$ restricts to an isomorphism $U^{\perp_Q}\to W$ of Hodge structures whose inverse is the required section, so the sequence splits. For semisimplicity, choose in a nonzero polarizable $V$ a nonzero rational sub-Hodge structure $U$ of least dimension; $U$ is simple, and $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$ with polarizable complement of smaller dimension, so induction on $\dim V$ exhibits $V$ as a finite direct sum of simple structures. A rational splitting or direct-sum decomposition is given by rational matrices satisfying bidegree-wise linear identities (idempotence of the projections, and Q(x,U)=0 for the complement); these identities persist under scalar extension to any characteristic-zero field, so the splitting and the decomposition extend with it, and positivity is never invoked over that field.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the argument is finite-dimensional rational and complex linear algebra over fixed finite-dimensional structures; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations for smooth projective varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold in the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] and let $0\le k\le n$. On the primitive space $P^k$ put $$Q_k(a,b)=\epsilon(k)\int_Xa\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k}.$$ This form is $(-1)^k$-symmetric, pairs $P^{p,q}$ only with $P^{q,p}$, and for nonzero $a\in P^{p,q}$ satisfies $$i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)=(n-k)!\,\|a_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2>0.$$ If $[\omega]=\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, then $Q_k$ is a rational polarization of $P^k$. Full $H^k$ is polarized by the orthogonal direct sum form that on $L^rP^{k-2r}$ is $(-1)^rQ_k$; degrees $k>n$ are polarized by transporting the polarization of $H^{2n-k}$ along $L^{k-n}$, with Tate shift. In particular this applies to smooth closed complex projective submanifolds of projective space with a hyperplane polarization, hence to smooth projective complex varieties through their smooth projective analytifications; more generally it applies to every real Kähler class, including $\ell+\epsilon\eta$ when represented by a positive closed form. For any continuous family of Kähler classes the primitive kernels (of every fixed degree $0\le k\le n$) vary continuously as subspaces; rational primitive spaces are asserted only at rational classes.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route (Schnell, Class 18, §'The Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations', Theorem 18.15, printed pp. 5-6; Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.1.15)-(2.1.17), printed pp. 26-27; Demailly, Chapter VI §4 (4.4)-(4.6) for the projective instance). Step 1 (well-definedness, symmetry, types, positivity). If $b$ is closed and $a$ is replaced by $a+du$, the integrand changes by $d\bigl(u\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k}\bigr)$ up to sign, so the integral depends only on the cohomology classes by the general Stokes theorem [[thm-general-stokes-theorem]] and the de Rham comparison; the same argument applies in the second variable, and [[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]] supplies the comparison maps. Wedge signs give $Q_k(b,a)=(-1)^kQ_k(a,b)$, and a class of type $(p,q)$ paired with one of type $(a,b)$ contributes only if $p+a+n-k=n=q+b+n-k$, i.e. $(a,b)=(q,p)$. Hard Lefschetz [[thm-kahler-identities-give-lefschetz-sl-two-and-hard-lefschetz]] identifies $P^k$ with the primitive harmonic $k$-forms, and the pointwise Weil-star identity of [[lem-hermitian-exterior-lefschetz-decomposition-and-weil-star-identity]] applied to the primitive form $\bar a$ of type $(q,p)$ gives $*\bar a=\epsilon(k)i^{p-q}L^{n-k}\bar a/(n-k)!$; integrating $a\wedge*\bar a$ (the $L^2$ inner product) yields $i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)=(n-k)!\|a\|^2>0$, the displayed positivity, and nondegeneracy. If $\ell$ is rational, [[lem-de-rham-top-integral-is-fundamental-class-evaluation]] and the cup-product compatibility identify $Q_k$ with $\epsilon(k)\langle a\smile b\smile\ell^{n-k},[X]\rangle$, a rational number on rational classes, so $Q_k$ is a rational polarization of $P^k$. Step 2 (the full cohomology form and the high-degree transport). Write a class of degree $k\le n$ as $a=L^ru$, $b=L^rv$ with $u,v$ primitive of degree $t=k-2r$. Since $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^r\epsilon(t)$, one has $Q_k(L^ru,L^rv)=(-1)^rQ_t(u,v)$; hence the form $(-1)^rQ_k$ on the summand $L^rP^{k-2r}$ equals $Q_t$ on primitive vectors, so its Weil form is the positive form of Step 1 and distinct string summands are orthogonal (for $r<s$ the integral contains $L^{n-k+r+s}u=L^{n-t+s-r}u=0$ by primitivity of $u$). The orthogonal direct sum over $r\ge\max(0,k-n)$ is therefore a rational polarization of $H^k$. For $k>n$ transport along the rational isomorphism $L^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$, which shifts both Hodge indices by $k-n$ and preserves the difference $p-q$ and the symmetry parity, so the transported form is again a polarization with the Tate shift of the conventions. Step 3 (the projective instance). The projective cases follow from Steps 1-2 applied to the compact Kähler manifold and rational class supplied by [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]]: for a smooth closed complex submanifold of projective space take the restriction of the Fubini-Study metric, and for a general smooth projective variety use the positive closed $(1,1)$-form representing the chosen ample rational class; in both cases the class is rational and the computations of Steps 1-2 apply verbatim. Step 4 (continuous variation). For fixed $0\le k\le n$ the map $A(\omega)=L^{n-k+1}:H^k\to H^{2n-k+2}$ has constant rank along Kähler classes: its rank is $\dim H^{k-2}$, a topological constant, by the primitive decomposition of Step 2 (zero when $k<2$). Selecting a nonvanishing maximal minor of its continuous matrix near a parameter and solving the pivot equations exhibits the kernel as the graph of a continuous family of matrices; this proves continuity of the primitive kernels. Positivity for each real Kähler class is the statement of Step 1 applied to that metric; continuity is not used to infer positivity at a limiting non-Kähler class. AC accounting: the suppliers [[lem-de-rham-top-integral-is-fundamental-class-evaluation]], [[lem-first-chern-form-agrees-with-the-topological-line-class]], [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]], [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] and [[thm-kahler-identities-give-lefschetz-sl-two-and-hard-lefschetz]] state AC; the general Stokes theorem assumes only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, obtained from AC by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]].

items.title: Polarized Hodge and hard Lefschetz package for smooth projective varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the suppliers below. For a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of pure dimension $n$ with a chosen ample line class $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, its rational cohomology is finite-dimensional pure Hodge in each degree, functorial for pullback along holomorphic maps of the analytifications. Cup product has Hodge type $(0,0)$ and $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$. For $0\le k\le n$ the hard-Lefschetz maps $\ell^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ are rational isomorphisms, and for $k>n$ so are their inverses $\ell^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$; the rational primitive summands satisfy the Hodge-Riemann positivity of [[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], and the sign-adjusted full cohomology pairing is a rational polarization. Rational Hodge substructures split orthogonally. The same absolute positivity and hard-Lefschetz statements hold for real Kähler classes, and primitive kernels vary continuously along Kähler families. Rational splittings and isomorphisms persist after extension to any characteristic-zero field. This package does not supply weak hyperplane Lefschetz, relative hard Lefschetz, singular intersection-cohomology purity, or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: assemble the analytification, the compact Kähler Hodge theorem and the absolute Lefschetz package on the resulting compact Kähler manifold; source: Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.2.1), printed p. 27 (compact Kähler, 'par exemple projective lisse'), with Schnell, Class 18, Theorems 18.5, 18.13-18.15. Step 1 (Hodge structure and Hodge type). By [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]] the analytification $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a compact Kähler manifold and the class $\ell$ is the real image of an integral class represented by a positive closed $(1,1)$-form. The compact Kähler Hodge theorem [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] gives the finite-dimensional Hodge decomposition of each $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ and the functoriality and cup-product compatibility for holomorphic maps, while [[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]] supplies the rational structure and its scalar extensions; the class $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$ by the positive closed $(1,1)$-form clause of [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]]. Step 2 (hard Lefschetz and polarization). [[thm-kahler-identities-give-lefschetz-sl-two-and-hard-lefschetz]] provides the rational hard-Lefschetz isomorphisms and primitive decomposition in degrees $\le n$, and [[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]] provides the primitive Hodge-Riemann positivity, the sign-adjusted full-cohomology polarization (including the transport for $k>n$) and the continuous variation of primitive kernels along Kähler families. [[lem-polarized-hodge-structures-have-orthogonal-semisimple-substructures]] then splits every rational sub-Hodge structure orthogonally. Both the splitting matrices and the Lefschetz matrices are rational, so they persist under extension to any characteristic-zero field, as proved in the two suppliers. Every conclusion is absolute in the stated degree; no relative, weak-Lefschetz, intersection-cohomology or local-system assertion is used.

items.title: Primitive one-forms and the Weil star sign
items.statement: With the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]: on the oriented Euclidean two-plane with positively oriented orthonormal basis $e,f$, Kähler form $\omega=e\wedge f$ and compatible complex structure with $Je=f$, the type-$(1,0)$ form $u=e+if$ is primitive and satisfies $*u=-iu$. Its positive norm density is $u\wedge*\bar u=2\,e\wedge f$.
items.strategy: Choice-free finite-dimensional linear algebra; source: Schnell, Class 17, the $n=1$ case of the proof of Weil's identity and the two-plane table (printed pp. 3-4), and Schnell, Class 18, Theorem 18.15. Step 1 (primitivity and the star). The adjoint $\Lambda$ lowers degree by two, so $\Lambda u=0$ and $u$ is primitive; equivalently $L^{n-k+1}u=L^{1}u=0$ for $n=k=1$. The complementary-basis formula [[thm-hodge-star-exists-uniquely-and-has-the-orthonormal-basis-formula]] gives $*e=f$ and $*f=-e$, hence $*u=*e+i\,*f=f-ie=-i(e+if)=-iu$; this is the primitive-star formula of [[lem-hermitian-exterior-lefschetz-decomposition-and-weil-star-identity]] with $n=k=1$, $(p,q)=(1,0)$, namely $*u=\epsilon(1)i^{q-p}L^{0}u/(0)!=-iu$. Step 2 (the norm density). Since $\bar u=e-if$ is primitive of type $(0,1)$, the same formula gives $*\bar u=i\bar u$; and $u\wedge\bar u=(e+if)\wedge(e-if)=-2i\,e\wedge f$. Hence $u\wedge*\bar u=i\,u\wedge\bar u=2\,e\wedge f$, which is positive for the prescribed orientation. The verification consumes only the choice-free pointwise suppliers.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the verification is a finite-dimensional computation on a two-plane and consumes only the choice-free pointwise suppliers.

items.title: The finite von Neumann ordinals, and $\omega$ as the least limit ordinal
items.statement: With $0=\varnothing$ and $\sigma(n)=n\cup\{n\}$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]) and the ordinals of [[def-ordinal]]: (i) $0,1,2,3$ are ordinals, $1=\{0\}$, $2=\{0,1\}$, $3=\{0,1,2\}=2\cup\{2\}=2^{+}$, and for each $k\le 3$ the set $k$ is exactly the set of ordinals below $k$, so $k=\{\xi:\xi<k\}$; (ii) $\omega=\mathbb{N}$ is an ordinal, $\omega$ is a limit ordinal, $\omega=\bigcup\omega$, and every element of $\omega$ is $0$ or a successor, so no element of $\omega$ is a limit ordinal; (iii) $\omega$ is the least limit ordinal: $\omega\le\gamma$ for every limit ordinal $\gamma$ ([[def-limit-ordinal]], [[lem-omega-least-limit-ordinal]]). No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: For (i), expand the four sets and check the definition of an ordinal directly: each element of $k$ is a subset of $k$ for $k\le3$ (transitivity), and membership on $k$ is irreflexive, transitive, trichotomous and has a least element in every nonempty subset, because membership is the usual order on the natural numbers ([[lem-omega-least-limit-ordinal]] claim (i)) and a nonempty finite subset of $\mathbb{N}$ has a least element (claim (i) plus [[lem-nat-transitive-irreflexive]] for the elements). Identify $3=2\cup\{2\}=2^{+}$. For (ii) and (iii), cite claims (ii)-(iv) of [[lem-omega-least-limit-ordinal]]: $\omega$ is an ordinal, it is a limit ordinal, every $\alpha\in\omega$ is $0$ or a successor, and $\omega\le\gamma$ for every limit ordinal. The identity $\omega=\bigcup\omega$ is then the union characterisation in [[def-limit-ordinal]] applied at $\alpha=\omega$ (a nonzero ordinal is a limit ordinal if and only if $\alpha=\bigcup\alpha$), together with $\bigcup\omega\subseteq\omega$ from transitivity. No step selects from a family of sets.

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 4 (Ordinals), Lemmas 4.17-4.23; Section 5 opening (successors)

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)
references.locator: Section 3, Theorems 3.1-3.3 and the successor/limit discussion

items.title: A set of ordinals that is not an ordinal: $\{0,1,\omega\}$
items.statement: **FALSE.** Every set of ordinals ([[def-ordinal]]) is itself an ordinal, since membership well-orders any such set. Witness: $A=\{0,1,\omega\}$ is a set whose members are ordinals and on which $\in$ is a strict well-order, but $A$ is not transitive: $2\in\omega\in A$ while $2\notin A$, so $A$ is not an ordinal.
items.strategy:
First check that membership restricted to $A$ is a strict well-order: irreflexivity is [[lem-ordinal-basics]] claim (b), transitivity of the relation on $A$ is immediate for the only two-step chain $0\in1\in\omega$ together with $0\in\omega$, trichotomy is [[lem-ordinal-trichotomy]], and every nonempty subset of $A$ has an $\in$-least element by the second part of [[lem-ordinal-trichotomy]], a set of ordinals being well ordered by membership. Then check transitivity of the set $A$: $\omega$ is an ordinal ([[lem-omega-least-limit-ordinal]]), $2\in\omega$ because $2$ is a natural number, but $2
otin A$ since $2
e0$, $2
e1$ and $2
e\omega$ (the last because $\omega$ is a limit ordinal while $2$ is a successor, [[def-limit-ordinal]]). Hence $A$ is not transitive and therefore not an ordinal; the two clauses of [[def-ordinal]] are genuinely independent, and the well-ordering clause alone does not suffice.

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 4 (Ordinals), Definition 4.3 and Exercise 4.1 (transitivity)

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)
references.locator: Section 3 (an ordinal is a transitive set well ordered by membership)

items.title: Lexicographic orders: $\{0,1\}\times\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$
items.statement: Order pairs of natural numbers lexicographically: $(m,n)\prec(m',n')$ if and only if $m<m'$, or $m=m'$ and $n<n'$. Then (i) $W=\{0,1\}\times\mathbb{N}$ is well ordered by $\prec$, its initial segment below $(1,0)$ is exactly $\{0\}\times\mathbb{N}$, and $n\mapsto(0,n)$ is an order isomorphism $(\mathbb{N},<)\to(W_{<(1,0)},\prec)$; consequently $\mathbb{N}$ is order isomorphic to a proper initial segment of $W$ and not to $W$, by the mutual exclusivity in [[lem-well-order-comparability]], the unique witness being $(1,0)$; (ii) $\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$ is well ordered by $\prec$; (iii) if $F$ is the collapsing isomorphism of [[thm-mostowski-collapse]] for $W$, then $F(0,n)=n$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $F(1,0)=\omega$, so the order type of $W$ is an ordinal to which $\omega$ belongs. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: For (i), let $S\subseteq W$ be nonempty; if $S$ meets $\{0\}\times\mathbb{N}$ let $n_0$ be the least $n$ with $(0,n)\in S$ ([[thm-well-ordering-principle]]), and $(0,n_0)$ is the least element of $S$ because every $(0,n)\prec(1,k)$; otherwise $S\subseteq\{1\}\times\mathbb{N}$ and the same argument in the second coordinate applies. Every element below $(1,0)$ is of the form $(0,n)$, and $(0,n)\prec(0,m)\iff n<m$, so $n\mapsto(0,n)$ is an order isomorphism onto $W_{<(1,0)}$; this is the alternative (ii) of [[lem-well-order-comparability]] for the pair $(\mathbb{N},<)$, $W$, with witness $(1,0)$, and mutual exclusivity rules out an isomorphism $\mathbb{N}\to W$. For (ii), given nonempty $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$ let $m$ be the least first coordinate occurring in $S$ and then $k$ the least $n$ with $(m,n)\in S$ ([[thm-well-ordering-principle]]); no member of $S$ has first coordinate below $m$ and none with first coordinate $m$ has second coordinate below $k$, so $(m,k)$ is the $\prec$-least member of $S$. For (iii), the recursion $F(x)=\{F(y):y\prec x\}$ gives $F(0,n)=n$ by induction on $n$ (the predecessors of $(0,n)$ are exactly the $(0,j)$ with $j<n$, [[def-initial-segment]]), hence $F(1,0)=\{F(0,n):n\in\mathbb{N}\}=\omega$ by the defining equation and the identification of $\mathbb{N}$ with $\omega$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]); since $\mathrm{ot}(W)=\{F(x):x\in W\}$ ([[thm-mostowski-collapse]]), $\omega$ is a member of the order type of $W$.

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 5, Exercise 5.9 (ordinal product is the lexicographic order on $\alpha\times\beta$)
