items.title: The one-point extension of a well-order, and $\omega$ with a new top element
items.statement: Let $(V,<)$ be a well-order and let $\infty\notin V$; put $W=V\cup\{\infty\}$ and define $x\prec y$ if and only if $x,y\in V$ and $x<y$, or $x\in V$ and $y=\infty$. Then (i) $W$ is a well-order, $W_{<\infty}=V$, and $V$ is order isomorphic to the proper initial segment $W_{<\infty}$, so in [[lem-well-order-comparability]] applied to $(V,<)$ and $(W,\prec)$ it is alternative (ii) that holds, with the unique witness $b=\infty$; (ii) for $V=\mathbb{N}=\omega$ the extension is equinumerous with $\omega$ ([[def-equinumerous]]) but is not order isomorphic to $(\omega,<)$: the extension has a greatest element and $\omega$ does not; (iii) the collapsing map of [[thm-mostowski-collapse]] carries this extension of $\omega$ to an order isomorphism onto the ordinal $\omega^{+}=\omega\cup\{\omega\}$, so its order type is $\omega^{+}$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: For (i), let $S\subseteq W$ be nonempty: if $S$ meets $V$ then the least element of $S\cap V$ is the $\prec$-least element of $S$, since every member of $V$ precedes $\infty$; otherwise $S=\{\infty\}$. Every member of $V$ is below $\infty$ and no other element is, so $W_{<\infty}=V$, and the identity is an order isomorphism $V\to W_{<\infty}$; the alternatives of [[lem-well-order-comparability]] are mutually exclusive, so alternative (i) fails and the witness in (ii) is unique. For (ii) with $V=\omega$, the map sending $\infty$ to $0$ and $n$ to $\sigma(n)$ is a bijection $W\to\omega$, because $\sigma$ is injective and its image is exactly the nonzero natural numbers ([[thm-omega-is-peano-system]], [[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]); so $W\approx\omega$. An order isomorphism preserves the property of being a greatest element, and $\infty$ is greatest in $W$, while $\omega$ has no greatest element, since $n<\sigma(n)\in\omega$ for every $n$. For (iii), the collapse satisfies $F(n)=n$ for $n\in\omega$ by induction, hence $F(\infty)=\{F(n):n\in\omega\}=\omega$, and $\mathrm{ot}(W)=\{F(x):x\in W\}=\omega\cup\{\omega\}=\omega^{+}$, an ordinal by [[lem-ordinal-basics]] claim (c).

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 4, Lemmas 4.17-4.19 (successor ordinals); Section 5, Example $1+\omega=\omega<\omega+1$

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)
references.locator: Section 3 (successor ordinals and $\omega$); Section 5 (ordering $1+\omega<\omega+1$)

items.title: The lexicographic order on $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ is not a well-order
items.statement: **FALSE.** The lexicographic order $\prec$ on $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$, defined by $(a,b)\prec(c,d)$ if and only if $a<c$, or $a=c$ and $b<d$ ([[def-int-order]]), is a well-order ([[def-well-order]]). It is a total order, being the lexicographic order of two total orders, but the nonempty subset $\{0\}\times\mathbb{Z}$ has no $\prec$-least element: for every integer $n$ the element $(0,n-1)$ is already in the subset and satisfies $(0,n-1)\prec(0,n)$. So this total order is not a well-order.
items.strategy:
Totality: for distinct pairs $(a,b)
e(c,d)$, either $a
e c$ and the total order of $\mathbb{Z}$ decides, or $a=c$ and $b
e d$ and the total order of $\mathbb{Z}$ decides ([[thm-int-ordered-ring]]). Then exhibit the nonempty subset $\{0\}	imes\mathbb{Z}$: for each $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ the integer $n-1$ exists in $\mathbb{Z}$ (closure under subtraction, [[thm-int-comm-ring]]) with $n-1<n$ and $0=0$, so $(0,n-1)\prec(0,n)$ lies in the subset and is strictly below $(0,n)$; hence no member is least, the subset has no least element, and [[def-well-order]] fails. The same argument shows the lexicographic order on any product one of whose factors is not well ordered fails to be a well-order, by the same one-column witness.

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 5, Exercise 5.9 and the remark that lexicographic orders on $\alpha\times\beta$ are well-orders only for ordinals $\alpha,\beta$

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)
references.locator: Section 5 (lexicographic products of well-orders versus arbitrary linear orders)

items.title: An explicit well-ordering of the integers: $0\prec1\prec-1\prec2\prec-2\prec\cdots$
items.statement: On $\mathbb{Z}$ define $a\prec b$ if and only if $|a|<|b|$, or $|a|=|b|$, $a\ne b$ and $0<a$ ([[def-abs-value]], [[def-int-order]]); explicitly $0\prec1\prec-1\prec2\prec-2\prec\cdots$. Then $\prec$ is a well-order of $\mathbb{Z}$: every nonempty $S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ has a $\prec$-least element, namely the unique $s\in S$ attaining the least element of $\{|s|:s\in S\}\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ with the positive one preferred, and the initial segment below $0$ is empty; for $a\ne0$ the initial segment below $a$ consists of $0$ and of every $\pm n$ with $1\le n<|a|$ together with $-a$ when $a<0$. The usual order of $\mathbb{Z}$ is not a well-order, so this is a different well-order of the same set; the order is given by an explicit formula and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
The relation is a strict total order: it compares the naturals $|a|$ first, with the tie $|a|=|b|$, $a
e b$ settled by putting the positive element first, and both keys are decided by the linear order of $\mathbb{N}$ ([[def-nat-order]], [[thm-nat-linear-order]]; [[lem-int-abs-properties]]). For the least-element property let $S
e\emptyset$; the set $M=\{|s|:s\in S\}$ is a nonempty subset of $\mathbb{N}$ and has a least element $m$ ([[thm-well-ordering-principle]]). If $m=0$ then $0\in S$, and $0$ is least because every other member has positive absolute value. If $m>0$ then some $s\in S$ has $|s|=m$, and $|s|=m$ means $s=m$ or $s=-m$ ([[lem-int-abs-properties]]); if $m\in S$ then $m\prec s$ for every other $s\in S$, since $|s|\ge m$ and $|s|=m$, $s
e m$ forces $s=-m$; otherwise $-m\in S$ and the same argument shows $-m$ is $\prec$-least. Because all members of $S$ have $|s|\ge m$, no member is missed. The initial segments are computed from [[def-initial-segment]] and the definition of $\prec$: $W_{<0}=\varnothing$, $W_{<1}=\{0\}$, $W_{<-1}=\{0,1\}$, $W_{<2}=\{0,1,-1\}$, and for $a
e0$ in general $W_{<a}=\{0\}\cup\{\pm n:1\le n<|a|\}$, with $-a$ added when $a<0$. The relation is given by one explicit formula on $\mathbb{Z}$, so nothing is selected.

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 3 (wellorderings; the remark that $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{R}$ with their usual orders are not wellordered)

items.title: The shift $x\mapsto x+1$ is a nonidentity order automorphism of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$
items.statement: **FALSE.** Each of claims (a) and (c) of [[lem-well-order-rigid]] holds for every total order, i.e. totality in place of well-ordering suffices. Witness: on $\mathbb{Z}$ with its usual order ([[def-int-order]]) the shift $\sigma(x)=x+1$ is an order isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ ([[def-order-isomorphism]]) with $\sigma(x)\ne x$ for every $x$, so the identity is not the only order automorphism; and $x\mapsto x-1$ is strictly increasing while $x-1<x$ for every $x$, so a strictly increasing self-map need not satisfy $a\le f(a)$.
items.strategy: Verify the counterexample directly. The map $\sigma(x)=x+1$ is a bijection of $\mathbb{Z}$ with inverse $x\mapsto x-1$, and it preserves and reflects the order: $x<y$ if and only if $x+1<y+1$, since $x+1<y+1\iff0<y-x$ ([[thm-int-ordered-ring]], [[def-int-order]]); so $\sigma$ is an order isomorphism onto $\mathbb{Z}$ by [[def-order-isomorphism]] and it is not the identity because $\sigma(0)=1\ne0$. Likewise $x\mapsto x-1$ is strictly increasing and moves every point down, so claim (a) of [[lem-well-order-rigid]] fails for this total order. The proof of claim (a) uses the least-element property once, on $\{a:f(a)<a\}$; $\mathbb{Z}$ has no least element and the set of downward-moved points has no minimal member, which is exactly where the well-order hypothesis enters.

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 3, Lemmas 3.2-3.3 (rigidity of wellorderings) and the surrounding discussion

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)
references.locator: Section 3 (order automorphisms of well ordered sets); Section 5 ($1+\omega<\omega+1$)

items.title: The Mostowski collapse of a finite chain computes its order type
items.statement: Let $W=\{a,b,c,d\}$ carry the well-order $d\prec a\prec b\prec c$ ([[def-well-order]]). The collapsing map $F(x)=\{F(y):y\prec x\}$ of [[thm-mostowski-collapse]] then has $F(d)=\varnothing=0$, $F(a)=\{0\}=1$, $F(b)=\{0,1\}=2$ and $F(c)=\{0,1,2\}=3$, so $F$ is the order isomorphism of $W$ onto the ordinal $4=\{0,1,2,3\}$ and the order type of $W$ is $4$. Any function $F'$ on $W$ with $F'(x)=\{F'(y):y\prec x\}$ for all $x\in W$ equals $F$, by the uniqueness in [[thm-mostowski-collapse]].
items.strategy: Compute the four values in order $d,a,b,c$ using the defining equation and $W_{<d}=\varnothing$, $W_{<a}=\{d\}$, $W_{<b}=\{d,a\}$, $W_{<c}=\{d,a,b\}$ ([[def-initial-segment]]): each value is the set of previous values, and the finite von Neumann numerals are $0=\varnothing$, $1=\{0\}$, $2=\{0,1\}$ and $3=\{0,1,2\}$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), all ordinals by [[lem-ordinal-basics]] claim (c) applied twice from $0$. The image of $F$ is $4=\{0,1,2,3\}$, an ordinal, and $x\prec y\iff F(x)\in F(y)$ holds by the computation, so $F$ is an order isomorphism onto $4$; uniqueness is the uniqueness clause of [[thm-mostowski-collapse]], which does not require inspecting another isomorphism.

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 4, Lemma 4.15 and Definition 4.16 (every wellordering is isomorphic to a unique ordinal) and Exercise 4.12

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)
references.locator: Section 6, Corollaries 6.1-6.2 (Mostowski collapse, order type)

items.title: The collapsing recursion has no solution on $(\mathbb{Z},<)$
items.statement: **FALSE.** The recursive equation $F(a)=\{F(b):b<a\}$ has a solution for every total order, so the theorem schema [[thm-transfinite-recursion]] and its corollary [[thm-mostowski-collapse]] need only a linear order. Witness: on $(\mathbb{Z},<)$ ([[def-int-order]]) there is no function $F$ with $F(a)=\{F(b):b<a\}$ for every $a\in\mathbb{Z}$; so the least-element hypothesis cannot be weakened to totality. In ZF with Foundation ([[def-axiom-of-foundation]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-replacement]]) the equation is inconsistent, and the failure is exactly the infinite descending sequence $-1>-2>-3>\cdots$.
items.strategy: Argue by contradiction. Suppose $F$ satisfies $F(a)=\{F(b):b<a\}$ for every integer $a$; then for $a<b$ one has $F(a)\in\{F(b'):b'<b\}=F(b)$. The composition $n\mapsto F(-(n+1))$ is a class function of $n$ on $\omega$ (using the embedding of the naturals in $\mathbb{Z}$ and additive inverses, [[lem-nat-embeds-int]], [[thm-int-ordered-ring]]), so Replacement applied to it makes $S=\{F(-(n+1)):n\in\omega\}$ a set. Writing $x_n=F(-(n+1))$ we have $x_{n+1}\in x_n$ for every $n$. $S$ is nonempty, so Foundation applied to $S$, a set, produces $x\in S$ with $x\cap S=\varnothing$; writing $x=x_m$ we get $x_{m+1}\in x_m\cap S$, a contradiction. Hence no such $F$ exists: with only totality, the recursion has no solution, while [[thm-mostowski-collapse]] supplies one for every well-order precisely because the least element of each complementary set is used to run the recursion on a set and not on a proper class. The argument uses only Foundation, Replacement and the integer order; no choice principle is used.

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 6 (wellfounded relations) and Section 7 ($V_\alpha$ and rank); Exercise 2.5 (no finite $\in$-cycles)

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)
references.locator: Section 4, Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 6.4 (rank functions exist exactly for well-founded relations)

items.title: The Hartogs number of a finite set is its successor ordinal
items.statement: Let $A\approx n$ for some natural number $n$ ([[def-equinumerous]], [[def-natural-numbers]]). Then the Hartogs number $\aleph(A)$ of [[thm-hartogs]] equals $n^{+}=n\cup\{n\}=\{0,1,\dots,n\}$: the set of order types of well-orders of subsets of $A$ is exactly the set of ordinals $\alpha$ with $\alpha\le n$, and $n^{+}$ is the least ordinal that does not inject into $A$. In particular the cardinality of $A$ determines its Hartogs number, and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: First show $\aleph(A)=\{\alpha:\alpha\ \text{injects into}\ A\}$. If $\alpha=\mathrm{ot}(S,R)$ for $S\subseteq A$ then the order isomorphism $\alpha\to S$ is an injection, giving $\alpha\preceq A$ ([[thm-hartogs]], [[thm-mostowski-collapse]]); conversely, given an injection $j:\alpha\to A$, put $S=j[\alpha]$ and $R=\{(j(\xi),j(\eta)):\xi\in\eta\}$, so that $j$ is an order isomorphism $(\alpha,\in)\to(S,R)$, $R$ well-orders $S$ and $\mathrm{ot}(S,R)=\alpha$ by uniqueness of order type. So $\aleph(A)=\{\alpha:\alpha\preceq A\}=\{\alpha:\alpha\preceq n\}$, using the bijection $A\to n$ to transport injections. Next, $\alpha\preceq n$ if and only if $\alpha\le n$: the inclusion $\alpha\subseteq n$ gives the backward direction ([[lem-ordinal-basics]] claim (f)); for the forward direction suppose $n\in\alpha$; then $n\subseteq\alpha$ by transitivity, so $n\preceq\alpha$, and with $\alpha\preceq n$ Schroeder-Bernstein ([[thm-schroder-bernstein]]) gives $n\approx\alpha$. If $\alpha\ge\omega$ then $\omega\preceq\alpha\preceq n$ and $n\preceq\omega$ give $\omega\approx n$, contradicting [[lem-pigeonhole]] claim 4; if $\alpha<\omega$ then $\alpha$ is a natural number and claim 3 forces $\alpha=n$. Hence $\alpha\le n$ in both cases. Therefore $\aleph(A)=\{\alpha:\alpha\le n\}=\{0,1,\dots,n\}=n^{+}$, and $n^{+}$ indeed does not inject into $A$, consistent with the defining property of $\aleph(A)$ in [[thm-hartogs]].

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 9, Theorem 9.6 (Hartogs' theorem) and Definition 9.4 (cardinals)

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)

items.title: The Hartogs number of $\omega$ is a limit ordinal above $\omega$
items.statement: Let $H=\aleph(\omega)$ be the least ordinal that admits no injection into $\omega$ ([[thm-hartogs]]). Then $H$ is a limit ordinal ([[def-limit-ordinal]]) with $\omega\in H$, so $\omega<H$ and $H$ is uncountable ([[def-countable]]); explicitly $H=\{\alpha:\alpha\ \text{is at most countable}\}$ is the set of countable ordinals, and $H$ is not the successor of any ordinal. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: As in the finite case, $\aleph(\omega)=\{\alpha:\alpha\preceq\omega\}$, because an injection $\alpha\to\omega$ transports membership to a well-order of its image with order type $\alpha$ and conversely an order type anti-embeds into $\omega$ ([[thm-hartogs]], [[thm-mostowski-collapse]]). An ordinal $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha\preceq\omega$ exactly when it is at most countable: every subset of $\omega$ is at most countable ([[lem-subset-of-countable]]) and an at most countable set embeds in $\omega$, while conversely $\alpha\preceq\omega$ presents $\alpha$ as equinumerous with a subset of $\omega$. The identity embeds $\omega$ into $\omega$, so $\omega\in H$ and $H\ne0$. $H$ is not a successor: if $H=\alpha^{+}$ then $\alpha\in H$, so there is an injection $j:\alpha\to\omega$, and the map extending $j$ by $\alpha\mapsto0$ and $\beta\mapsto\sigma(j(\beta))$ is an injection $\alpha^{+}\to\omega$ ([[thm-omega-is-peano-system]], [[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]), so $H=\alpha^{+}$ would inject into $\omega$, against the defining property of $H$. Hence $H$ is a nonzero ordinal that is not a successor, that is a limit ordinal, with $\omega\in H$. Uncountability is the defining property read against [[def-countable]].

references.title: A. Marks, Set Theory (Berkeley lecture notes, 2026)
references.locator: Section 9, Theorem 9.6 and the sentence identifying $\omega_1$ as the least uncountable ordinal; Section 10 (cofinality)

references.title: J. T. Moore, MATH 6870: Set Theory (Cornell lecture notes)
references.locator: Section 6, Theorem 6.6 (Hartog ordinal); Section 7 (countability of a set means cardinality at most $\omega$)

items.title: Transfinite induction fails if the least element is exempted from the hypothesis
items.statement:
**FALSE.** The hypothesis of [[thm-transfinite-induction]] may be checked only at elements other than the least element of the well-order: for a well-order $W$ with least element $m$, if $W_{<a}\subseteq S$ implies $a\in S$ for every $a
e m$, then $S=W$. Witness: $W=\omega$ with its usual order and $S=\omega\setminus\{0\}$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]); the implication holds at every $a
e0$ vacuously, and it fails at $a=0$, where $W_{<0}=\varnothing\subseteq S$ while $0
otin S$. Hence $S
e W$.
items.strategy:
Verify the two halves. For $a
e0$ in $\omega$ we have $0<a$, so $0\in W_{<a}$ while $0
otin S$; hence $W_{<a}\subseteq S$ is false and the implication $W_{<a}\subseteq S\Rightarrow a\in S$ holds vacuously ([[def-initial-segment]], [[lem-nat-order-is-membership]] gives $W_{<a}=a=\{m:m<a\}$ and $0\in a$ for $a
e0$). At $a=0$ the initial segment $W_{<0}=\varnothing$ is contained in $S$, but $0
otin S$, so the hypothesis of [[thm-transfinite-induction]] fails exactly at the least element. Therefore $S
otin\{W\}$ and the conclusion of transfinite induction is false for this $S$, even though the hypothesis holds at every element except the least. The result explains why the theorem is stated with the single hypothesis at every $a$ and why the least element needs no separate base case: applied there, the hypothesis itself is the base case.

references.locator: Section 5, Theorem 5.1 (three-case transfinite induction) and Exercise 5.2 (single-hypothesis form)

items.title: Proper continuous maps of topological spaces
items.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces ([[def-topological-space]]) and let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous ([[def-continuous-map-top]]). Then $f$ is **proper** when for every compact subset $K\subseteq Y$ ([[def-compact-space]]) its preimage $f^{-1}(K)$ is a compact subset of $X$. Compactness of subsets is the intrinsic condition of [[def-compact-space]], namely compactness of the subspace $f^{-1}(K)$ with the subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]); by [[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]] it is equivalent to the ambient reading, so a subset is compact exactly when every cover by open subsets of the ambient space has a finite subcover, and the two readings are used interchangeably below without further comment. This is the notion of properness used throughout the analytic six-operation development on this page, where the spaces involved are locally compact Hausdorff ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). The stability properties consumed by the later items — closed inclusions are proper, composites of proper maps are proper, properness is preserved by base change along a continuous map into a Hausdorff space, and fibres and closed subspaces of a proper map inherit properness — are proved in the lemma `lem-proper-continuous-map-stability` on this page. The definition involves no choice principle: it quantifies over compact subsets and preimages only.

items.title: Basic stability of proper continuous maps
items.statement: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be topological spaces ([[def-topological-space]]), with properness as in [[def-proper-continuous-map]]. 1. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion of a closed subset, then $i$ is proper. 2. If $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ are proper continuous maps, then the composite $gf:X\to Z$ is proper. 3. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, $Y$ is Hausdorff ([[def-hausdorff-space]]) and $u:Y'\to Y$ is continuous, then the pullback $$f':X\times_YY'\longrightarrow Y',\qquad X\times_YY'=\{(x,y')\in X\times Y': f(x)=u(y')\},$$ the subset carrying the subspace topology of the product ([[def-product-topology]], [[def-subspace-topology-top]]), is proper. 4. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, then every fibre $f^{-1}(y)$ is a compact subset of $X$. 5. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper and $S\subseteq X$ is closed, then the restriction $f|_S:S\to Y$ is proper. 6. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper and $Y$ is locally compact Hausdorff ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), then $f$ is a closed map: the image of every closed subset of $X$ is closed in $Y$. These are the stability properties consumed by the closed-support functor $f_!$ on this page; no choice principle is used in any of them.

items.title: Derived tensor–Hom and inverse/direct image for field sheaves
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and let $k$ be a field. Inverse image of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) is exact and $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, where $Rf_*$ is computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements ([[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]], [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]). For bounded complexes $A,B$ ([[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]) the derived tensor over $k$ is their signed total tensor ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]), and for bounded $A$ and bounded-below $B$ the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom(A,B)$ is computed by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I_B)$ in a $k$-linear bounded-below injective model $B\to I_B$ ([[def-sheaf-hom]], [[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]). Flasque $k$-sheaves ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) are acyclic for sections on every open set ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The tensor-Hom adjunction and the dg associativity, evaluation and symmetry identities are natural. No bounded-constructibility claim for the internal Hom is made here; that requires the local geometric supplier of the later constructible items.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: read the ordinary operations off stalks, construct the signed total tensor and the injective Hom model, prove flasque acyclicity from the flasque-kernel lifting theorem, and finish with the chain-Hom adjunction. Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS1 pp. 339-341 (injective models in $D^+$ and the basic properties of $f_!$) and Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, SS12 (Definition 12.1, Lemma 12.2, Lemma 12.3, Lemma 12.5). Step 1 (inverse and direct image). The stalk of $f^{-1}G$ at $x$ is $G_{f(x)}$ ([[lem-stalk-inverse-image-sheaf]]), so $f^*=f^{-1}$ is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms; the inverse/direct-image adjunction ([[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]]) is $k$-linear, and for injective $I$ on $X$ the functor $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(-,f_*I)$ is naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*(-),I)$, so $f_*I$ is injective and the chain-Hom adjunction gives $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ on $D^+$. Step 2 (tensor). Define $F\otimes_kG$ by sheafifying the sectionwise tensor presheaf; its stalks are $F_x\otimes_kG_x$ ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) because filtered colimits commute with finite tensor expressions. All $k$-vector spaces are flat, so tensoring is stalk-exact, and a bounded complex is K-flat: filter the finite-column total tensor against an acyclic complex by $A$-degree and use that each column is acyclic. Hence the signed total tensor of bounded representatives computes $A\otimes^L_kB$ independently of the representatives. Step 3 (internal Hom). For a bounded-below injective replacement $B\to I_B$ and a bounded representative $A$, put $R\mathcal Hom(A,B)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I_B)$ with $d(\varphi)=d_I\varphi-(-1)^n\varphi d_A$; each $\mathcal Hom(A^p,I^q)$ is injective because it is right adjoint to the exact functor $-\otimes A^p$, the total complex is bounded below and termwise injective, and replacing $A$ or $I_B$ changes it only by a quasi-isomorphism (test on the open extensions $j_U!$ and use stalk exactness). This is the actual internal derived Hom, not a sectionwise Hom of stalks. Step 4 (flasque acyclicity). An injective $k$-sheaf is flasque since $\operatorname{Hom}(j_U!k_U,I)=I(U)$ and injectivity extends sections along $j_U!k_U\to j_V!k_V$ for $U\subset V$. Embed a flasque $F$ into an injective $I$; the flasque-kernel lifting theorem ([[lem-flasque-kernel-lifts-quotient-sections]]) makes the quotient flasque with $I(U)\to Q(U)$ onto for every open $U$, so the long exact sequence gives $H^1(U,F)=0$ and $H^{n+1}(U,F)\cong H^n(U,Q)$; induction on degree proves vanishing, and for a bounded-below flasque complex the same degreewise comparison computes derived sections on each open by the ordinary section complex. Step 5 (adjunction identities). The signed chain transposition $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(C\otimes A,I)\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I))$ is an isomorphism (Koszul reordering), and since $I$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I)$ are K-injective and bounded $C$ is K-flat, $H^0$ yields tensor $\dashv$ $R\mathcal Hom$ on $D^b$ with bounded-below target; restriction to opens gives the internal version, and associativity, symmetry, evaluation and currying hold on pure tensors and hence on sheaves. No constructibility of the internal Hom is asserted; that is supplied later on this page by the geometric finite conical/cochain models and the derived incidence model, which are not prerequisites of this lemma.

items.title: Derived operations on analytic field sheaves
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be locally compact Hausdorff spaces ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) viewed as modules over the constant ring sheaf $k_X$, and form derived categories in those sheaves ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]). For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$, set $f^*=f^{-1}$ ([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) and define $f_!F$ on an open $V\subseteq Y$ to consist of the sections of $F$ on $f^{-1}(V)$ whose closed support ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]], [[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]) maps properly to $V$, properness being that of [[def-proper-continuous-map]] together with its stability lemma [[lem-proper-continuous-map-stability]]. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ are computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements. Tensor means the signed total tensor over $k$ ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) and internal derived Hom is the injective construction of [[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]] ([[def-sheaf-hom]]). Suppose the uniform all-fibre-open cohomological dimension bound of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]] holds, and choose its finite resolution $k_X\to K$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ put $K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]], [[def-c-soft-sheaf]]). For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $Y$, define the exceptional inverse-image candidate to be the sheaf complex with open sections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y^\bullet(f_!K_U,I)$. [[thm-compactly-supported-derived-pushforward-has-exceptional-inverse-image-adjoint]] proves that this candidate is a sheaf complex and is independent of the chosen resolution. Set $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_XA=R\mathcal Hom(A,\omega_X)$ when the terminal map satisfies the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. Constructible restriction is a separate geometric theorem; none of these definitions asserts a generic six-functor axiom. The prescriptions are those of Verdier's exposé: $f^*$ is the exact inverse image, $f_!$ is the sheaf of sections whose closed support is proper over the base — a presheaf by the local nature of properness, whose sheaf property on bounded-below injective inputs is proved by the exceptional-adjoint theorem recorded in `justified_by` — $Rf_*$ is derived from the direct image [[def-direct-image-sheaf]] on bounded-below injective replacements, and the terms of the chosen finite resolution are $c$-soft and hence acyclic for compact support ([[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]]). The ordinary-operations lemma also supplies the flasque acyclicity ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) used to compare resolutions. AC is used only for injective replacements; the proper-support sections, extension by zero and the exceptional candidate itself are choice-free constructions. Cohomological shifts obey $H^i(A[r])=H^{i+r}(A)$ in the convention of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].
items.strategy: This item is definitional: it fixes the categorical setting, the functors, and the exceptional candidate, and its only well-definedness obligation is the exceptional-inverse-image adjoint theorem of the next item on this page (recorded as that definition's justified_by target at authoring, not as a prerequisite of this definition). Source route: Verdier, expose 300, SS1-SS2 pp. 339-343 (definition and left exactness of $f_!$, the finite fibrewise-$c$-soft resolution $k_X\to K$, and the construction of $f^!$ from $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Y(f_!K_U,I)$), and Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves SS12 (flasque acyclicity, used by the resolution). Step 1 fixes $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ as an abelian category of module sheaves over $k_X$ and its derived category. Step 2 defines $f^*=f^{-1}$, $f_!$ by proper support of sections, $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ by bounded-below injective replacements, and recalls $\otimes_k^L$ and $R\mathcal Hom$ from the ordinary-operations lemma. Step 3 assumes the uniform all-fibre-open bound, fixes the finite resolution $k_X\to K$ of the bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolution lemma, and forms $K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ for opens $U$. Step 4 defines the exceptional inverse-image candidate by the section complexes $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Y(f_!K_U,I)$; the adjoint theorem proves this is a sheaf and independent of the choices, so the definition is well posed. Step 5 defines $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ under the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. No generic six-functor axiom, no constructible restriction and no unrestricted right adjunction is asserted here.

items.title: Exceptional inverse image as the adjoint of derived proper-support image
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound $d$ of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the proper-support functor $f_!$ of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]] is left exact, satisfies $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ on every fibre, and maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. Its exceptional inverse-image candidate $f^!$ represents the natural Hom transposition $$\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,f^!B)$$ for bounded source objects $A$ and bounded-below target objects $B$, and has lower cohomological bound $\inf(B)-d$. When the later geometric theorem proves that $f^!$ preserves the bounded constructible subcategory, this becomes the right adjunction $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ there; on that bounded constructible specialization the adjunction unit, counit and resolution comparisons satisfy the triangle, identity and cocycle laws. The proper-support evaluation constructs the counit directly. The proof constructs this adjoint from a finite fibrewise-soft resolution and generator complexes, independently of Verdier biduality; it does not infer an unrestricted $D^+$-source adjunction from the bounded-source generator argument.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS1 pp. 339-341 (left exactness, proper-support stalk formula, finite cohomological dimension, $Y$-mou resolutions) and SS2 pp. 341-343 (the resolution $k_X\to K$, the complex $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Y(f_!K_U,I)$, flasqueness and the evaluation $\gamma$); Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves SS12 (flasque acyclicity), SS16-SS18 (compact-neighbourhood continuity and ordinary proper base change as an independent check), SS21 (localization). Step 1: $f_!$ is a sheaf, left exact, equals $f_*$ for proper $f$ and extension by zero / direct image for open / closed inclusions. Step 2: the stalk map $(f_!A)_y\to\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ is injective and surjective by the compact-neighbourhood gluing lemma [[lem-sections-near-a-compact-set-are-sections-on-that-set]] and the collar argument. Step 3: for injective $A$ the fibre restrictions are $c$-soft ([[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]]), so $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ and the finite bound gives $Rf_!:D^b\to D^b$ with fibrewise-$c$-soft acyclicity. Step 4: choose the finite resolution $k_X\to K$ in degrees $0,\dots,d$, set $K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$, and form $H_K(I)(U)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Y(f_!K_U,I)$; the augmented extension-by-zero Cech complex is exact on stalks and its cycles are $f_!$-acyclic by dimension shifting past the bound $d$, so $H_K(I)$ is a flasque sheaf complex with lower bound $\inf(I)-d$. Step 5: for $E_U=j_{U!}k_U$ the complex $K_U$ resolves $E_U$ by $f_!$-acyclic terms, giving $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(E_U,H_K(I))=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Y(f_!K_U,I)$; the descending kernel recursion from [[lem-abelian-sheaves-admit-bounded-above-flat-resolutions]] builds a bounded-above generator complex $M\to A$ quasi-isomorphic and stalk-surjective over $k$, and the bounded-diagonal Hom comparison against an injective replacement of $H_K(I)$ proves $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(A,H_K(I))\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!A,I)$ for bounded $A$ and bounded-below $I$. Step 6: $H^0$ gives the Hom transposition, $f^!B:=H_K(I_B)$ is the represented adjoint, and the counit is constructed directly from $k_V\to f_*k_Q\to f_*(K|Q)$ over closed $Q$ proper over $V$; the flasque terms are $f_!$-acyclic, and on the bounded constructible specialization (after the geometric bounded-output theorem) the triangle and cocycle laws follow by inverse transposition. The bounded-source generator argument alone is not called an unrestricted adjunction.

items.title: Support localization, base change, projection and trace calculus
items.statement: Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS1.2 p. 340 (base change), SS1.5 p. 341 (compose), SS2.3 p. 342-343 (the trace $\gamma:\ f_!f^!(G)\to G$) and SS2 p. 341-342 (flasque terms); Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves SS17-SS18 (base change map and proper base change, as an independent verification of the canonical exchange) and SS21 (the localization triangle of $R\Gamma_Z$). Step 1 (closed support). Put $\Gamma_ZF=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$; it has zero stalks off $Z$, hence equals $i_*i^{-1}\Gamma_ZF$ by [[lem-sheaf-supported-on-a-closed-subset-is-a-pushforward]], and $i^!_0=i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$ is right adjoint to the exact $i_*$ and preserves injectives; the stalk exact sequence from [[lem-extension-by-zero-short-exact-sequence]] gives both localization triangles, and tensor-Hom transposition with the closed adjunction identifies $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ with $R\Gamma_ZA$ locally on every open. Step 2 (base change). For a Cartesian square, inverse image of an injective on $X$ restricts on each fibre of $f'$ to the restriction of the original injective, hence is fibrewise-$c$-soft and $f'_!$-acyclic; the fibre-stalk formula of the exceptional-adjunction theorem identifies $u^*f_!I\to f'_!v^*I$ on stalks, and applying to an injective complex proves $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$; for proper $f$ this is ordinary proper base change. Step 3 (projection). On fibres, $f^*B$ is the constant complex $B_y$ and tensoring a $c$-soft complex with a vector space stays $c$-soft, with $\Gamma_c(E\otimes V)=\Gamma_c(E)\otimes V$ for finite tensor presentations; this proves the canonical map $Rf_!A\otimes B\to Rf_!(A\otimes f^*B)$ is a stalk isomorphism and identifies it with the adjoint of the counit tensored with $\mathrm{id}$. Step 4 (composition and traces). The support definition proves $(gf)_!=g_!f_!$ (proper support over $Y$ and $Z$ agree by the two properness conditions), and applying the two support functors to an injective resolution gives the canonical composition isomorphism; the trace homomorphisms are the actual counits of the exceptional adjunction, and $\mathrm{tr}_{gf}=\mathrm{tr}_g\circ Rg_!(\mathrm{tr}_f)g^!$ follows by transposing the identity of $f^!g^!$. Step 5 (pasting). The two composites of base-change maps in a pasted square restrict a representative section to the same fibre section before deriving, and both projection composites send a pure tensor to the same pullback tensor; all identities hold in the dg resolution model. Extraordinary proper exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ is deliberately NOT claimed here: it is proved only after constructible biduality on this page, in the later duality theorem that is not a prerequisite of this lemma.

items.title: Constructible Verdier duality and complex orientation
items.statement: Assume AC and the actual finite conical/triangulation and derived-incidence-model suppliers listed below. On the analytic space $X$ of a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, constructible complexes admit the fixed-space finite models required by those suppliers. Then $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ preserve bounded constructible objects and the natural evaluation $A\to D_XD_XA$ is an isomorphism. On a smooth complex $d$-variety, the complex orientation normalizes $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$. For constructible maps for which the geometric supplier proves the stated bounded outputs, $Rf_*D_X\simeq D_YRf_!$, $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$. Proper base change has the coherent extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. The fixed-space triangulation is not an assumed globally simplicial model of $f$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS2 p. 341-343 (the candidate $f^!$ and the trace), SS3 pp. 343-345 (the duality theorem, proved on generators $A_V$ and then by descent), SS1.1-SS1.4 pp. 339-341 (localization; compact support; finite dimension); BBD, Faisceaux pervers, SS1.4.1-1.4.10 (recollement localization triangles) and SS2.1.1-2.1.7 (perversity on stratified spaces), as an independent treatment of the local intermediate-extension construction; Bernstein-Lunts, Part I SS1.6.1-1.6.3 (dualizing object and Verdier duality $Df_!=f_*D$, $f^!D=Df^*$). Step 1: dualizing transitivity $f^!\omega_Y\simeq\omega_X$ is computed on local section complexes $R\Gamma(U,f^!\omega_Y)=R\mathrm{Hom}_Y(Rf_!j_{U!}k,\omega_Y)\simeq R\mathrm{Hom}_k(R\Gamma_c(U,k),k)=R\Gamma(U,\omega_X)$, using the exceptional-adjunction Hom formula and compact-support composition, and $R\Gamma(U,D_XA)=R\mathrm{Hom}_k(R\Gamma_c(U,A),k)$; over a field the injective coefficient is $k$, so this is the signed dual cochain model with no integral Ext correction. Step 2: on an oriented real $n$-manifold the compact-support cochains of a small ball have one generator in degree $n$ normalized by the positive orientation (finite relative cellular model of the closed simplex, with excision), so $\omega_X\simeq or_X[n]$ and complex orientation trivializes $or_X$ to give $k_X[2d]$ on a smooth complex $d$-variety. Step 3: for a finite-rank local system $L$ on a smooth stratum, $D_XL\simeq L^\vee[n]$ and finite-dimensional double-dual evaluation is an isomorphism; the boundary-link induction may not assume $DD(j_!L)=j_!DD(L)$. Step 4: choose a finite regular triangulation $P$ with deleted subcomplex $L$ modelling $X$, subordinate to the constructible datum (geometric supplier); the derived-incidence supplier identifies the bounded derived category of finite face diagrams with the constructible subcategory, with injective cogenerators $I_\sigma$ given by $k$ on the closed simplex extended by zero. Step 5: compute $D_XI_\sigma=j_{\mathrm{int}\sigma!}k[\dim\sigma]$ and its inverse on a star by the finite relative cellular model of a half-line times a disk; evaluation $I_\sigma\to D_XD_XI_\sigma$ is ordinary finite-dimensional double-dual evaluation and is an isomorphism; finite injective incidence resolutions propagate this through cones, proving $A\to D_XD_XA$ for all bounded constructible $A$ and bounded constructibility of $D_X$. Step 6: after biduality, $Rf_*D_XA\simeq D_YRf_!A$ (both represent $R\mathcal Hom(Rf_!A,\omega_Y)$ with source-side $D_XA$), applying $D_Y$ gives $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and the transpositions $\operatorname{Hom}(A,D_Xf^*D_YB)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(f^*D_YB,D_XA)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!A,B)$ identify $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$ on the bounded constructible category; proper base change dualizes to $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. Pasting coherence follows from naturality of the evaluation and the sectionwise base-change maps.

items.title: Coherent six operations on analytic constructible field sheaves
items.statement: Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models below; proper maps already satisfy it. Their finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS1.2 p. 340 (base change), SS1.5 p. 341 (composition), SS5 p. 348 (submersive maps and the projection formula for a product projection); Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves SS17-SS18 (base-change map and proper base change) and SS54 (projection formula Lemma 54.2); Bernstein-Lunts, Part I SS1.8 (smooth base change and compatibility with all functors). Step 1: apply the support-and-trace lemma to the actual analytic maps; its proper-support section and injective models give ordinary exchange, the projection formula, both support-localization triangles, canonical composition, units and traces, all as section-level identities carried through the same resolution comparisons. Step 2: apply the constructible Verdier theorem to the actual finite conical/incidence models; it supplies duality, orientation and the extraordinary exchange by dualizing the canonical proper base-change map, and functoriality carries pasting and trace squares to their dual squares, while the tensor-Hom and inverse/direct-image adjunctions are the signed dg comparisons of the ordinary-operations lemma. Step 3 (product projection): tensor the finite base diagram resolution with the fibre constant-diagram resolution ([[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]]); each realized term has support a product of closed cells minus deleted faces, and its intersection with a small base star times $F$ has contractible factors, so the constant-sheaf comparison [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]] makes it section-acyclic; applying sections gives the natural finite double complex $B|_{\mathrm{star}}\otimes C^*(F;k)$ and identifies the derived image and its unit with $B\otimes C^*(F;k)$ and $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. For smooth base change of an open inclusion $j$, a local smooth chart is a product with a contractible ball, and the boundary-star section model becomes the old finite cochain model tensored with the ball cochains, whose augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by an explicit contraction. If the supplied $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper, combine this exchange with the constructed proper base-change map for $p$; compatibility with composition identifies the composite with the canonical $f$ exchange. No compactification existence theorem is inferred: the clause applies only to the stated supplied factorization. Step 4 (coefficient extension): use the geometric supplier's finite local cellular/cochain models; scalar extension is exact on vector spaces, commutes with finite sums, cohomology and finite-dimensional duals, so ordinary inverse image, finite cochain pushforward, tensor, internal Hom and the support-defined Verdier comparisons extend termwise, and the exceptional comparison follows from $f^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$; no infinite product of injective stalks is involved.

items.title: Actual analytic constructible sheaves admit coherent six operations
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts, Part I SS1.4.1-SS1.4.6 (tensor-Hom, composition, adjunctions, proper equality, open localization triangles and base change) and SS1.6-SS1.7 (dualizing object, Verdier duality for continuous maps, and smooth maps of relative dimension $d$), together with the finite resolution construction of Part I SS1.9/Appendices A and the derived-category simplicial comparison; BBD, Faisceaux pervers, SS1.4.1-1.4.10 (the recollement localization triangles giving localization and gluing), as an independent treatment. Step 1: the actual compact-support adjoint and coherent six-operation suppliers construct the functors and their adjunction units/counits, not just unrelated isomorphisms; their ordinary coherent composition, Cartesian exchange, projection/trace and localization diagrams are the asserted diagrams, including proper equality $Rf_!=Rf_*$ and the smooth local-product comparisons. All vector-space and injective constructions apply over an arbitrary field; their signed cochains use only $0$ and the units $\pm1$, so no characteristic hypothesis enters. Step 2: the actual finite conical and incidence suppliers prove bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models for the stated finite collection, so the constructed operations restrict to $D_c^b$ and their finite local cochain comparisons commute with field extension; the actual support construction for compactly supported operations is used, and no infinite tensor of injective products is formed. Step 3: the oriented stratified Verdier supplier gives its evaluation isomorphism and identifies the dualizing object on a smooth complex $d$-fold with $k[2d]$ through the positive complex orientation; its adjunction construction gives duality exchange and the stated smooth extraordinary pullback $f^!=f^*[2d]$, and all these maps use the same ordinary units/counits and orientation, so their coherence is the coherence of the actual construction. The integral orientation generator maps to the nonzero unit $1\in k$ over every field, including characteristic two.

Every remaining step is a finite-dimensional or canonical comparison and is choice-free.

items.title: Ordinary middle perverse t structure, recollement and intersection complexes
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: BBD, Faisceaux pervers, SS1.4.1-1.4.26 (recollement: Theoreme 1.4.10 constructing the glued t-structure from t-structures on an open $U$ and its closed complement, and the definitions/properties of $j_!$, $j_*$, $i^*$, $i^!$) and SS2.1.1-2.1.23 (perversity on a stratified space, the perverse t-structure of Proposition 2.1.3, the intermediate extension $j_{!*}$ of Definition 1.4.22/Corollaries 1.4.24-1.4.25, and the simple objects of Proposition 1.4.26); Bernstein-Lunts, Part I SS1.4.5 (open localization triangles) as a second treatment of the recollement input. Step 1: the six-operation supplier gives $j_!\dashv j^*\dashv Rj_*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*\dashv i^!$, full faithfulness of $i_*$ and $j_!$, $j^*i_*=0$ and the two localization triangles; defining $T^{\le0}$ by $j^*K\le0$, $i^*K\le0$ and $T^{\ge0}$ by $j^*K\ge0$, $i^!K\ge0$, orthogonality follows from $j_!j^*A\to A\to i_*i^*A$ and truncation is built through the standard octahedral completion; induction on the finite number of strata, starting from the ordinary t-structure shifted by $\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ on each smooth stratum, proves the bounded t-structure stays in $D_c^b$. Step 2: for a refinement $T\subset S$ of complex codimension $c$, ordinary pullback preserves the upper bound $-\dim_{\mathbb C}S\le-\dim_{\mathbb C}T$ and extraordinary pullback is ordinary pullback shifted by $-2c$, so the lower bound improves; both old halves lie in the refined halves and uniqueness of truncation gives equality on the old category, whence common refinement gives independence. Step 3: duality exchange $i_S^!D_XA=D_Si_S^*A$, $i_S^*D_XA=D_Si_S^!A$ together with the finite-dimensional dual $H^j(D_SK)=(H^{-j-2e}K)^\vee$ for finite-rank local systems converts the upper inequality into the lower one and conversely, over every field, since $2e$ is an integral shift; applying the same argument to $D_XA$ and Verdier biduality gives equality of the exchanged aisles. Step 4: the heart is abelian because kernel and cokernel of a heart map are the perverse cohomologies in degrees $-1$ and $0$ of its cone; define $j_{!*}L$ as the image of ${}^pH^0j_!L\to{}^pH^0Rj_*L$; its supported subobjects and quotients are removed by the intermediate-image construction using the localization triangles, and conversely any extension without boundary subobject or quotient is this image by adjunction. A subobject of $j_{!*}L$ restricts to a subobject of $L$, so for simple $L$ the intersection complex is simple; conversely a simple heart object has a nonzero restriction to a suitable open stratum which must be simple, and the no-boundary characterization identifies the object with its intermediate extension. On a fixed finite compatible stratification, finite-dimensional local systems have finite length, and induction through the two localization sequences proves finite length of the heart. Step 5: for $m<0$, $B[m]$ lies in $T^{\ge1}$ and $A$ in $T^{\le0}$, so orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$; a nonzero endomorphism of a simple object has kernel $0$ and image the whole object, hence is invertible, so its endomorphism ring is a division algebra over every field. No equivariant, semisimple or noncharacteristic input is used.

references.title: A. A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein, P. Deligne, Faisceaux pervers, Astérisque 100 (1982); §1.4 recollement t-structures and §2.1 perverse sheaves on stratified spaces

The recollement, duality-exchange, heart and finite-length arguments are otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Smooth complex pullback is exact for the middle perverse t structure
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $a:X\to Y$ be a smooth algebraic map of pure relative complex dimension $d$ between separated finite-type complex varieties, over an arbitrary coefficient field $k$. Then $a^*[d]$ is exact for the ordinary middle-perverse t structures of [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]] on $D_c^b(-;k)$, and it commutes with their truncation and cohomology functors. Complex orientation gives $a^!=a^*[2d]$. If $a$ is surjective, its normalized pullback is conservative and reflects the perverse support and cosupport inequalities. The compatible finite stratifications used are those of [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]].
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: BBD, Faisceaux pervers, SS2.1.1-2.1.23 (the perverse t-structure on stratified spaces and its behavior under open/closed restriction and smooth strata); Bernstein-Lunts, Part I SS1.7 (smooth maps of relative dimension $d$ have invertible dualizing object, locally $C[d]$, so $f^!\simeq f^*\otimes D_f\simeq f^*[d]$ up to the stated normalization) and SS1.4.3-1.4.4 (adjunctions and proper equality), as an independent treatment. Step 1 (upper aisle): on a smooth target stratum $S$ of complex dimension $e$, the nonempty smooth preimage strata have dimension $e+d$; exact inverse image gives $H^q(a^*A[d])=a^*H^{q+d}(A)$, and for $A$ in the upper middle-perverse aisle the right-hand side vanishes on these strata when $q+d>-e$, precisely when $q>-(e+d)$; local smooth product charts preserve the compatible target stratification ([[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]]), so this proves preservation of the upper aisle. Step 2 (lower aisle): the ordinary six-operation construction gives $D_Xa^*=a^!D_Y$ and complex orientation gives $a^!=a^*[2d]$; hence $D_X(a^*A[d])=a^*D_YA[d]$, and since the ordinary middle-perverse core identifies the lower aisle as the dual of the upper aisle, Step 1 proves preservation of the lower aisle too. The orientation unit is nonzero over every field, exact finite-dimensional duality is field-general, and $[2d]$ is a cohomological shift, so the argument applies over arbitrary $k$. Step 3 (truncation and reflection): applying the t-exact functor to a truncation triangle produces the unique target truncation triangle, proving commutation with perverse truncations and cohomology; if $a$ is surjective, inverse image is stalkwise conservative and reflects ordinary cohomological vanishings, and the same dimension calculation applied to support and dual support reflects both perverse inequalities.

title: Analytic Derived Six Operations And Duality Examples

items.title: Dualizing and support shifts on the complex line
items.statement: With the conventions of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]] and coefficient field $k$: on the complex line $\mathbb C$ (an oriented smooth complex 1-fold) the dualizing object is $\omega_{\mathbb C}=k_{\mathbb C}[2]$. For the closed inclusion $i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$ one has $i^!k_{\mathbb C}=k[-2]$ and $i^!\omega_{\mathbb C}=k$. The example consumes the AC-assumed Verdier supplier; the displayed computation itself is choice-free.
items.strategy: Assume the conventions of the Verdier supplier (including AC). Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS4-SS5 pp. 345-348 (local orientation and the $\omega$ normalization for a real $n$-manifold), SS1.1 p. 339-340 (for a map to a point, $f_!$ is compactly supported sections), and Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves SS21 (the localization triangle $R\Gamma_Z\to R\Gamma\to R\Gamma_U$ identifying closed-support cohomology with relative cohomology of the pair). Step 1: a positively complex-oriented disk $D\subset\mathbb C$ has compact-support cochain complex with a single cohomology generator in degree $2$ over $k$, so the dualizing complex of the smooth complex $1$-fold is $k_{\mathbb C}[2]$ by the orientation normalization $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$ at $d=1$. Step 2: by [[lem-analytic-six-operation-support-and-trace-calculus]] the closed-support object is $i^!k_{\mathbb C}=R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbb C,k_{\mathbb C})$ (the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$ for the closed inclusion $i$), and by the Stacks localization triangle this is the relative cohomology of $(D,D\setminus\{0\})$ for a small disk $D$; radial retraction of the punctured disk $D\setminus\{0\}\simeq S^1$ gives the relative cellular model with its single generator in degree $2$, so $i^!k_{\mathbb C}=k[-2]$. Step 3: the same object is obtained by the duality route $i^!\simeq D_{\{0\}}i^*D_{\mathbb C}$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]]: $D_{\mathbb C}k_{\mathbb C}=k_{\mathbb C}[2]$, $i^*(k_{\mathbb C}[2])=k[2]$ and $D_{\{0\}}(k[2])=k[-2]$. Applying the shift to $\omega_{\mathbb C}=k_{\mathbb C}[2]$ gives $i^!\omega_{\mathbb C}=k[-2]\,[2]=k$, consistently with dualizing transitivity and with the same positive orientation generator used in both computations.

title: Equivariant Constructible Perverse Foundations

items.title: Equivariant constructible derived category of complex varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) carrying an algebraic action of a product $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]). Form the analytic action nerve $G^p\times X$: the simplicial space whose $p$-th space is $G^p\times X$ with the usual face and degeneracy structure maps. In the abelian category of all simplicial sheaves of $k$-vector spaces on this nerve ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]), take its bounded derived category ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]). The full subcategory $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ consists of the complexes whose cohomology sheaves are Cartesian under every nerve structure map and whose restrictions to the degree-zero space $X$ are algebraically constructible with finite-dimensional stalks ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Boundedness means uniform cohomological boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category. Morphisms are morphisms in that ambient derived category, not morphisms in the derived category of naive equivariant sheaves. Set $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary cochain shift. Restriction to $X$ is the forgetful functor. The ambient category and its explicit coinduced injective resolutions are supplied by [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]; triangulatedness, local smallness, conservative restriction and the finite GL Stiefel resolution comparisons are established by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]], recorded as this definition's well-definedness discharge.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §2.1.1-2.1.7 (resolutions $p:P\to X$ and the categories $D^b(X,P)$), §2.2.1-2.2.5 (the limit definition of $D^b_G(X)$), §2.4.1-2.4.6 (the fibered-category description), §2.8 (constructible objects) and Appendix B1-B3 (the simplicial description: simplicial sheaves on $[G\backslash X]_\bullet$, the subcategory with isomorphism structure maps, and its bounded derived category); BBD §1.4.3 and §2.1.1-2.1.3 for the ordinary t-structure language. Step 1 (ambient category). The abelian category of all simplicial $k$-sheaves on the action nerve and its explicit coinduced injective resolutions are constructed by [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], with bounded-below injective models from [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Step 2 (the full subcategory). Cartesian cohomology is the condition that every nerve structure map is an isomorphism on cohomology; degree-zero algebraic constructibility is read through [[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and the shift convention is ordinary cohomological shift in the ambient derived category. Step 3 (well-definedness). Triangulatedness, local smallness, conservative restriction to $X$, idempotent completeness and the finite GL Stiefel resolution comparisons are the content of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]], recorded in justified_by rather than as a dependency edge because that lemma depends on this definition. This is a definition: no mathematical claim beyond well-formedness is made, and AC is inherited from the two construction suppliers.

The definition itself adds no further choice principle.

items.title: Acyclic product fibers stabilize bounded constructible pullback Hom
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:Y\to S$ be a locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]], with nonempty connected finite-type smooth fiber $F$. Suppose the constant-sheaf cohomology of the fiber is $k$ in degree zero and vanishes in degrees $1,\dots,r$. For $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ belongs to $D^{\ge b+r+1}$. For $A\in D_c^{\le a}$, pullback gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ whenever $m\le b+r-a$. It is fully faithful on $D_c^{[b,a]}$ when $r\ge a-b$, and its image is characterized by the counit $f^*\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to C$ being an isomorphism and is closed under direct summands. Extension closure is asserted only for the stronger bound $r\ge a-b+1$; at $r=a-b$ only the degree-zero Hom comparison and retract closure are claimed. No global tensor splitting $Rf_*f^*B\simeq B\otimes R\Gamma(F;k)$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: reduce the unit-cone bound to the finite local product cochain comparison, glue it by local vanishing, and derive the Hom comparison and image description from the bounded t-structure. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §1.9.1-1.9.4 (definition of an $n$-acyclic map; the interval characterization of the image of $f^*$; the criterion for an object of $D^I(X)$ to come from the base; the Vietoris-Begle criterion) and Appendix A2-A4 (the proofs), together with §2.2.1-2.2.4 (limit over resolutions and the interval equivalence). Step 1 (local cone bound): for algebraically constructible $B$ choose a common finite conical triangulation of a product chart of $S$ and a finite CW model of $F$; the ordinary constructible sheaf/cochain comparison of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] identifies $Rf_*f^*B$ locally with the tensor product of the local cochain model of $B$ with $C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$; the cone of $k\to C^*(F;k)$ has cohomology in degrees $\ge r+1$, so tensoring with $B^{\ge b}$ gives $C^{\ge b+r+1}$, and cohomological vanishing is local ([[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] supplies the compatible finite models and their coefficient-field compatibility). Step 2 (Hom comparison): in the triangle $B\to Rf_*f^*B\to C$ with $C\ge b+r+1$, the long exact Hom sequence and the derived adjunction $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ of [[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]] give the displayed isomorphism for $m\le b+r-a$, because $\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m])$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m-1])$ vanish by [[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]] orthogonality ([[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]] is the underlying sheaf adjunction, and the ambient derived model is [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]). Step 3 (image and closure): for an interval $I=[b,a]$ the counit $f^*\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to C$ exhibits $C$ as a pullback precisely when it is an isomorphism; this characterizes the image and proves closure under direct summands. If $r\ge a-b+1$ the degree-one comparison also lifts the connecting morphism of an extension, proving extension closure; at $r=a-b$ that lift is unavailable and is deliberately not used. No global tensor splitting is asserted: the comparison is local and characteristic-class transgressions are allowed. The statement keeps the corrected retract/extension boundary at $r=a-b$ exactly as the owner correction requires.

items.title: General linear frame spaces have the Stiefel cohomology gap
items.statement: Assume AC. For $n_i\ge1$, $N_i\ge n_i+1$ and a field $k$, put $U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i})$ and $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Each $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is homotopy equivalent to the Stiefel space $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$; each $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ is a compact path-connected smooth manifold homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, and the forgetting map $V_n(\mathbb C^N)\to V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ is a numerable locally trivial bundle with fiber $S^{2(N-n)+1}$, hence a Serre fibration. Consequently $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: retract the full-rank frame space onto the Stiefel manifold by Gram-Schmidt, verify the sphere-bundle structure of the forgetting map, and run the cohomological Serre spectral sequence on finite CW models. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, 3.1 (the Stiefel manifold of frames is an n-acyclic free manifold); Hatcher, Algebraic Topology Section 4.2 pp. 375-378 (Theorem 4.41) and the standard sphere-bundle induction computing the cohomology of the complex Stiefel manifolds. Step 1 (retraction): the QR factorization of a full-rank matrix is continuous with positive diagonal triangular factor, and contracting that factor to the identity deforms $\operatorname{Inj}$ onto $V_n$. Step 2 (manifold and CW model): $V_n$ is the regular level set $A^*A=I$ of a submersion on the full-rank locus, hence a compact smooth manifold, and the finite triangulation theorem and finite polyhedra give finite CW models. Step 3 (fibration): the forgetting map is locally trivial with sphere fiber and numerable over the compact base, hence a Serre fibration, and the base is path-connected by induction. Step 4 (spectral sequence): in total degrees at most $2(N-n)$ the only nonzero $E_2$ terms have fiber degree zero, so the induction on $n$ gives the stated gap; iterating the trivial product fibrations gives the product bound $r_N$.

items.title: General linear Stiefel approximations stabilize bounded constructible Hom
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $G$ acts on $U_N$ by precomposition of frames and on $U_N\times X$
diagonally, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct
   isomorphism of functors with different target categories is asserted;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$, $B_N$ and $X_N$ are $X$
   or a point, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

No global tensor splitting
$Ra_{N*}a_N^*B\simeq B\otimes_kR\Gamma(U_N;k)$ is asserted for the
frame-bundle projection $a_N:P_N\to B_N$; the comparison is used only on the
nerve and through the finite local models.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: build the free frame-space quotient, prove the fiber cohomology gap, and apply the bounded pullback comparison on the free-action nerve. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §3.1 (the Stiefel manifold of frames is an $n$-acyclic free manifold for a linear group, giving smooth resolutions) with §2.2.1-2.2.5 and §2.7.1-2.7.2 (limits over resolutions and the finite-resolution picture); Hatcher, Algebraic Topology §4.2 pp. 375-378 (fiber bundles over paracompact base spaces are fibrations, Theorem 4.41) for the fibration input to the Serre spectral sequence. Step 1 (frame space and quotient): nonvanishing pivot minors give graph charts and algebraic sections of $U_N\to B_N$, exhibiting $U_N\to B_N$ as a locally trivial principal $G$-bundle with an algebraic section over each chart; the action is free ([[def-free-group-action]], [[def-locally-trivial-fiber-bundle]]) and $X_N$ is the associated construction of [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]] with local charts $V\times X$. Step 2 (fiber cohomology gap): [[lem-general-linear-stiefel-frame-spaces-have-the-cohomology-gap]] supplies, by Gram-Schmidt and the cohomological Serre spectral sequence of the complex Stiefel sphere bundles, $H^0(U_N;k)=k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$. Step 3 (stabilization): pullback along the simplicial map $G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$ is levelwise a locally trivial bundle with fiber $U_N$, so the bounded pullback comparison of [[lem-locally-trivial-acyclic-fibers-give-bounded-derived-pullback-equivalences]] applies in every nerve degree with the finite models of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]]; locally split Cech descent ([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]) identifies the equivariant Hom groups with Hom groups on $X_N$ in the stated range, gives the resolution-triple description of the image and retract closure, and shows independence of $N$ by applying the image criterion on products of resolutions where inverse comparisons are unique. No global splitting $Ra_{N*}a_N^*B=B\otimes R\Gamma(U_N;k)$ is asserted; the comparison is used only to bound the unit cone and test descent, so genuine characteristic-class transgressions are preserved. [AC as declared]

items.title: Cartesian simplicial sheaves model actual equivariant derived Hom
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The definition [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] gives a locally small triangulated category with conservative restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift. Coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived morphisms. Locally split free-action descent identifies its finite GL Stiefel resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$. The bounded Hom and image comparisons of [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]] hold, including the degree-zero ring comparison and retract closure. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: build the ambient simplicial derived category, transport the Stiefel comparisons through locally split descent, and split idempotents by the telescope construction. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, Appendix B1-B6 (simplicial description of $D^b_G(X)$ and its triangulated equivalence with the Cartesian-cohomology subcategory) and §2.4.1-2.4.6, §2.5.1-2.5.4 (fibered-category description and triangulated structure); BBD §1.4.3 and §2.1.1-2.1.3 for the ordinary t-structure input. Step 1 (triangulated structure): Cartesian cohomology is preserved by truncation, shifts and cones because the nerve inverse images are exact and cohomology is computed by the long exact sequence; constructibility of the degree-zero restriction is closed under the same operations by [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]] and [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]; restriction to $X$ detects the zero object because Cartesian cohomology is determined in degree zero, and the Hom groups are set-sized because the ambient derived category has an injective model. Step 2 (Stiefel comparison): apply locally split Cech derived descent to the free Stiefel resolution $G^\bullet\times P_N\to X_N$; the unit-cone bound and image criterion of [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]] give exactly the resolution triples and the bounded Hom comparison, and uniqueness of the comparisons supplies the coherence cocycles; the degree-zero comparison respects composition, hence is a ring comparison, and retract closure needs no degree-one extension-closure assumption. Step 3 (idempotents): for an idempotent $e$ on a bounded object $K$, form the telescope: let $S$ be the countable sum of copies of $K$ in the bounded-below derived category of all simplicial sheaves and let $T=\operatorname{Cone}(1-\operatorname{shift}(e):S\to S)$; exact coproducts give $H(T)=\operatorname{colim}(H(K),H(e))=\operatorname{im}H(e)$, so $T$ is bounded with Cartesian finite-rank constructible cohomology; the first-summand map $i:K\to T$ satisfies $ie=i$, the componentwise-$e$ map $S\to K$ gives $p:T\to K$ with $pi=e$, and $ip$ is an isomorphism, so replacing $p$ by $p(ip)^{-1}$ splits $e$ inside the category. This proves idempotent completeness without importing a Karoubi completion. No derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is claimed. [AC as declared]
