items.title: Artin vanishing on complex affine varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the constructible derived-category construction. If $Z$ is a complex affine algebraic variety of complex dimension $d$ and $F$ is an algebraically constructible sheaf of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, then $H^q(Z,F)=0$ for $q>d$. More precisely the bound is the dimension of the closure of its support. If $P\in{}^pD^{\le0}_c(Z;k)$, then $H^q(Z,P)=0$ for $q>0$. If $P\in{}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Z;k)$, then $H_c^q(Z,P)=0$ for $q<0$. The empty variety and zero coefficients give zero groups.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from the constructible derived-category construction. Sources: Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, Theorem 13.7 (local Morse data for constructible coefficients) and SS17 (Theorems 17.7 and 17.9), together with the local stratified Morse product and complex-link description supplied by [[lem-complex-stratified-morse-data-have-tangential-normal-product-and-link-description]]. Step 1 (tangential index bound). On a complex manifold of complex dimension s a strongly plurisubharmonic function has tangent Morse index at most s: otherwise the negative Hessian subspace would contain a real two-plane spanned by v and sqrt(-1)v, on which the Hessian sum would be a positive multiple of the Levi form, contradicting negativity. Step 2 (codimension induction). Suppose the stalks of a constructible complex A satisfy H^q(A)_x=0 for q>d-s on every stratum of complex dimension s, and set c=d-s. At a codimension-c stratum, the complex link has dimension at most c-1; use c-1 as the allowed upper dimension, even for nonpure links. An empty link has zero cohomology. A critical point of the collar-compatible logarithmic exhaustion on the link lies on a link stratum of dimension c-1-c' with c'<c, whose unrefined stalk bound holds by hypothesis and only weakens under refinement; by induction its normal Morse cohomology vanishes above c' and the Morse index is at most c-1-c'. The long exact sequences at the finitely many critical values then make the link cohomology vanish above c-1, and the collared-link and regular-interval clauses identify this with the full complex link. Step 3 (normal triangle). The stalk term of the normal Morse triangle vanishes above c by hypothesis and the link term in degree q-1 vanishes above c-1 by Step 2, so normal Morse cohomology vanishes above c; this completes the codimension induction. At the top dimension d, the normal degree is at most d-s and the tangential index at most s, so each relative group vanishes above d, and the finitely many critical-value sequences together with the regular interval above the last value give H^q(Z,A)=0 for q>d. Step 4 (sharpened support bound). A degree-zero constructible sheaf satisfies the stalk hypothesis, giving the dimension-d bound; replacing Z by the closed algebraic support closure of F and using extension by zero gives the sharpened bound q>dim(supp F). Step 5 (perverse consequences). For P in the upper perverse aisle the hypercohomology spectral sequence E_2^{a,b}=H^a(Z,H^b(P)) has H^b(P) supported in dimension at most -b, so E_2^{a,b}=0 whenever a+b>0, and boundedness gives H^q(Z,P)=0 for q>0. For P in the lower aisle apply this to DP and the finite constructible duality H_c^q(Z,P)=H^{-q}(Z,DP)^vee to obtain H_c^q(Z,P)=0 for q<0. The empty variety and zero coefficients give zero groups.

references.title: M. Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves (version of June 26, 2026)
references.locator: §13 (Morse theory with constructible coefficients) and §17.7, §17.9 (complex-link vanishing and Stein/affine vanishing)

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed as inherited from the constructible derived-category construction, consumed through [[lem-complex-stratified-morse-data-have-tangential-normal-product-and-link-description]] and the AC-declared distance-exhaustion supplier [[lem-affine-algebraic-whitney-strata-admit-finite-critical-strongly-plurisubharmonic-distance-exhaustions]]; the perverse spectral sequence and duality steps are choice-free.

items.title: Affine morphisms have one-sided perverse exactness
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. For an affine morphism $u:X\to Y$ of complex algebraic varieties and finite-dimensional field coefficients, $Ru_*$ sends ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ and $Ru_!$ sends ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Y)$. More precisely a bounded constructible $K$ belongs to ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ if and only if $H^q(V,K)=0$ for every affine Zariski open $V\subset Y$ and every $q>0$.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited AC. Source: BBD SS4.1.1-4.1.8 (Theorem 4.1.1: for an affine morphism Rf_* is left t-exact; Corollary 4.1.2 and the relative version of 4.1.7-4.1.8 characterize the upper perverse aisle by the vanishing of H^q(V,-) on affine opens V). Step 1 (local-system detector). Let U be a smooth irreducible affine variety of dimension i>=1 and L a nonzero finite-rank local system. Noether normalisation and the affine-dimension theorem give i functions whose common zero set S is finite and nonempty; local complex orientation and local constancy identify H_S^{2i}(U,L) with the nonzero sum of the stalks L_s, while absolute Artin vanishing gives H^{2i}(U,L)=0, so the support long exact sequence gives H^{2i-1}(U setminus S,L) nonzero. Cover U setminus S by the i principal opens D(f_j); every finite intersection is affine, so absolute Artin vanishing bounds its cohomology by i, and the Cech index is at most i-1; in total degree 2i-1 only H^i(D(f_1...f_i),L) can contribute, so it is nonzero. For i=0 the detector is the nonzero stalk at an isolated point. Step 2 (converse characterization). Suppose all positive-degree H^q(V,K) vanish for affine opens V of Y. Write U_i=Y setminus F_{i-1} and argue downwards in i that the stalk cohomology on U_i satisfies the upper perverse support bound. On U_i put A=tau_{<=-i}K and Q=tau_{>-i}K; the induction hypothesis and the layer bound make A upper perverse, so on each affine V the triangle A->K->Q gives H^q(V,Q)=0 for q>0, and all cohomology sheaves of Q are local systems supported on the closed smooth layer W_i. If Q is nonzero, let b>-i be its largest nonzero cohomological degree and L=H^b(Q)|_{W_i}; the detector supplies an affine V inside U_i with H^i(V cap W_i,L) nonzero, and the bounded spectral sequence H^a(V cap W_i,H^t(Q)) => H^{a+t}(V,Q) has a unique nonzero term in total degree i+b>0, a contradiction; hence Q=0 and the induction closes. Step 3 (application). For P in the upper perverse aisle on X and an affine open V subset of Y, the inverse image u^{-1}V is affine, so derived composition and absolute Artin vanishing give H^q(V,Ru_*P)=H^q(u^{-1}V,P)=0 for q>0; the characterization then puts Ru_*P in the upper aisle. For P in the lower aisle apply this to DP and dualize (D Ru_* D = Ru_!) to obtain the claim for Ru_!. Empty and zero cases follow from the same zero triangles. The arithmetic-purity step of BBD 4.1.7 is replaced by the explicit oriented complex local cohomology detector; no Stein local-characterization theorem or nonproper restriction claim is used.

references.locator: §4.1.1-4.1.8 (affine morphisms are t-exact on one side; the affine-open characterization of the upper perverse aisle)

items.title: General projective hyperplanes decrease the defect of semismallness
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the algebraic dimension and Bertini suppliers. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties with $X$ smooth, nonempty and irreducible of dimension $n$. Fix a projective embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d$ with $d\ge1$ and let $Y_i=\{y:\dim f^{-1}(y)=i\}$. Put $r(f)=\max_{Y_i\ne\varnothing}(2i+\dim Y_i-n)$. For the universal hyperplane incidence $g:\mathcal X\to Y\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ one has $r(g)\le r(f)-1$ if $r(f)>0$. If $r(f)=0$, $g$ is small: it has defect zero and every positive-fiber-dimensional stratum gives a strictly negative defect contribution.

There is a nonempty Zariski open subset of the hyperplane parameter space such that every hyperplane $H$ in it has smooth $X_H=X\cap H$ and satisfies the same conclusions for $f_H:X_H\to Y$: its defect is at most $r(f)-1$ if $r(f)>0$, and it is small if $r(f)=0$. Empty hyperplane sections are omitted from the defect computation and have zero pushforward. Successive general sections therefore lower a positive defect at every nonempty step. A finite prescribed algebraic Whitney stratification can also be met transversally by shrinking this open subset when the separately supplied stratified transversality theorem is applicable.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from the algebraic dimension and Bertini suppliers. Source: de Cataldo-Migliorini, Theorem 4.7.4 (r(f) goes down) and its proof. Step 1 (universal incidence). The incidence X={(x,H): x in X cap H} is the total space of a projective-space bundle of relative dimension d-1 over X, because the linear forms vanishing at a point form a rank-d subbundle of the dual of the ambient linear space; hence X is smooth of dimension n+d-1. The fibre of g at (y,H) is f^{-1}(y) cap H, and a nonempty hyperplane cut of a projective variety of dimension i+1 is pure of dimension i unless the hyperplane contains a top-dimensional component, in which case it is i+1. Step 2 (universal bound). Partition the universal locus of fibre dimension i into A_i, where dim(f^{-1}(y) cap H)=i with y in Y_i, and B_i, where y in Y_{i+1}; both are constructible by upper semicontinuity of projective fibre dimension. For fixed y in Y_i, hyperplanes containing a top-dimensional component of f^{-1}(y) form a parameter locus of dimension at most d-i-1, so componentwise generic-fibre dimension bounds give dim A_i <= dim Y_i + d-i-1 and dim B_i <= dim Y_{i+1}+d; subtracting n+d-1 from twice the fibre dimension plus these parameter dimensions gives contributions at most r(f)-i and at most r(f)-1, while the A_0 bound is dim Y_0-n <= 0. Hence r(g) <= r(f)-1 when r(f)>0; if r(f)=0 the bounds are strictly negative for i>0 and zero is attained on the dense image of the generically finite map, so g is small. Step 3 (fixed general hyperplane). Project each of the finitely many locally closed components of A_i and B_i to the dual projective space; components with nondense image are absent from a general parameter fibre, and components with dense image have general parameter-fibre dimension at most their dimension minus d. Intersecting the resulting nonempty parameter opens with the Bertini smooth-section open and repeating the arithmetic of Step 2 with source dimension n-1 and parameter dimension d gives the fixed-hyperplane conclusions, including smallness when r(f)=0; empty hyperplane sections are omitted and have zero pushforward. Iterating on the successive smooth nonempty sections lowers a positive defect at every step. The prescribed finite stratified transversality clause is the separately supplied condition named in the Statement, not a consequence of ordinary Bertini alone. No counting-of-constants theorem asserting that a hyperplane avoids every fibre component is needed.

references.title: M. A. A. de Cataldo and L. Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030v2 (complete final-version PDF)
references.locator: Theorem 4.7.4 and its proof (defect r(f), universal hyperplane family)

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the algebraic dimension and Bertini suppliers [[thm-upper-semicontinuity-fibre-dimension-projective]] and [[thm-bertini-smooth-hyperplane-section]] and from the published dimension suppliers [[cor-dimension-of-image-plus-generic-fibre]] and [[lem-projective-hypersurface-dimension-drop]]; the incidence, componentwise generic-fibre and parameter-fibre estimates are otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Universal hyperplanes give relative weak Lefschetz and maximal pullback subobjects
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective map of complex varieties, with a fixed closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d$ and $d\ge1$. Set $Y'=Y\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$, $p:Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$, $p':X'\to X$, and let $i:\mathcal X\hookrightarrow X'$ be the universal hyperplane incidence. Write $g=(f\times1)i$, and for $K\in\operatorname{Perv}(X;k)$ put $M=i^*p'^*K[d-1]$. Then $M$ is perverse and the restriction/Gysin maps give isomorphisms $p^*{}^pH^l(Rf_*K)[d]\to{}^pH^{l+1}(Rg_*M)$ for $l\le-2$ and monomorphisms for $l=-1$, with dual isomorphisms for $l\ge2$ and epimorphisms for $l=1$. In particular $p^*{}^pH^{-1}(Rf_*K)[d]$ identifies with the largest perverse subobject of ${}^pH^0(Rg_*M)$ belonging to the essential image of $p^*[d]$, and $p^*{}^pH^1(Rf_*K)[d]$ with the largest such quotient.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited AC. Sources: BBD SS4.2.5-4.2.6.2 (for a smooth map of relative dimension d with connected geometric fibres, f^*[d] is fully faithful on perverse sheaves and the adjoints pH^d f_!, pH^{-d} f_* identify the largest subobject and quotient from the base) and SS5.4.11-5.4.13 (universal hyperplane family: the maximal-perverse-subobject statement (5.4.11.iii) and the projective-bundle formula (5.4.12)), with de Cataldo-Migliorini Propositions 4.7.8-4.7.9 as an independently printed version. Step 1 (relative weak Lefschetz). Let j be the open inclusion of the complement of the universal incidence and u=(f x 1)j. Over an affine chart of the hyperplane parameter space the complement is an affine d-space bundle, so u is affine. Apply R(f x 1)_! to the localization triangle j_!j^*p'^*K[d] -> p'^*K[d] -> i_*i^*p'^*K[d]. The affine one-sided exactness supplier makes the first term have no negative perverse cohomology; proper base change and the noncharacteristic pullback supplier identify the second with p^*Rf_*K[d] and the third with Rg_*M[1]. The long exact perverse sequence gives the restriction isomorphisms for l<=-2 and the monomorphism for l=-1, and duality gives the Gysin isomorphisms for l>=2 and epimorphism for l=1, with i^!=i^*[-2] in the compatible normalization. Step 2 (projective-bundle formula). Cup powers of the tautological Euler class pulled back from the dual projective space define a morphism from the direct sum; on every fibre it is the standard projective-space cohomology basis, so proper base change proves Rp_*p^*T = sum_{a=0}^{d} T[-2a] for every constructible T, and the same formula with d-1 holds for p'i. The integral power basis is [[lem-complex-tautological-euler-class-restricts-to-the-projective-fiber-generator]] (sphere-bundle Gysin sequence) and finiteness is preserved by [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]]. Consequently Hom(p^*A[d],p^*B[d])=Hom(A,B) for heart objects A,B, since the terms Hom(A,B[-2a]) for a>0 vanish in the heart. Step 3 (maximal subobject and quotient). p^*[d] sends a simple intersection complex to a simple intersection complex and is exact and fully faithful; its image is closed under subobjects and quotients by induction on the finite length of the heart objects, so the perverse adjoints l=pH^d Rp_! and r=pH^{-d} Rp_* identify p^*[d]r(C)->C as the largest subobject and C->p^*[d]l(C) as the largest quotient from Y. Step 4 (truncation). Put V=R(f x 1)_*p'^*K and U=Rg_*i^*p'^*K. Step 1 gives pH tau_{<d-1} V = pH tau_{<d-1} U and a monomorphism pH^{d-1}V -> pH^{d-1}U. The discarded summand Rf_*K[-2d] has perverse amplitude at least d, because every fibre of f has dimension at most d (BBD 4.2.4 amplitude estimates together with the proper adjunctions), so Rp_* of the two truncated triangles shows r(pH^{d-1}V)=r(pH^{d-1}U); since pH^{d-1}V=p^*pH^{-1}(Rf_*K)[d] lies in the pullback image, where r is inverse to p^*[d], naturality identifies its injection into pH^{d-1}U=pH^0(Rg_*M) with the maximal-subobject counit. Dualizing the proved statement for DK gives the maximal-quotient identification p^*pH^1(Rf_*K)[d]. No pure-sheaf, arithmetic-comparison or decomposition-theorem input is used; the affine one-sided exactness and noncharacteristic pullback items are separate necessary suppliers on this page and are not silently identified with the absolute Artin bound.

items.title: Universal hyperplanes lower the defect for projective space to a point
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. For $f:\mathbb P^n\to\mathrm{pt}$ with $n\ge1$, the defect is $r(f)=n$. The universal hyperplane family maps to the dual space $(\mathbb P^n)^\vee$ with fibers $\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and has defect $n-1$.
items.strategy: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. Step 1. For f:P^n->pt with n>=1 the source dimension is n, the only fibre has dimension n, and the image has dimension zero, so the defect r(f)=2n-n=n. The universal incidence is a projective-space bundle over the dual projective space with fibre P^{n-1}, so its total space has dimension 2n-1. Step 2. The only fibre dimension of the universal family is n-1, so its defect is 2(n-1)+n-(2n-1)=n-1, strictly below n; this checks the positive-defect clause of [[lem-projective-hyperplane-sections-decrease-the-defect-of-semismallness]] directly, including n=1, where the universal family is the identity on the dual projective line.

items.title: Complex-oriented diagonal Thom classes realize exceptional exchange on supports
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the analytic six-functor and equivariant constructible suppliers below. In the analytic constructible six-functor setting, let $M$ be a smooth complex manifold of pure dimension $d$, and let $A\to M$, $B\to M$ be algebraic maps whose fiber product is $T$. Assume the supplied duality construction has localization, tensor-Hom adjunction, coherent exchange maps, and the smooth orientation normalized by the positive compactly supported generator on a complex coordinate ball ([[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]), with its equivariant constructible form supplied by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]. The refined pullback of dualizing classes on the support $A\times B$ by the ambient middle diagonal $M\to M\times M$ is the operation induced by the mate $a^*q^!\to b^!u^*$ of $b_!a^*\to u^*q_!$, after tensor evaluation and dualizing transitivity. It equals cap product with the positive middle-diagonal Thom class and lowers Borel-Moore degree by $2d$, even for singular, nontransverse supports. Ordered iterated diagonals are compatible with composed refined operations. For a complex vector bundle, zero-section self-intersection is cap product with its oriented Euler class.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Sources: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS2 (convolution in Borel-Moore homology: the general supported construction, its dependence on the ambient orientations, and associativity; PDF pp. 7-10) and SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the diagonal-restriction chain identifying the convolution algebra with Ext; PDF pp. 18-19); Varshavsky, Lefschetz-Verdier trace formula, SS0.3-0.4 and SS1.1 (adjunction, base-change mates, projection formula and correspondence composition; PDF pp. 5-8). Step 1 (diagonal normal model): for the diagonal $i:M\hookrightarrow M\times M$ a tubular normal chart has normal pair $(\mathbb C^d,\mathbb C^d\setminus\{0\})$, whose relative cohomology is $k$ in degree $2d$ and zero in other degrees by the long exact sequence of the sphere and the contraction of the disk; hence $i^!k_{M\times M}=k_M[-2d]$ under the positive local generator. The orientation sheaf has trivial transition signs because a complex transition has positive real determinant, so compatible local positive generators specify its global isomorphism with no higher-degree gluing ambiguity, and this is exactly the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TM$. Step 2 (supported tensor-Hom evaluation): for a closed embedding $z:Z\hookrightarrow N$ the injective model $z^!=z^{-1}\Gamma_Z$ and its localization triangle identify $R\operatorname{Hom}(z_*k_Z,F)$ with $R\Gamma_Z(F)$, so on a closed support in an ambient manifold exceptional restriction is computed by relative sections and tensor evaluation realizes cup/cap product of supported classes as the tensor-Hom evaluation map. Pulling the orientation map of Step 1 back to $A\times B$ along the support square and applying tensor-Hom adjunction gives the mate exchange: its left adjoint is the base-change map $b_!a^*\to u^*q_!$ followed by evaluation, and conversely the right adjoint of this base-change evaluation is the pulled-back supported orientation map. This is an equality of the two explicit adjoint maps, not an inference from equality of their values after forgetting support, so cap product with the Thom class and the exceptional exchange agree without a transversality assertion on the support. Step 3 (iterated diagonals and Euler class): for two ordered diagonals the normal model is the ordered direct sum of their complex normal bundles; on the product of normal coordinate disks the relative cup product of the two positive generators evaluates to $+1$ on the ordered product disk, which is the positive generator of the sum, and local uniqueness as in Step 1 with base-change mate pasting as in Step 2 gives the composed operation on every support. For a vector-bundle zero section its pullback of the Thom class is by definition the Euler class, so applying zero-section refined pullback after zero-section pushforward caps with this class. All real degrees $2d$ are even, so ordering the normal summands introduces no additional sign. Only the declared localization, tensor-Hom, exchange, orientation and trace clauses are used; the remaining steps are choice-free.

items.title: Equivariant Borel–Moore homology and oriented correspondence convolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the equivariant
constructible and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Let $G=\prod_v\mathrm{GL}_{n_v}(\mathbb C)$,
let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, and use bounded algebraically constructible complexes of
$k$-sheaves in the analytic topology, in the equivariant derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(-;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].
All functors are derived.

**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, for a free smooth approximation: a $G$-invariant open subset $U$ of a
finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation on which $G$ acts freely, and
$b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the group is the eventual stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$; existence of the stable value and its independence of the
approximation are supplied by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Correspondences.** Let $f_i:X_i\to E$ be finitely many proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps
with $X_i$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d_i$. Put $Z_{ij}=X_i\times_EX_j$ (reduced
analytically), $T_{ijk}=X_i\times_EX_j\times_EX_k$, and let $h:T_{ijk}\to Z_{ik}$ forget the
middle point; it is proper, being the base change of $f_j$. The first coordinate is the source.
For $a\in H_p^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij})$, $b\in H_q^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{jk})$, define
$$a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^{!}(a\boxtimes b)\in H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik}).$$
Here $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ is the refined oriented middle-diagonal operation on supports of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]]: it
restricts the external class to $T_{ijk}$ by the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TX_j$
of $X_j\hookrightarrow X_j\times X_j$. It is defined on arbitrary closed supports; no
transversality of $Z_{ij}$ and $Z_{jk}$ is assumed. Proper pushforward is the dualizing trace.
The ordered coordinates are $(i,j,j,k)$, and the two middle factors are contracted without a
permutation. If intermediate indices differ, the product is set to zero. Put degree $d_i+d_j-p$
on the $(i,j)$ corner. The normalized diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ has corner degree zero.

**Sheaf model.** The sheaf model of the refined Thom operation uses the exchange morphism
$u^*v^!\to v'^!u'^*$ for the middle Cartesian square: with $u:Z_{ij}\to X_j$,
$v:Z_{jk}\to X_j$, $T=Z_{ij}\times_{X_j}Z_{jk}$ and projections $v':T\to Z_{ij}$,
$u':T\to Z_{jk}$, the morphism is obtained as the adjunction mate of proper base change
$u'_!v'^*\cong v^*u_!$. It is a morphism, not an asserted isomorphism for arbitrary supports.
Its orientation is fixed by the Thom class restricting to $+1$ on every positively
complex-oriented normal fiber. Agreement of this model with the stated refined geometric
operation, and compatibility with composition, are proved in
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] after the
foundational six-functor inputs are available.

**Well-formedness.** The definition is independent of the chosen free smooth approximation
because the stable Borel value exists and stabilizes by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the product is
defined because the refined middle-diagonal operation of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] is
defined on arbitrary closed supports and $h$ is proper, so its dualizing trace is available; the
degree bookkeeping is fixed by the pure complex dimension $d_j$ of the middle factor. The claim
that the sheaf model and the geometric operation agree, and that the product is compatible with
composition and units, is not assumed here: it is the content of
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]], which is
recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that theorem depends on this
definition. The Axiom of Choice is consumed exactly through the three cited suppliers, whose
constructions (equivariant descent, injective replacements, Borel stabilization) declare it;
the definition itself introduces no further choice principle.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Sources: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS2 (the supported convolution product, its dependence on the ambient orientations, and associativity; PDF pp. 7-10) and SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the corner normalization; PDF pp. 18-19); Varagnolo-Vasserot, SS1.1-1.10 (equivariant Borel-Moore corners and the source-first convention; PDF pp. 1-12). Step 1 (ambient object and normalization): the equivariant category and its degreewise-finite Morphism spaces are those of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]], and the stable Borel value is supplied by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the dualizing normalization $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$ is the normalized one fixed by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]], not the unnormalized quotient-stack shift. Step 2 (the geometric product): $h$ is proper because it is the base change of the proper map $f_j$, so the proper pushforward in the product is the dualizing trace; the refined diagonal restriction $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ on arbitrary closed supports is the operation of [[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]], which also proves that it agrees with the mate of proper base change used by the sheaf model. No transversality or smoothness of the $Z_{ij}$ is used. Step 3 (degrees and unit): the middle factor $X_j$ has pure complex dimension $d_j$, so the refined diagonal operation lowers Borel-Moore degree by $2d_j$ and the product lands in $H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik})$; the corner degree $d_i+d_j-p$ makes the diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ have degree $d_i+d_i-2d_i=0$, and nonmatching indices multiply to zero by the definition. The definition is otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Proper-pushforward Ext is equivariant Borel–Moore homology of the fiber product
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the constructible six-functor and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Use the constructible equivariant setting $D^b_{G,c}(E;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] and proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps $f_i:X_i\to E$ with smooth sources $X_i$ of pure complex dimension $d_i$, as in [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. Put $L_i=f_{i!}k_{X_i}[d_i]$. For every integer $r$ and every pair $(i,j)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\Phi_{ij}^r:\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(E;k)}(L_i,L_j[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k).$$
All groups are degreewise finite-dimensional for these finite-type algebraic varieties and $G$; no finite-dimensionality of their direct sum over all degrees is asserted. The isomorphism is equivariant-cohomology linear, commutes with enlargement of the Borel approximation, and is natural in constructible coefficient morphisms before smooth orientation is applied. No semismallness, decomposition theorem, purity, or smoothness of $E$ or $Z_{ij}$ is required.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Source: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the Cartesian-square chain $H^\bullet(Z,D_Z)\cong H^\bullet(N_\Delta,i^!(L^\vee\boxtimes L))\cong\operatorname{Ext}^\bullet(L,L)$; PDF pp. 18-19) together with Varshavsky, Lefschetz-Verdier trace formula, SS0.3-0.4 and SS1.1 (adjunction, base-change mates, projection formula, dualizing transitivity; PDF pp. 5-8). Step 1 (adjunction chain): write $p:Z_{ij}\to X_i$, $q:Z_{ij}\to X_j$ and $t=r+d_j-d_i$. Removing the source shift by $[-d_i]$ and using $f_{i!}\dashv f_i^!$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_E(f_{i!}k_i,f_{j!}k_j[t])=\operatorname{Hom}_{X_i}(k_i,f_i^!f_{j!}k_j[t])$. In the Cartesian square with lower arrow $f_j$ and right arrow $f_i$, the dual mate of proper base change of [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]] gives $f_i^!f_{j!}k_j=p_*q^!k_j$ because both maps are proper, so $p^*\dashv p_*$ identifies the group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{Z_{ij}}(k_Z,q^!k_j[t])$. This is the complete cornerwise chain, including negative $r$. Step 2 (orientation and degree): smooth orientation on $X_j$ says $k_j=\omega_{X_j}[-2d_j]$, and transitivity of the exceptional inverse image gives $q^!k_j=\omega_Z[-2d_j]$; hence the group is $\operatorname{Hom}(k_Z,\omega_Z[r-d_i-d_j])$, which is exactly $H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k)$ in the normalization fixed by [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. At a finite Borel approximation of dimension offset $b$, $X_j\times_GU$ has dimension $d_j+b$ while the descended complex retains the shift $d_j$, so the identical calculation gives ordinary Borel-Moore degree $d_i+d_j+2b-r$; removing $2b$ gives the stated equivariant degree, and no stack-dimension shift is inserted into $\omega_X^G$. Step 3 (naturality, linearity, finiteness): every map in the chain is an adjunction, base-change, or orientation map supplied naturally; they commute with approximation transition pullbacks by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]], so they induce an isomorphism in each stable degree. Coherent scalar pullback from the base point and the projection formula give equivariant-cohomology linearity, and degreewise finiteness is exactly that lemma's conclusion, not a boundedness assertion about the total equivariant Ext. Smoothness is used only for the orientation on $X_j$ and properness only in base change and in the identification of the two pushforwards.

items.title: Verdier-duality identification intertwines Yoneda product and oriented convolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the constructible six-functor and Borel-stabilization suppliers. For the data and cornerwise maps $\Phi$ of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]], let $\alpha:L_i\to L_j[r]$, $\beta:L_j\to L_k[s]$. With multiplication $\alpha*\beta=\beta[r]\circ\alpha$ one has
$$\Phi_{ik}^{r+s}(\beta[r]\circ\alpha)=\Phi_{ij}^r(\alpha)*\Phi_{jk}^s(\beta).$$
Here the right product is the external-product, refined middle-diagonal Thom intersection, proper-pushforward convolution of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], not a product transported by definition from Ext. The map sends $\operatorname{id}_{L_i}$ to $[\Delta_{X_i}]$. Consequently the direct sum of all corners is an isomorphism of unital graded algebras with this opposite-composition convention; nonmatching corners multiply to zero.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Sources: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS2 (associativity of the supported convolution and its dependence on the ambient orientation; PDF pp. 8-10) and SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the algebra identification, whose compatibility of products is stated there to be proved in [Chriss-Ginzburg, Theorem 8.6.7]; PDF pp. 18-19), together with Varshavsky SS1.1.6(b) (proper-pushforward composition by base-change pasting; PDF pp. 6-8). The product-compatibility clause is reconstructed locally below rather than cited. Step 1 (typed correspondences): at an ordinary finite Borel approximation, write $A=Z_{ij}$, $B=Z_{jk}$, $C=Z_{ik}$, $T=T_{ijk}$ and the projections $p,q,u,v,a,b,h,\ell,m$ of the typed triple diagram, with $qa=ub$, $pa=\ell h$, $vb=mh$; the middle square is Cartesian and every displayed projection is proper. Put $t=r+d_j-d_i$ and $w=s+d_k-d_j$; the adjoint representatives of $\Phi(\alpha)$ and $\Phi(\beta)$ are cohomological correspondences $U:q_!k_A\to k_j[t]$ and $V:v_!k_B\to k_k[w]$, with kernel forms $\kappa:k_A\to q^!k_j[t]$ and $\lambda:k_B\to v^!k_k[w]$. Step 2 (the explicit composite): let $\mathrm{BC}:b_!a^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*q_!$ be proper base change and form $W:(vb)_!k_T=v_!b_!a^*k_A\xrightarrow{v_!\mathrm{BC}}v_!u^*q_!k_A\xrightarrow{v_!u^*U}v_!k_B[t]\xrightarrow{V[t]}k_k[t+w]$. Its adjoint $k_T\to(vb)^!k_k[t+w]$ is exactly the composite $k_T\xrightarrow{a^*\kappa}a^*q^!k_j[t]\to b^!u^*k_j[t]=b^!k_B[t]\xrightarrow{b^!\lambda[t]}(vb)^!k_k[t+w]$, where the middle arrow is the mate exchange of $\mathrm{BC}$; this follows by applying $(vb)_!\dashv(vb)^!$ to both maps, so the defining evaluation of the mate gives precisely the three arrows of $W$ and no exchange isomorphism is assumed. Step 3 (geometric interpretation): place $A\times B$ as its closed support in $X_i\times X_j\times X_j\times X_k$ and pull it back by $\operatorname{id}_{X_i}\times\Delta_{X_j}\times\operatorname{id}_{X_k}$. External product of $\kappa,\lambda$ corresponds by smooth orientation to the external dualizing class; the pulled-back diagonal is defined on this support by the exceptional-pullback exchange of [[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]], contracting the two middle orientation factors, and its dualizing representative is the map of Step 2. Restricting the ambient diagonal to a normal coordinate ball in $X_j$ shows that the exceptional-pullback orientation and the complex Thom class of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]] both take value $+1$ on the ordered real coordinates, so they are the same map and the refined operation is given by the Thom contraction even when the support is singular or nontransverse. Step 4 (push to the third corner): pushing the correspondence on $T$ to $C$ gives $U_C:m_!k_C\xrightarrow{m_!\eta_h}m_!h_*k_T=(vb)_!k_T\xrightarrow{W}k_k[t+w]$, whose kernel form is $k_C\to h_*k_T\to h_*h^!m^!k_k[t+w]\xrightarrow{\epsilon_h}m^!k_k[t+w]$ with $\epsilon_h$ the dualizing proper trace; transitivity identifies the middle dualizing object with $\omega_T[-2d_k+t+w]$ and Step 3 identifies this class with $h_*\Delta_{X_j}^!(\Phi(\alpha)\boxtimes\Phi(\beta))$. Step 5 (composition square on its arrows): the inverse of the chain of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] sends $U$ to $f_{i!}k_i\xrightarrow{f_{i!}\eta_p}f_{i!}p_*k_A=f_{j!}q_!k_A\xrightarrow{f_{j!}U}f_{j!}k_j[t]$ and $V$ analogously; naturality of $\eta_u$ moves $f_{j!}U$ past the second unit, proper base change identifies the resulting units with the composed unit of $pa=\ell h$, and taking left adjoints gives the identity on $a^*p^*k_i=k_T$ by the two adjunction triangle equations, so both routes give $f_{i!}k_i\xrightarrow{f_{i!}\eta_{pa}}f_{k!}(vb)_!k_T\xrightarrow{f_{k!}W}f_{k!}k_k[t+w]$. The inverse map applied to $U_C$ gives the same expression because the composed-unit formula $\eta_{\ell h}=\ell_*\eta_h\ell^*\circ\eta_\ell$ follows from the same triangle equations, so the whole product square commutes for arbitrary cohomological correspondences before orientation or grading is applied. Step 6 (shifts and units): restoring object shifts gives $t+w=r+s+d_k-d_i$, the corner degrees $d_i+d_j-r$ and $d_j+d_k-s$ add and lose $2d_j$ to give $d_i+d_k-r-s$, and at a finite approximation every incoming degree acquires $2b$; homogeneous maps compose as $V[t]\circ U=\beta[r]\circ\alpha$ with no interchanged factors and no $(-1)^{rs}$ sign, since the normal orientation has even real degree. For $i=j$ the identity inverse-correspondence is the diagonal unit under the adjunction triangle equations, and its kernel is the positive complex diagonal fundamental class by the orientation check of Step 3, so $\Phi(\operatorname{id}_{L_i})=[\Delta X_i]$; product compatibility transfers associativity and these units from composition, and distinct corners are zero on both sides by source/target matching. All foundational six-operation, duality and stabilization clauses are used through the declared suppliers; the remaining arguments are formal.

items.title: Stable-flag incidence spaces admit the oriented proper correspondence calculus
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited through the smooth-projective flag-variety and Euler-to-Chern suppliers. Let $Q$ be any finite loopless quiver, allowing multiple arrows and arrows in both directions, let $V= igoplus_vV_v$ be finite-dimensional over $\mathbb C$, and put $G=\prod_v\mathrm{GL}(V_v)$ and $E_V= igoplus_{h:v	o w}\operatorname{Hom}(V_v,V_w)$. For a word $
u$ of vertex labels with multiplicities $\dim V_v$, let $B_
u$ be its graded complete flag variety and $X_
u=\{(x,F)\in E_V	imes B_
u:x_h(F^a_v)\subseteq F^a_w	ext{ for all }a,h\}$. Then $X_
u	o B_
u$ is a complex algebraic vector bundle, $X_
u$ is smooth, and $\pi_
u:X_
u	o E_V$ is projective. Every middle-forgetting projection $X_
u	imes_{E_V}X_\eta	imes_{E_V}X_	heta	o X_
u	imes_{E_V}X_	heta$ is proper. All orientations and refined middle-diagonal operations required by the preceding Ext/convolution theorems of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] and [[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] exist equivariantly, without a smoothness or transversality assertion for fiber products. With $d_
u=\dim_{\mathbb C}X_
u$ and $L_
u=R\pi_{

items.strategy:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Sources: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS2 (convolution with supports) and SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the flag-incidence/Ext dictionary; PDF pp. 7-10, 18-19); Varagnolo-Vasserot SS1.1-1.10 (the quiver-flag incidence spaces, their dimension shifts and the convolution corners; PDF pp. 1-12). Step 1 (incidence as an associated bundle): fix a graded reference flag, whose stabilizer is the product of upper triangular subgroups in the individual $\mathrm{GL}(V_v)$; its orbit $B_
u$ is the product of complete flag varieties $\prod_v\mathrm{Flag}(V_v)$ by [[lem-flag-variety-of-a-vector-space]]. In an ordinary flag chart choose ordered basis vectors compatible with the flags; the stability condition for an arrow $h:v	o w$ says that its matrix coefficient from source position $a$ to target position $b$ vanishes whenever $b>a$ in the full word $
u$. Thus the fiber is a fixed linear subspace $S_
u\subset E_V$, of dimension the sum over arrows of the number of allowed pairs; the stabilizer preserves $S_
u$, and $X_
u=G	imes_{P_
u}S_
u$ is the associated vector bundle (the chosen flag charts trivialize it with these matrix entries as linear coordinates; multiple arrows contribute separate summands and arrows in both directions impose conditions on separate matrices). Step 2 (smoothness, projectivity, properness): flag charts are affine spaces and each nontrivial flag factor is smooth projective, so $X_
u$ is smooth of pure dimension $d_
u=\sum_v\dim\mathrm{Flag}(V_v)+\dim S_
u$; stability is the vanishing of the bundle maps $F^a_v	o V_w/F^a_w$ induced by $x_h$, so $X_
u$ is closed in $E_V	imes B_
u$ and $\pi_
u$ is a restriction of the projective product projection; the middle-forgetting map is its base change for $\pi_\eta$, hence proper, although neither its fibers nor the total spaces are asserted smooth. Step 3 (orientations and equivariance): every $X_
u$ has its complex orientation and its diagonal has complex normal bundle $TX_
u$; applying the Thom class of [[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] to the pulled-back closed support gives the refined diagonal operation of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], whether or not the support is transverse, and proper trace along the map of Step 2 supplies convolution. All constructions use equivariant bundle maps and the invariant complex orientation, so they descend to smooth free approximations; the equivariant setting is that of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] and it is supplied to the Ext and product theorems [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] and [[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] with exactly the dimension shift $d_
u$, not the dimension of the flag base alone; the Borel approximations have finite CW type by [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]]. Step 4 (zero sections and Euler classes): for a rank-$c$ complex bundle the normal pair of its zero section is its oriented disk/sphere pair; multiplication by the positive Thom class defines the Gysin operation, and pulling that class back by the zero section gives its Euler class, which equals the top Chern class by [[thm-top-chern-class-equals-euler-class-of-the-underlying-real-bundle]] on each CW-type approximation component. Smooth complex bundle and flag-bundle maps use the relative orientation, so they have the stated oriented pullbacks, and these operations commute with proper pushforward and Cartesian pullback by the projection formula and trace/base-change mates. This supplies the calculus, not the numerical signed crossing formulas of a geometric KLR presentation.

title: Equivariant Borel Moore Correspondence Convolution And Constructible Ext Examples

items.title: Unequal-dimensional proper pushforwards carry the summed-dimension Ext/Borel–Moore degree
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. For trivial $G$, $E=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_1=\mathrm{pt}$ and $X_2=\mathbb P^1$ with $d_1=0$, $d_2=1$, put $L_1=k$ and $L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$ in the setting of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. Then $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_1,L_2)$ is $k$ for $r=-1,1$ and zero otherwise, and the corresponding summed-dimension Borel-Moore degrees $d_1+d_2-r$ are $2$ and $0$; the reverse corner $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_2,L_1)$ has the same two nonzero degrees. The unaugmented shifts $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_1-r= -r$ and $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_2-r=2-r$ give the wrong degrees in at least one corner, so the summed $d_1+d_2$ normalization of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] is the one compatible with the two unequal source dimensions.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Route: for the trivial group take the identity Borel model, so [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] reduces to the ordinary bounded constructible category and $Z_{12}=Z_{21}=\mathbb P^1$. Step 1 (the two objects): $f_1:\mathrm{pt}\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper and $d_1=0$, so $L_1=k$; $f_2:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper and $d_2=1$, so $L_2=f_{2!}k_{\mathbb P^1}[1]=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$. Step 2 (cohomology of the projective line): $\mathbb P^1=\operatorname{Gr}_1(\mathbb C^2)$ has the finite Schubert CW structure of [[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]], [[def-schubert-cells-in-real-and-complex-grassmannians]] and [[thm-schubert-cells-give-the-stable-grassmannian-cw-structure]] with one cell in real dimension $0$ and one in real dimension $2$, and no two cells in adjacent dimensions; the cellular boundary differentials vanish by [[cor-a-cw-complex-with-no-cells-in-adjacent-dimensions-has-zero-cellular-boundary]], so the cellular cochain complex with constant coefficients $k$ computes $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)=k$, $H^1=0$, $H^2=k$ by [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]], and $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)\simeq k\oplus k[-2]$. Step 3 (forward corner): $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_1,L_2)=\operatorname{Hom}(k,R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1+r])=H^{1+r}(\mathbb P^1,k)$ is nonzero exactly for $r=-1$ (from $H^0$) and $r=1$ (from $H^2$), and zero otherwise. Step 4 (reverse corner and degree shift): $\operatorname{Hom}(R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1],k[r])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R\Gamma,k[r-1])$ is nonzero exactly for $r\in\{-1,1\}$ by the same two cohomology groups, so both corners have the same two Ext degrees. By [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] these corners are $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{1-r}(\mathbb P^1;k)$, which in the normalization of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]] is $H^{2-(1-r)}(\mathbb P^1,k)$: it is $k$ for $1-r=2$ and for $1-r=0$, that is, for the Borel-Moore degrees $2$ and $0$, and vanishes elsewhere. The naive source-only shifts $-r$ and $2-r$ are not both compatible with these two degrees. Sources: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example 0.6 (cells of $\mathbb CP^n$), SS2.2 (the no-adjacent-cells computation) and SS3.2 (cohomology of $\mathbb CP^n$), and the local packet contract for the corner computation.

items.title: A point and projective-line check of source-first convolution and opposite composition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. In the point/projective-line geometry of [[ex-unequal-dimensional-proper-pushforwards-have-the-summed-dimension-ext-bm-shift]], let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$ be the unit $k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ and let $\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$ be point evaluation $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, that is, evaluation $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)\to k$ shifted by $1$ and extended by zero on $H^2$. Then $\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], and under the correspondence isomorphism of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] one has $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$: the refined diagonal intersection of the fundamental class of $\mathbb P^1$ with the point class is the point class, and proper pushforward to the point corner gives its generator.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Route: keep the point/projective-line geometry and the identification $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)\simeq k\oplus k[-2]$ of [[ex-unequal-dimensional-proper-pushforwards-have-the-summed-dimension-ext-bm-shift]] (Schubert cells and the cellular cochain theorem applied to $\mathbb P^1=\operatorname{Gr}_1(\mathbb C^2)$). Step 1 (the two classes): the unit $\alpha:k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ includes $H^0$ and is the generator of $\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$; the evaluation map onto $H^0$ followed by the shift gives $\beta:R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, the generator of $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$. Step 2 (composition): $\beta[-1]\circ\alpha:k\to k$ is evaluation of the constant class $1\in H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)$ at the chosen point, hence the identity; by [[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] this composite is $\Phi^{-1}$ of the convolution product, so $\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ and $i=j=k=1$ recovers the diagonal unit in the opposite-composition convention. Step 3 (geometric product): $\Phi(\alpha)$ is the positive fundamental class $[\mathbb P^1]\in H^{\mathrm{BM}}_2(\mathbb P^1;k)$ and $\Phi(\beta)$ is the normalized point class $[\mathrm{pt}]\in H^{\mathrm{BM}}_0(\mathbb P^1;k)$, both fixed by the positive complex orientation; the product theorem gives $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=\Phi(\alpha*\beta)=[\mathrm{pt}]$. Concretely, the middle factor is $X_2=\mathbb P^1$, its normal contributes the drop $2d_2=2$, the external-product refined diagonal intersection of the two classes is the point class, and the proper-forgetting pushforward to $Z_{11}=\mathrm{pt}$ integrates it to the generator. This independently checks the middle drop $2$, the source-first order and the absence of an extra shift sign; the swapped corner is not confused with the identity. Sources: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example 0.6 and SS3.2 (cells and cohomology of $\mathbb CP^n$), and the local packet contract for the convolution check.

title: Proper Cohomological Descent And Constructible Hypercovers

items.title: Bicosimplicial total complexes agree with diagonal totalization
items.statement: For a bicosimplicial complex $K^{p,r,q}$ of modules over a commutative ring, with $p,r\geq0$ and one fixed lower bound $q\geq a$, the alternating-face total complex and the diagonal alternating-face total complex are naturally chain-homotopy equivalent: $$\operatorname{Tot}_{p,r,q}K^{p,r,q}\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_{n,q}K^{n,n,q}.$$ On the left total degree is $p+r+q$ and differential is $\delta_h+(-1)^p\delta_v+(-1)^{p+r}d$; on the right total degree is $n+q$ and differential is $\delta_{\mathrm{diag}}+(-1)^nd$. These comparisons preserve augmentation and apply to coherent derived diagrams after a supplied functorial strict resolution. They require no dimensional finiteness of the coefficient modules and no choice principle. Normalization can be applied on either side without changing the conclusion.
items.strategy: Sources: Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, Appendix A (acyclic-model comparison of bisimplicial totals, PDF pp. 35-36, read in full) and Stacks Project, Simplicial Methods, Sections 23 and 27 (normalization, simplex and prism identities, read in full). Write [[def-chain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]] for complexes and chain homotopies and [[def-direct-sum-total-complex-of-a-double-complex]] for Tot. Step 1 (specified contractions on universal models). The evaluation $M\mapsto M_{p,r}$ is represented by the free bisimplicial module $Q_{p,r}$ on $\Delta[p]\times\Delta[r]$: an element $x\in M_{p,r}$ defines the unique homomorphism sending the universal generator to $x$. The diagonal alternating-face complex of $Q_{p,r}$ is the simplicial chain complex of the product of the two standard simplices, while the double total complex is the tensor product of their separate simplicial chain complexes. Both have a specified contraction onto the vertex $(0,0)$: the monotone contraction to the initial vertex gives a simplicial homotopy whose chain homotopy is the prism of [[lem-simplicial-normalization-prism-and-trivial-fibration-criterion]], and the unnormalized point complex is contracted by $e_j\mapsto e_{j+1}$ for odd $j$ and zero for even $j$; for the tensor product the contraction is $H(x\otimes y)=h(x)\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}e(x)\otimes h(y)$, where $e$ is the vertex projector, and direct expansion gives $\partial H+H\partial=1-e\otimes e$. Every positive-degree cycle and augmentation-zero degree-zero cycle in either model thus has a specified finite filling. Step 2 (natural maps by universal recursion). Construct a natural chain map from the diagonal complex to the double total complex recursively. In degree zero it is the identity on $M_{0,0}$. On the universal diagonal degree-$n$ generator of $Q_{n,n}$, the already constructed image of its boundary is a cycle, of augmentation zero if $n=1$; fill this cycle by the contraction of Step 1, and send an arbitrary element of $M_{n,n}$ to the image of this filling under its unique representing map. This is additive and natural because the representing map is linear in that element, and its boundary is the required lower-degree image. The same recursion on a universal total degree-$n$ generator in each $Q_{p,r}$ with $p+r=n$ constructs a chain map in the reverse direction. Both maps are the identity in degree zero. Step 3 (homotopy inverse). Any two natural maps constructed this way that agree in degree zero are naturally chain homotopic: on a universal degree-$n$ generator $z$, the difference of the two maps on $z$ minus the already chosen homotopy on its boundary is an augmentation-zero cycle, filled by the same specified model contraction, and evaluated on arbitrary elements using their representing maps; this gives $\partial H+H\partial=f-g$ in every degree. Apply this to the two composite maps and the identities. All maps and homotopies are finite linear combinations of face and degeneracy operators, so no unspecified filling is selected. Step 4 (opposite category, no duality). Reverse those finite operator formulas to obtain the cochain maps and cochain homotopies for bicosimplicial modules: a universal operator identity is an equality in the free additive category on $\Delta\times\Delta$, and reversing every arrow turns a simplicial identity into its cosimplicial identity and reverses the direction of each natural map. Hence the two composite identities and their homotopies remain valid for every bicosimplicial module without taking an algebraic dual or imposing finite-dimensionality. Apply them separately in each internal degree $q$; they commute with the internal differential by naturality, and the signs in the Statement make the internal terms cancel in the homotopy equation, since each cochain homotopy lowers $p+r$ by one. Step 5 (finiteness, totals and normalization). In total degree $m$, only $p+r\leq m-a$ contributes on the left and $n\leq m-a$ on the right, so every map and homotopy uses finitely many coefficient terms and [[prop-sum-and-product-totalisations-agree-on-finite-diagonal-double-complexes]] permits either sum or product total notation. Normalization is a natural homotopy equivalence by [[lem-simplicial-normalization-prism-and-trivial-fibration-criterion]], also in the opposite cosimplicial category, so it may be applied on either side. The constructions preserve the unique degree-zero augmentation and commute with morphisms of complexes; a supplied strict derived resolution is used only to present a coherent diagram, and the natural homotopy equivalence descends to the derived category independently of that presentation.

items.title: Proper surjections have cohomological descent for constructible field sheaves
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the supplied injective-resolution six-functor construction. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper surjective morphism of finite-type complex algebraic varieties, and let $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ for a field $k$. Write $Y_p=Y\times_X\cdots\times_XY$ with $p+1$ factors, $f_p:Y_p\to X$, and $F_p=f_p^*F$. In the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]] the natural augmented derived Cech map is a quasi-isomorphism: $$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Rf_{p*}F_p.$$ Here totalization is the normalized or unnormalized alternating-face total supplied by the simplicial-derived construction. There is one fixed lower cochain bound; consequently its diagonals are finite in every degree. The claim commutes with arbitrary algebraic base change and coefficient morphisms. In particular $R\Gamma(X,F)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_pR\Gamma(Y_p,F_p)$. Individual fibers of $f$ need not be cohomologically acyclic, connected, or smooth.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen Appendix A (proper Cech descent by stalk contraction; PDF pp. 35-36, read in full) and Stacks Project, Hypercoverings, Lemma 3.9 and Lemmas 4.2-4.5 (general-site cohomological descent; PDF pp. 5-10, read in full). [F1] The coherent six-operation contract over an arbitrary coefficient field for analytic algebraic maps on bounded constructible complexes is [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]: it gives exact inverse image, ordinary proper base change, its naturality for all Cech faces and degeneracies, and the identification of $f_p^*F$ restricted to a geometric fiber with the constant pullback of $F_x$. The coefficient category is [[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and the restriction of the operations to it over every field, with each pulled coefficient again bounded below, is [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]]. [F2] [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] supplies the functorial simplicial-derived total model with a uniform internal lower bound and finite-degree truncations; its local-section descent conclusion is not used as proper descent. [F3] [[thm-bounded-filtered-complex-spectral-sequence-abuts-to-filtered-homology]] gives convergence for degreewise finite filtrations, with cohomological reindexing. [A1] AC is inherited only by the supplied resolution construction; selecting one point for the stalk argument requires only a single nonempty-set selection, not a simultaneously chosen family of sections. Step 1.1 (bounded model and finite diagonals). Choose a lower bound $a$ for the cochain model of $F$; exact pullback preserves it and right-derived pushforward gives a functorial double model in degrees $p\geq0$, $q\geq a$, so in total degree $m$ there are only $0\leq p\leq m-a$ terms. Take the cone of the augmented map and filter by $p$, still bounded below after placing the augmentation in column $p=-1$. Stalks commute with its finite pieces, so by the finite-filtration spectral sequence of [F3] it suffices to prove exactness of every augmented horizontal stalk row after taking internal cohomology. Step 2.1 (stalk rows and one chosen point). Fix $x\in X$ and put $K=F_x$; surjectivity gives a nonempty proper fiber $S=Y_x$, and proper base change identifies the augmented horizontal row in internal degree $q$ with $H^q(K)\to H^q(S,K)\to H^q(S^2,K)\to\cdots$, where $K$ on each $S^{p+1}$ is its constant derived pullback from the point; [F1] intertwines all deletion and repetition maps. Pick one point $y\in S$; for $p\geq1$ let $j_p:S^p\to S^{p+1}$ insert $y$ as first coordinate and let $j_0:\mathrm{pt}\to S$ be this point. Pullback gives maps $h_p=j_p^*:H^q(S^{p+1},K)\to H^q(S^p,K)$, with $h_0$ landing in $H^q(K)$. No assertion that any positive cohomology group of $S$ vanishes is made. Step 3.1 (explicit contraction). If $d_i:S^{p+2}\to S^{p+1}$ deletes coordinate $i$, the insertion identities are $d_0j_{p+1}=\operatorname{id}$ and $d_ij_{p+1}=j_pd_{i-1}$ for $i>0$. On the augmented row put $\delta_p=\sum_{i=0}^{p+1}(-1)^id_i^*$ and let $\delta_{-1}:H^q(K)\to H^q(S,K)$ be constant pullback. The displayed identities give $h_{p+1}\delta_p+\delta_{p-1}h_p=\operatorname{id}$ for every $p\geq0$, and $h_0\delta_{-1}=\operatorname{id}$: the $i=0$ term is the identity and the terms $i>0$ are precisely the negatives of $\delta_{p-1}h_p$. Every horizontal stalk row is thus contracted, including its augmentation and every internal degree $q$; this uses functorial pullback on cohomology, not an acyclicity assumption about individual fibers or a global section of $f$. Step 4.1 (conclusion). The horizontal spectral sequence of the augmented cone has zero next page at every stalk by Step 3.1; its filtration is finite in each total degree by Step 1.1, so [F3] gives zero stalk cohomology of the cone. A complex of sheaves with all cohomology stalks zero is acyclic, proving the asserted quasi-isomorphism. All algebraic base changes of $f$ remain proper surjective and the same base-change identifications prove the pulled-back assertion without choosing compatible points; naturality of the augmentation follows from its units and face maps. Applying derived global sections to the supplied finite-diagonal total model gives the global statement. AC is inherited exactly through [A1].

items.title: Proper hypercovers compute constructible derived cohomology
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Assume $X_0\to X$ is proper surjective and, for each $p>0$, $X_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$ is proper surjective over $X$, where skeleton and coskeleton are the standard finite-limit constructions of the simplicial category and the target is the matching object. Such an object is a proper hypercover; no smoothness or fiber acyclicity is assumed. For $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ over a field, and $a_p:X_p\to X$, the augmentation gives $$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Ra_{p*}a_p^*F,\qquad R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F).$$ There is a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$. If $F$ has cochain lower bound $a$, every diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite; degree $m$ and its differential are determined by levels through $p=m-a+1$. All proper-hypercover refinements induce the same comparison via the base object; any two such hypercovers have a proper common refinement. For $F=k_X$, $a=0$, this is the first-quadrant spectral sequence required for smooth-projective hyperresolutions.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen Appendix A Proposition A.4, Lemma A.5 and Corollaries A.7-A.9 (bounded-hypercover bisimplicial Cech and retract argument; PDF pp. 35-38, read in full) and Stacks Project, Hypercoverings, Lemmas 4.2-4.5 and 5.1-5.3 (PDF pp. 5-10, read in full). [F1] [[lem-proper-surjective-maps-have-cohomological-descent-for-constructible-field-sheaves]] proves actual proper Cech descent, including arbitrary base change for bounded constructible coefficient complexes over any field. [F2] [[lem-bicosimplicial-derived-total-complex-agrees-with-diagonal-totalization]] supplies the natural alternating-face diagonal/double-total homotopy equivalence. [F3] [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]] and [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] supply the ordinary coherent operations on bounded algebraically constructible complexes ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]), while [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] supplies functorial coherent derived diagrams, strict simplicial resolutions, right-derived composition and their uniformly bounded-below total model; [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]] fixes the analytic topology of the varieties. [F4] [[thm-bounded-filtered-complex-spectral-sequence-abuts-to-filtered-homology]] gives convergence for degreewise finite filtrations. [A1] AC is inherited only through the resolution inputs and [F1]; the finite coskeleton, product and retract constructions below make no new arbitrary selections. The proof reconstructs the matching-map vocabulary of [[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]] inline: for the augmented simplicial variety $X_\bullet\to X$, $\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}$ is the simplicial truncation and $\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}$ its right adjoint, formed by the finite limit formulas, and the matching object at level $p$ is $M_p=\lim_{[p]\to[k],k<p}X_k$. Step 1.1 (height zero). Let $U\to X$ be a bounded proper hypercover of height zero, that is $U=\operatorname{cosk}_0U_0$; this is the Cech nerve of the proper surjection $U_0\to X$, so [F1] proves both the sheaf and global augmentations. Suppose inductively they are proved for all bounded heights at most $n$, and let $U=\operatorname{cosk}_{n+1}U$ have height $n+1$. Put $V=\operatorname{cosk}_nU$: it is a proper hypercover of height at most $n$, since its original matching maps through degree $n$ are unchanged and its later matching maps are isomorphisms, so the inductive hypothesis applies to $V$. Step 2.1 (levelwise proper surjectivity). For every $j$, $U_j\to V_j$ is proper surjective. For $j\leq n$ it is the identity; in higher degree it is the map $\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{sk}_{n+1}\Delta[j],U)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{sk}_n\Delta[j],U)$ between finite matching limits, and attaching the finitely many nondegenerate $(n+1)$-faces of $\Delta[j]$ to its $n$-skeleton makes it a Cartesian pullback of the finite product of the matching map $U_{n+1}\to M_{n+1}U$. A finite product over $X$ of proper surjections and any base change thereof is proper surjective; no local sections are required. Step 3.1 (bisimplicial Cech model). Form $W_{r,j}=U_j\times_{V_j}\cdots\times_{V_j}U_j$ with $r+1$ factors, horizontally the Cech nerve of $U_j\to V_j$, and pull coefficients from $X$ throughout. By [F1] and Step 2.1 every horizontally augmented derived row computes the coefficient complex on $V_j$, before and after pushing to $X$, so the induced augmentation into the double total is a quasi-isomorphism: apply [F4] to the triple-complex model of [F3], whose degrees $r,j\geq0$, $q\geq a$ have finite total diagonals. The inductive augmentation for $V$ then gives $F\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_{r,j}Ra_{W_{r,j}*}F_{W_{r,j}}$ and the analogous global statement; by [F2] this double total is naturally equivalent to the total on the diagonal $D_j=W_{j,j}$. Step 4.1 (retract over $X$). The bounded hypercover $U$ is a retract over $X$ of $D$: the map $i:U\to D$ repeats the same $U_j$ point in all $j+1$ horizontal factors, and through degree $n$ the map $U_j\to V_j$ is the identity, so $D_j=U_j$ there; in degree $n+1$ choose the first projection $D_{n+1}\to U_{n+1}$, whose faces and degeneracies agree with the degree-$\leq n$ identity maps because every horizontal factor has the same image in $V$ and those lower-degree maps are identities. This defines a map of $(n+1)$-truncations, and the universal property $U=\operatorname{cosk}_{n+1}U$ extends it uniquely to $r:D\to U$; the composite $ri$ is the identity through degree $n+1$, hence in every degree by the same universal property. Coefficient pullback reverses these maps, so the augmented total for $U$ is a retract of the augmented total for $D$, and a retract of an acyclic cone is acyclic. This completes the bounded-height induction. Step 5.1 (arbitrary height by truncation). For an arbitrary proper hypercover $U$, its $N$-coskeleton $U^{(N)}=\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NU$ is a bounded proper hypercover, so Step 4.1 applies to it; the map $U\to U^{(N)}$ is the identity through simplicial degree $N$. In the strict derived total model every internal degree is at least $a$, so total degrees $m-1,m,m+1$ use only simplicial degrees at most $m-a+1$. Choosing $N\geq\max(0,m-a+1)$ makes the totals for $U$ and $U^{(N)}$ have the same objects and differentials in these three degrees, hence the same degree-$m$ cohomology and the same augmentation maps; since this holds for every $m$, the augmentation for $U$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This is a finite-degree truncation argument, not an interchange of stalks or cohomology with an unjustified infinite product. Step 6.1 (spectral sequence and convergence). Filter the global total by simplicial degree. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)$ with alternating pullback by faces as first differential. In degree $m$ its filtration has only $0\leq p\leq m-a$ nonzero pieces, so [F4] identifies the stationary page with the finite associated graded of $H^m(X,F)$, proving strong convergence; no finite-dimensionality of the individual $H^q$ groups is needed. Step 7.1 (refinements and constant coefficients). For two proper hypercovers $U,V$ over $X$, their levelwise product $R_j=U_j\times_XV_j$ is a common proper hypercover: finite matching limits commute with products, so each matching map of $R$ is the product over $X$ of the matching maps of $U$ and $V$ and is proper surjective, and its projections give the two refinements. By Step 5.1 both augmentations identify their totals with the same coefficient complex on $X$, so the comparison maps coincide after those identifications. A smooth-projective refinement is a separate supplied construction: the product of smooth maps over singular $X$ need not be smooth. For $F=k_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the page is exactly the stated first-quadrant spectral sequence. AC is inherited precisely through [A1].

title: Proper Cohomological Descent And Constructible Hypercovers Examples

items.title: Proper Cech descent does not require acyclic fibers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; it is inherited from the descent lemma and from the field-dual corollary. Let $k$ be a field and let $S=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ be the complex projective line, realized as the classical complex algebraic variety obtained by gluing two affine lines along their punctured overlaps by $z=1/w$, with its analytic topology (equivalently, the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$). Then the unique morphism $f:S\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper surjective, the single fiber $S$ satisfies $H^2(S;k)\cong k\neq0$ and is therefore not cohomologically acyclic, and yet the augmented Cech complex computes the constant sheaf: the unaugmented product total $\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(S^{p+1},k)$ has cohomology $k$ in degree $0$ and zero in all other degrees. In every internal degree $q$ the augmented row $H^q(k)\to H^q(S,k)\to H^q(S^2,k)\to\cdots$ is contracted by inserting one chosen point as first coordinate, even though the $q=2$ row contains the nonzero group $H^2(S;k)$ at $p=0$.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Step 1 (the space). Construct $S=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ as the classical complex algebraic variety obtained by gluing the two affine models $\mathbb C$ with coordinate $z$ and $\mathbb C$ with coordinate $w$ along the principal open subsets $z\neq0$ and $w\neq0$ by the regular isomorphism $z=1/w$: the gluing of two affine models along an open subset is a classical prevariety by the definition, it is separated (the diagonal is closed, checked on the two charts), and the finite two-chart cover makes it finite type over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]); it carries the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]. The same two charts identify $S$ with the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ of [[def-one-point-compactification]]: the $z$-chart is a homeomorphism onto $\mathbb C$, the $w$-chart identifies the remaining point with $\infty$, and the transition $w=1/z$ is the corresponding homeomorphism of the pointed charts. Hence the analytic topology of $S$ is the one-point compactification topology and $S$ is compact Hausdorff ([[thm-one-point-compactification-properties]]). Step 2 (the map is proper surjective). $f$ is surjective because $S$ is nonempty. It is a projective morphism of classical varieties: the identity is a closed immersion $S\hookrightarrow \mathrm{pt}\times\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ and the projection to the point is the structure map ([[def-projective-morphism-classical]]); projective algebraic morphisms are proper in the analytic topology, and the descent lemma uses that properness ([[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]], [[lem-proper-surjective-maps-have-cohomological-descent-for-constructible-field-sheaves]]). Step 3 (the fiber is not acyclic). Stereographic projection is a homeomorphism $\widehat{\mathbb C}\to S^2$ ([[thm-stereographic-projection-riemann-sphere-homeomorphism]]); a homeomorphism is a homotopy equivalence, so it induces isomorphisms on singular homology ([[thm-homotopy-equivalences-induce-isomorphisms-on-singular-homology]]). Thus $H_2(S;k)\cong H_2(S^2;k)\cong k$ by [[cor-homology-of-spheres]], and the field-dual corollary gives $H^2(S;k)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_2(S;k),k)\cong k$ ([[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]]); in particular the single fiber of $f$ is not cohomologically acyclic. Step 4 (the rows are still contracted). The fiber of $f$ over the unique point is $S$ and the fiber powers are $S^{p+1}$. Choose one point $y\in S$ and let $j_p:S^p\to S^{p+1}$ insert $y$ as first coordinate for $p\geq1$, with $j_0:\mathrm{pt}\to S$ this point; putting $h_p=j_p^*$ and letting $\delta$ be the alternating sum of deletion pullbacks, the insertion identities $d_0j_{p+1}=\operatorname{id}$ and $d_ij_{p+1}=j_pd_{i-1}$ for $i>0$ give $h_{p+1}\delta_p+\delta_{p-1}h_p=\operatorname{id}$ in every internal degree $q$, including the augmentation. So the $q=2$ row, whose $p=0$ term is the nonzero group $H^2(S;k)\cong k$, is nevertheless exact with only the augmentation surviving. Step 5 (conclusion). By [[lem-proper-surjective-maps-have-cohomological-descent-for-constructible-field-sheaves]] applied to $f$ and the constant sheaf $k$, the augmented Cech total computes $k$: the unaugmented product total $\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(S^{p+1},k)$ has cohomology $k$ in degree $0$ and zero elsewhere. The example shows that proper Cech descent does not require acyclic fibers: the nonvanishing $H^2$ of the fiber is retained throughout the contracted rows and does not obstruct the descent quasi-isomorphism.

items.title: Hypercover total degree uses only a finite matching truncation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the proper-hypercover theorem. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be a proper hypercover and let $F$ be a coefficient complex in $D^b_c(X;k)$ with cochain lower bound $a$ ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]). Then the cohomology of the total complex in degree $m$, and its differential, are determined by the simplicial levels $p\leq m-a+1$ only; every hypercover truncation $\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NX_\bullet$ with $N\geq m-a+1$ computes the same $H^m(X,F)$. In particular for the constant sheaf $F=k_X$, where $a=0$, degree $n$ uses only levels through $n+1$. Keeping only the cochain terms through level $n$ and omitting the outgoing differential does not suffice in general: the differential out of the term $(p,q)=(n,0)$ of the Cech complex lands in the level $n+1$ term $(n+1,0)$.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]]. Step 1 (degree bookkeeping). In the total complex of the hypercover, the term in bidegree $(p,q)$ has $p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$; it contributes to total degree $p+q$. For a fixed total degree $m$, this gives $0\leq p\leq m-a$. The differentials entering and leaving total degree $m$ involve terms of total degree $m-1$, $m$ and $m+1$, so the largest simplicial level appearing there is $p=m+1-a$. Step 2 (truncation agrees). By [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]], the comparison of $X_\bullet$ with its $N$-coskeleton truncation $\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NX_\bullet$ is the identity through simplicial degree $N$, and the total complex in a fixed total degree uses only finitely many levels. Choosing $N\geq m-a+1$ makes the two total complexes agree in degrees $m-1$, $m$, $m+1$, hence they have the same $H^m$ and the same augmentation maps there; since $m$ was arbitrary, every truncation above the stated bound computes the same cohomology. Step 3 (constant coefficients and sharpness). For $F=k_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$, so degree $n$ uses levels through $n+1$. The bound is sharp: the term $(p,q)=(n,0)$ is $H^0(X_n,k)$, and its outgoing differential is the alternating sum of face pullbacks into the level $n+1$ term $H^0(X_{n+1},k)$ of total degree $n+1$; knowing $H^n$ requires this differential, so level $n$ alone is not enough. No infinite product and no separate convergence argument is used beyond the quoted total-degree statements of the theorem.
